(Ga) anulomapuggalokāsā

(C) Positive Inquiry: Person and Location

151. (Ka) yassa [M 2.0051] yattha kāyasaṅkhāro uppajjati tassa tattha vacīsaṅkhāro nirujjhissatīti?

151. (A) For a person for whom the bodily formation is arising in a certain plane, for that person, in that plane, will the verbal formation cease?

Dutiyajjhānaṃ tatiyajjhānaṃ samāpannānaṃ assāsapassāsānaṃ uppādakkhaṇe tesaṃ tattha kāyasaṅkhāro uppajjati, no ca tesaṃ tattha vacīsaṅkhāro nirujjhissati. Paṭhamajjhānaṃ samāpannānaṃ kāmāvacarānaṃ assāsapassāsānaṃ uppādakkhaṇe tesaṃ tattha kāyasaṅkhāro ca uppajjati vacīsaṅkhāro ca nirujjhissati.

For those who have entered the second jhāna and the third jhāna, at the arising-moment of in-breaths and out-breaths, for them, in that plane, the bodily formation is arising, but the verbal formation will not cease for them in that plane. For sense-sphere beings who have entered the first jhāna, at the arising-moment of in-breaths and out-breaths, for them, in that plane, the bodily formation is arising and the verbal formation will cease.

(Kha) yassa vā pana yattha vacīsaṅkhāro nirujjhissati tassa tattha kāyasaṅkhāro uppajjatīti?

(B) Or, for a person for whom the verbal formation will cease in a certain plane, for that person, in that plane, is the bodily formation arising?

Paṭhamajjhānaṃ samāpannānaṃ kāmāvacarānaṃ assāsapassāsānaṃ bhaṅgakkhaṇe tesaṃyeva vinā assāsapassāsehi cittassa uppādakkhaṇe rūpāvacarānaṃ arūpāvacarānaṃ tesaṃ tattha vacīsaṅkhāro nirujjhissati, no ca tesaṃ tattha kāyasaṅkhāro uppajjati. Paṭhamajjhānaṃ samāpannānaṃ kāmāvacarānaṃ assāsapassāsānaṃ [V 2.0072] uppādakkhaṇe tesaṃ tattha vacīsaṅkhāro ca nirujjhissati kāyasaṅkhāro ca uppajjati.

For sense-sphere beings who have entered the first jhāna, at the dissolution-moment of in-breaths and out-breaths; for those same persons, at the arising-moment of consciousness without in-breaths and out-breaths; and for beings of the fine-material sphere and the immaterial sphere—for them, in that plane, the verbal formation will cease, but the bodily formation is not arising for them in that plane. For sense-sphere beings who have entered the first jhāna, at the arising-moment of in-breaths and out-breaths, for them, in that plane, the verbal formation will cease and the bodily formation is arising.

(Ka) yassa yattha kāyasaṅkhāro uppajjati tassa tattha cittasaṅkhāro nirujjhissatīti? Āmantā.

(A) For a person for whom the bodily formation is arising in a certain plane, for that person, in that plane, will the mental formation cease? Yes.

(Kha) yassa vā pana yattha cittasaṅkhāro nirujjhissati tassa tattha kāyasaṅkhāro uppajjatīti?

(B) Or, for a person for whom the mental formation will cease in a certain plane, for that person, in that plane, is the bodily formation arising?

Sabbesaṃ cittassa bhaṅgakkhaṇe vinā assāsapassāsehi cittassa uppādakkhaṇe tesaṃ tattha cittasaṅkhāro nirujjhissati, no ca tesaṃ tattha [T 1.0429] kāyasaṅkhāro uppajjati. Assāsapassāsānaṃ uppādakkhaṇe tesaṃ tattha cittasaṅkhāro ca nirujjhissati kāyasaṅkhāro ca uppajjati.

For all beings at the dissolution-moment of consciousness, and for those at the arising-moment of consciousness without in-breaths and out-breaths—for them, in that plane, the mental formation will cease, but the bodily formation is not arising for them in that plane. At the arising-moment of in-breaths and out-breaths, for them, in that plane, the mental formation will cease and the bodily formation is arising.

152. (Ka) yassa yattha vacīsaṅkhāro uppajjati tassa tattha cittasaṅkhāro nirujjhissatīti? Āmantā.

152. (A) For a person for whom the verbal formation is arising in a certain plane, for that person, in that plane, will the mental formation cease? Yes.

(Kha) yassa vā pana yattha cittasaṅkhāro nirujjhissati tassa tattha vacīsaṅkhāro uppajjatīti?

(B) Or, for a person for whom the mental formation will cease in a certain plane, for that person, in that plane, is the verbal formation arising?

Sabbesaṃ cittassa bhaṅgakkhaṇe vinā vitakkavicārehi cittassa uppādakkhaṇe tesaṃ tattha cittasaṅkhāro nirujjhissati, no ca tesaṃ tattha vacīsaṅkhāro uppajjati. Vitakkavicārānaṃ uppādakkhaṇe tesaṃ tattha cittasaṅkhāro ca nirujjhissati vacīsaṅkhāro ca uppajjati.

For all beings at the dissolution-moment of consciousness, and for those at the arising-moment of consciousness without initial thought and sustained thought—for them, in that plane, the mental formation will cease, but the verbal formation is not arising for them in that plane. At the arising-moment of initial thought and sustained thought, for them, in that plane, the mental formation will cease and the verbal formation is arising.

(Gha) paccanīkapuggalo

(D) Negative Inquiry: Person

153. (Ka) yassa kāyasaṅkhāro nuppajjati tassa vacīsaṅkhāro na nirujjhissatīti?

153. (A) For one whose bodily formation is not arising, will his verbal formation not cease?

Sabbesaṃ cittassa bhaṅgakkhaṇe vinā assāsapassāsehi cittassa uppādakkhaṇe [M 2.0052] nirodhasamāpannānaṃ asaññasattānaṃ tesaṃ kāyasaṅkhāro nuppajjati, no ca tesaṃ vacīsaṅkhāro na nirujjhissati. Savitakkasavicārapacchimacittassa bhaṅgakkhaṇe avitakkaavicārapacchimacittasamaṅgīnaṃ yassa [V 2.0073] cittassa anantarā avitakkaavicāraṃ pacchimacittaṃ uppajjissati tesaṃ kāyasaṅkhāro ca nuppajjati vacīsaṅkhāro ca na nirujjhissati.

For all beings at the dissolution-moment of consciousness, for those at the arising-moment of consciousness without in-breaths and out-breaths, for those who have entered the attainment of cessation, and for non-percipient beings—for these the bodily formation is not arising, but for them the verbal formation will cease. For those at the dissolution-moment of the final consciousness with applied and sustained thought, for those endowed with the final consciousness without applied and sustained thought, and for those for whom, immediately after a certain consciousness, the final consciousness without applied and sustained thought will arise—for these, both the bodily formation is not arising and the verbal formation will not cease.

(Kha) yassa vā pana vacīsaṅkhāro na nirujjhissati tassa kāyasaṅkhāro nuppajjatīti? Āmantā.

(Kha) Or, for whom the verbal formation will not cease, for him is the bodily formation not arising? Yes.

(Ka) yassa kāyasaṅkhāro nuppajjati tassa cittasaṅkhāro na nirujjhissatīti?

(Ka) For whom the bodily formation is not arising, for him will the mental formation not cease?

Sabbesaṃ cittassa bhaṅgakkhaṇe vinā assāsapassāsehi cittassa [T 1.0430] uppādakkhaṇe nirodhasamāpannānaṃ asaññasattānaṃ tesaṃ kāyasaṅkhāro nuppajjati, no ca tesaṃ cittasaṅkhāro na nirujjhissati. Pacchimacittassa bhaṅgakkhaṇe tesaṃ kāyasaṅkhāro ca nuppajjati cittasaṅkhāro ca na nirujjhissati.

For all beings at the dissolution-moment of consciousness, for those at the arising-moment of consciousness without in-breaths and out-breaths, for those who have entered the attainment of cessation, and for non-percipient beings—for these the bodily formation is not arising, but for them the mental formation will cease. For those at the dissolution-moment of the final consciousness, for these both the bodily formation is not arising and the mental formation will not cease.

(Kha) yassa vā pana cittasaṅkhāro na nirujjhissati tassa kāyasaṅkhāro nuppajjatīti? Āmantā.

(Kha) Or, for whom the mental formation will not cease, for him is the bodily formation not arising? Yes.

154. (Ka) yassa vacīsaṅkhāro nuppajjati tassa cittasaṅkhāro na nirujjhissatīti?

154. (Ka) For whom the verbal formation is not arising, for him will the mental formation not cease?

Sabbesaṃ cittassa bhaṅgakkhaṇe vinā vitakkavicārehi cittassa uppādakkhaṇe nirodhasamāpannānaṃ asaññasattānaṃ tesaṃ vacīsaṅkhāro nuppajjati, no ca tesaṃ cittasaṅkhāro na nirujjhissati. Pacchimacittassa bhaṅgakkhaṇe tesaṃ vacīsaṅkhāro ca nuppajjati cittasaṅkhāro ca na nirujjhissati.

For all beings at the dissolution-moment of consciousness, for those at the arising-moment of consciousness without applied and sustained thought, for those who have entered the attainment of cessation, and for non-percipient beings—for these the verbal formation is not arising, but for them the mental formation will cease. For those at the dissolution-moment of the final consciousness, for these both the verbal formation is not arising and the mental formation will not cease.

(Kha) yassa vā pana cittasaṅkhāro na nirujjhissati tassa vacīsaṅkhāro nuppajjatīti? Āmantā.

(Kha) Or, for whom the mental formation will not cease, for him is the verbal formation not arising? Yes.

(Ṅa) paccanīkaokāso

(Ṅa) The Contrary Occasion

155. Yattha kāyasaṅkhāro nuppajjati…pe….

155. Where the bodily formation is not arising…pe….

(Ca) paccanīkapuggalokāsā

(Ca) The Contrary Persons and Occasions

156. (Ka) yassa yattha kāyasaṅkhāro nuppajjati tassa tattha vacīsaṅkhāro na nirujjhissatīti?

156. (Ka) For whom, where the bodily formation is not arising, for him, there, will the verbal formation not cease?

Paṭhamajjhānaṃ samāpannānaṃ kāmāvacarānaṃ assāsapassāsānaṃ bhaṅgakkhaṇe tesaṃyeva vinā assāsapassāsehi cittassa uppādakkhaṇe rūpāvacarānaṃ arūpāvacarānaṃ [V 2.0074] tesaṃ tattha kāyasaṅkhāro nuppajjati, no ca tesaṃ tattha vacīsaṅkhāro na nirujjhissati. Savitakkasavicārapacchimacittassa bhaṅgakkhaṇe avitakkaavicārapacchimacittasamaṅgīnaṃ yassa cittassa anantarā avitakkaavicāraṃ pacchimacittaṃ uppajjissati dutiyajjhānaṃ [T 1.0431] tatiyajjhānaṃ samāpannānaṃ [M 2.0053] assāsapassāsānaṃ bhaṅgakkhaṇe tesaṃyeva vinā assāsapassāsehi cittassa uppādakkhaṇe catutthajjhānaṃ samāpannānaṃ asaññasattānaṃ tesaṃ tattha kāyasaṅkhāro ca nuppajjati vacīsaṅkhāro ca na nirujjhissati.

For sense-sphere beings who have attained the first jhāna, at the dissolution-moment of in-breaths and out-breaths; for those same beings, at the arising-moment of consciousness without in-breaths and out-breaths; and for those in the form sphere and the formless sphere—for them, there, the bodily formation is not arising, but for them, there, the verbal formation will cease. For those at the dissolution-moment of the final consciousness with applied and sustained thought; for those endowed with the final consciousness without applied and sustained thought; for those for whom, immediately after a certain consciousness, the final consciousness without applied and sustained thought will arise; for those who have attained the second and third jhānas, at the dissolution-moment of in-breaths and out-breaths; for those same beings, at the arising-moment of consciousness without in-breaths and out-breaths; for those who have attained the fourth jhāna; and for non-percipient beings—for them, there, both the bodily formation is not arising and the verbal formation will not cease.

(Kha) yassa vā pana yattha vacīsaṅkhāro na nirujjhissati tassa tattha kāyasaṅkhāro nuppajjatīti?

(Kha) Or again, for whom, where the verbal formation will not cease, for him, there, is the bodily formation not arising?

Dutiyajjhānaṃ tatiyajjhānaṃ samāpannānaṃ assāsapassāsānaṃ uppādakkhaṇe tesaṃ tattha vacīsaṅkhāro na nirujjhissati, no ca tesaṃ tattha kāyasaṅkhāro nuppajjati. Savitakkasavicārapacchimacittassa bhaṅgakkhaṇe avitakkaavicārapacchimacittasamaṅgīnaṃ yassa cittassa anantarā avitakkaavicāraṃ pacchimacittaṃ uppajjissati dutiyajjhānaṃ tatiyajjhānaṃ samāpannānaṃ assāsapassāsānaṃ bhaṅgakkhaṇe tesaṃyeva vinā assāsapassāsehi cittassa uppādakkhaṇe catutthajjhānaṃ samāpannānaṃ asaññasattānaṃ tesaṃ tattha vacīsaṅkhāro ca na nirujjhissati kāyasaṅkhāro ca nuppajjati.

For those who have attained the second and third jhānas, at the arising-moment of in-breaths and out-breaths, for them, there, the verbal formation will not cease, but for them, there, the bodily formation is arising. For those at the dissolution-moment of the final consciousness with applied and sustained thought; for those endowed with the final consciousness without applied and sustained thought; for those for whom, immediately after a certain consciousness, the final consciousness without applied and sustained thought will arise; for those who have attained the second and third jhānas, at the dissolution-moment of in-breaths and out-breaths; for those same beings at the arising-moment of consciousness without in-breaths and out-breaths; for those who have attained the fourth jhāna; and for non-percipient beings—for them, there, both the verbal formation will not cease and the bodily formation is not arising.

(Ka) yassa yattha kāyasaṅkhāro nuppajjati tassa tattha cittasaṅkhāro na nirujjhissatīti?

(Ka) For whom, where the bodily formation is not arising, for him, there, will the mental formation not cease?

Sabbesaṃ cittassa bhaṅgakkhaṇe vinā assāsapassāsehi cittassa uppādakkhaṇe tesaṃ tattha kāyasaṅkhāro nuppajjati, no ca tesaṃ tattha cittasaṅkhāro na nirujjhissati. Pacchimacittassa bhaṅgakkhaṇe asaññasattānaṃ tesaṃ tattha kāyasaṅkhāro ca nuppajjati cittasaṅkhāro ca na nirujjhissati.

At the dissolution-moment of consciousness of all beings, and at the arising-moment of consciousness without in-breaths and out-breaths—for them, there, the bodily formation is not arising, but for them, there, the mental formation will cease. At the dissolution-moment of the final consciousness, and for non-percipient beings—for them, there, both the bodily formation is not arising and the mental formation will not cease.

(Kha) yassa vā pana yattha cittasaṅkhāro na nirujjhissati tassa tattha kāyasaṅkhāro nuppajjatīti? Āmantā.

(Kha) Or again, for whom, where the mental formation will not cease, for him, there, is the bodily formation not arising? Yes.

157. (Ka) yassa [T 1.0432][V 2.0075] yattha vacīsaṅkhāro nuppajjati tassa tattha cittasaṅkhāro na nirujjhissatīti?

157. (Ka) For whom, where the verbal formation is not arising, for him, there, will the mental formation not cease?

Sabbesaṃ cittassa bhaṅgakkhaṇe vinā vitakkavicārehi cittassa uppādakkhaṇe tesaṃ tattha vacīsaṅkhāro nuppajjati, no ca tesaṃ tattha cittasaṅkhāro na nirujjhissati. Pacchimacittassa bhaṅgakkhaṇe asaññasattānaṃ tesaṃ tattha vacīsaṅkhāro ca nuppajjati cittasaṅkhāro ca na nirujjhissati.

At the dissolution-moment of consciousness of all beings, and at the arising-moment of consciousness without applied and sustained thought—for them, there, the verbal formation is not arising, but for them, there, the mental formation will cease. At the dissolution-moment of the final consciousness, and for non-percipient beings—for them, there, both the verbal formation is not arising and the mental formation will not cease.

(Kha) yassa vā pana yattha cittasaṅkhāro na nirujjhissati tassa tattha vacīsaṅkhāro nuppajjatīti? Āmantā.

(Kha) Or again, for whom, where the mental formation will not cease, for him, there, is the verbal formation not arising? Yes.

(6) Atītānāgatavāro

(6) The Section on the Past and Future

(Ka) anulomapuggalo

(Ka) Forward Section: Persons

158. (Ka) yassa kāyasaṅkhāro uppajjittha tassa vacīsaṅkhāro nirujjhissatīti?

158. (Ka) For whom the bodily formation has arisen, for him will the verbal formation cease?

Savitakkasavicārapacchimacittassa bhaṅgakkhaṇe avitakkaavicārapacchimacittasamaṅgīnaṃ yassa cittassa anantarā avitakkaavicāraṃ pacchimacittaṃ uppajjissati tesaṃ [M 2.0054] kāyasaṅkhāro uppajjittha, no ca tesaṃ vacīsaṅkhāro nirujjhissati. Itaresaṃ tesaṃ kāyasaṅkhāro ca uppajjittha vacīsaṅkhāro ca nirujjhissati.

For those at the dissolution-moment of the final consciousness with initial and sustained thought, for those endowed with the final consciousness without initial and sustained thought, and for those for whom, immediately after a certain consciousness, a final consciousness without initial and sustained thought will arise—for them the bodily formation has arisen, but for them the verbal formation will not cease. For the others, the bodily formation has also arisen and the verbal formation will also cease.

(Kha) yassa vā pana vacīsaṅkhāro nirujjhissati tassa kāyasaṅkhāro uppajjitthāti? Āmantā.

Or again, for a person for whom the verbal formation will cease, for that person has the bodily formation arisen? Yes.

(Ka) yassa kāyasaṅkhāro uppajjittha tassa cittasaṅkhāro nirujjhissatīti?

For a person for whom the bodily formation has arisen, for that person will the mental formation cease?

Pacchimacittassa bhaṅgakkhaṇe tesaṃ kāyasaṅkhāro uppajjittha, no ca tesaṃ cittasaṅkhāro nirujjhissati. Itaresaṃ tesaṃ kāyasaṅkhāro ca uppajjittha cittasaṅkhāro ca nirujjhissati.

For those at the dissolution-moment of the final consciousness, the bodily formation has arisen, but for them the mental formation will not cease. For the others, the bodily formation has also arisen and the mental formation will also cease.

(Kha) yassa vā [T 1.0433] pana cittasaṅkhāro nirujjhissati tassa kāyasaṅkhāro uppajjitthāti? Āmantā.

Or again, for a person for whom the mental formation will cease, for that person has the bodily formation arisen? Yes.

(Yathā nirodhavāre atītānāgatā pucchā anulomampi paccanīkampi evaṃ [V 2.0076] uppādanirodhavārepi atītānāgatā pucchā anulomampi paccanīkampi vibhajitabbaṃ asammohantena nirodhavārena sadisaṃ, natthi nānākaraṇaṃ.)

Just as in the Cessation Section the questions on the past and future, both forward and reverse, were analyzed, so too in the Arising-Cessation Section the questions on the past and future, both forward and reverse, should be analyzed without confusion. It is similar to the Cessation Section; there is no difference.

Uppādanirodhavāro.

The Arising-Cessation Section is finished.

3. Pariññāvāro

3. 6. The Section on Full Understanding of Formations

1-6. Paccuppannavārādi

1-6. The Section on the Present, etc.

159. (Ka) yo kāyasaṅkhāraṃ parijānāti so vacīsaṅkhāraṃ parijānātīti? Āmantā.

159. Does a person who fully understands the bodily formation also fully understand the verbal formation? Yes.

(Kha) yo vā pana vacīsaṅkhāraṃ parijānāti so kāyasaṅkhāraṃ parijānātīti? Āmantā.

Or again, does a person who fully understands the verbal formation also fully understand the bodily formation? Yes.

(Yathā khandhayamake pariññāvāraṃ vibhattaṃ evaṃ saṅkhārayamakepi pariññāvāraṃ vibhajitabbaṃ.)

Just as the Section on Full Understanding was analyzed in the Yamaka on the Aggregates, so too in the Yamaka on the Formations the Section on Full Understanding should be analyzed.

Pariññāvāro.

The Section on Full Understanding is finished.

Saṅkhārayamakaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Yamaka on Formations is finished.

Namo tassa bhagavato arahato sammāsambuddhassa

Homage to that Blessed One, the Arahant, the Perfectly Self-Enlightened One.

7. Anusayayamakaṃ

7. 7. The Yamaka on Underlying Tendencies

1. Sattānusayā [T 1.0434][M 2.0055][V 2.0077] – kāmarāgānusayo, paṭighānusayo, mānānusayo, diṭṭhānusayo, vicikicchānusayo, bhavarāgānusayo, avijjānusayo.

1. There are seven underlying tendencies: the underlying tendency to sensual lust, the underlying tendency to aversion, the underlying tendency to conceit, the underlying tendency to views, the underlying tendency to doubt, the underlying tendency to craving for existence, and the underlying tendency to ignorance.

1. Uppattiṭṭhānavāro

1. The Section on the Basis of Occurrence

2. Kattha kāmarāgānusayo anuseti? Kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu ettha kāmarāgānusayo anuseti.

2. Where does the underlying tendency of sensual lust lie? In the sense-sphere element and in two feelings; herein the underlying tendency of sensual lust lies.

Kattha paṭighānusayo anuseti? Dukkhāya vedanāya ettha paṭighānusayo anuseti.

Where does the underlying tendency of aversion lie? In painful feeling; herein the underlying tendency of aversion lies.

Kattha mānānusayo anuseti? Kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā ettha mānānusayo anuseti.

Where does the underlying tendency of conceit lie? In the sense-sphere element, in two feelings, in the fine-material element, and in the immaterial element; herein the underlying tendency of conceit lies.

Kattha diṭṭhānusayo anuseti? Sabbasakkāyapariyāpannesu dhammesu ettha diṭṭhānusayo anuseti.

Where does the underlying tendency of views lie? In all phenomena comprised in personality; herein the underlying tendency of views lies.

Kattha vicikicchānusayo anuseti? Sabbasakkāyapariyāpannesu dhammesu ettha vicikicchānusayo anuseti.

Where does the underlying tendency of doubt lie? In all phenomena comprised in personality; herein the underlying tendency of doubt lies.

Kattha bhavarāgānusayo anuseti? Rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā ettha bhavarāgānusayo anuseti.

Where does the underlying tendency of craving for existence lie? In the fine-material element and the immaterial element; herein the underlying tendency of craving for existence lies.

Kattha [V 2.0078] avijjānusayo anuseti? Sabbasakkāyapariyāpannesu dhammesu ettha avijjānusayo anuseti.

Where does the underlying tendency of ignorance lie? In all phenomena comprised in personality; herein the underlying tendency of ignorance lies.

Uppattiṭṭhānavāro.

The Section on the Basis of Occurrence is finished.

2. Mahāvāro 1. anusayavāro

2. Great Section 1. Section on Underlying Tendencies

(Ka) anulomapuggalo

Forward (Persons)

3. (Ka) yassa [M 2.0056] kāmarāgānusayo anuseti tassa paṭighānusayo anusetīti? Āmantā.

3. For whomever the underlying tendency of sensual lust lies, for them does the underlying tendency of aversion lie? Yes.

(Kha) yassa vā pana paṭighānusayo anuseti tassa kāmarāgānusayo anusetīti? Āmantā.

Or, for whomever the underlying tendency of aversion lies, for them does the underlying tendency of sensual lust lie? Yes.

(Ka) yassa kāmarāgānusayo anuseti [T 1.0435] tassa mānānusayo anusetīti? Āmantā.

For whomever the underlying tendency of sensual lust lies, for them does the underlying tendency of conceit lie? Yes.

(Kha) yassa vā pana mānānusayo anuseti tassa kāmarāgānusayo anusetīti?

Or, for whomever the underlying tendency of conceit lies, for them does the underlying tendency of sensual lust lie?

Anāgāmissa mānānusayo anuseti, no ca tassa kāmarāgānusayo anuseti. Tiṇṇaṃ puggalānaṃ mānānusayo ca anuseti kāmarāgānusayo ca anuseti.

For a non-returner, the underlying tendency of conceit lies, but the underlying tendency of sensual lust does not lie for them. For the three persons, both the underlying tendency of conceit and the underlying tendency of sensual lust lie.

(Ka) yassa kāmarāgānusayo anuseti tassa diṭṭhānusayo anusetīti?

For whomever the underlying tendency of sensual lust lies, for them does the underlying tendency of views lie?

Dvinnaṃ puggalānaṃ kāmarāgānusayo anuseti, no ca tesaṃ diṭṭhānusayo anuseti. Puthujjanassa kāmarāgānusayo ca anuseti diṭṭhānusayo ca anuseti.

For two persons, the underlying tendency of sensual lust lies, but the underlying tendency of views does not lie for them. For a worldling, both the underlying tendency of sensual lust and the underlying tendency of views lie.

(Kha) yassa [V 2.0079] vā pana diṭṭhānusayo anuseti tassa kāmarāgānusayo anusetīti? Āmantā.

Or, for whomever the underlying tendency of views lies, for them does the underlying tendency of sensual lust lie? Yes.

(Ka) yassa kāmarāgānusayo anuseti tassa vicikicchānusayo anusetīti?

For whomever the underlying tendency of sensual lust lies, for them does the underlying tendency of doubt lie?

Dvinnaṃ puggalānaṃ kāmarāgānusayo anuseti, no ca tesaṃ vicikicchānusayo anuseti. Puthujjanassa kāmarāgānusayo ca anuseti vicikicchānusayo ca anuseti.

For two persons, the underlying tendency of sensual lust lies, but the underlying tendency of doubt does not lie for them. For a worldling, both the underlying tendency of sensual lust and the underlying tendency of doubt lie.

(Kha) yassa vā pana vicikicchānusayo anuseti tassa kāmarāgānusayo anusetīti? Āmantā.

Or, for whomever the underlying tendency of doubt lies, for them does the underlying tendency of sensual lust lie? Yes.

(Ka) yassa kāmarāgānusayo anuseti tassa bhavarāgānusayo anusetīti? Āmantā.

For whomever the underlying tendency of sensual lust lies, for them does the underlying tendency of craving for existence lie? Yes.

(Kha) yassa vā pana bhavarāgānusayo anuseti tassa kāmarāgānusayo anusetīti?

(b) Or, for whomever the latent tendency of craving for existence lies latent, for them does the latent tendency of sensual lust lie latent?

Anāgāmissa bhavarāgānusayo anuseti, no ca tassa kāmarāgānusayo anuseti. Tiṇṇaṃ puggalānaṃ bhavarāgānusayo ca anuseti kāmarāgānusayo ca anuseti.

For a non-returner, the latent tendency of craving for existence lies latent, but for them the latent tendency of sensual lust does not lie latent. For the three persons, both the latent tendency of craving for existence and the latent tendency of sensual lust lie latent.

(Ka) yassa kāmarāgānusayo anuseti tassa avijjānusayo anusetīti? Āmantā.

(a) For whomever the latent tendency of sensual lust lies latent, for them does the latent tendency of ignorance lie latent? Yes.

(Kha) yassa vā pana avijjānusayo anuseti tassa [M 2.0057] kāmarāgānusayo anusetīti?

(b) Or, for whomever the latent tendency of ignorance lies latent, for them does the latent tendency of sensual lust lie latent?

Anāgāmissa [T 1.0436] avijjānusayo anuseti, no ca tassa kāmarāgānusayo anuseti. Tiṇṇaṃ puggalānaṃ avijjānusayo ca anuseti kāmarāgānusayo ca anuseti.

For a non-returner, the latent tendency of ignorance lies latent, but for them the latent tendency of sensual lust does not lie latent. For the three persons, both the latent tendency of ignorance and the latent tendency of sensual lust lie latent.

4. (Ka) yassa paṭighānusayo anuseti tassa mānānusayo anusetīti? Āmantā.

4. (a) For whomever the latent tendency of aversion lies latent, for them does the latent tendency of conceit lie latent? Yes.

(Kha) yassa vā pana mānānusayo anuseti tassa paṭighānusayo anusetīti?

(b) Or, for whomever the latent tendency of conceit lies latent, for them does the latent tendency of aversion lie latent?

Anāgāmissa mānānusayo anuseti, no ca tassa paṭighānusayo anuseti[V 2.0080]. Tiṇṇaṃ puggalānaṃ mānānusayo ca anuseti paṭighānusayo ca anuseti.

For a non-returner, the latent tendency of conceit lies latent, but for them the latent tendency of aversion does not lie latent. For the three persons, both the latent tendency of conceit and the latent tendency of aversion lie latent.

Yassa paṭighānusayo anuseti tassa diṭṭhānusayo…pe… vicikicchānusayo anusetīti? Dvinnaṃ puggalānaṃ paṭighānusayo anuseti, no ca tesaṃ vicikicchānusayo anuseti. Puthujjanassa paṭighānusayo ca anuseti vicikicchānusayo ca anuseti.

For whomever the latent tendency of aversion lies latent, for them does the latent tendency of views... the latent tendency of doubt lie latent? For two persons, the latent tendency of aversion lies latent, but for them the latent tendency of doubt does not lie latent. For a worldling, both the latent tendency of aversion and the latent tendency of doubt lie latent.

Yassa vā pana vicikicchānusayo anuseti tassa paṭighānusayo anusetīti? Āmantā.

Or, for whomever the latent tendency of doubt lies latent, for them does the latent tendency of aversion lie latent? Yes.

Yassa paṭighānusayo anuseti tassa bhavarāgānusayo…pe… avijjānusayo anusetīti? Āmantā.

For whomever the latent tendency of aversion lies latent, for them does the latent tendency of craving for existence... the latent tendency of ignorance lie latent? Yes.

Yassa vā pana avijjānusayo anuseti tassa paṭighānusayo anusetīti?

Or, for whomever the latent tendency of ignorance lies latent, for them does the latent tendency of aversion lie latent?

Anāgāmissa avijjānusayo anuseti, no ca tassa paṭighānusayo anuseti. Tiṇṇaṃ puggalānaṃ avijjānusayo ca anuseti paṭighānusayo ca anuseti.

For a non-returner, the latent tendency of ignorance lies latent, but for them the latent tendency of aversion does not lie latent. For the three persons, both the latent tendency of ignorance and the latent tendency of aversion lie latent.

5. Yassa mānānusayo anuseti tassa diṭṭhānusayo…pe… vicikicchānusayo anusetīti?

5. For whomever the latent tendency of conceit lies latent, for them does the latent tendency of views... the latent tendency of doubt lie latent?

Tiṇṇaṃ puggalānaṃ mānānusayo anuseti, no ca tesaṃ vicikicchānusayo anuseti. Puthujjanassa mānānusayo ca anuseti [T 1.0437] vicikicchānusayo ca anuseti.

For the three persons, the latent tendency of conceit lies latent, but for them the latent tendency of doubt does not lie latent. For a worldling, both the latent tendency of conceit and the latent tendency of doubt lie latent.

Yassa vā pana vicikicchānusayo anuseti tassa mānānusayo anusetīti? Āmantā.

Or, for whomever the latent tendency of doubt lies latent, for them does the latent tendency of conceit lie latent? Yes.

Yassa mānānusayo anuseti tassa bhavarāgānusayo…pe… avijjānusayo anusetīti? Āmantā.

For whomever the latent tendency of conceit lies latent, for them does the latent tendency of craving for existence... the latent tendency of ignorance lie latent? Yes.

Yassa vā pana avijjānusayo anuseti tassa mānānusayo anusetīti? Āmantā.

Or, for whomever the latent tendency of ignorance lies latent, for them does the latent tendency of conceit lie latent? Yes.

6. (Ka) yassa [M 2.0058][V 2.0081] diṭṭhānusayo anuseti tassa vicikicchānusayo anusetīti? Āmantā.

6. (a) For whomever the latent tendency of views lies latent, for them does the latent tendency of doubt lie latent? Yes.

(Kha) yassa vā pana vicikicchānusayo anuseti tassa diṭṭhānusayo anusetīti? Āmantā.

(b) Or, for whomever the latent tendency of doubt lies latent, for them does the latent tendency of views lie latent? Yes.

Yassa diṭṭhānusayo anuseti tassa bhavarāgānusayo…pe… avijjānusayo anusetīti? Āmantā.

For whomever the latent tendency of views lies latent, for them does the latent tendency of craving for existence... the latent tendency of ignorance lie latent? Yes.

Yassa vā pana avijjānusayo anuseti tassa diṭṭhānusayo anusetīti?

Or, for whomever the latent tendency of ignorance lies latent, for them does the latent tendency of views lie latent?

Tiṇṇaṃ puggalānaṃ avijjānusayo anuseti, no ca tesaṃ diṭṭhānusayo anuseti. Puthujjanassa avijjānusayo ca anuseti diṭṭhānusayo ca anuseti.

For the three persons, the latent tendency of ignorance lies latent, but for them the latent tendency of views does not lie latent. For a worldling, both the latent tendency of ignorance and the latent tendency of views lie latent.

7. Yassa vicikicchānusayo anuseti tassa bhavarāgānusayo…pe… avijjānusayo anusetīti? Āmantā.

7. For whomever the latent tendency of doubt lies latent, for them does the latent tendency of craving for existence... the latent tendency of ignorance lie latent? Yes.

Yassa vā pana avijjānusayo anuseti tassa [T 1.0438] vicikicchānusayo anusetīti?

Or, for whomever the latent tendency of ignorance lies latent, for them does the latent tendency of doubt lie latent?

Tiṇṇaṃ puggalānaṃ avijjānusayo anuseti, no ca tesaṃ vicikicchānusayo anuseti. Puthujjanassa avijjānusayo ca anuseti vicikicchānusayo ca anuseti.

For the three persons, the latent tendency of ignorance lies latent, but for them the latent tendency of doubt does not lie latent. For a worldling, both the latent tendency of ignorance and the latent tendency of doubt lie latent.

8. (Ka) yassa bhavarāgānusayo anuseti tassa avijjānusayo anusetīti? Āmantā.

8. (a) For whomever the latent tendency of craving for existence lies latent, for them does the latent tendency of ignorance lie latent? Yes.

(Kha) yassa vā pana avijjānusayo anuseti tassa bhavarāgānusayo anusetīti? Āmantā. (Ekamūlakaṃ )

(b) Or, for whomever the latent tendency of ignorance lies latent, for them does the latent tendency of craving for existence lie latent? Yes. (The Single-rooted Section)

9. (Ka) yassa kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca anusenti tassa mānānusayo anusetīti? Āmantā.

9. (a) For whomever the latent tendencies of sensual lust and aversion lie latent, for them does the latent tendency of conceit lie latent? Yes.

(Kha) yassa [V 2.0082] vā pana mānānusayo anuseti tassa kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca anusentīti?

(b) Or, for whomever the latent tendency of conceit lies latent, for them do the latent tendencies of sensual lust and aversion lie latent?

Anāgāmissa mānānusayo anuseti, no ca tassa kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca anusenti. Tiṇṇaṃ puggalānaṃ mānānusayo ca anuseti kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca anusenti.

For a non-returner, the latent tendency of conceit lies latent, but for them the latent tendencies of sensual lust and aversion do not lie latent. For the three persons, the latent tendency of conceit also lies latent, and the latent tendencies of sensual lust and aversion lie latent.

Yassa kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca anusenti tassa diṭṭhānusayo…pe… vicikicchānusayo anusetīti?

For whomever the latent tendencies of sensual lust and aversion lie latent, for them does the latent tendency of views... the latent tendency of doubt lie latent?

Dvinnaṃ puggalānaṃ kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca anusenti, no ca tesaṃ vicikicchānusayo anuseti. Puthujjanassa kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca anusenti [M 2.0059] vicikicchānusayo ca anuseti.

For two persons, the latent tendencies of sensual lust and aversion lie latent, but for them the latent tendency of doubt does not lie latent. For a worldling, the latent tendencies of sensual lust and aversion lie latent, and the latent tendency of doubt also lies latent.

Yassa vā pana vicikicchānusayo anuseti tassa kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca anusentīti? Āmantā.

Or, for whomever the latent tendency of doubt lies latent, for them do the latent tendencies of sensual lust and aversion lie latent? Yes.

Yassa kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca anusenti tassa bhavarāgānusayo…pe… avijjānusayo anusetīti? Āmantā.

For whomever the latent tendencies of sensual lust and aversion lie latent, for them does the latent tendency of craving for existence... the latent tendency of ignorance lie latent? Yes.

Yassa vā pana avijjānusayo anuseti tassa kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca anusentīti?

Or, for whomever the latent tendency of ignorance lies latent, for them do the latent tendencies of sensual lust and aversion lie latent?

Anāgāmissa avijjānusayo anuseti, no ca tassa kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca anusenti. Tiṇṇaṃ puggalānaṃ avijjānusayo ca anuseti kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca anusenti. (Dukamūlakaṃ)

For a non-returner, the latent tendency of ignorance lies latent, but for them the latent tendencies of sensual lust and aversion do not lie latent. For the three persons, the latent tendency of ignorance also lies latent, and the latent tendencies of sensual lust and aversion lie latent. (The Double-rooted Section)

10. Yassa [T 1.0439] kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca mānānusayo ca anusenti tassa diṭṭhānusayo…pe… vicikicchānusayo anusetīti?

10. For whomever the latent tendencies of sensual lust, aversion, and conceit lie latent, for them does the latent tendency of views... the latent tendency of doubt lie latent?

Dvinnaṃ puggalānaṃ kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca mānānusayo ca anusenti, no ca tesaṃ vicikicchānusayo anuseti. Puthujjanassa kāmarāgānusayo [V 2.0083] ca paṭighānusayo ca mānānusayo ca anusenti vicikicchānusayo ca anuseti.

For two persons, the underlying tendencies to sensual lust, to aversion, and to conceit lie latent, but the underlying tendency to doubt does not lie latent in them. For the worldling, the underlying tendencies to sensual lust, to aversion, and to conceit lie latent, and the underlying tendency to doubt also lies latent.

Yassa vā pana vicikicchānusayo anuseti tassa kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca mānānusayo ca anusentīti? Āmantā.

Or for one in whom the underlying tendency to doubt lies latent, do the underlying tendencies to sensual lust, to aversion, and to conceit also lie latent in him? Yes.

Yassa kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca mānānusayo ca anusenti tassa bhavarāgānusayo…pe… avijjānusayo anusetīti? Āmantā.

For one in whom the underlying tendencies to sensual lust, to aversion, and to conceit lie latent, does the underlying tendency to craving for existence… to ignorance also lie latent in him? Yes.

Yassa vā pana avijjānusayo anuseti tassa kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca mānānusayo ca anusentīti?

Or for one in whom the underlying tendency to ignorance lies latent, do the underlying tendencies to sensual lust, to aversion, and to conceit also lie latent in him?

Anāgāmissa avijjānusayo ca mānānusayo ca anusenti, no ca tassa kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca anusenti. Tiṇṇaṃ puggalānaṃ avijjānusayo ca anuseti kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca mānānusayo ca anusenti. (Tikamūlakaṃ)

For the non-returner, the underlying tendencies to ignorance and to conceit lie latent, but the underlying tendencies to sensual lust and to aversion do not lie latent in him. For three persons, the underlying tendency to ignorance lies latent, and the underlying tendencies to sensual lust, to aversion, and to conceit also lie latent.

11. (Ka) yassa kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca mānānusayo ca diṭṭhānusayo ca anusenti tassa vicikicchānusayo anusetīti? Āmantā.

11. For one in whom the underlying tendencies to sensual lust, to aversion, to conceit, and to views lie latent, does the underlying tendency to doubt also lie latent in him? Yes.

(Kha) yassa vā pana vicikicchānusayo anuseti tassa kāmarāgānusayo [M 2.0060] ca paṭighānusayo ca mānānusayo ca diṭṭhānusayo ca anusentīti? Āmantā.

Or for one in whom the underlying tendency to doubt lies latent, do the underlying tendencies to sensual lust, to aversion, to conceit, and to views also lie latent in him? Yes.

Yassa kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca mānānusayo ca diṭṭhānusayo ca anusenti [T 1.0440] tassa bhavarāgānusayo…pe… avijjānusayo anusetīti? Āmantā.

For one in whom the underlying tendencies to sensual lust, to aversion, to conceit, and to views lie latent, does the underlying tendency to craving for existence… to ignorance also lie latent in him? Yes.

Yassa vā pana avijjānusayo anuseti tassa kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca mānānusayo ca diṭṭhānusayo ca anusentīti?

Or for one in whom the underlying tendency to ignorance lies latent, do the underlying tendencies to sensual lust, to aversion, to conceit, and to views also lie latent in him?

Anāgāmissa avijjānusayo ca mānānusayo ca anusenti, no ca tassa kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca diṭṭhānusayo ca anusenti. Dvinnaṃ puggalānaṃ avijjānusayo ca kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca mānānusayo ca anusenti, no ca tesaṃ diṭṭhānusayo anuseti[V 2.0084]. Puthujjanassa avijjānusayo ca anuseti kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca mānānusayo ca diṭṭhānusayo ca anusenti. (Catukkamūlakaṃ)

For the non-returner, the underlying tendencies to ignorance and to conceit lie latent, but the underlying tendencies to sensual lust, to aversion, and to views do not lie latent in him. For two persons, the underlying tendencies to ignorance, to sensual lust, to aversion, and to conceit lie latent, but the underlying tendency to views does not lie latent in them. For the worldling, the underlying tendency to ignorance lies latent, and the underlying tendencies to sensual lust, to aversion, to conceit, and to views also lie latent.

12. Yassa kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca mānānusayo ca diṭṭhānusayo ca vicikicchānusayo ca anusenti tassa bhavarāgānusayo…pe… avijjānusayo anusetīti? Āmantā.

12. For one in whom the underlying tendencies to sensual lust, to aversion, to conceit, to views, and to doubt lie latent, does the underlying tendency to craving for existence… to ignorance also lie latent in him? Yes.

Yassa vā pana avijjānusayo anuseti tassa kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca mānānusayo ca diṭṭhānusayo ca vicikicchānusayo ca anusentīti?

Or for one in whom the underlying tendency to ignorance lies latent, do the underlying tendencies to sensual lust, to aversion, to conceit, to views, and to doubt also lie latent in him?

Anāgāmissa avijjānusayo ca mānānusayo ca anusenti, no ca tassa kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca diṭṭhānusayo ca vicikicchānusayo ca anusenti. Dvinnaṃ puggalānaṃ avijjānusayo ca kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca mānānusayo ca anusenti, no ca tesaṃ diṭṭhānusayo ca vicikicchānusayo ca anusenti. Puthujjanassa avijjānusayo ca anuseti kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca mānānusayo ca diṭṭhānusayo [T 1.0441] ca vicikicchānusayo ca anusenti. (Pañcakamūlakaṃ)

For the non-returner, the underlying tendencies to ignorance and to conceit lie latent, but the underlying tendencies to sensual lust, to aversion, to views, and to doubt do not lie latent in him. For two persons, the underlying tendencies to ignorance, to sensual lust, to aversion, and to conceit lie latent, but the underlying tendencies to views and to doubt do not lie latent in them. For the worldling, the underlying tendency to ignorance lies latent, and the underlying tendencies to sensual lust, to aversion, to conceit, to views, and to doubt also lie latent.

13. (Ka) yassa kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca mānānusayo ca diṭṭhānusayo ca vicikicchānusayo ca bhavarāgānusayo ca anusenti tassa avijjānusayo anusetīti? Āmantā.

13. For one in whom the underlying tendencies to sensual lust, to aversion, to conceit, to views, to doubt, and to craving for existence lie latent, does the underlying tendency to ignorance also lie latent in him? Yes.

(Kha) yassa vā pana avijjānusayo anuseti tassa kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca mānānusayo [M 2.0061] ca diṭṭhānusayo ca vicikicchānusayo ca bhavarāgānusayo ca anusentīti?

Or for one in whom the underlying tendency to ignorance lies latent, do the underlying tendencies to sensual lust, to aversion, to conceit, to views, to doubt, and to craving for existence also lie latent in him?

Anāgāmissa avijjānusayo ca mānānusayo ca bhavarāgānusayo ca anusenti, no ca tassa kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca diṭṭhānusayo [V 2.0085] ca vicikicchānusayo ca anusenti. Dvinnaṃ puggalānaṃ avijjānusayo ca kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca mānānusayo ca bhavarāgānusayo ca anusenti, no ca tesaṃ diṭṭhānusayo ca vicikicchānusayo ca anusenti. Puthujjanassa avijjānusayo ca anuseti kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca mānānusayo ca diṭṭhānusayo ca vicikicchānusayo ca bhavarāgānusayo ca anusenti. (Chakkamūlakaṃ)

For the non-returner, the underlying tendencies to ignorance, to conceit, and to craving for existence lie latent, but the underlying tendencies to sensual lust, to aversion, to views, and to doubt do not lie latent in him. For two persons, the underlying tendencies to ignorance, to sensual lust, to aversion, to conceit, and to craving for existence lie latent, but the underlying tendencies to views and to doubt do not lie latent in them. For the worldling, the underlying tendency to ignorance lies latent, and the underlying tendencies to sensual lust, to aversion, to conceit, to views, to doubt, and to craving for existence also lie latent.

(Kha) anulomaokāso

(b) Forward Order: Location

14. (Ka) yattha kāmarāgānusayo anuseti tattha paṭighānusayo anusetīti? No.

14. (a) Where the underlying tendency to sensual lust lies latent, does the underlying tendency to aversion lie latent there? No.

(Kha) yattha vā pana paṭighānusayo anuseti tattha kāmarāgānusayo anusetīti? No.

(b) Or, where the underlying tendency to aversion lies latent, does the underlying tendency to sensual lust lie latent there? No.

(Ka) yattha kāmarāgānusayo anuseti tattha mānānusayo anusetīti? Āmantā.

(a) Where the underlying tendency to sensual lust lies latent, does the underlying tendency to conceit lie latent there? Yes.

(Kha) yattha vā pana mānānusayo anuseti tattha kāmarāgānusayo anusetīti?

(b) Or, where the underlying tendency to conceit lies latent, does the underlying tendency to sensual lust lie latent there?

Rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā ettha mānānusayo anuseti, no ca tattha kāmarāgānusayo anuseti. Kāmadhātuyā [T 1.0442] dvīsu vedanāsu ettha mānānusayo ca anuseti kāmarāgānusayo ca anuseti.

In the form realm and the formless realm, the underlying tendency to conceit lies latent, but the underlying tendency to sensual lust does not lie latent there. In the sense-sphere realm, in regard to two feelings, both the underlying tendency to conceit and the underlying tendency to sensual lust lie latent.

Yattha kāmarāgānusayo anuseti tattha diṭṭhānusayo…pe… vicikicchānusayo anusetīti? Āmantā.

Where the underlying tendency to sensual lust lies latent, do the underlying tendency to views… to doubt lie latent there? Yes.

Yattha vā pana vicikicchānusayo anuseti tattha kāmarāgānusayo anusetīti?

Or, where the underlying tendency to doubt lies latent, does the underlying tendency to sensual lust lie latent there?

Dukkhāya vedanāya rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā ettha vicikicchānusayo anuseti, no ca tattha kāmarāgānusayo anuseti. Kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu ettha vicikicchānusayo ca anuseti kāmarāgānusayo ca anuseti.

In regard to painful feeling, in the form realm, and in the formless realm, the underlying tendency to doubt lies latent, but the underlying tendency to sensual desire does not lie latent there. In the sense-sphere realm and in two feelings, both the underlying tendency to doubt and the underlying tendency to sensual desire lie latent.

(Ka) yattha kāmarāgānusayo anuseti tattha bhavarāgānusayo anusetīti? No.

(a) Where the underlying tendency to sensual desire lies latent, does the underlying tendency to craving for existence lie latent there? No.

(Kha) yattha vā pana bhavarāgānusayo anuseti tattha kāmarāgānusayo anusetīti? No.

(b) Or, where the underlying tendency to craving for existence lies latent, does the underlying tendency to sensual desire lie latent there? No.

(Ka) yattha [M 2.0062][V 2.0086] kāmarāgānusayo anuseti tattha avijjānusayo anusetīti? Āmantā.

(a) Where the underlying tendency to sensual desire lies latent, does the underlying tendency to ignorance lie latent there? Yes.

(Kha) yattha vā pana avijjānusayo anuseti tattha kāmarāgānusayo anusetīti?

(b) Or, where the underlying tendency to ignorance lies latent, does the underlying tendency to sensual desire lie latent there?

Dukkhāya vedanāya rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā ettha avijjānusayo anuseti, no ca tattha kāmarāgānusayo anuseti. Kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu ettha avijjānusayo ca anuseti kāmarāgānusayo ca anuseti.

In regard to painful feeling, in the form realm, and in the formless realm, the underlying tendency to ignorance lies latent, but the underlying tendency to sensual desire does not lie latent there. In the sense-sphere realm and in two feelings, both the underlying tendency to ignorance and the underlying tendency to sensual desire lie latent.

15. (Ka) yattha paṭighānusayo anuseti tattha mānānusayo anusetīti? No.

15. (a) Where the underlying tendency to aversion lies latent, does the underlying tendency to conceit lie latent there? No.

(Kha) yattha vā pana mānānusayo anuseti tattha paṭighānusayo anusetīti? No.

(b) Or, where the underlying tendency to conceit lies latent, does the underlying tendency to aversion lie latent there? No.

Yattha paṭighānusayo anuseti tattha diṭṭhānusayo…pe… vicikicchānusayo anusetīti? Āmantā.

Where the underlying tendency to aversion lies latent, does the underlying tendency to views… the underlying tendency to doubt lie latent there? Yes.

Yattha vā pana vicikicchānusayo anuseti tattha paṭighānusayo anusetīti?

Or, where the underlying tendency to doubt lies latent, does the underlying tendency to aversion lie latent there?

Kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā ettha vicikicchānusayo anuseti, no [T 1.0443] ca tattha paṭighānusayo anuseti. Dukkhāya vedanāya ettha vicikicchānusayo ca anuseti paṭighānusayo ca anuseti.

In the sense-sphere realm, in two feelings, in the form realm, and in the formless realm, the underlying tendency to doubt lies latent, but the underlying tendency to aversion does not lie latent there. In regard to painful feeling, both the underlying tendency to doubt and the underlying tendency to aversion lie latent.

(Ka) yattha paṭighānusayo anuseti tattha bhavarāgānusayo anusetīti? No.

(a) Where the underlying tendency to aversion lies latent, does the underlying tendency to craving for existence lie latent there? No.

(Kha) yattha vā pana bhavarāgānusayo anuseti tattha paṭighānusayo anusetīti? No.

(b) Or, where the underlying tendency to craving for existence lies latent, does the underlying tendency to aversion lie latent there? No.

(Ka) yattha paṭighānusayo anuseti tattha avijjānusayo anusetīti? Āmantā.

(a) Where the underlying tendency to aversion lies latent, does the underlying tendency to ignorance lie latent there? Yes.

(Kha) yattha vā pana avijjānusayo anuseti tattha paṭighānusayo anusetīti?

(b) Or, where the underlying tendency to ignorance lies latent, does the underlying tendency to aversion lie latent there?

Kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā ettha avijjānusayo anuseti, no [V 2.0087] ca tattha paṭighānusayo anuseti. Dukkhāya vedanāya ettha avijjānusayo ca anuseti paṭighānusayo ca anuseti.

In the sense-sphere realm, in two feelings, in the form realm, and in the formless realm, the underlying tendency to ignorance lies latent, but the underlying tendency to aversion does not lie latent there. In regard to painful feeling, both the underlying tendency to ignorance and the underlying tendency to aversion lie latent.

16. Yattha mānānusayo anuseti tattha diṭṭhānusayo…pe… vicikicchānusayo anusetīti? Āmantā.

16. Where the underlying tendency to conceit lies latent, does the underlying tendency to views… the underlying tendency to doubt lie latent there? Yes.

Yattha vā pana vicikicchānusayo anuseti tattha mānānusayo anusetīti?

Or, where the underlying tendency to doubt lies latent, does the underlying tendency to conceit lie latent there?

Dukkhāya vedanāya ettha vicikicchānusayo anuseti, no ca tattha mānānusayo anuseti. Kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā ettha vicikicchānusayo ca anuseti mānānusayo ca anuseti.

In regard to painful feeling, the underlying tendency to doubt lies latent, but the underlying tendency to conceit does not lie latent there. In the sense-sphere realm, in two feelings, in the form realm, and in the formless realm, both the underlying tendency to doubt and the underlying tendency to conceit lie latent.

(Ka) yattha [M 2.0063] mānānusayo anuseti tattha bhavarāgānusayo anusetīti?

(a) Where the underlying tendency to conceit lies latent, does the underlying tendency to craving for existence lie latent there?

Kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu ettha mānānusayo anuseti, no ca tattha bhavarāgānusayo anuseti. Rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā ettha mānānusayo ca anuseti bhavarāgānusayo ca anuseti.

In the sense-sphere realm and in two feelings, the underlying tendency to conceit lies latent, but the underlying tendency to craving for existence does not lie latent there. In the form realm and the formless realm, both the underlying tendency to conceit and the underlying tendency to craving for existence lie latent.

(Kha) yattha vā pana bhavarāgānusayo anuseti tattha mānānusayo anusetīti? Āmantā.

(b) Or, where the underlying tendency to craving for existence lies latent, does the underlying tendency to conceit lie latent there? Yes.

(Ka) yattha mānānusayo anuseti tattha [T 1.0444] avijjānusayo anusetīti? Āmantā.

(a) Where the underlying tendency to conceit lies latent, does the underlying tendency to ignorance lie latent there? Yes.

(Kha) yattha vā pana avijjānusayo anuseti tattha mānānusayo anusetīti?

(b) Or, where the underlying tendency to ignorance lies latent, does the underlying tendency to conceit lie latent there?

Dukkhāya vedanāya ettha avijjānusayo anuseti, no ca tattha mānānusayo anuseti. Kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā ettha avijjānusayo ca anuseti mānānusayo ca anuseti.

In regard to painful feeling, the underlying tendency to ignorance lies latent, but the underlying tendency to conceit does not lie latent there. In the sense-sphere realm, in two feelings, in the form realm, and in the formless realm, both the underlying tendency to ignorance and the underlying tendency to conceit lie latent.

17. (Ka) yattha diṭṭhānusayo anuseti tattha vicikicchānusayo anusetīti? Āmantā.

17. (a) Where the underlying tendency to views lies latent, does the underlying tendency to doubt lie latent there? Yes.

(Kha) yattha [V 2.0088] vā pana vicikicchānusayo anuseti tattha diṭṭhānusayo anusetīti? Āmantā.

(b) Or, where the underlying tendency to doubt lies latent, does the underlying tendency to views lie latent there? Yes.

(Ka) yattha diṭṭhānusayo anuseti tattha bhavarāgānusayo anusetīti?

(a) Where the underlying tendency to views lies latent, does the underlying tendency to craving for existence lie latent there?

Kāmadhātuyā tīsu vedanāsu ettha diṭṭhānusayo anuseti, no ca tattha bhavarāgānusayo anuseti. Rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā ettha diṭṭhānusayo ca anuseti bhavarāgānusayo ca anuseti.

In the sense-sphere realm and in the three feelings, the underlying tendency to views lies latent, but the underlying tendency to craving for existence does not lie latent there. In the form realm and the formless realm, both the underlying tendency to views and the underlying tendency to craving for existence lie latent.

(Kha) yattha vā pana bhavarāgānusayo anuseti tattha diṭṭhānusayo anusetīti? Āmantā.

(b) Or, where the underlying tendency to craving for existence lies latent, does the underlying tendency to views lie latent there? Yes.

(Ka) yattha diṭṭhānusayo anuseti tattha avijjānusayo anusetīti? Āmantā.

(a) Where the underlying tendency to views lies latent, does the underlying tendency to ignorance lie latent there? Yes.

(Kha) yattha vā pana avijjānusayo anuseti tattha diṭṭhānusayo anusetīti? Āmantā.

(b) Or, where the underlying tendency to ignorance lies latent, does the underlying tendency to views lie latent there? Yes.

18. (Ka) yattha vicikicchānusayo anuseti tattha bhavarāgānusayo anusetīti?

18. (a) Where the underlying tendency to doubt lies latent, does the underlying tendency to craving for existence lie latent there?

Kāmadhātuyā tīsu vedanāsu ettha vicikicchānusayo anuseti, no ca tattha bhavarāgānusayo anuseti. Rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā ettha vicikicchānusayo ca anuseti bhavarāgānusayo ca anuseti.

In the sense-sphere realm and in the three feelings, the underlying tendency to doubt lies latent, but the underlying tendency to craving for existence does not lie latent there. In the form realm and the formless realm, both the underlying tendency to doubt and the underlying tendency to craving for existence lie latent.

(Kha) yattha vā pana bhavarāgānusayo anuseti tattha vicikicchānusayo anusetīti? Āmantā[T 1.0445].

(b) Or, where the underlying tendency to craving for existence lies latent, does the underlying tendency to doubt lie latent there? Yes.

(Ka) yattha [M 2.0064] vicikicchānusayo anuseti tattha avijjānusayo anusetīti? Āmantā.

(a) Where the underlying tendency to doubt lies latent, does the underlying tendency to ignorance lie latent there? Yes.

(Kha) yattha vā pana avijjānusayo anuseti tattha vicikicchānusayo anusetīti? Āmantā.

(b) Or, where the underlying tendency to ignorance lies latent, does the underlying tendency to doubt lie latent there? Yes.

19. (Ka) yattha bhavarāgānusayo anuseti tattha avijjānusayo anusetīti? Āmantā.

19. (a) Where the underlying tendency to craving for existence lies latent, does the underlying tendency to ignorance lie latent there? Yes.

(Kha) yattha vā pana avijjānusayo anuseti tattha bhavarāgānusayo anusetīti?

(b) Or, where the underlying tendency to ignorance lies latent, does the underlying tendency to craving for existence lie latent there?

Kāmadhātuyā [V 2.0089] tīsu vedanāsu ettha avijjānusayo anuseti, no ca tattha bhavarāgānusayo anuseti. Rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā ettha avijjānusayo ca anuseti bhavarāgānusayo ca anuseti. (Ekamūlakaṃ)

In the sense-sphere realm, in regard to the three feelings, the underlying tendency to ignorance lies latent, but the underlying tendency to craving for existence does not lie latent there. In the form realm and the formless realm, both the underlying tendency to ignorance and the underlying tendency to craving for existence lie latent. (The Section on a Single Root)

20. (Ka) yattha kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca anusenti tattha mānānusayo anusetīti? Natthi.

20. (a) Where both the underlying tendency to sensual desire and the underlying tendency to aversion lie latent, does the underlying tendency to conceit lie latent there? There is no such case.

(Kha) yattha vā pana mānānusayo anuseti tattha kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca anusentīti?

(b) Or, where the underlying tendency to conceit lies latent, do both the underlying tendency to sensual desire and the underlying tendency to aversion lie latent there?

Rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā ettha mānānusayo anuseti, no ca tattha kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca anusenti. Kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu ettha mānānusayo ca kāmarāgānusayo ca anusenti, no ca tattha paṭighānusayo anuseti.

In the form realm and the formless realm, the underlying tendency to conceit lies latent, but both the underlying tendency to sensual desire and the underlying tendency to aversion do not lie latent there. In the sense-sphere realm, in regard to two feelings, both the underlying tendency to conceit and the underlying tendency to sensual desire lie latent, but the underlying tendency to aversion does not lie latent there.

Yattha kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca anusenti tattha diṭṭhānusayo…pe… vicikicchānusayo anusetīti? Natthi.

Where both the underlying tendency to sensual desire and the underlying tendency to aversion lie latent, does the underlying tendency to views …pe… the underlying tendency to doubt lie latent there? There is no such case.

Yattha vā pana vicikicchānusayo [T 1.0446] anuseti tattha kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca anusentīti?

Or, where the underlying tendency to doubt lies latent, do both the underlying tendency to sensual desire and the underlying tendency to aversion lie latent there?

Rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā ettha vicikicchānusayo anuseti, no ca tattha kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca anusenti. Kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu ettha vicikicchānusayo ca kāmarāgānusayo ca anusenti, no ca tattha paṭighānusayo anuseti. Dukkhāya vedanāya ettha vicikicchānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca anusenti, no ca tattha kāmarāgānusayo anuseti.

In the form realm and the formless realm, the underlying tendency to doubt lies latent, but both the underlying tendency to sensual desire and the underlying tendency to aversion do not lie latent there. In the sense-sphere realm, in regard to two feelings, both the underlying tendency to doubt and the underlying tendency to sensual desire lie latent, but the underlying tendency to aversion does not lie latent there. In regard to painful feeling, both the underlying tendency to doubt and the underlying tendency to aversion lie latent, but the underlying tendency to sensual desire does not lie latent there.

(Ka) yattha kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca anusenti tattha bhavarāgānusayo anusetīti? Natthi.

(a) Where both the underlying tendency to sensual desire and the underlying tendency to aversion lie latent, does the underlying tendency to craving for existence lie latent there? There is no such case.

(Kha) yattha vā pana bhavarāgānusayo anuseti tattha kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca anusentīti? No.

(b) Or, where the underlying tendency to craving for existence lies latent, do both the underlying tendency to sensual desire and the underlying tendency to aversion lie latent there? No.

(Ka) yattha [M 2.0065][V 2.0090] kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca anusenti tattha avijjānusayo anusetīti? Natthi.

(a) Where both the underlying tendency to sensual desire and the underlying tendency to aversion lie latent, does the underlying tendency to ignorance lie latent there? There is no such case.

(Kha) yattha vā pana avijjānusayo anuseti tattha kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca anusentīti?

(b) Or, where the underlying tendency to ignorance lies latent, do both the underlying tendency to sensual desire and the underlying tendency to aversion lie latent there?

Rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā ettha avijjānusayo anuseti, no ca tattha kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca anusenti. Kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu ettha avijjānusayo ca kāmarāgānusayo ca anusenti, no ca tattha paṭighānusayo anuseti. Dukkhāya vedanāya ettha avijjānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca anusenti, no ca tattha kāmarāgānusayo anuseti. (Dukamūlakaṃ)

In the form realm and the formless realm, the underlying tendency to ignorance lies latent, but both the underlying tendency to sensual desire and the underlying tendency to aversion do not lie latent there. In the sense-sphere realm, in regard to two feelings, both the underlying tendency to ignorance and the underlying tendency to sensual desire lie latent, but the underlying tendency to aversion does not lie latent there. In regard to painful feeling, both the underlying tendency to ignorance and the underlying tendency to aversion lie latent, but the underlying tendency to sensual desire does not lie latent there. (The Section on the Dyad as Root)

21. Yattha kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca mānānusayo ca anusenti tattha diṭṭhānusayo…pe… vicikicchānusayo anusetīti? Natthi[T 1.0447].

21. Where the underlying tendency to sensual desire, the underlying tendency to aversion, and the underlying tendency to conceit lie latent, does the underlying tendency to views …pe… the underlying tendency to doubt lie latent there? There is no such case.

Yattha vā pana vicikicchānusayo anuseti tattha kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca mānānusayo ca anusentīti?

Or, where the underlying tendency to doubt lies latent, do the underlying tendency to sensual desire, the underlying tendency to aversion, and the underlying tendency to conceit lie latent there?

Rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā ettha vicikicchānusayo ca mānānusayo ca anusenti, no ca tattha kāmārāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca anusenti. Kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu ettha vicikicchānusayo ca kāmarāgānusayo ca mānānusayo ca anusenti, no ca tattha paṭighānusayo anuseti. Dukkhāya vedanāya ettha vicikicchānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca anusenti, no ca tattha kāmarāgānusayo ca mānānusayo ca anusenti.

In the form realm and the formless realm, the underlying tendency to doubt and the underlying tendency to conceit lie latent, but the underlying tendency to sensual desire and the underlying tendency to aversion do not lie latent there. In the sense-sphere realm, in regard to two feelings, the underlying tendency to doubt, the underlying tendency to sensual desire, and the underlying tendency to conceit lie latent, but the underlying tendency to aversion does not lie latent there. In regard to painful feeling, the underlying tendency to doubt and the underlying tendency to aversion lie latent, but the underlying tendency to sensual desire and the underlying tendency to conceit do not lie latent there.

(Ka) yattha kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca mānānusayo ca anusenti tattha bhavarāgānusayo anusetīti? Natthi.

(a) Where the underlying tendency to sensual desire, the underlying tendency to aversion, and the underlying tendency to conceit lie latent, does the underlying tendency to craving for existence lie latent there? There is no such case.

(Kha) yattha vā pana bhavarāgānusayo anuseti tattha kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca mānānusayo ca anusentīti?

(b) Or, where the underlying tendency to craving for existence lies latent, do the underlying tendency to sensual desire, the underlying tendency to aversion, and the underlying tendency to conceit lie latent there?

Rūpadhātuyā [V 2.0091] arūpadhātuyā ettha bhavarāgānusayo ca mānānusayo ca anusenti, no ca tattha kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca anusenti.

In the form realm and the formless realm, the underlying tendency to craving for existence and the underlying tendency to conceit lie latent, but the underlying tendency to sensual desire and the underlying tendency to aversion do not lie latent there.

(Ka) yattha kāmarāgānusayo [T 1.0448] ca paṭighānusayo ca mānānusayo ca anusenti tattha avijjānusayo anusetīti? Natthi.

(a) Where the underlying tendency to sensual desire, the underlying tendency to aversion, and the underlying tendency to conceit lie latent, does the underlying tendency to ignorance lie latent there? There is no such case.

(Kha) yattha vā pana avijjānusayo anuseti tattha kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca mānānusayo ca anusentīti?

(b) Or, where the underlying tendency to ignorance lies latent, do the underlying tendency to sensual desire, the underlying tendency to aversion, and the underlying tendency to conceit lie latent there?

Rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā ettha avijjānusayo [M 2.0066] ca mānānusayo ca anusenti, no ca tattha kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca anusenti. Kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu ettha avijjānusayo ca kāmarāgānusayo ca mānānusayo ca anusenti, no ca tattha paṭighānusayo anuseti. Dukkhāya vedanāya ettha avijjānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca anusenti, no ca tattha kāmarāgānusayo ca mānānusayo ca anusenti. (Tikamūlakaṃ)

In the form realm and the formless realm, the underlying tendency to ignorance and the underlying tendency to conceit lie latent, but the underlying tendency to sensual desire and the underlying tendency to aversion do not lie latent there. In the sense-sphere realm, in regard to two feelings, the underlying tendency to ignorance, the underlying tendency to sensual desire, and the underlying tendency to conceit lie latent, but the underlying tendency to aversion does not lie latent there. In regard to painful feeling, the underlying tendency to ignorance and the underlying tendency to aversion lie latent, but the underlying tendency to sensual desire and the underlying tendency to conceit do not lie latent there. (The Section on the Triad as Root)

22. (Ka) yattha kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca mānānusayo ca diṭṭhānusayo ca anusenti tattha vicikicchānusayo anusetīti? Natthi.

22. (a) Where the underlying tendency to sensual desire, the underlying tendency to aversion, the underlying tendency to conceit, and the underlying tendency to views lie latent, does the underlying tendency to doubt lie latent there? There is no such case.

(Kha) yattha vā pana vicikicchānusayo anuseti tattha kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca mānānusayo ca diṭṭhānusayo ca anusentīti?

(b) Or, where the underlying tendency to doubt lies latent, do the underlying tendency to sensual desire, the underlying tendency to aversion, the underlying tendency to conceit, and the underlying tendency to views lie latent there?

Rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā ettha vicikicchānusayo ca mānānusayo ca diṭṭhānusayo ca anusenti, no ca tattha kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca anusenti. Kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu ettha vicikicchānusayo ca kāmarāgānusayo ca mānānusayo ca diṭṭhānusayo ca anusenti, no ca tattha paṭighānusayo anuseti. Dukkhāya vedanāya ettha vicikicchānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca diṭṭhānusayo ca anusenti, no ca tattha kāmarāgānusayo ca mānānusayo ca anusenti.

In the form-sphere and the formless-sphere, the underlying tendency to doubt, the underlying tendency to conceit, and the underlying tendency to views lie latent here, but the underlying tendency to sensual desire and the underlying tendency to aversion do not lie latent there. In the desire-sphere, in regard to two feelings, the underlying tendency to doubt, the underlying tendency to sensual desire, the underlying tendency to conceit, and the underlying tendency to views lie latent here, but the underlying tendency to aversion does not lie latent there. In regard to painful feeling, the underlying tendency to doubt, the underlying tendency to aversion, and the underlying tendency to views lie latent here, but the underlying tendency to sensual desire and the underlying tendency to conceit do not lie latent there.

(Ka) yattha kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo [T 1.0449] ca mānānusayo ca diṭṭhānusayo ca anusenti tattha bhavarāgānusayo anusetīti? Natthi.

Wherever the underlying tendency to sensual desire, the underlying tendency to aversion, the underlying tendency to conceit, and the underlying tendency to views lie latent, does the underlying tendency to craving for becoming also lie latent there? No.

(Kha) yattha [V 2.0092] vā pana bhavarāgānusayo anuseti tattha kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca mānānusayo ca diṭṭhānusayo ca anusentīti?

Or wherever the underlying tendency to craving for becoming lies latent, do the underlying tendency to sensual desire, the underlying tendency to aversion, the underlying tendency to conceit, and the underlying tendency to views also lie latent there?

Rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā ettha bhavarāgānusayo ca mānānusayo ca diṭṭhānusayo ca anusenti, no ca tattha kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca anusenti.

In the form-sphere and the formless-sphere, the underlying tendency to craving for becoming, the underlying tendency to conceit, and the underlying tendency to views lie latent here, but the underlying tendency to sensual desire and the underlying tendency to aversion do not lie latent there.

(Ka) yattha kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca mānānusayo ca diṭṭhānusayo ca anusenti tattha avijjānusayo anusetīti? Natthi.

Wherever the underlying tendency to sensual desire, the underlying tendency to aversion, the underlying tendency to conceit, and the underlying tendency to views lie latent, does the underlying tendency to ignorance also lie latent there? No.

(Kha) yattha vā pana avijjānusayo anuseti tattha kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca mānānusayo ca diṭṭhānusayo ca anusentīti?

Or wherever the underlying tendency to ignorance lies latent, do the underlying tendency to sensual desire, the underlying tendency to aversion, the underlying tendency to conceit, and the underlying tendency to views also lie latent there?

Rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā ettha avijjānusayo ca mānānusayo ca diṭṭhānusayo [M 2.0067] ca anusenti, no ca tattha kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca anusenti.

In the form-sphere and the formless-sphere, the underlying tendency to ignorance, the underlying tendency to conceit, and the underlying tendency to views lie latent here, but the underlying tendency to sensual desire and the underlying tendency to aversion do not lie latent there.

Kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu ettha avijjānusayo ca kāmarāgānusayo ca mānānusayo ca diṭṭhānusayo ca anusenti, no ca tattha paṭighānusayo anuseti[T 1.0450]. Dukkhāya vedanāya ettha avijjānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca diṭṭhānusayo ca anusenti, no ca tattha kāmarāgānusayo ca mānānusayo ca anusenti. (Catukkamūlakaṃ)

In the desire-sphere, in regard to two feelings, the underlying tendency to ignorance, the underlying tendency to sensual desire, the underlying tendency to conceit, and the underlying tendency to views lie latent here, but the underlying tendency to aversion does not lie latent there. In regard to painful feeling, the underlying tendency to ignorance, the underlying tendency to aversion, and the underlying tendency to views lie latent here, but the underlying tendency to sensual desire and the underlying tendency to conceit do not lie latent there. (The Tetrad as Root)

23. (Ka) yattha kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca mānānusayo ca diṭṭhānusayo ca vicikicchānusayo ca anusenti tattha bhavarāgānusayo anusetīti? Natthi.

23. Wherever the underlying tendency to sensual desire, the underlying tendency to aversion, the underlying tendency to conceit, the underlying tendency to views, and the underlying tendency to doubt lie latent, does the underlying tendency to craving for becoming also lie latent there? No.

(Kha) yattha vā pana bhavarāgānusayo anuseti tattha kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca mānānusayo ca diṭṭhānusayo ca vicikicchānusayo ca anusentīti?

Or wherever the underlying tendency to craving for becoming lies latent, do the underlying tendency to sensual desire, the underlying tendency to aversion, the underlying tendency to conceit, the underlying tendency to views, and the underlying tendency to doubt also lie latent there?

Rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā ettha bhavarāgānusayo ca mānānusayo ca diṭṭhānusayo ca vicikicchānusayo ca anusenti, no ca tattha kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca anusenti.

In the form-sphere and the formless-sphere, the underlying tendency to craving for becoming, the underlying tendency to conceit, the underlying tendency to views, and the underlying tendency to doubt lie latent here, but the underlying tendency to sensual desire and the underlying tendency to aversion do not lie latent there.

(Ka) yattha [V 2.0093] kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca mānānusayo ca diṭṭhānusayo ca vicikicchānusayo ca anusenti tattha avijjānusayo anusetīti? Natthi.

Wherever the underlying tendency to sensual desire, the underlying tendency to aversion, the underlying tendency to conceit, the underlying tendency to views, and the underlying tendency to doubt lie latent, does the underlying tendency to ignorance also lie latent there? No.

(Kha) yattha vā pana avijjānusayo anuseti tattha kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo [T 1.0451] ca mānānusayo ca diṭṭhānusayo ca vicikicchānusayo ca anusentīti?

Or wherever the underlying tendency to ignorance lies latent, do the underlying tendency to sensual desire, the underlying tendency to aversion, the underlying tendency to conceit, the underlying tendency to views, and the underlying tendency to doubt also lie latent there?

Rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā ettha avijjānusayo ca mānānusayo ca diṭṭhānusayo ca vicikicchānusayo ca anusenti, no ca tattha kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca anusenti. Kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu ettha avijjānusayo ca kāmarāgānusayo ca mānānusayo ca diṭṭhānusayo ca vicikicchānusayo ca anusenti, no ca tattha paṭighānusayo anuseti. Dukkhāya vedanāya ettha avijjānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca diṭṭhānusayo ca vicikicchānusayo ca anusenti, no ca tattha kāmarāgānusayo ca mānānusayo ca anusenti. (Pañcakamūlakaṃ)

In the form-sphere and the formless-sphere, the underlying tendency to ignorance, the underlying tendency to conceit, the underlying tendency to views, and the underlying tendency to doubt lie latent here, but the underlying tendency to sensual desire and the underlying tendency to aversion do not lie latent there. In the desire-sphere, in regard to two feelings, the underlying tendency to ignorance, the underlying tendency to sensual desire, the underlying tendency to conceit, the underlying tendency to views, and the underlying tendency to doubt lie latent here, but the underlying tendency to aversion does not lie latent there. In regard to painful feeling, the underlying tendency to ignorance, the underlying tendency to aversion, the underlying tendency to views, and the underlying tendency to doubt lie latent here, but the underlying tendency to sensual desire and the underlying tendency to conceit do not lie latent there. (The Pentad as Root)

24. (Ka) yattha kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca mānānusayo ca diṭṭhānusayo ca vicikicchānusayo ca bhavarāgānusayo ca anusenti tattha avijjānusayo anusetīti? Natthi.

24. (a) Wherever the underlying tendency to sensual desire, the underlying tendency to aversion, the underlying tendency to conceit, the underlying tendency to views, the underlying tendency to doubt, and the underlying tendency to craving for becoming lie latent, does the underlying tendency to ignorance also lie latent there? Rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā ettha avijjānusayo ca mānānusayo ca diṭṭhānusayo ca vicikicchānusayo ca bhavarāgānusayo ca anusenti, no ca tattha kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca anusenti.
