In the sense-sphere, in regard to two feelings, one is there subject to the underlying tendencies to ignorance, sensual lust, conceit, and views, but not to the underlying tendency to aversion. In regard to painful feeling, one is there subject to the underlying tendencies to ignorance, aversion, and views, but not to the underlying tendencies to sensual lust and conceit. (The Fourfold-Root Section)

86. (Ka) yato [T 1.0512] kāmarāgānusayena ca paṭighānusayena ca mānānusayena ca diṭṭhānusayena [V 2.0148] ca vicikicchānusayena ca sānusayo tato bhavarāgānusayena sānusayoti? Natthi.

86. Where one is subject to the underlying tendencies to sensual lust, aversion, conceit, views, and doubt, is one there also subject to the underlying tendency to lust for existence? No.

(Kha) yato vā pana bhavarāgānusayena sānusayo tato kāmarāgānusayena ca paṭighānusayena ca mānānusayena ca diṭṭhānusayena ca vicikicchānusayena ca sānusayoti?

Or conversely, where one is subject to the underlying tendency to lust for existence, is one there also subject to the underlying tendencies to sensual lust, aversion, conceit, views, and doubt?

Mānānusayena ca diṭṭhānusayena ca vicikicchānusayena ca sānusayo.

One is subject to the underlying tendencies to conceit, views, and doubt.

(Ka) yato kāmarāgānusayena ca paṭighānusayena ca mānānusayena ca diṭṭhānusayena ca vicikicchānusayena ca sānusayo tato avijjānusayena sānusayoti? Natthi.

Where one is subject to the underlying tendencies to sensual lust, aversion, conceit, views, and doubt, is one there also subject to the underlying tendency to ignorance? No.

(Kha) yato vā pana avijjānusayena sānusayo tato kāmarāgānusayena ca paṭighānusayena ca mānānusayena ca diṭṭhānusayena ca vicikicchānusayena ca sānusayoti?

Or conversely, where one is subject to the underlying tendency to ignorance, is one there also subject to the underlying tendencies to sensual lust, aversion, conceit, views, and doubt?

Rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā tato avijjānusayena ca mānānusayena ca diṭṭhānusayena ca vicikicchānusayena ca sānusayo, no ca tato kāmarāgānusayena ca paṭighānusayena ca sānusayo. Kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu tato avijjānusayena ca kāmarāgānusayena ca mānānusayena ca diṭṭhānusayena ca vicikicchānusayena ca sānusayo, no ca tato paṭighānusayena sānusayo. Dukkhāya vedanāya tato avijjānusayena [T 1.0513] ca paṭighānusayena ca diṭṭhānusayena ca vicikicchānusayena ca sānusayo, no ca tato kāmarāgānusayena ca mānānusayena ca sānusayo. (Pañcakamūlakaṃ)

In the form realm and the formless realm, with respect to what arises from there, one is subject to the underlying tendencies of ignorance, conceit, views, and doubt, but not to the underlying tendencies of sensual lust and aversion. In the sense-sphere realm, in two feelings, with respect to what arises from there, one is subject to the underlying tendencies of ignorance, sensual lust, conceit, views, and doubt, but not to the underlying tendency of aversion. In regard to painful feeling, with respect to what arises from there, one is subject to the underlying tendencies of ignorance, aversion, views, and doubt, but not to the underlying tendencies of sensual lust and conceit. (The Fivefold-Root Section)

87. (Ka) yato kāmarāgānusayena ca paṭighānusayena ca mānānusayena ca diṭṭhānusayena ca vicikicchānusayena ca bhavarāgānusayena ca sānusayo [M 2.0113] tato avijjānusayena sānusayoti? Natthi.

87. (a) Where one has the underlying tendencies of sensual lust, aversion, conceit, views, doubt, and lust for existence, does one there also have the underlying tendency of ignorance? No.

(Kha) yato vā pana avijjānusayena sānusayo tato kāmarāgānusayena ca paṭighānusayena [V 2.0149] ca mānānusayena ca diṭṭhānusayena ca vicikicchānusayena ca bhavarāgānusayena ca sānusayoti?

(b) Or, where one has the underlying tendency of ignorance, does one there also have the underlying tendencies of sensual lust, aversion, conceit, views, doubt, and lust for existence?

Rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā tato avijjānusayena ca mānānusayena ca diṭṭhānusayena ca vicikicchānusayena ca bhavarāgānusayena ca sānusayo, no ca tato kāmarāgānusayena ca paṭighānusayena ca sānusayo. Kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu tato avijjānusayena ca kāmarāgānusayena ca mānānusayena ca diṭṭhānusayena ca vicikicchānusayena ca sānusayo, no ca tato paṭighānusayena ca bhavarāgānusayena ca sānusayo. Dukkhāya vedanāya tato avijjānusayena ca paṭighānusayena ca diṭṭhānusayena ca vicikicchānusayena ca sānusayo, no ca tato kāmarāgānusayena ca mānānusayena ca bhavarāgānusayena ca sānusayo. (Chakkamūlakaṃ)

In the form realm and the formless realm, with respect to what arises from there, one is subject to the underlying tendencies of ignorance, conceit, views, doubt, and lust for existence, but not to the underlying tendencies of sensual lust and aversion. In the sense-sphere realm and in two feelings, with respect to what arises from there, one is subject to the underlying tendencies of ignorance, sensual lust, conceit, views, and doubt, but not to the underlying tendencies of aversion and lust for existence. With respect to painful feeling, with respect to what arises from there, one is subject to the underlying tendencies of ignorance, aversion, views, and doubt, but not to the underlying tendencies of sensual lust, conceit, and lust for existence. (The Sixfold-Root Section)

(Ga) anulomapuggalokāsā

(c) Forward Order: Person and Realm

88. (Ka) yo yato kāmarāgānusayena sānusayo so tato paṭighānusayena sānusayoti? No.

88. (a) Whatever person, with respect to whichever realm, has the underlying tendency of sensual lust, does that person, with respect to that same realm, have the underlying tendency of aversion? No.

(Kha) yo vā pana yato paṭighānusayena sānusayo so tato kāmarāgānusayena sānusayoti? No.

(b) Or again, whatever person, with respect to whichever realm, has the underlying tendency of aversion, does that person, with respect to that same realm, have the underlying tendency of sensual lust? No.

(Ka) yo yato kāmarāgānusayena [T 1.0514] sānusayo so tato mānānusayena sānusayoti? Āmantā.

(a) Whatever person, with respect to whichever realm, has the underlying tendency of sensual lust, does that person, with respect to that same realm, have the underlying tendency of conceit? Yes.

(Kha) yo vā pana yato mānānusayena sānusayo so tato kāmarāgānusayena sānusayoti?

(b) Or again, whatever person, with respect to whichever realm, has the underlying tendency of conceit, does that person, with respect to that same realm, have the underlying tendency of sensual lust?

Anāgāmī kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā so tato mānānusayena sānusayo, no ca so tato kāmarāgānusayena sānusayo. Tayo puggalā rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā te tato mānānusayena sānusayā, no ca te tato kāmarāgānusayena sānusayā. Teva puggalā kāmadhātuyā [V 2.0150] dvīsu vedanāsu te tato mānānusayena ca sānusayā kāmarāgānusayena ca sānusayā.

A non-returner—in the sense-sphere realm, in two feelings, in the form realm, and in the formless realm—is subject to the underlying tendency of conceit in those respects, but not to the underlying tendency of sensual lust. Three persons, in the form realm and the formless realm, are subject to the underlying tendency of conceit in those respects, but not to the underlying tendency of sensual lust. Those same three persons, in the sense-sphere realm and in two feelings, are subject to both the underlying tendency of conceit and the underlying tendency of sensual lust in those respects.

Yo [M 2.0114] yato kāmarāgānusayena sānusayo so tato diṭṭhānusayena…pe… vicikicchānusayena sānusayoti?

Whatever person, with respect to whichever realm, has the underlying tendency of sensual lust, does that person, with respect to that same realm, have the underlying tendency of views… and so on… the underlying tendency of doubt?

Dve puggalā kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu te tato kāmarāgānusayena sānusayā, no ca te tato vicikicchānusayena sānusayā. Puthujjano kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu so tato kāmarāgānusayena ca sānusayo vicikicchānusayena ca sānusayo.

Or again, is a person who, with respect to something, is subject to the underlying tendency of doubt, also subject, with respect to that, to the underlying tendency of sensual lust, the underlying tendency of aversion, and the underlying tendency of conceit?

Puthujjano rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā so tato vicikicchānusayena ca mānānusayena ca sānusayo, no ca so tato kāmarāgānusayena ca paṭighānusayena ca sānusayo. Sveva puggalo kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu so tato vicikicchānusayena ca kāmarāgānusayena ca mānānusayena ca sānusayo, no ca so tato paṭighānusayena sānusayo. Sveva puggalo dukkhāya vedanāya so tato vicikicchānusayena ca paṭighānusayena ca sānusayo, no ca so tato kāmarāgānusayena ca mānānusayena ca sānusayo.

A worldling, in the form element and in the formless element, is, with respect to that, subject to the underlying tendency of doubt and the underlying tendency of conceit, but is not, with respect to that, subject to the underlying tendency of sensual lust and the underlying tendency of aversion. That same person, in the sense-sphere element and in the two feelings, is, with respect to that, subject to the underlying tendency of doubt, the underlying tendency of sensual lust, and the underlying tendency of conceit, but is not, with respect to that, subject to the underlying tendency of aversion. That same person, in regard to painful feeling, is, with respect to that, subject to the underlying tendency of doubt and the underlying tendency of aversion, but is not, with respect to that, subject to the underlying tendency of sensual lust and the underlying tendency of conceit.

(Ka) yo yato kāmarāgānusayena ca paṭighānusayena ca mānānusayena ca sānusayo so tato bhavarāgānusayena sānusayoti? Natthi.

(a) Is a person who, with respect to something, is subject to the underlying tendency of sensual lust, the underlying tendency of aversion, and the underlying tendency of conceit, also subject, with respect to that, to the underlying tendency of lust for becoming? There is not.

(Kha) yo vā pana yato bhavarāgānusayena sānusayo so tato kāmarāgānusayena ca paṭighānusayena ca mānānusayena ca sānusayoti?

(b) Or again, is a person who, with respect to something, is subject to the underlying tendency of lust for becoming, also subject, with respect to that, to the underlying tendency of sensual lust, the underlying tendency of aversion, and the underlying tendency of conceit?

Mānānusayena sānusayo.

He is subject to the underlying tendency of conceit.

(Ka) yo [V 2.0157] yato kāmarāgānusayena ca paṭighānusayena ca mānānusayena ca sānusayo so tato avijjānusayena sānusayoti? Natthi.

(a) Is a person who, with respect to something, is subject to the underlying tendency of sensual lust, the underlying tendency of aversion, and the underlying tendency of conceit, also subject, with respect to that, to the underlying tendency of ignorance? There is not.

(Kha) yo vā pana yato avijjānusayena sānusayo so tato kāmarāgānusayena ca paṭighānusayena ca mānānusayena ca sānusayoti?

(b) Or again, is a person who, with respect to something, is subject to the underlying tendency of ignorance, also subject, with respect to that, to the underlying tendency of sensual lust, the underlying tendency of aversion, and the underlying tendency of conceit?

Anāgāmī dukkhāya vedanāya so tato avijjānusayena sānusayo[T 1.0522], no ca so tato kāmarāgānusayena ca paṭighānusayena ca mānānusayena ca sānusayo. Sveva puggalo kāmadhātuyā [M 2.0120] dvīsu vedanāsu rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā so tato avijjānusayena ca mānānusayena ca sānusayo, no ca so tato kāmarāgānusayena ca paṭighānusayena ca sānusayo. Tayo puggalā rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā te tato avijjānusayena ca mānānusayena ca sānusayā, no ca te tato kāmarāgānusayena ca paṭighānusayena ca sānusayā. Teva puggalā kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu te tato avijjānusayena ca kāmarāgānusayena ca mānānusayena ca sānusayā, no ca te tato paṭighānusayena sānusayā. Teva puggalā dukkhāya vedanāya te tato avijjānusayena ca paṭighānusayena ca sānusayā, no ca te tato kāmarāgānusayena ca mānānusayena ca sānusayā. (Tikamūlakaṃ)

A non-returner, in regard to painful feeling, has the underlying tendency to ignorance, but does not have the underlying tendencies to sensual lust, aversion, and conceit. That same person, in regard to the sense-sphere, the two feelings, the form-sphere, and the formless-sphere, has the underlying tendencies to ignorance and conceit, but does not have the underlying tendencies to sensual lust and aversion. Three persons, in regard to the form-sphere and the formless-sphere, have the underlying tendencies to ignorance and conceit, but do not have the underlying tendencies to sensual lust and aversion. Those same persons, in regard to the sense-sphere and the two feelings, have the underlying tendencies to ignorance, sensual lust, and conceit, but do not have the underlying tendency to aversion. Those same persons, in regard to painful feeling, have the underlying tendencies to ignorance and aversion, but do not have the underlying tendencies to sensual lust and conceit.

96. (Ka) yo yato kāmarāgānusayena ca paṭighānusayena ca mānānusayena ca diṭṭhānusayena ca sānusayo so tato vicikicchānusayena sānusayoti? Natthi.

96. Does a person who, with respect to something, has the underlying tendencies to sensual lust, aversion, conceit, and views, also have, with respect to that, the underlying tendency to doubt? No.

(Kha) yo vā pana yato vicikicchānusayena sānusayo so tato kāmarāgānusayena ca paṭighānusayena ca mānānusayena ca diṭṭhānusayena ca sānusayoti?

Or, does a person who, with respect to something, has the underlying tendency to doubt, also have, with respect to that, the underlying tendencies to sensual lust, aversion, conceit, and views?

Puthujjano rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā so tato vicikicchānusayena ca mānānusayena ca diṭṭhānusayena ca sānusayo, no ca so tato kāmarāgānusayena ca paṭighānusayena ca sānusayo. Sveva puggalo kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu so tato vicikicchānusayena [T 1.0523] ca kāmarāgānusayena [V 2.0158] ca mānānusayena ca diṭṭhānusayena ca sānusayo, no ca so tato paṭighānusayena sānusayo. Sveva puggalo dukkhāya vedanāya so tato vicikicchānusayena ca paṭighānusayena ca diṭṭhānusayena ca sānusayo, no ca so tato kāmarāgānusayena ca mānānusayena ca sānusayo…pe…. (Catukkamūlakaṃ)

An ordinary person, in regard to the form-sphere and the formless-sphere, has the underlying tendencies to doubt, conceit, and views, but does not have the underlying tendencies to sensual lust and aversion. That same person, in regard to the sense-sphere and the two feelings, has the underlying tendencies to doubt, sensual lust, conceit, and views, but does not have the underlying tendency to aversion. That same person, in regard to painful feeling, has the underlying tendencies to doubt, aversion, and views, but does not have the underlying tendencies to sensual lust and conceit.

97. (Ka) yo yato kāmarāgānusayena ca paṭighānusayena ca mānānusayena ca diṭṭhānusayena ca vicikicchānusayena ca sānusayo so tato bhavarāgānusayena sānusayoti? Natthi.

97. Does a person who, with respect to something, has the underlying tendencies to sensual lust, aversion, conceit, views, and doubt, also have, with respect to that, the underlying tendency to craving for existence? No.

(Kha) yo vā pana yato bhavarāgānusayena sānusayo so tato kāmarāgānusayena ca paṭighānusayena [M 2.0121] ca mānānusayena ca diṭṭhānusayena ca vicikicchānusayena ca sānusayoti?

Or, does a person who, with respect to something, has the underlying tendency to craving for existence, also have, with respect to that, the underlying tendencies to sensual lust, aversion, conceit, views, and doubt?

Tayo puggalā rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā te tato bhavarāgānusayena ca mānānusayena ca sānusayā, no ca te tato kāmarāgānusayena ca paṭighānusayena ca diṭṭhānusayena ca vicikicchānusayena ca sānusayā. Puthujjano rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā so tato bhavarāgānusayena ca mānānusayena ca diṭṭhānusayena ca vicikicchānusayena ca sānusayo, no ca so tato kāmarāgānusayena ca paṭighānusayena ca sānusayo.

Three persons, in regard to the form-sphere and the formless-sphere, have the underlying tendencies to craving for existence and conceit, but they do not have the underlying tendencies to sensual lust, aversion, views, and doubt. An ordinary person, in regard to the form-sphere and the formless-sphere, has the underlying tendencies to craving for existence, conceit, views, and doubt, but does not have the underlying tendencies to sensual lust and aversion.

(Ka) yo yato kāmarāgānusayena ca paṭighānusayena ca mānānusayena ca diṭṭhānusayena ca vicikicchānusayena ca sānusayo so tato avijjānusayena sānusayoti? Natthi.

Does a person who, with respect to something, has the underlying tendencies to sensual lust, aversion, conceit, views, and doubt, also have, with respect to that, the underlying tendency to ignorance? No.

(Kha) yo vā pana yato avijjānusayena sānusayo so tato kāmarāgānusayena ca paṭighānusayena ca mānānusayena [T 1.0524] ca diṭṭhānusayena ca vicikicchānusayena ca sānusayoti?

Or, does a person who, with respect to something, has the underlying tendency to ignorance, also have, with respect to that, the underlying tendencies to sensual lust, aversion, conceit, views, and doubt?

Anāgāmī dukkhāya vedanāya so tato avijjānusayena sānusayo, no ca so tato kāmarāgānusayena ca paṭighānusayena ca mānānusayena ca diṭṭhānusayena ca vicikicchānusayena ca sānusayo. Sveva puggalo kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā so tato [V 2.0159] avijjānusayena ca mānānusayena ca sānusayo, no ca so tato kāmarāgānusayena ca paṭighānusayena ca diṭṭhānusayena ca vicikicchānusayena ca sānusayo. Dve puggalā rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā te tato avijjānusayena ca mānānusayena ca sānusayā, no ca te tato kāmarāgānusayena ca paṭighānusayena ca diṭṭhānusayena ca vicikicchānusayena ca sānusayā. Teva puggalā kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu te tato avijjānusayena ca kāmarāgānusayena ca mānānusayena ca sānusayā, no ca te tato paṭighānusayena ca diṭṭhānusayena ca vicikicchānusayena ca sānusayā. Teva puggalā dukkhāya vedanāya te tato avijjānusayena ca paṭighānusayena ca sānusayā, no ca te tato kāmarāgānusayena ca mānānusayena ca diṭṭhānusayena ca vicikicchānusayena ca sānusayā. Puthujjano rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā so tato avijjānusayena ca mānānusayena [M 2.0122] ca diṭṭhānusayena ca vicikicchānusayena ca sānusayo, no ca so tato kāmarāgānusayena ca paṭighānusayena ca sānusayo. Sveva puggalo kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu so [T 1.0525] tato avijjānusayena ca kāmarāgānusayena ca mānānusayena ca diṭṭhānusayena ca vicikicchānusayena ca sānusayo, no ca so tato paṭighānusayena sānusayo. Sveva puggalo dukkhāya vedanāya so tato avijjānusayena ca paṭighānusayena ca diṭṭhānusayena ca vicikicchānusayena ca sānusayo, no ca so tato kāmarāgānusayena ca mānānusayena ca sānusayo. (Pañcakamūlakaṃ)

A non-returner, in regard to painful feeling, has the underlying tendency of ignorance, but does not have the underlying tendencies of sensual lust, aversion, conceit, views, or doubt. That same person, in regard to the sensual sphere, the two feelings, the form sphere, and the formless sphere, has the underlying tendencies of ignorance and conceit, but does not have the underlying tendencies of sensual lust, aversion, views, or doubt. Two persons, in regard to the form sphere and the formless sphere, have the underlying tendencies of ignorance and conceit, but do not have the underlying tendencies of sensual lust, aversion, views, or doubt. Those same persons, in regard to the sensual sphere and the two feelings, have the underlying tendencies of ignorance, sensual lust, and conceit, but do not have the underlying tendencies of aversion, views, or doubt. Those same persons, in regard to painful feeling, have the underlying tendencies of ignorance and aversion, but do not have the underlying tendencies of sensual lust, conceit, views, or doubt. An ordinary person, in regard to the form sphere and the formless sphere, has the underlying tendencies of ignorance, conceit, views, and doubt, but does not have the underlying tendencies of sensual lust or aversion. That same person, in regard to the sensual sphere and the two feelings, has the underlying tendencies of ignorance, sensual lust, conceit, views, and doubt, but does not have the underlying tendency of aversion. That same person, in regard to painful feeling, has the underlying tendencies of ignorance, aversion, views, and doubt, but does not have the underlying tendencies of sensual lust or conceit. (The section rooted in the five)

98. (Ka) yo yato kāmarāgānusayena ca paṭighānusayena ca mānānusayena ca diṭṭhānusayena ca vicikicchānusayena ca bhavarāgānusayena ca sānusayo so tato avijjānusayena sānusayoti? Natthi.

98. (a) Does a person who, in regard to a certain sphere, has the underlying tendencies of sensual lust, aversion, conceit, views, doubt, and craving for existence, also have, in regard to that sphere, the underlying tendency of ignorance? No.

(Kha) yo vā pana yato avijjānusayena sānusayo so tato kāmarāgānusayena ca paṭighānusayena ca mānānusayena ca diṭṭhānusayena ca vicikicchānusayena ca bhavarāgānusayena ca sānusayoti?

(b) Or again, does a person who, in regard to a certain sphere, has the underlying tendency of ignorance, also have, in regard to that sphere, the underlying tendencies of sensual lust, aversion, conceit, views, doubt, and craving for existence?

Anāgāmī [V 2.0160] dukkhāya vedanāya so tato avijjānusayena sānusayo, no ca so tato kāmarāgānusayena ca paṭighānusayena ca mānānusayena ca diṭṭhānusayena ca vicikicchānusayena ca bhavarāgānusayena ca sānusayo. Sveva puggalo kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu so tato avijjānusayena ca mānānusayena ca sānusayo, no ca so tato kāmarāgānusayena ca paṭighānusayena ca diṭṭhānusayena ca vicikicchānusayena ca bhavarāgānusayena ca sānusayo. Sveva puggalo rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā so tato avijjānusayena ca mānānusayena ca bhavarāgānusayena ca sānusayo, no ca so tato kāmarāgānusayena [T 1.0526] ca paṭighānusayena ca diṭṭhānusayena ca vicikicchānusayena ca sānusayo. Dve puggalā rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā te tato avijjānusayena ca mānānusayena ca bhavarāgānusayena ca sānusayā, no ca te tato kāmarāgānusayena ca paṭighānusayena ca diṭṭhānusayena ca vicikicchānusayena ca sānusayā. Teva puggalā kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu te tato avijjānusayena ca kāmarāgānusayena ca mānānusayena [M 2.0123] ca sānusayā, no ca te tato paṭighānusayena ca diṭṭhānusayena ca vicikicchānusayena ca bhavarāgānusayena ca sānusayā. Teva puggalā dukkhāya vedanāya te tato avijjānusayena ca paṭighānusayena ca sānusayā, no ca te tato kāmarāgānusayena ca mānānusayena ca diṭṭhānusayena ca vicikicchānusayena ca bhavarāgānusayena ca sānusayā. Puthujjano rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā so tato avijjānusayena ca mānānusayena ca diṭṭhānusayena ca vicikicchānusayena ca bhavarāgānusayena ca sānusayo, no ca so tato kāmarāgānusayena ca paṭighānusayena ca sānusayo. Sveva puggalo kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu so tato avijjānusayena ca kāmarāgānusayena ca mānānusayena ca diṭṭhānusayena ca vicikicchānusayena ca sānusayo, no ca so tato paṭighānusayena ca bhavarāgānusayena ca sānusayo. Sveva puggalo dukkhāya vedanāya so tato [V 2.0161] avijjānusayena ca paṭighānusayena ca diṭṭhānusayena ca vicikicchānusayena ca sānusayo, no ca so tato kāmarāgānusayena ca mānānusayena [T 1.0527] ca bhavarāgānusayena ca sānusayo. (Chakkamūlakaṃ)

A non-returner, in regard to painful feeling, has the underlying tendency of ignorance, but does not have the underlying tendencies of sensual lust, aversion, conceit, views, doubt, or craving for existence. That same person, in regard to the sensual sphere and the two feelings, has the underlying tendencies of ignorance and conceit, but does not have the underlying tendencies of sensual lust, aversion, views, doubt, or craving for existence. That same person, in the form sphere and the formless sphere, has the underlying tendencies of ignorance, conceit, and craving for existence, but does not have the underlying tendencies of sensual lust, aversion, views, or doubt. Two persons, in the form sphere and the formless sphere, have the underlying tendencies of ignorance, conceit, and craving for existence, but do not have the underlying tendencies of sensual lust, aversion, views, or doubt. Those same persons, in regard to the sensual sphere and the two feelings, have the underlying tendencies of ignorance, sensual lust, and conceit, but do not have the underlying tendencies of aversion, views, doubt, or craving for existence. Those same persons, in regard to painful feeling, have the underlying tendencies of ignorance and aversion, but do not have the underlying tendencies of sensual lust, conceit, views, doubt, or craving for existence. An ordinary person, in the form sphere and the formless sphere, has the underlying tendencies of ignorance, conceit, views, doubt, and craving for existence, but does not have the underlying tendencies of sensual lust and aversion. That same person, in regard to the sensual sphere and the two feelings, has the underlying tendencies of ignorance, sensual lust, conceit, views, and doubt, but does not have the underlying tendencies of aversion or craving for existence. That same person, in regard to painful feeling, has the underlying tendencies of ignorance, aversion, views, and doubt, but does not have the underlying tendencies of sensual lust, conceit, or craving for existence. (The section rooted in the six)

Sānusayavāre anulomaṃ.

The Positive Method in the Section on Underlying Tendencies.

2. Sānusayavāra

2. The Section on Underlying Tendencies

(Gha) paṭilomapuggalo

(d) The Negative Method: Persons

99. (Ka) yo kāmarāgānusayena niranusayo so paṭighānusayena niranusayoti? Āmantā.

99. (a) Is a person who is free from the underlying tendency of sensual lust also free from the underlying tendency of aversion? Yes.

(Kha) yo vā pana paṭighānusayena niranusayo so kāmarāgānusayena niranusayoti? Āmantā.

(b) Or is a person who is free from the underlying tendency to aversion also free from the underlying tendency to sensual lust? Yes.

(Ka) yo kāmarāgānusayena niranusayo so mānānusayena niranusayoti?

(a) Is a person who is free from the underlying tendency to sensual lust also free from the underlying tendency to conceit?

Anāgāmī kāmarāgānusayena niranusayo, no ca mānānusayena niranusayo. Arahā kāmarāgānusayena ca niranusayo mānānusayena ca niranusayo.

The non-returner is free from the underlying tendency to sensual lust, but not free from the underlying tendency to conceit. The Arahant is free from both the underlying tendency to sensual lust and the underlying tendency to conceit.

(Kha) yo vā pana mānānusayena niranusayo so kāmarāgānusayena niranusayoti? Āmantā.

(b) Or is a person who is free from the underlying tendency to conceit also free from the underlying tendency to sensual lust? Yes.

Yo [M 2.0124] kāmarāgānusayena niranusayo so diṭṭhānusayena…pe… vicikicchānusayena niranusayoti? Āmantā.

Is a person who is free from the underlying tendency to sensual lust also free from the underlying tendency to views… and the underlying tendency to doubt? Yes.

Yo vā pana vicikicchānusayena niranusayo so kāmarāgānusayena niranusayoti?

Or is a person who is free from the underlying tendency to doubt also free from the underlying tendency to sensual lust?

Dve puggalā vicikicchānusayena niranusayā, no ca kāmarāgānusayena niranusayā. Dve puggalā vicikicchānusayena ca niranusayā kāmarāgānusayena ca niranusayā.

Two persons are free from the underlying tendency to doubt, but not from the underlying tendency to sensual lust. Two persons are free from both the underlying tendency to doubt and the underlying tendency to sensual lust.

Yo [V 2.0162] kāmarāgānusayena niranusayo so bhavarāgānusayena…pe… avijjānusayena niranusayoti?

Is a person who is free from the underlying tendency to sensual lust also free from the underlying tendency to craving for existence… and the underlying tendency to ignorance?

Anāgāmī kāmarāgānusayena niranusayo, no ca avijjānusayena niranusayo. Arahā kāmarāgānusayena ca niranusayo avijjānusayena [T 1.0528] ca niranusayo.

The non-returner is free from the underlying tendency to sensual lust, but not free from the underlying tendency to ignorance. The Arahant is free from both the underlying tendency to sensual lust and the underlying tendency to ignorance.

Yo vā pana avijjānusayena niranusayo so kāmarāgānusayena niranusayoti? Āmantā.

Or is a person who is free from the underlying tendency to ignorance also free from the underlying tendency to sensual lust? Yes.

100. (Ka) yo paṭighānusayena niranusayo so mānānusayena niranusayoti?

100. (a) Is a person who is free from the underlying tendency to aversion also free from the underlying tendency to conceit?

Anāgāmī paṭighānusayena niranusayo, no ca mānānusayena niranusayo. Arahā paṭighānusayena ca niranusayo mānānusayena ca niranusayo.

The non-returner is free from the underlying tendency to aversion, but not free from the underlying tendency to conceit. The Arahant is free from both the underlying tendency to aversion and the underlying tendency to conceit.

(Kha) yo vā pana mānānusayena niranusayo so paṭighānusayena niranusayoti? Āmantā.

(b) Or is a person who is free from the underlying tendency to conceit also free from the underlying tendency to aversion? Yes.

Yo paṭighānusayena niranusayo so diṭṭhānusayena…pe… vicikicchānusayena niranusayoti? Āmantā.

Is a person who is free from the underlying tendency to aversion also free from the underlying tendency to views… and the underlying tendency to doubt? Yes.

Yo vā pana vicikicchānusayena niranusayo so paṭighānusayena niranusayoti?

Or is a person who is free from the underlying tendency to doubt also free from the underlying tendency to aversion?

Dve puggalā vicikicchānusayena niranusayā, no ca paṭighānusayena niranusayā. Dve puggalā vicikicchānusayena ca niranusayā paṭighānusayena ca niranusayā.

Two persons are free from the underlying tendency to doubt, but not from the underlying tendency to aversion. Two persons are free from both the underlying tendency to doubt and the underlying tendency to aversion.

Yo paṭighānusayena niranusayo so bhavarāgānusayena…pe… avijjānusayena niranusayoti?

Is a person who is free from the underlying tendency to aversion also free from the underlying tendency to craving for existence… and the underlying tendency to ignorance?

Anāgāmī paṭighānusayena niranusayo, no ca avijjānusayena niranusayo. Arahā paṭighānusayena ca niranusayo avijjānusayena ca niranusayo.

The non-returner is free from the underlying tendency to aversion, but not free from the underlying tendency to ignorance. The Arahant is free from both the underlying tendency to aversion and the underlying tendency to ignorance.

Yo vā pana avijjānusayena niranusayo so paṭighānusayena niranusayoti? Āmantā.

Or is a person who is free from the underlying tendency to ignorance also free from the underlying tendency to aversion? Yes.

101. Yo [M 2.0125][V 2.0163] mānānusayena niranusayo so diṭṭhānusayena…pe… vicikicchānusayena niranusayoti? Āmantā.

101. Is a person who is free from the underlying tendency to conceit also free from the underlying tendency to views… and the underlying tendency to doubt? Yes.

Yo vā pana vicikicchānusayena niranusayo so mānānusayena niranusayoti?

Or is a person who is free from the underlying tendency to doubt also free from the underlying tendency to conceit?

Tayo puggalā vicikicchānusayena niranusayā, no ca mānānusayena niranusayā. Arahā vicikicchānusayena [T 1.0529] ca niranusayo mānānusayena ca niranusayo.

Three persons are free from the underlying tendency to doubt, but not from the underlying tendency to conceit. The Arahant is free from both the underlying tendency to doubt and the underlying tendency to conceit.

Yo mānānusayena niranusayo so bhavarāgānusayena…pe… avijjānusayena niranusayoti? Āmantā.

Is a person who is free from the underlying tendency to conceit also free from the underlying tendency to craving for existence… and the underlying tendency to ignorance? Yes.

Yo vā pana avijjānusayena niranusayo so mānānusayena niranusayoti? Āmantā.

Or is a person who is free from the underlying tendency to ignorance also free from the underlying tendency to conceit? Yes.

102. (Ka) yo diṭṭhānusayena niranusayo so vicikicchānusayena niranusayoti? Āmantā.

102. (a) Is a person who is free from the underlying tendency to views also free from the underlying tendency to doubt? Yes.

(Kha) yo vā pana vicikicchānusayena niranusayo so diṭṭhānusayena niranusayoti? Āmantā …pe….

(b) Or is a person who is free from the underlying tendency to doubt also free from the underlying tendency to views? Yes. …and so on…

103. Yo vicikicchānusayena niranusayo so bhavarāgānusayena…pe… avijjānusayena niranusayoti?

103. Is a person who is free from the underlying tendency to doubt also free from the underlying tendency to craving for existence… and the underlying tendency to ignorance?

Tayo puggalā vicikicchānusayena niranusayā, no ca avijjānusayena niranusayā. Arahā vicikicchānusayena ca niranusayo avijjānusayena ca niranusayo.

Three persons are free from the underlying tendency to doubt, but not from the underlying tendency to ignorance. The Arahant is free from both the underlying tendency to doubt and the underlying tendency to ignorance.

Yo vā pana avijjānusayena niranusayo so vicikicchānusayena niranusayoti? Āmantā.

Or again, is a person who is free from the underlying tendency to ignorance also free from the underlying tendency to doubt? Yes.

104. (Ka) yo bhavarāgānusayena niranusayo so avijjānusayena niranusayoti? Āmantā.

104. (a) Is a person who is free from the underlying tendency to craving for existence also free from the underlying tendency to ignorance? Yes.

(Kha) yo [V 2.0164] vā pana avijjānusayena niranusayo so bhavarāgānusayena niranusayoti? Āmantā. (Ekamūlakaṃ)

(b) Or again, is a person who is free from the underlying tendency to ignorance also free from the underlying tendency to craving for existence? Yes. (The Single-Root Section)

105. (Ka) yo kāmarāgānusayena ca paṭighānusayena ca niranusayo so mānānusayena niranusayoti?

105. (a) Is a person who is free from the underlying tendencies to sensual lust and aversion also free from the underlying tendency to conceit?

Anāgāmī kāmarāgānusayena ca paṭighānusayena ca niranusayo, no ca mānānusayena niranusayo. Arahā kāmarāgānusayena ca paṭighānusayena ca niranusayo mānānusayena ca niranusayo.

The non-returner is free from the underlying tendencies to sensual lust and aversion, but not from the underlying tendency to conceit. The Arahant is free from the underlying tendencies to sensual lust and aversion, and also from the underlying tendency to conceit.

(Kha) yo vā pana mānānusayena niranusayo so kāmarāgānusayena [T 1.0530] ca paṭighānusayena ca niranusayoti? Āmantā.

(b) Or again, is a person who is free from the underlying tendency to conceit also free from the underlying tendencies to sensual lust and aversion? Yes.

Yo [M 2.0126][V 2.0165] kāmarāgānusayena ca paṭighānusayena ca niranusayo so diṭṭhānusayena…pe… vicikicchānusayena niranusayoti? Āmantā.

Is a person who is free from the underlying tendencies to sensual lust and aversion also free from the underlying tendency to views... and the underlying tendency to doubt? Yes.

Yo vā pana vicikicchānusayena niranusayo so kāmarāgānusayena ca paṭighānusayena ca niranusayoti?

Or again, is a person who is free from the underlying tendency to doubt also free from the underlying tendencies to sensual lust and aversion?

Dve puggalā vicikicchānusayena niranusayā, no ca kāmarāgānusayena ca paṭighānusayena ca niranusayā. Dve puggalā vicikicchānusayena ca niranusayā kāmarāgānusayena ca paṭighānusayena ca niranusayā.

Two persons are free from the underlying tendency to doubt, but not from the underlying tendencies to sensual lust and aversion. Two persons are free from the underlying tendency to doubt and also from the underlying tendencies to sensual lust and aversion.

Yo kāmarāgānusayena ca paṭighānusayena ca niranusayo so bhavarāgānusayena…pe… avijjānusayena niranusayoti?

Is a person who is free from the underlying tendencies to sensual lust and aversion also free from the underlying tendency to craving for existence... and the underlying tendency to ignorance?

Anāgāmī kāmarāgānusayena ca paṭighānusayena ca niranusayo, no ca avijjānusayena niranusayo. Arahā kāmarāgānusayena ca paṭighānusayena ca niranusayo avijjānusayena ca niranusayo.

The Non-returner is without the latent tendencies to sensual lust and aversion, but not without the latent tendency to ignorance. The Arahant is without the latent tendencies to sensual lust and aversion, and also without the latent tendency to ignorance.

Yo vā pana avijjānusayena niranusayo so kāmarāgānusayena ca paṭighānusayena ca niranusayoti? Āmantā. (Dukamūlakaṃ)

Or again, is a person who is without the latent tendency to ignorance also without the latent tendencies to sensual lust and aversion? Yes.

106. Yo kāmarāgānusayena ca paṭighānusayena ca mānānusayena ca niranusayo so diṭṭhānusayena…pe… vicikicchānusayena niranusayoti? Āmantā.

106. Is a person who is without the latent tendencies to sensual lust, aversion, and conceit also without the latent tendency to views... and the latent tendency to doubt? Yes.

Yo vā pana vicikicchānusayena niranusayo so kāmarāgānusayena ca paṭighānusayena ca mānānusayena ca niranusayoti?

Or again, is a person who is without the latent tendency to doubt also without the latent tendencies to sensual lust, aversion, and conceit?

Dve puggalā vicikicchānusayena niranusayā, no ca kāmarāgānusayena ca paṭighānusayena ca mānānusayena ca niranusayā. Anāgāmī vicikicchānusayena [T 1.0531] ca kāmarāgānusayena ca paṭighānusayena ca niranusayo, no ca mānānusayena niranusayo. Arahā vicikicchānusayena ca niranusayo kāmarāgānusayena ca paṭighānusayena ca mānānusayena ca niranusayo.

Two persons are without the latent tendency to doubt, but not without the latent tendencies to sensual lust, aversion, and conceit. The Non-returner is without the latent tendencies to doubt, sensual lust, and aversion, but not without the latent tendency to conceit. The Arahant is without the latent tendency to doubt, and also without the latent tendencies to sensual lust, aversion, and conceit.

Yo kāmarāgānusayena ca paṭighānusayena ca mānānusayena ca niranusayo so bhavarāgānusayena…pe… avijjānusayena niranusayoti? Āmantā.

Is a person who is without the latent tendencies to sensual lust, aversion, and conceit also without the latent tendency to craving for existence... and the latent tendency to ignorance? Yes.

Yo vā pana avijjānusayena niranusayo so kāmarāgānusayena ca paṭighānusayena ca mānānusayena ca niranusayoti? Āmantā. (Tikamūlakaṃ)

Or again, is a person who is without the latent tendency to ignorance also without the latent tendencies to sensual lust, aversion, and conceit? Yes.

107. (Ka) yo [M 2.0127] kāmarāgānusayena ca paṭighānusayena ca mānānusayena ca diṭṭhānusayena ca niranusayo so vicikicchānusayena niranusayoti? Āmantā.

107. Is a person who is without the latent tendencies to sensual lust, aversion, conceit, and views also without the latent tendency to doubt? Yes.

(Kha) yo vā pana vicikicchānusayena niranusayo so kāmarāgānusayena ca paṭighānusayena ca mānānusayena ca diṭṭhānusayena ca niranusayoti?

Or again, is a person who is without the latent tendency to doubt also without the latent tendencies to sensual lust, aversion, conceit, and views?

Dve puggalā vicikicchānusayena ca diṭṭhānusayena ca niranusayā, no ca kāmarāgānusayena ca paṭighānusayena ca mānānusayena ca niranusayā. Anāgāmī vicikicchānusayena ca kāmarāgānusayena ca paṭighānusayena ca diṭṭhānusayena ca niranusayo, no ca mānānusayena niranusayo. Arahā vicikicchānusayena ca niranusayo kāmarāgānusayena ca [V 2.0166] paṭighānusayena ca mānānusayena ca diṭṭhānusayena ca niranusayo …pe…. (Catukkamūlakaṃ)

Two persons are without the latent tendencies to doubt and views, but not without the latent tendencies to sensual lust, aversion, and conceit. The Non-returner is without the latent tendencies to doubt, sensual lust, aversion, and views, but not without the latent tendency to conceit. The Arahant is without the latent tendency to doubt, and also without the latent tendencies to sensual lust, aversion, conceit, and views...

108. Yo kāmarāgānusayena ca paṭighānusayena ca mānānusayena ca diṭṭhānusayena ca vicikicchānusayena ca niranusayo so bhavarāgānusayena [T 1.0532] …pe… avijjānusayena niranusayoti? Āmantā.

108. Is a person who is without the latent tendencies to sensual lust, aversion, conceit, views, and doubt also without the latent tendency to craving for existence... and the latent tendency to ignorance? Yes.

Yo vā pana avijjānusayena niranusayo so kāmarāgānusayena ca paṭighānusayena ca mānānusayena ca diṭṭhānusayena ca vicikicchānusayena ca niranusayoti? Āmantā. (Pañcakamūlakaṃ)

Or again, is a person who is without the latent tendency to ignorance also without the latent tendencies to sensual lust, aversion, conceit, views, and doubt? Yes.

109. (Ka) yo kāmarāgānusayena ca paṭighānusayena ca mānānusayena ca diṭṭhānusayena ca vicikicchānusayena ca bhavarāgānusayena ca niranusayo so avijjānusayena niranusayoti? Āmantā.

109. Is a person who is without the latent tendencies to sensual lust, aversion, conceit, views, doubt, and craving for existence also without the latent tendency to ignorance? Yes.

(Kha) yo vā pana avijjānusayena niranusayo so kāmarāgānusayena ca paṭighānusayena ca mānānusayena ca diṭṭhānusayena ca vicikicchānusayena ca bhavarāgānusayena ca niranusayoti? Āmantā. (Chakkamūlakaṃ)

Or again, is a person who is without the latent tendency to ignorance also without the latent tendencies to sensual lust, aversion, conceit, views, doubt, and craving for existence? Yes.

(Ṅa) paṭilomaokāso

(Ṅa) The Reverse Plane

110. (Ka) yato kāmarāgānusayena niranusayo tato paṭighānusayena niranusayoti?

Where one is without the latent tendency of sensual lust, is one there also without the latent tendency of aversion?

Dukkhāya vedanāya tato kāmarāgānusayena niranusayo, no ca tato paṭighānusayena niranusayo. Rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā apariyāpanne tato kāmarāgānusayena ca niranusayo paṭighānusayena ca niranusayo.

110. In regard to painful feeling, one is there without the latent tendency of sensual lust, but not without the latent tendency of aversion. In the form realm, the formless realm, and in the unincluded, one is there without the latent tendency of sensual lust and also without the latent tendency of aversion.

(Kha) yato vā pana paṭighānusayena niranusayo [M 2.0128] tato kāmarāgānusayena niranusayoti?

Conversely, where one is without the latent tendency of aversion, is one there also without the latent tendency of sensual lust?

Kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu tato paṭighānusayena niranusayo, no ca tato kāmarāgānusayena niranusayo. Rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā apariyāpanne [V 2.0167] tato paṭighānusayena ca niranusayo kāmarāgānusayena ca niranusayo.

In the desire realm, in regard to two feelings, one is there without the latent tendency of aversion, but not without the latent tendency of sensual lust. In the form realm, the formless realm, and in the unincluded, one is there without the latent tendency of aversion and also without the latent tendency of sensual lust.

(Ka) yato kāmarāgānusayena niranusayo tato mānānusayena niranusayoti?

Where one is without the latent tendency of sensual lust, is one there also without the latent tendency of conceit?

Rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā tato kāmarāgānusayena [T 1.0533] niranusayo, no ca tato mānānusayena niranusayo. Dukkhāya vedanāya apariyāpanne tato kāmarāgānusayena ca niranusayo mānānusayena ca niranusayo.

In the form realm and the formless realm, one is there without the latent tendency of sensual desire, but not without the latent tendency of conceit. In regard to painful feeling and in the unincluded, one is there without the latent tendency of sensual desire and also without the latent tendency of conceit.

(Kha) yato vā pana mānānusayena niranusayo tato kāmarāgānusayena niranusayoti? Āmantā.

(Kha) Conversely, where one is without the latent tendency of conceit, is one there also without the latent tendency of sensual desire? Yes.

Yato kāmarāgānusayena niranusayo tato diṭṭhānusayena…pe… vicikicchānusayena niranusayoti?

Where one is without the latent tendency of sensual desire, is one there also without the latent tendency of views…pe… and of doubt?

Dukkhāya vedanāya rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā tato kāmarāgānusayena niranusayo, no ca tato vicikicchānusayena niranusayo. Apariyāpanne tato kāmarāgānusayena ca niranusayo vicikicchānusayena ca niranusayo.

In regard to painful feeling, in the form realm, and in the formless realm, one is there without the latent tendency of sensual desire, but not without the latent tendency of doubt. In the unincluded, one is there without the latent tendency of sensual desire and also without the latent tendency of doubt.

Yato vā pana vicikicchānusayena niranusayo tato kāmarāgānusayena niranusayoti? Āmantā.

Conversely, where one is without the latent tendency of doubt, is one there also without the latent tendency of sensual lust? Yes.

(Ka) yato kāmarāgānusayena niranusayo tato bhavarāgānusayena niranusayoti?

Where one is without the latent tendency of sensual lust, is one there also without the latent tendency of craving for existence?

Rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā tato kāmarāgānusayena niranusayo, no ca tato bhavarāgānusayena niranusayo. Dukkhāya vedanāya apariyāpanne tato kāmarāgānusayena ca niranusayo bhavarāgānusayena ca niranusayo.

In the form realm and the formless realm, from that one is without the latent tendency of sensual desire, but not without the latent tendency of craving for existence. In regard to painful feeling and in the unincluded, from that one is without both the latent tendency of sensual desire and the latent tendency of craving for existence.

(Kha) yato vā pana bhavarāgānusayena niranusayo tato kāmarāgānusayena niranusayoti?

Or from where one is without the latent tendency of craving for existence, from there is one without the latent tendency of sensual desire?

Kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu tato bhavarāgānusayena niranusayo, no ca tato kāmarāgānusayena niranusayo. Dukkhāya vedanāya apariyāpanne tato bhavarāgānusayena ca niranusayo kāmarāgānusayena ca niranusayo.

In the desire realm and in regard to the two feelings, from that one is without the latent tendency of craving for existence, but not without the latent tendency of sensual desire. In regard to painful feeling and in the unincluded, from that one is without both the latent tendency of craving for existence and the latent tendency of sensual desire.

(Ka) yato [V 2.0168] kāmarāgānusayena niranusayo tato avijjānusayena niranusayoti?

From where one is without the latent tendency of sensual desire, from there is one without the latent tendency of ignorance?

Dukkhāya vedanāya rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā tato kāmarāgānusayena [M 2.0129] niranusayo, no ca tato avijjānusayena [T 1.0534] niranusayo. Apariyāpanne tato kāmarāgānusayena ca niranusayo avijjānusayena ca niranusayo.

In regard to painful feeling, in the form realm, and in the formless realm, from that one is without the latent tendency of sensual desire, but not without the latent tendency of ignorance. In the unincluded, from that one is without both the latent tendency of sensual desire and the latent tendency of ignorance.

(Kha) yato vā pana avijjānusayena niranusayo tato kāmarāgānusayena niranusayoti? Āmantā.

Or from where one is without the latent tendency of ignorance, from there is one without the latent tendency of sensual desire? Yes.

111. (Ka) yato paṭighānusayena niranusayo tato mānānusayena niranusayoti?

111. From where one is without the latent tendency of aversion, from there is one without the latent tendency of conceit?

Kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā tato paṭighānusayena niranusayo, no ca tato mānānusayena niranusayo. Apariyāpanne tato paṭighānusayena ca niranusayo mānānusayena ca niranusayo.

In the desire realm, in regard to the two feelings, in the form realm, and in the formless realm, from that one is without the latent tendency of aversion, but not without the latent tendency of conceit. In the unincluded, from that one is without both the latent tendency of aversion and the latent tendency of conceit.

(Kha) yato vā pana mānānusayena niranusayo tato paṭighānusayena niranusayoti?

Or from where one is without the latent tendency of conceit, from there is one without the latent tendency of aversion?

Dukkhāya vedanāya tato mānānusayena niranusayo, no ca tato paṭighānusayena niranusayo. Apariyāpanne tato mānānusayena ca niranusayo paṭighānusayena ca niranusayo.

In regard to painful feeling, from that one is without the latent tendency of conceit, but not without the latent tendency of aversion. In the unincluded, from that one is without both the latent tendency of conceit and the latent tendency of aversion.

Yato paṭighānusayena niranusayo tato diṭṭhānusayena…pe… vicikicchānusayena niranusayoti?

From where one is without the latent tendency of aversion, from there is one without the latent tendency of views… and of doubt?

Kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā tato paṭighānusayena niranusayo, no ca tato vicikicchānusayena niranusayo. Apariyāpanne tato paṭighānusayena ca niranusayo vicikicchānusayena ca niranusayo.

In the desire realm, in regard to the two feelings, in the form realm, and in the formless realm, from that one is without the latent tendency of aversion, but not without the latent tendency of doubt. In the unincluded, from that one is without both the latent tendency of aversion and the latent tendency of doubt.

Yato vā pana vicikicchānusayena niranusayo tato paṭighānusayena niranusayoti? Āmantā.

Or from where one is without the latent tendency of doubt, from there is one without the latent tendency of aversion? Yes.

(Ka) yato paṭighānusayena niranusayo tato bhavarāgānusayena niranusayoti?

From where one is without the latent tendency of aversion, from there is one without the latent tendency of craving for existence?

Rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā tato paṭighānusayena niranusayo, no ca tato [V 2.0169] bhavarāgānusayena niranusayo. Kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu apariyāpanne tato paṭighānusayena ca niranusayo bhavarāgānusayena ca niranusayo[T 1.0535].

In the form realm and the formless realm, from that one is without the latent tendency of aversion, but not without the latent tendency of craving for existence. In the desire realm, in regard to the two feelings, and in the unincluded, from that one is without both the latent tendency of aversion and the latent tendency of craving for existence.

(Kha) yato vā pana bhavarāgānusayena niranusayo tato paṭighānusayena niranusayoti?

Or from where one is without the latent tendency of craving for existence, from there is one without the latent tendency of aversion?

Dukkhāya vedanāya tato bhavarāgānusayena niranusayo, no ca tato paṭighānusayena niranusayo. Kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu apariyāpanne tato bhavarāgānusayena ca niranusayo paṭighānusayena ca niranusayo.

In regard to painful feeling, from that one is without the latent tendency of craving for existence, but not without the latent tendency of aversion. In the desire realm, in regard to the two feelings, and in the unincluded, from that one is without both the latent tendency of craving for existence and the latent tendency of aversion.

(Ka) yato [M 2.0130] paṭighānusayena niranusayo tato avijjānusayena niranusayoti?

From where one is without the latent tendency of aversion, from there is one without the latent tendency of ignorance?

Kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā tato paṭighānusayena niranusayo, no ca tato avijjānusayena niranusayo. Apariyāpanne tato paṭighānusayena ca niranusayo avijjānusayena ca niranusayo.

In the desire realm, in regard to the two feelings, in the form realm, and in the formless realm, from that one is without the latent tendency of aversion, but not without the latent tendency of ignorance. In the unincluded, from that one is without both the latent tendency of aversion and the latent tendency of ignorance.

(Kha) yato vā pana avijjānusayena niranusayo tato paṭighānusayena niranusayoti? Āmantā.

Or from where one is without the latent tendency of ignorance, from there is one without the latent tendency of aversion? Yes.

112. Yato mānānusayena niranusayo tato diṭṭhānusayena…pe… vicikicchānusayena niranusayoti?

112. From where one is without the latent tendency of conceit, from there is one without the latent tendency of views… and of doubt?

Dukkhāya vedanāya tato mānānusayena niranusayo, no ca tato vicikicchānusayena niranusayo. Apariyāpanne tato mānānusayena ca niranusayo vicikicchānusayena ca niranusayo.

In regard to painful feeling, from that one is without the latent tendency of conceit, but not without the latent tendency of doubt. In the unincluded, from that one is without both the latent tendency of conceit and the latent tendency of doubt.

Yato vā pana vicikicchānusayena niranusayo tato mānānusayena niranusayoti? Āmantā.

Or from where one is without the latent tendency of doubt, from there is one without the latent tendency of conceit? Yes.

(Ka) yato mānānusayena niranusayo tato bhavarāgānusayena niranusayoti? Āmantā.

From where one is without the latent tendency of conceit, from there is one without the latent tendency of craving for existence? Yes.

(Kha) yato vā pana bhavarāgānusayena niranusayo tato mānānusayena niranusayoti?

Or from where one is without the latent tendency of craving for existence, from there is one without the latent tendency of conceit?

Kāmadhātuyā [V 2.0170] dvīsu vedanāsu tato bhavarāgānusayena niranusayo, no ca tato mānānusayena niranusayo. Dukkhāya vedanāya apariyāpanne tato bhavarāgānusayena ca niranusayo mānānusayena [T 1.0536] ca niranusayo.

In the desire realm, in regard to the two feelings, from that one is without the latent tendency of craving for existence, but not without the latent tendency of conceit. In regard to painful feeling and in the unincluded, from that one is without both the latent tendency of craving for existence and the latent tendency of conceit.

(Ka) yato mānānusayena niranusayo tato avijjānusayena niranusayoti?

From where one is without the latent tendency of conceit, from there is one without the latent tendency of ignorance?

Dukkhāya vedanāya tato mānānusayena niranusayo, no ca tato avijjānusayena niranusayo. Apariyāpanne tato mānānusayena ca niranusayo avijjānusayena ca niranusayo.

In regard to painful feeling, from that one is without the latent tendency of conceit, but not without the latent tendency of ignorance. In the unincluded, from that one is without both the latent tendency of conceit and the latent tendency of ignorance.

(Kha) yato vā pana avijjānusayena niranusayo tato mānānusayena niranusayoti? Āmantā.

Or from where one is without the latent tendency of ignorance, from there is one without the latent tendency of conceit? Yes.

113. (Ka) yato diṭṭhānusayena niranusayo tato vicikicchānusayena niranusayoti? Āmantā.

113. From where one is without the latent tendency of views, from there is one without the latent tendency of doubt? Yes.

(Kha) yato vā pana vicikicchānusayena niranusayo tato diṭṭhānusayena niranusayoti? Āmantā …pe….

Or from where one is without the latent tendency of doubt, from there is one without the latent tendency of views? Yes…pe….

114. (Ka) yato [M 2.0131] vicikicchānusayena niranusayo tato bhavarāgānusayena niranusayoti? Āmantā.

114. From where one is without the latent tendency of doubt, from there is one without the latent tendency of craving for existence? Yes.

(Kha) yato vā pana bhavarāgānusayena niranusayo tato vicikicchānusayena niranusayoti?

Or from where one is without the latent tendency of craving for existence, from there is one without the latent tendency of doubt?

Kāmadhātuyā tīsu vedanāsu tato bhavarāgānusayena niranusayo, no ca tato vicikicchānusayena niranusayo. Apariyāpanne tato bhavarāgānusayena ca niranusayo vicikicchānusayena ca niranusayo.

In the desire realm, with respect to the three feelings, in that sphere one is without the latent tendency to lust for existence, but one is not without the latent tendency to doubt. In the supramundane, in that sphere one is without both the latent tendency to lust for existence and the latent tendency to doubt.

(Ka) yato vicikicchānusayena niranusayo tato avijjānusayena niranusayoti? Āmantā.

(a) Where one is without the latent tendency to doubt, is one there without the latent tendency to ignorance? Yes.

(Kha) yato vā pana avijjānusayena niranusayo tato vicikicchānusayena niranusayoti? Āmantā.

(b) Or where one is without the latent tendency to ignorance, is one there without the latent tendency to doubt? Yes.

115. (Ka) yato [V 2.0171] bhavarāgānusayena niranusayo tato avijjānusayena niranusayoti?

115. (a) Where one is without the latent tendency to lust for existence, is one there without the latent tendency to ignorance?

Kāmadhātuyā tīsu vedanāsu tato bhavarāgānusayena niranusayo, no ca tato avijjānusayena niranusayo. Apariyāpanne tato bhavarāgānusayena ca niranusayo avijjānusayena ca niranusayo.

In the desire realm, with respect to the three feelings, in that sphere one is without the latent tendency to lust for existence, but one is not without the latent tendency to ignorance. In the supramundane, in that sphere one is without both the latent tendency to lust for existence and the latent tendency to ignorance.

(Kha) yato vā pana avijjānusayena [T 1.0537] niranusayo tato bhavarāgānusayena niranusayoti? Āmantā. (Ekamūlakaṃ)

(b) Or where one is without the latent tendency to ignorance, is one there without the latent tendency to lust for existence? Yes. (Single-rooted section)

116. (Ka) yato kāmarāgānusayena ca paṭighānusayena ca niranusayo tato mānānusayena niranusayoti?

116. (a) Where one is without both the latent tendency to sensual lust and the latent tendency to aversion, is one there without the latent tendency to conceit?

Rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā tato kāmarāgānusayena ca paṭighānusayena ca niranusayo, no ca tato mānānusayena niranusayo. Apariyāpanne tato kāmarāgānusayena ca paṭighānusayena ca niranusayo mānānusayena ca niranusayo.

In the form realm and the formless realm, in that sphere one is without both the latent tendency to sensual lust and the latent tendency to aversion, but one is not without the latent tendency to conceit. In the supramundane, in that sphere one is without the latent tendency to sensual lust, the latent tendency to aversion, and also the latent tendency to conceit.

(Kha) yato vā pana mānānusayena niranusayo tato kāmarāgānusayena ca paṭighānusayena ca niranusayoti?

(b) Or where one is without the latent tendency to conceit, is one there without both the latent tendency to sensual lust and the latent tendency to aversion?

Dukkhāya vedanāya tato mānānusayena ca kāmarāgānusayena ca niranusayo, no ca tato paṭighānusayena niranusayo. Apariyāpanne tato mānānusayena ca niranusayo kāmarāgānusayena ca paṭighānusayena ca niranusayo.

With respect to painful feeling, in that sphere one is without both the latent tendency to conceit and the latent tendency to sensual lust, but one is not without the latent tendency to aversion. In the supramundane, in that sphere one is without the latent tendency to conceit, the latent tendency to sensual lust, and the latent tendency to aversion.

Yato kāmarāgānusayena ca paṭighānusayena ca niranusayo tato diṭṭhānusayena…pe… vicikicchānusayena niranusayoti?

Where one is without both the latent tendency to sensual lust and the latent tendency to aversion, is one there without the latent tendency to views... and so on... without the latent tendency to doubt?

Rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā tato kāmarāgānusayena ca paṭighānusayena ca niranusayo, no ca tato vicikicchānusayena niranusayo. Apariyāpanne [M 2.0132] tato kāmarāgānusayena ca paṭighānusayena ca niranusayo vicikicchānusayena ca niranusayo.

In the form realm and the formless realm, in that sphere one is without both the latent tendency to sensual lust and the latent tendency to aversion, but one is not without the latent tendency to doubt. In the supramundane, in that sphere one is without the latent tendency to sensual lust, the latent tendency to aversion, and also the latent tendency to doubt.

Yato vā pana vicikicchānusayena niranusayo tato kāmarāgānusayena ca paṭighānusayena ca niranusayoti? Āmantā.

Or where one is without the latent tendency to doubt, is one there without both the latent tendency to sensual lust and the latent tendency to aversion? Yes.

(Ka) yato [V 2.0172] kāmarāgānusayena ca paṭighānusayena ca niranusayo tato bhavarāgānusayena niranusayoti?

(a) Where one is without both the latent tendency to sensual lust and the latent tendency to aversion, is one there without the latent tendency to lust for existence?

Rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā tato kāmarāgānusayena ca paṭighānusayena ca niranusayo, no ca tato bhavarāgānusayena niranusayo[T 1.0538]. Apariyāpanne tato kāmarāgānusayena ca paṭighānusayena ca niranusayo bhavarāgānusayena ca niranusayo.

In the form realm and the formless realm, in that sphere one is without both the latent tendency to sensual lust and the latent tendency to aversion, but one is not without the latent tendency to lust for existence. In the supramundane, in that sphere one is without the latent tendency to sensual lust, the latent tendency to aversion, and also the latent tendency to lust for existence.

(Kha) yato vā pana bhavarāgānusayena niranusayo tato kāmarāgānusayena ca paṭighānusayena ca niranusayoti?

(b) Or where one is without the latent tendency to lust for existence, is one there without both the latent tendency to sensual lust and the latent tendency to aversion?

Dukkhāya vedanāya tato bhavarāgānusayena ca kāmarāgānusayena ca niranusayo, no ca tato paṭighānusayena niranusayo. Kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu tato bhavarāgānusayena ca paṭighānusayena ca niranusayo, no ca tato kāmarāgānusayena niranusayo. Apariyāpanne tato bhavarāgānusayena ca niranusayo kāmarāgānusayena ca paṭighānusayena ca niranusayo.

With respect to painful feeling, in that sphere one is without both the latent tendency to lust for existence and the latent tendency to sensual lust, but one is not without the latent tendency to aversion. In the desire realm, with respect to the two feelings, in that sphere one is without both the latent tendency to lust for existence and the latent tendency to aversion, but one is not without the latent tendency to sensual lust. In the supramundane, in that sphere one is without the latent tendency to lust for existence, the latent tendency to sensual lust, and the latent tendency to aversion.

(Ka) yato kāmarāgānusayena ca paṭighānusayena ca niranusayo tato avijjānusayena niranusayoti?

(a) Where one is without both the latent tendency to sensual lust and the latent tendency to aversion, is one there without the latent tendency to ignorance?

Rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā tato kāmarāgānusayena ca paṭighānusayena ca niranusayo, no ca tato avijjānusayena niranusayo. Apariyāpanne tato kāmarāgānusayena ca paṭighānusayena ca niranusayo avijjānusayena ca niranusayo.

In the form realm and the formless realm, in that sphere one is without both the latent tendency to sensual lust and the latent tendency to aversion, but one is not without the latent tendency to ignorance. In the supramundane, in that sphere one is without the latent tendency to sensual lust, the latent tendency to aversion, and also the latent tendency to ignorance.

(Kha) yato vā pana avijjānusayena niranusayo tato kāmarāgānusayena ca paṭighānusayena ca niranusayoti? Āmantā. (Dukamūlakaṃ)

(b) Or where one is without the latent tendency to ignorance, is one there without both the latent tendency to sensual lust and the latent tendency to aversion? Yes. (Two-rooted section)

117. Yato kāmarāgānusayena ca paṭighānusayena ca mānānusayena ca niranusayo tato diṭṭhānusayena…pe… vicikicchānusayena niranusayoti? Āmantā.

117. Where one is without the latent tendencies to sensual lust, to aversion, and to conceit, is one there without the latent tendency to views... and so on... without the latent tendency to doubt? Yes.

Yato vā pana vicikicchānusayena niranusayo tato kāmarāgānusayena ca paṭighānusayena ca mānānusayena ca niranusayoti? Āmantā.

Or where one is without the latent tendency to doubt, is one there without the latent tendencies to sensual lust, to aversion, and to conceit? Yes.

(Ka) yato [M 2.0133][V 2.0173] kāmarāgānusayena ca paṭighānusayena ca mānānusayena [T 1.0539] ca niranusayo tato bhavarāgānusayena niranusayoti? Āmantā.

(a) Where one is without the latent tendencies to sensual lust, to aversion, and to conceit, is one there without the latent tendency to lust for existence? Yes.

(Kha) yato vā pana bhavarāgānusayena niranusayo tato kāmarāgānusayena ca paṭighānusayena ca mānānusayena ca niranusayoti?

(b) Or where one is without the latent tendency to lust for existence, is one there without the latent tendencies to sensual lust, to aversion, and to conceit?

Dukkhāya vedanāya tato bhavarāgānusayena ca kāmarāgānusayena ca mānānusayena ca niranusayo, no ca tato paṭighānusayena niranusayo. Kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu tato bhavarāgānusayena ca paṭighānusayena ca niranusayo, no ca tato kāmarāgānusayena ca mānānusayena ca niranusayo. Apariyāpanne tato bhavarāgānusayena ca niranusayo kāmarāgānusayena ca paṭighānusayena ca mānānusayena ca niranusayo.

With respect to painful feeling, in that sphere one is without the latent tendencies to lust for existence, to sensual lust, and to conceit, but one is not without the latent tendency to aversion. In the desire realm, with respect to the two feelings, in that sphere one is without both the latent tendency to lust for existence and the latent tendency to aversion, but one is not without the latent tendencies to sensual lust and to conceit. In the supramundane, in that sphere one is without the latent tendencies to lust for existence, to sensual lust, to aversion, and to conceit.

(Ka) yato kāmarāgānusayena ca paṭighānusayena ca mānānusayena ca niranusayo tato avijjānusayena niranusayoti? Āmantā.

(a) Where one is without the latent tendencies to sensual lust, to aversion, and to conceit, is one there without the latent tendency to ignorance? Yes.

(Kha) yato vā pana avijjānusayena niranusayo tato kāmarāgānusayena ca paṭighānusayena ca mānānusayena ca niranusayoti? Āmantā. (Tikamūlakaṃ)

Or if one is without the underlying tendency to ignorance, is one thereby without the underlying tendencies to sensual lust, aversion, and conceit? Yes.

118. (Ka) yato kāmarāgānusayena ca paṭighānusayena ca mānānusayena ca diṭṭhānusayena ca niranusayo tato vicikicchānusayena niranusayoti? Āmantā.

118. If one is without the underlying tendencies to sensual lust, aversion, conceit, and views, is one thereby without the underlying tendency to doubt? Yes.

(Kha) yato vā pana vicikicchānusayena niranusayo tato kāmarāgānusayena ca paṭighānusayena ca mānānusayena ca diṭṭhānusayena ca niranusayoti? Āmantā …pe…. (Catukkamūlakaṃ)

Or, if one is without the underlying tendency to doubt, is one thereby without the underlying tendencies to sensual lust, aversion, conceit, and views? Yes. …pe….

119. (Ka) yato kāmarāgānusayena ca paṭighānusayena ca mānānusayena ca diṭṭhānusayena ca vicikicchānusayena ca niranusayo tato bhavarāgānusayena [T 1.0540] niranusayoti? Āmantā.

119. If one is without the underlying tendencies to sensual lust, aversion, conceit, views, and doubt, is one thereby without the underlying tendency to lust for existence? Yes.

(Kha) yato vā pana bhavarāgānusayena niranusayo tato kāmarāgānusayena ca paṭighānusayena ca mānānusayena ca diṭṭhānusayena ca vicikicchānusayena ca niranusayoti?

Or, if one is without the underlying tendency to lust for existence, is one thereby without the underlying tendencies to sensual lust, aversion, conceit, views, and doubt?

Dukkhāya [V 2.0174] vedanāya tato bhavarāgānusayena ca kāmarāgānusayena ca mānānusayena ca niranusayo, no ca tato paṭighānusayena ca diṭṭhānusayena ca vicikicchānusayena ca niranusayo. Kāmadhātuyā [M 2.0134] dvīsu vedanāsu tato bhavarāgānusayena ca paṭighānusayena ca niranusayo, no ca tato kāmarāgānusayena ca mānānusayena ca diṭṭhānusayena ca vicikicchānusayena ca niranusayo. Apariyāpanne tato bhavarāgānusayena ca niranusayo kāmarāgānusayena ca paṭighānusayena ca mānānusayena ca diṭṭhānusayena ca vicikicchānusayena ca niranusayo …pe…. (Pañcakamūlakaṃ)

In regard to painful feeling, one is without the underlying tendencies to lust for existence, sensual lust, and conceit, but not without the underlying tendencies to aversion, views, and doubt. In regard to the two feelings in the desire realm, one is without the underlying tendencies to lust for existence and aversion, but not without the underlying tendencies to sensual lust, conceit, views, and doubt. In the unincluded, one is without the underlying tendency to lust for existence and also without the underlying tendencies to sensual lust, aversion, conceit, views, and doubt. …pe….

120. (Ka) yato kāmarāgānusayena ca paṭighānusayena ca mānānusayena ca diṭṭhānusayena ca vicikicchānusayena ca bhavarāgānusayena ca niranusayo tato avijjānusayena niranusayoti? Āmantā.

120. If one is without the underlying tendencies to sensual lust, aversion, conceit, views, doubt, and lust for existence, is one thereby without the underlying tendency to ignorance? Yes.

(Kha) yato vā pana avijjānusayena niranusayo tato kāmarāgānusayena ca paṭighānusayena ca mānānusayena ca diṭṭhānusayena ca vicikicchānusayena ca bhavarāgānusayena ca niranusayoti? Āmantā. (Chakkamūlakaṃ)

Or, if one is without the underlying tendency to ignorance, is one thereby without the underlying tendencies to sensual lust, aversion, conceit, views, doubt, and lust for existence? Yes.

(Ca) paṭilomapuggalokāsā

(Ca) The Reverse Person-Plane

121. (Ka) yo yato kāmarāgānusayena niranusayo so tato paṭighānusayena niranusayoti?

Is a person who is without the underlying tendency to sensual lust in regard to a certain domain also without the underlying tendency to aversion in regard to that domain?

Tayo puggalā dukkhāya vedanāya te tato kāmarāgānusayena niranusayā, no ca te tato paṭighānusayena niranusayā.

121. Three persons, in regard to painful feeling, are without the underlying tendency to sensual lust, but they are not without the underlying tendency to aversion.

Teva [T 1.0541] puggalā rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā apariyāpanne te tato kāmarāgānusayena ca niranusayā paṭighānusayena ca niranusayā. Dve puggalā sabbattha kāmarāgānusayena ca niranusayā paṭighānusayena ca niranusayā.

Those same three persons, in regard to the form realm, the formless realm, and the supramundane, are without both the underlying tendency to sensual lust and the underlying tendency to aversion. Two persons are everywhere without both the underlying tendency to sensual lust and the underlying tendency to aversion.

(Kha) yo [V 2.0175] vā pana yato paṭighānusayena niranusayo so tato kāmarāgānusayena niranusayoti?

Or is a person who is without the underlying tendency to aversion in regard to a certain domain also without the underlying tendency to sensual lust in regard to that domain?

Tayo puggalā kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu te tato paṭighānusayena niranusayā, no ca te tato kāmarāgānusayena niranusayā. Teva puggalā rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā apariyāpanne te tato paṭighānusayena ca niranusayā kāmarāgānusayena ca niranusayā. Dve puggalā sabbattha paṭighānusayena ca niranusayā kāmarāgānusayena ca niranusayā.

Three persons, in regard to the two feelings in the sense-sphere, are without the underlying tendency to aversion, but they are not without the underlying tendency to sensual lust. Those same three persons, in regard to the form realm, the formless realm, and the supramundane, are without both the underlying tendency to aversion and the underlying tendency to sensual lust. Two persons are everywhere without both the underlying tendency to aversion and the underlying tendency to sensual lust.

(Ka) yo yato kāmarāgānusayena niranusayo so tato mānānusayena niranusayoti?

Is a person who is without the underlying tendency to sensual lust in regard to a certain domain also without the underlying tendency to conceit in regard to that domain?

Tayo puggalā rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā [M 2.0135] te tato kāmarāgānusayena niranusayā, no ca te tato mānānusayena niranusayā. Teva puggalā dukkhāya vedanāya apariyāpanne te tato kāmarāgānusayena ca niranusayā mānānusayena ca niranusayā. Anāgāmī kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā so tato kāmarāgānusayena niranusayo, no ca so tato mānānusayena niranusayo. Sveva puggalo dukkhāya vedanāya apariyāpanne so tato kāmarāgānusayena ca niranusayo mānānusayena ca niranusayo. Arahā sabbattha kāmarāgānusayena ca niranusayo mānānusayena ca niranusayo.

Three persons, in regard to the form realm and the formless realm, are without the underlying tendency to sensual lust, but they are not without the underlying tendency to conceit. Those same three persons, in regard to painful feeling and the supramundane, are without both the underlying tendency to sensual lust and the underlying tendency to conceit. The non-returner, in regard to the sense-sphere, the two feelings, the form realm, and the formless realm, is without the underlying tendency to sensual lust, but not without the underlying tendency to conceit. That same person, in regard to painful feeling and the supramundane, is without both the underlying tendency to sensual lust and the underlying tendency to conceit. The Arahant is everywhere without both the underlying tendency to sensual lust and the underlying tendency to conceit.

(Kha) yo vā pana yato mānānusayena niranusayo so tato kāmarāgānusayena niranusayoti? Āmantā[T 1.0542].

Or is a person who is without the underlying tendency to conceit in regard to a certain domain also without the underlying tendency to sensual lust in regard to that domain? Yes.

Yo yato kāmarāgānusayena niranusayo so tato diṭṭhānusayena…pe… vicikicchānusayena niranusayoti?

Is a person who is without the underlying tendency to sensual lust in regard to a certain domain also without the underlying tendency to views…pe… the underlying tendency to doubt?

Puthujjano dukkhāya vedanāya rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā so tato kāmarāgānusayena niranusayo, no ca so tato vicikicchānusayena niranusayo. Sveva puggalo apariyāpanne so tato kāmarāgānusayena ca niranusayo vicikicchānusayena ca niranusayo. Dve puggalā sabbattha kāmarāgānusayena ca niranusayā vicikicchānusayena ca niranusayā.

The worldling, in regard to painful feeling, the form realm, and the formless realm, is without the underlying tendency to sensual lust, but is not without the underlying tendency to doubt. That same person, in regard to the supramundane, is without both the underlying tendency to sensual lust and the underlying tendency to doubt. Two persons are everywhere without both the underlying tendency to sensual lust and the underlying tendency to doubt.

Yo [V 2.0176] vā pana yato vicikicchānusayena niranusayo so tato kāmarāgānusayena niranusayoti?

Or is a person who is without the underlying tendency to doubt in regard to a certain domain also without the underlying tendency to sensual lust in regard to that domain?

Dve puggalā kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu te tato vicikicchānusayena niranusayā, no ca te tato kāmarāgānusayena niranusayā. Teva puggalā dukkhāya vedanāya rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā apariyāpanne te tato vicikicchānusayena ca niranusayā kāmarāgānusayena ca niranusayā. Dve puggalā sabbattha vicikicchānusayena ca niranusayā kāmarāgānusayena ca niranusayā.

Two persons, with respect to the sense-sphere and the two feelings, are without the latent tendency to doubt that arises therefrom, but they are not without the latent tendency to sensual lust that arises therefrom. Those same persons, with respect to painful feeling, the form realm, the formless realm, and the supramundane, are without both the latent tendency to doubt and the latent tendency to sensual lust that arise therefrom. Two persons are everywhere without both the latent tendency to doubt and the latent tendency to sensual lust.

(Ka) yo yato kāmarāgānusayena niranusayo so tato bhavarāgānusayena niranusayoti?

Is a person who is without the latent tendency to sensual lust with respect to a certain domain also without the latent tendency to craving for existence with respect to that domain?

Tayo puggalā rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā te tato kāmarāgānusayena niranusayā, no ca te tato bhavarāgānusayena niranusayā. Teva puggalā dukkhāya vedanāya apariyāpanne te tato kāmarāgānusayena ca niranusayā bhavarāgānusayena [M 2.0136] ca niranusayā. Anāgāmī rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā so tato kāmarāgānusayena niranusayo, no ca so tato bhavarāgānusayena niranusayo. Sveva puggalo kāmadhātuyā tīsu [T 1.0543] vedanāsu apariyāpanne so tato kāmarāgānusayena ca niranusayo bhavarāgānusayena ca niranusayo. Arahā sabbattha kāmarāgānusayena ca niranusayo bhavarāgānusayena ca niranusayo.

Three persons, with respect to the form realm and the formless realm, are without the latent tendency to sensual lust that arises therefrom, but they are not without the latent tendency to craving for existence that arises therefrom. Those same persons, with respect to painful feeling and the supramundane, are without both the latent tendency to sensual lust and the latent tendency to craving for existence that arise therefrom. The non-returner, with respect to the form realm and the formless realm, is without the latent tendency to sensual lust that arises therefrom, but not without the latent tendency to craving for existence that arises therefrom. That same person, with respect to the sense-sphere, the three feelings, and the supramundane, is without both the latent tendency to sensual lust and the latent tendency to craving for existence that arise therefrom. The Arahant is everywhere without both the latent tendency to sensual lust and the latent tendency to craving for existence.

(Kha) yo vā pana yato bhavarāgānusayena niranusayo so tato kāmarāgānusayena niranusayoti?

Or again, is a person who is without the latent tendency to craving for existence with respect to a certain domain also without the latent tendency to sensual lust with respect to that domain?

Tayo puggalā kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu te tato bhavarāgānusayena niranusayā, no ca te tato kāmarāgānusayena niranusayā. Teva puggalā dukkhāya vedanāya apariyāpanne te tato bhavarāgānusayena ca niranusayā kāmarāgānusayena ca niranusayā. Arahā sabbattha bhavarāgānusayena ca niranusayo kāmarāgānusayena ca niranusayo.

Three persons, with respect to the sense-sphere and the two feelings, are without the latent tendency to craving for existence that arises therefrom, but they are not without the latent tendency to sensual lust that arises therefrom. Those same persons, with respect to painful feeling and the supramundane, are without both the latent tendency to craving for existence and the latent tendency to sensual lust that arise therefrom. The Arahant is everywhere without both the latent tendency to craving for existence and the latent tendency to sensual lust.

(Ka) yo [V 2.0177] yato kāmarāgānusayena niranusayo so tato avijjānusayena niranusayoti?
