Is a person who is without the latent tendency to sensual lust with respect to a certain domain also without the latent tendency to ignorance with respect to that domain?

Tayo puggalā dukkhāya vedanāya rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā te tato kāmarāgānusayena niranusayā, no ca te tato avijjānusayena niranusayā. Teva puggalā apariyāpanne te tato kāmarāgānusayena ca niranusayā avijjānusayena ca niranusayā. Anāgāmī kāmadhātuyā tīsu vedanāsu rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā so tato kāmarāgānusayena niranusayo, no ca so tato avijjānusayena niranusayo. Sveva puggalo apariyāpanne so tato kāmarāgānusayena ca niranusayo avijjānusayena ca niranusayo. Arahā sabbattha kāmarāgānusayena ca niranusayo avijjānusayena ca niranusayo.

Three persons, with respect to painful feeling, the form realm, and the formless realm, are without the latent tendency to sensual lust that arises therefrom, but they are not without the latent tendency to ignorance that arises therefrom. Those same persons, with respect to the supramundane, are without both the latent tendency to sensual lust and the latent tendency to ignorance that arise therefrom. The non-returner, with respect to the sense-sphere, the three feelings, the form realm, and the formless realm, is without the latent tendency to sensual lust that arises therefrom, but he is not without the latent tendency to ignorance that arises therefrom. That same person, with respect to the supramundane, is without both the latent tendency to sensual lust and the latent tendency to ignorance that arise therefrom. The Arahant is everywhere without both the latent tendency to sensual lust and the latent tendency to ignorance.

(Kha) yo vā pana yato avijjānusayena niranusayo so tato kāmarāgānusayena niranusayoti? Āmantā.

Or again, is a person who is without the latent tendency to ignorance with respect to a certain domain also without the latent tendency to sensual lust with respect to that domain? Yes.

122. (Ka) yo [T 1.0544] yato paṭighānusayena niranusayo so tato mānānusayena niranusayoti?

122. Is a person who is without the latent tendency to aversion with respect to a certain domain also without the latent tendency to conceit with respect to that domain?

Tayo puggalā kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā te tato paṭighānusayena niranusayā, no ca te tato mānānusayena niranusayā. Teva puggalā apariyāpanne te tato paṭighānusayena ca niranusayā mānānusayena [M 2.0137] ca niranusayā. Anāgāmī kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā so tato paṭighānusayena niranusayo, no ca so tato mānānusayena niranusayo. Sveva puggalo dukkhāya vedanāya apariyāpanne so tato paṭighānusayena ca niranusayo mānānusayena ca niranusayo. Arahā sabbattha paṭighānusayena ca niranusayo mānānusayena ca niranusayo.

Three persons, with respect to the sense-sphere, the two feelings, the form realm, and the formless realm, are without the latent tendency to aversion that arises therefrom, but they are not without the latent tendency to conceit that arises therefrom. Those same persons, with respect to the supramundane, are without both the latent tendency to aversion and the latent tendency to conceit that arise therefrom. The non-returner, with respect to the sense-sphere, the two feelings, the form realm, and the formless realm, is without the latent tendency to aversion that arises therefrom, but he is not without the latent tendency to conceit that arises therefrom. That same person, with respect to painful feeling and the supramundane, is without both the latent tendency to aversion and the latent tendency to conceit that arise therefrom. The Arahant is everywhere without both the latent tendency to aversion and the latent tendency to conceit.

(Kha) yo vā pana yato mānānusayena niranusayo so tato paṭighānusayena niranusayoti?

Or again, is a person who is without the latent tendency to conceit with respect to a certain domain also without the latent tendency to aversion with respect to that domain?

Tayo puggalā dukkhāya vedanāya te tato mānānusayena niranusayā, no [V 2.0178] ca te tato paṭighānusayena niranusayā. Teva puggalā apariyāpanne te tato mānānusayena ca niranusayā paṭighānusayena ca niranusayā. Arahā sabbattha mānānusayena ca niranusayo paṭighānusayena ca niranusayo.

Three persons, with respect to painful feeling, are without the latent tendency to conceit that arises therefrom, but they are not without the latent tendency to aversion that arises therefrom. Those same persons, with respect to the supramundane, are without both the latent tendency to conceit and the latent tendency to aversion that arise therefrom. The Arahant is everywhere without both the latent tendency to conceit and the latent tendency to aversion.

Yo yato paṭighānusayena niranusayo so tato diṭṭhānusayena…pe… vicikicchānusayena niranusayoti?

Is a person who is without the latent tendency to aversion with respect to a certain domain also without the latent tendency to views... and the latent tendency to doubt with respect to that domain?

Puthujjano kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā so tato paṭighānusayena niranusayo, no ca so tato vicikicchānusayena niranusayo. Sveva puggalo apariyāpanne so tato paṭighānusayena ca niranusayo vicikicchānusayena ca niranusayo. Dve [T 1.0545] puggalā sabbattha paṭighānusayena ca niranusayā vicikicchānusayena ca niranusayā.

A worldling, with respect to the sense-sphere, the two feelings, the form realm, and the formless realm, is without the latent tendency to aversion that arises therefrom, but he is not without the latent tendency to doubt that arises therefrom. That same person, with respect to the supramundane, is without both the latent tendency to aversion and the latent tendency to doubt that arise therefrom. Two persons are everywhere without both the latent tendency to aversion and the latent tendency to doubt.

Yo vā pana yato vicikicchānusayena niranusayo so tato paṭighānusayena niranusayoti?

Or again, is a person who is without the latent tendency to doubt with respect to a certain domain also without the latent tendency to aversion with respect to that domain?

Dve puggalā dukkhāya vedanāya te tato vicikicchānusayena niranusayā, no ca te tato paṭighānusayena niranusayā. Teva puggalā kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā apariyāpanne te tato vicikicchānusayena ca niranusayā paṭighānusayena ca niranusayā. Dve puggalā sabbattha vicikicchānusayena ca niranusayā paṭighānusayena ca niranusayā.

Two persons, with respect to painful feeling, are without the latent tendency to doubt that arises therefrom, but they are not without the latent tendency to aversion that arises therefrom. Those same persons, with respect to the sense-sphere, the two feelings, the form realm, the formless realm, and the supramundane, are without both the latent tendency to doubt and the latent tendency to aversion that arise therefrom. Two persons are everywhere without both the latent tendency to doubt and the latent tendency to aversion.

(Ka) yo yato paṭighānusayena niranusayo so tato bhavarāgānusayena niranusayoti?

Is a person who is without the latent tendency of aversion in regard to a certain sphere also without the latent tendency of lust for becoming in regard to that sphere?

Tayo puggalā rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā te tato paṭighānusayena niranusayā, no ca te tato bhavarāgānusayena niranusayā. Teva puggalā kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu [M 2.0138] apariyāpanne te tato paṭighānusayena ca niranusayā bhavarāgānusayena ca niranusayā. Anāgāmī rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā so tato paṭighānusayena niranusayo, no ca so tato bhavarāgānusayena [V 2.0179] niranusayo. Sveva puggalo kāmadhātuyā tīsu vedanāsu apariyāpanne so tato paṭighānusayena ca niranusayo bhavarāgānusayena ca niranusayo. Arahā sabbattha paṭighānusayena ca niranusayo bhavarāgānusayena ca niranusayo.

Three persons—in regard to the form realm and the formless realm—are without the latent tendency of aversion in regard to these, but they are not without the latent tendency of lust for becoming in regard to these. Those same persons—in regard to the sense-sphere realm, the two feelings, and the unincluded—are without both the latent tendency of aversion and the latent tendency of lust for becoming in regard to these. The non-returner—in regard to the form realm and the formless realm—is without the latent tendency of aversion in regard to these, but he is not without the latent tendency of lust for becoming in regard to these. That same person—in regard to the sense-sphere realm, the three feelings, and the unincluded—is without both the latent tendency of aversion and the latent tendency of lust for becoming in regard to these. The Arahant is, in all spheres, without both the latent tendency of aversion and the latent tendency of lust for becoming.

(Kha) yo vā pana yato bhavarāgānusayena niranusayo so tato paṭighānusayena niranusayoti?

Or again, is a person who is without the latent tendency of lust for becoming in regard to a certain sphere also without the latent tendency of aversion in regard to that sphere?

Tayo puggalā dukkhāya vedanāya te tato bhavarāgānusayena niranusayā, no ca te tato paṭighānusayena niranusayā. Teva puggalā kāmadhātuyā dvīsu [T 1.0546] vedanāsu apariyāpanne te tato bhavarāgānusayena ca niranusayā paṭighānusayena ca niranusayā. Arahā sabbattha bhavarāgānusayena ca niranusayo paṭighānusayena ca niranusayo.

Three persons, in regard to painful feeling, are without the latent tendency of lust for becoming in regard to it, but they are not without the latent tendency of aversion in regard to it. Those same persons—in regard to the sense-sphere realm, the two feelings, and the unincluded—are without both the latent tendency of lust for becoming and the latent tendency of aversion in regard to these. The Arahant is, in all spheres, without both the latent tendency of lust for becoming and the latent tendency of aversion.

(Ka) yo yato paṭighānusayena niranusayo so tato avijjānusayena niranusayoti?

Is a person who is without the latent tendency of aversion in regard to a certain sphere also without the latent tendency of ignorance in regard to that sphere?

Tayo puggalā kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā te tato paṭighānusayena niranusayā, no ca te tato avijjānusayena niranusayā. Teva puggalā apariyāpanne te tato paṭighānusayena ca niranusayā avijjānusayena ca niranusayā. Anāgāmī kāmadhātuyā tīsu vedanāsu rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā so tato paṭighānusayena niranusayo no ca so tato avijjānusayena niranusayo. Sveva puggalo apariyāpanne so tato paṭighānusayena ca niranusayo avijjānusayena ca niranusayo. Arahā sabbattha paṭighānusayena ca niranusayo avijjānusayena ca niranusayo.

Three persons—in regard to the sense-sphere realm, the two feelings, the form realm, and the formless realm—are without the latent tendency of aversion in regard to these, but they are not without the latent tendency of ignorance in regard to these. Those same persons, in regard to the unincluded, are without both the latent tendency of aversion and the latent tendency of ignorance in regard to it. The non-returner—in regard to the sense-sphere realm, the three feelings, the form realm, and the formless realm—is without the latent tendency of aversion in regard to these, but he is not without the latent tendency of ignorance in regard to these. That same person, in regard to the unincluded, is without both the latent tendency of aversion and the latent tendency of ignorance in regard to it. The Arahant is, in all spheres, without both the latent tendency of aversion and the latent tendency of ignorance.

(Kha) yo vā pana yato avijjānusayena niranusayo so tato paṭighānusayena niranusayoti? Āmantā.

Or again, is a person who is without the latent tendency of ignorance in regard to a certain sphere also without the latent tendency of aversion in regard to that sphere? Yes.

123. Yo yato mānānusayena niranusayo so tato diṭṭhānusayena…pe… vicikicchānusayena niranusayoti?

123. Is a person who is without the latent tendency of conceit in regard to a certain sphere also without the latent tendency of views... and so on... the latent tendency of doubt in regard to that sphere?

Puthujjano dukkhāya vedanāya so tato mānānusayena niranusayo, no [V 2.0180] ca so tato vicikicchānusayena niranusayo. Sveva puggalo apariyāpanne so [M 2.0139] tato mānānusayena ca niranusayo vicikicchānusayena ca niranusayo. Arahā sabbattha mānānusayena ca niranusayo vicikicchānusayena ca niranusayo.

An ordinary person, in regard to painful feeling, is without the latent tendency of conceit in regard to it, but he is not without the latent tendency of doubt in regard to it. That same person, in regard to the unincluded, is without both the latent tendency of conceit and the latent tendency of doubt in regard to it. The Arahant is, in all spheres, without both the latent tendency of conceit and the latent tendency of doubt.

Yo vā pana yato [T 1.0547] vicikicchānusayena niranusayo so tato mānānusayena niranusayoti?

Or again, is a person who is without the latent tendency of doubt in regard to a certain sphere also without the latent tendency of conceit in regard to that sphere?

Tayo puggalā kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā te tato vicikicchānusayena niranusayā, no ca te tato mānānusayena niranusayā. Teva puggalā dukkhāya vedanāya apariyāpanne te tato vicikicchānusayena ca niranusayā mānānusayena ca niranusayā. Arahā sabbattha vicikicchānusayena ca niranusayo mānānusayena ca niranusayo.

Three persons—in regard to the sense-sphere realm, the two feelings, the form realm, and the formless realm—are without the latent tendency of doubt in regard to these, but they are not without the latent tendency of conceit in regard to these. Those same persons—in regard to painful feeling and the unincluded—are without both the latent tendency of doubt and the latent tendency of conceit in regard to these. The Arahant is, in all spheres, without both the latent tendency of doubt and the latent tendency of conceit.

(Ka) yo yato mānānusayena niranusayo so tato bhavarāgānusayena niranusayoti? Āmantā.

Is a person who is without the latent tendency of conceit in regard to a certain sphere also without the latent tendency of lust for becoming in regard to that sphere? Yes.

(Kha) yo vā pana yato bhavarāgānusayena niranusayo so tato mānānusayena niranusayoti?

Or again, is a person who is without the latent tendency of lust for becoming in regard to a certain sphere also without the latent tendency of conceit in regard to that sphere?

Cattāro puggalā kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu te tato bhavarāgānusayena niranusayā, no ca te tato mānānusayena niranusayā. Teva puggalā dukkhāya vedanāya apariyāpanne te tato bhavarāgānusayena ca niranusayā mānānusayena ca niranusayā. Arahā sabbattha bhavarāgānusayena ca niranusayo mānānusayena ca niranusayo.

Four persons—in regard to the sense-sphere realm and the two feelings—are without the latent tendency of lust for becoming in regard to these, but they are not without the latent tendency of conceit in regard to these. Those same persons—in regard to painful feeling and the unincluded—are without both the latent tendency of lust for becoming and the latent tendency of conceit in regard to these. The Arahant is, in all spheres, without both the latent tendency of lust for becoming and the latent tendency of conceit.

(Ka) yo yato mānānusayena niranusayo so tato avijjānusayena niranusayoti?

Is a person who is without the latent tendency of conceit in regard to a certain sphere also without the latent tendency of ignorance in regard to that sphere?

Cattāro puggalā dukkhāya vedanāya te tato mānānusayena niranusayā, no ca te tato avijjānusayena niranusayā. Teva puggalā apariyāpanne te tato mānānusayena ca niranusayā avijjānusayena ca niranusayā. Arahā sabbattha mānānusayena ca niranusayo avijjānusayena ca niranusayo.

Four persons, in regard to painful feeling, are without the latent tendency of conceit in regard to it, but they are not without the latent tendency of ignorance in regard to it. Those same persons, in regard to the unincluded, are without both the latent tendency of conceit and the latent tendency of ignorance in regard to it. The Arahant is, in all spheres, without both the latent tendency of conceit and the latent tendency of ignorance.

(Kha) yo [V 2.0181] vā pana yato avijjānusayena niranusayo so tato mānānusayena niranusayoti? Āmantā.

Or again, is a person who is without the latent tendency of ignorance in regard to a certain sphere also without the latent tendency of conceit in regard to that sphere? Yes.

124. (Ka) yo [T 1.0548] yato diṭṭhānusayena niranusayo so tato vicikicchānusayena niranusayoti? Āmantā.

124. Is a person who is without the latent tendency of views in regard to a certain sphere also without the latent tendency of doubt in regard to that sphere? Yes.

(Kha) yo vā pana yato vicikicchānusayena niranusayo so tato diṭṭhānusayena niranusayoti? Āmantā…pe….

Or again, is a person who is without the latent tendency of doubt in regard to a certain sphere also without the latent tendency of views in regard to that sphere? Yes... and so on...

125. (Ka) yo [M 2.0140] yato vicikicchānusayena niranusayo so tato bhavarāgānusayena niranusayoti?

125. Is a person who is without the latent tendency of doubt in regard to a certain sphere also without the latent tendency of lust for becoming in regard to that sphere?

Tayo puggalā rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā te tato vicikicchānusayena niranusayā, no ca te tato bhavarāgānusayena niranusayā. Teva puggalā kāmadhātuyā tīsu vedanāsu apariyāpanne te tato vicikicchānusayena ca niranusayā bhavarāgānusayena ca niranusayā. Arahā sabbattha vicikicchānusayena ca niranusayo bhavarāgānusayena ca niranusayo.

Three individuals are devoid of the underlying tendency to doubt that arises from the form realm and the formless realm, but they are not devoid of the underlying tendency to craving for existence that arises therefrom. Those same individuals are devoid of both the underlying tendency to doubt and the underlying tendency to craving for existence that arise from the sense-sphere realm, the three feelings, and the unincluded. The Arahant is everywhere devoid of both the underlying tendency to doubt and the underlying tendency to craving for existence.

(Kha) yo vā pana yato bhavarāgānusayena niranusayo so tato vicikicchānusayena niranusayoti?

(Kha) Or again, is an individual who is devoid of the underlying tendency to craving for existence that arises from a certain sphere also devoid of the underlying tendency to doubt that arises from that sphere?

Puthujjano kāmadhātuyā tīsu vedanāsu so tato bhavarāgānusayena niranusayo, no ca so tato vicikicchānusayena niranusayo. Sveva puggalo apariyāpanne so tato bhavarāgānusayena ca niranusayo vicikicchānusayena ca niranusayo. Arahā sabbattha bhavarāgānusayena ca niranusayo vicikicchānusayena ca niranusayo.

An ordinary person is devoid of the underlying tendency to craving for existence that arises from the sense-sphere realm and the three feelings, but he is not devoid of the underlying tendency to doubt that arises therefrom. That same individual, in regard to the unincluded, is devoid of both the underlying tendency to craving for existence and the underlying tendency to doubt that arise therefrom. The Arahant is everywhere devoid of both the underlying tendency to craving for existence and the underlying tendency to doubt.

(Ka) yo yato vicikicchānusayena niranusayo so tato avijjānusayena niranusayoti?

(Ka) Is an individual who is devoid of the underlying tendency to doubt that arises from a certain sphere also devoid of the underlying tendency to ignorance that arises from that sphere?

Tayo puggalā kāmadhātuyā tīsu vedanāsu rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā te tato vicikicchānusayena niranusayā, no ca te tato avijjānusayena niranusayā. Teva puggalā apariyāpanne te tato vicikicchānusayena ca niranusayā avijjānusayena ca niranusayā. Arahā [V 2.0182] sabbattha vicikicchānusayena ca niranusayo [T 1.0549] avijjānusayena ca niranusayo.

Three individuals are devoid of the underlying tendency to doubt that arises from the sense-sphere realm, the three feelings, the form realm, and the formless realm, but they are not devoid of the underlying tendency to ignorance that arises therefrom. Those same individuals, in regard to the unincluded, are devoid of both the underlying tendency to doubt and the underlying tendency to ignorance that arise therefrom. The Arahant is everywhere devoid of both the underlying tendency to doubt and the underlying tendency to ignorance.

(Kha) yo vā pana yato avijjānusayena niranusayo so tato vicikicchānusayena niranusayoti? Āmantā.

(Kha) Or again, is an individual who is devoid of the underlying tendency to ignorance that arises from a certain sphere also devoid of the underlying tendency to doubt that arises from that sphere? Yes.

126. (Ka) yo yato bhavarāgānusayena niranusayo so tato avijjānusayena niranusayoti?

126. (Ka) Is an individual who is devoid of the underlying tendency to craving for existence that arises from a certain sphere also devoid of the underlying tendency to ignorance that arises from that sphere?

Cattāro puggalā kāmadhātuyā tīsu vedanāsu te tato bhavarāgānusayena niranusayā, no ca te tato avijjānusayena niranusayā. Teva puggalā apariyāpanne te tato bhavarāgānusayena ca niranusayā avijjānusayena ca niranusayā. Arahā sabbattha bhavarāgānusayena ca niranusayo avijjānusayena ca niranusayo.

Four individuals, in the sense-sphere realm and in the three feelings, are devoid of the underlying tendency to craving for existence that arises therefrom, but they are not devoid of the underlying tendency to ignorance that arises therefrom. Those same individuals, in regard to the unincluded, are devoid of both the underlying tendency to craving for existence and the underlying tendency to ignorance that arise therefrom. The Arahant is everywhere devoid of both the underlying tendency to craving for existence and the underlying tendency to ignorance.

(Kha) yo vā pana yato avijjānusayena niranusayo [M 2.0141] so tato bhavarāgānusayena niranusayoti? Āmantā. (Ekamūlakaṃ)

(Kha) Or again, is an individual who is devoid of the underlying tendency to ignorance that arises from a certain sphere also devoid of the underlying tendency to craving for existence that arises from that sphere? Yes. (Single-Root Section)

127. (Ka) yo yato kāmarāgānusayena ca paṭighānusayena ca niranusayo so tato mānānusayena niranusayoti?

127. (Ka) Is an individual who is devoid of the underlying tendencies to sensual lust and aversion that arise from a certain sphere also devoid of the underlying tendency to conceit that arises from that sphere?

Tayo puggalā rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā te tato kāmarāgānusayena ca paṭighānusayena ca niranusayā, no ca te tato mānānusayena niranusayā. Teva puggalā apariyāpanne te tato kāmarāgānusayena ca paṭighānusayena ca niranusayā mānānusayena ca niranusayā. Anāgāmī kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā so tato kāmarāgānusayena ca paṭighānusayena ca niranusayo, no ca so tato mānānusayena ca niranusayo. Sveva puggalo dukkhāya vedanāya apariyāpanne so tato kāmarāgānusayena ca paṭighānusayena ca niranusayo mānānusayena ca niranusayo. Arahā sabbattha [T 1.0550] kāmarāgānusayena ca paṭighānusayena ca niranusayo mānānusayena ca niranusayo.

Three individuals, in the form realm and the formless realm, are devoid of the underlying tendencies to sensual lust and aversion that arise therefrom, but they are not devoid of the underlying tendency to conceit that arises therefrom. Those same individuals, in regard to the unincluded, are devoid of the underlying tendencies to sensual lust, aversion, and conceit that arise therefrom. The non-returner—in the sense-sphere realm, with respect to the two feelings, in the form realm, and in the formless realm—is devoid of the underlying tendencies to sensual lust and aversion that arise therefrom, but is not devoid of the underlying tendency to conceit that arises therefrom. That same individual, with respect to painful feeling and in regard to the unincluded, is devoid of the underlying tendencies to sensual lust, aversion, and conceit that arise therefrom. The Arahant is everywhere devoid of the underlying tendencies to sensual lust, aversion, and conceit.

(Kha) yo [V 2.0183] vā pana yato mānānusayena niranusayo so tato kāmarāgānusayena ca paṭighānusayena ca niranusayoti?

(Kha) Or again, is an individual who is devoid of the underlying tendency to conceit that arises from a certain sphere also devoid of the underlying tendencies to sensual lust and aversion that arise from that sphere?

Tayo puggalā dukkhāya vedanāya te tato mānānusayena ca kāmarāgānusayena ca niranusayā, no ca te tato paṭighānusayena niranusayā. Teva puggalā apariyāpanne te tato mānānusayena ca niranusayā kāmarāgānusayena ca paṭighānusayena ca niranusayā. Arahā sabbattha mānānusayena ca niranusayo kāmarāgānusayena ca paṭighānusayena ca niranusayo.

Three individuals, with respect to painful feeling, are devoid of the underlying tendencies to conceit and sensual lust that arise therefrom, but they are not devoid of the underlying tendency to aversion that arises therefrom. Those same individuals, in regard to the unincluded, are devoid of the underlying tendencies to conceit, sensual lust, and aversion that arise therefrom. The Arahant is everywhere devoid of the underlying tendencies to conceit, sensual lust, and aversion.

Yo yato kāmarāgānusayena ca paṭighānusayena ca niranusayo so tato diṭṭhānusayena…pe… vicikicchānusayena niranusayoti?

Is an individual who is devoid of the underlying tendencies to sensual lust and aversion that arise from a certain sphere also devoid of the underlying tendency to views... up to... the underlying tendency to doubt that arises from that sphere?

Puthujjano rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā so tato kāmarāgānusayena ca paṭighānusayena ca niranusayo, no ca so tato vicikicchānusayena niranusayo. Sveva puggalo apariyāpanne so tato kāmarāgānusayena ca paṭighānusayena ca niranusayo vicikicchānusayena ca niranusayo. Dve puggalā sabbattha kāmarāgānusayena ca paṭighānusayena ca niranusayā vicikicchānusayena ca niranusayā.

An ordinary person, in the form realm and the formless realm, is devoid of the underlying tendencies to sensual lust and aversion that arise therefrom, but is not devoid of the underlying tendency to doubt that arises therefrom. That same individual, in regard to the unincluded, is devoid of the underlying tendencies to sensual lust, aversion, and doubt that arise therefrom. Two individuals are everywhere devoid of the underlying tendencies to sensual lust, aversion, and doubt.

Yo vā pana yato vicikicchānusayena niranusayo so [M 2.0142] tato kāmarāgānusayena ca paṭighānusayena ca niranusayoti?

Or again, is an individual who is devoid of the underlying tendency to doubt that arises from a certain sphere also devoid of the underlying tendencies to sensual lust and aversion that arise from that sphere?

Dve puggalā dukkhāya vedanāya te tato vicikicchānusayena ca kāmarāgānusayena ca niranusayā, no ca te tato paṭighānusayena niranusayā. Teva puggalā kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu te tato vicikicchānusayena ca paṭighānusayena ca niranusayā, no [T 1.0551] ca te tato kāmarāgānusayena niranusayā. Teva puggalā rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā apariyāpanne te tato vicikicchānusayena ca niranusayā kāmarāgānusayena ca paṭighānusayena ca niranusayā. Dve puggalā sabbattha vicikicchānusayena ca niranusayā kāmarāgānusayena ca paṭighānusayena ca niranusayā.

Two individuals, with respect to painful feeling, are devoid of the underlying tendencies to doubt and sensual lust that arise therefrom, but they are not devoid of the underlying tendency to aversion that arises therefrom. Those same individuals, in the sense-sphere realm and with respect to the two feelings, are devoid of the underlying tendencies to doubt and aversion that arise therefrom, but they are not devoid of the underlying tendency to sensual lust that arises therefrom. Those same individuals, in the form realm, the formless realm, and in regard to the unincluded, are devoid of the underlying tendencies to doubt, sensual lust, and aversion that arise therefrom. Two individuals are everywhere devoid of the underlying tendencies to doubt, sensual lust, and aversion.

(Ka) yo [V 2.0184] yato kāmarāgānusayena ca paṭighānusayena ca niranusayo so tato bhavarāgānusayena niranusayoti?

Is a person who is without the latent tendencies of sensual lust and aversion in regard to a certain sphere thereby without the latent tendency of craving for existence in regard to it?

Tayo puggalā rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā te tato kāmarāgānusayena ca paṭighānusayena ca niranusayā, no ca te tato bhavarāgānusayena niranusayā. Teva puggalā apariyāpanne te tato kāmarāgānusayena ca paṭighānusayena ca niranusayā bhavarāgānusayena ca niranusayā. Anāgāmī rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā so tato kāmarāgānusayena ca paṭighānusayena ca niranusayo, no ca so tato bhavarāgānusayena niranusayo. Sveva puggalo kāmadhātuyā tīsu vedanāsu apariyāpanne so tato kāmarāgānusayena ca paṭighānusayena ca niranusayo bhavarāgānusayena ca niranusayo. Arahā sabbattha kāmarāgānusayena ca paṭighānusayena ca niranusayo bhavarāgānusayena ca niranusayo.

Three persons, in the form realm and the formless realm, are without the latent tendencies of sensual lust and aversion in regard to that, but they are not without the latent tendency of craving for existence in regard to that. Those same persons, in the unincluded, are without the latent tendencies of sensual lust and aversion, and are without the latent tendency of craving for existence in regard to that. A non-returner, in the form realm and the formless realm, is without the latent tendencies of sensual lust and aversion in regard to that, but is not without the latent tendency of craving for existence in regard to that. That same person, in the sense-sphere realm, with respect to the three feelings, and in the unincluded, is without the latent tendencies of sensual lust and aversion, and is without the latent tendency of craving for existence in regard to that. The Arahant is everywhere without the latent tendencies of sensual lust and aversion, and is without the latent tendency of craving for existence.

(Kha) yo vā pana yato bhavarāgānusayena niranusayo so tato kāmarāgānusayena ca paṭighānusayena ca niranusayoti?

Or again, is a person who is without the latent tendency of craving for existence in regard to a certain sphere thereby without the latent tendencies of sensual lust and aversion in regard to it?

Tayo puggalā dukkhāya vedanāya te tato bhavarāgānusayena ca kāmarāgānusayena ca niranusayā, no ca te tato paṭighānusayena niranusayā. Teva puggalā kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu te tato bhavarāgānusayena ca paṭighānusayena [T 1.0552] ca niranusayā, no ca te tato kāmarāgānusayena niranusayā. Teva puggalā apariyāpanne te tato bhavarāgānusayena ca niranusayā kāmarāgānusayena ca paṭighānusayena ca niranusayā[M 2.0143]. Arahā sabbattha bhavarāgānusayena niranusayo kāmarāgānusayena ca paṭighānusayena ca niranusayo.

Three persons, with respect to painful feeling, are without the latent tendencies of craving for existence and sensual lust in regard to that, but they are not without the latent tendency of aversion in regard to that. Those same persons, in the sense-sphere realm with respect to two feelings, are without the latent tendencies of craving for existence and aversion in regard to that, but they are not without the latent tendency of sensual lust in regard to that. Those same persons, in the unincluded, are without the latent tendency of craving for existence, and are without the latent tendencies of sensual lust and aversion in regard to that. The Arahant is everywhere without the latent tendency of craving for existence, and is without the latent tendencies of sensual lust and aversion.

(Ka) yo yato kāmarāgānusayena ca paṭighānusayena ca niranusayo so tato avijjānusayena niranusayoti?

Is a person who is without the latent tendencies of sensual lust and aversion in regard to a certain sphere thereby without the latent tendency of ignorance in regard to that sphere?

Tayo puggalā rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā te tato kāmarāgānusayena ca paṭighānusayena ca niranusayā, no ca te tato avijjānusayena niranusayā. Teva puggalā apariyāpanne te tato kāmarāgānusayena ca paṭighānusayena ca niranusayā avijjānusayena ca niranusayā. Anāgāmī kāmadhātuyā [V 2.0185] tīsu vedanāsu rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā so tato kāmarāgānusayena ca paṭighānusayena ca niranusayo, no ca so tato avijjānusayena niranusayo. Sveva puggalo apariyāpanne so tato kāmarāgānusayena ca paṭighānusayena ca niranusayo avijjānusayena ca niranusayo. Arahā sabbattha kāmarāgānusayena ca paṭighānusayena ca niranusayo avijjānusayena ca niranusayo.

Three persons, in the form realm and the formless realm, are without the latent tendencies of sensual lust and aversion in regard to that, but they are not without the latent tendency of ignorance in regard to that. Those same persons, in the unincluded, are without the latent tendencies of sensual lust and aversion, and are without the latent tendency of ignorance in regard to that. A non-returner—in the sense-sphere realm with respect to the three feelings, and in the form and formless realms—is without the latent tendencies of sensual lust and aversion in regard to that, but is not without the latent tendency of ignorance in regard to that. That same person, in the unincluded, is without the latent tendencies of sensual lust and aversion, and is without the latent tendency of ignorance in regard to that. The Arahant is everywhere without the latent tendencies of sensual lust and aversion, and is without the latent tendency of ignorance.

(Kha) yo vā pana yato avijjānusayena niranusayo so tato kāmarāgānusayena ca paṭighānusayena ca niranusayoti? Āmantā. (Dukamūlakaṃ)

Or again, is a person who is without the latent tendency of ignorance in regard to a certain sphere thereby without the latent tendencies of sensual lust and aversion in regard to that sphere? Yes.

128. Yo yato kāmarāgānusayena ca paṭighānusayena ca mānānusayena ca niranusayo so tato diṭṭhānusayena…pe… vicikicchānusayena niranusayoti? Āmantā.

128. Is a person who is without the latent tendencies of sensual lust, aversion, and conceit in regard to a certain sphere thereby without the latent tendency of views… up to… the latent tendency of doubt in regard to that sphere? Yes.

Yo vā pana yato vicikicchānusayena niranusayo so [T 1.0553] tato kāmarāgānusayena ca paṭighānusayena ca mānānusayena ca niranusayoti?

But is a person who is without the latent tendency of doubt in regard to a certain sphere thereby without the latent tendencies of sensual lust, aversion, and conceit in regard to that sphere?

Dve puggalā dukkhāya vedanāya te tato vicikicchānusayena ca kāmarāgānusayena ca mānānusayena ca niranusayā, no ca te tato paṭighānusayena niranusayā. Teva puggalā kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu te tato vicikicchānusayena ca paṭighānusayena ca niranusayā, no ca te tato kāmarāgānusayena ca mānānusayena ca niranusayā. Teva puggalā rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā te tato vicikicchānusayena ca kāmarāgānusayena ca paṭighānusayena ca niranusayā, no ca te tato mānānusayena niranusayā. Teva puggalā apariyāpanne te tato vicikicchānusayena ca niranusayā kāmarāgānusayena [M 2.0144] ca paṭighānusayena ca mānānusayena ca niranusayā. Anāgāmī kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā so tato vicikicchānusayena ca kāmarāgānusayena ca paṭighānusayena ca niranusayo, no ca so tato mānānusayena niranusayo. Sveva puggalo dukkhāya vedanāya apariyāpanne so [V 2.0186] tato vicikicchānusayena ca niranusayo kāmarāgānusayena ca paṭighānusayena ca mānānusayena ca niranusayo. Arahā sabbattha vicikicchānusayena ca niranusayo kāmarāgānusayena ca paṭighānusayena ca mānānusayena ca niranusayo.

Two persons, with respect to painful feeling, are without the latent tendencies of doubt, sensual lust, and conceit in regard to that, but they are not without the latent tendency of aversion in regard to that. Those same persons, in the sense-sphere realm with respect to two feelings, are without the latent tendencies of doubt and aversion in regard to that, but they are not without the latent tendencies of sensual lust and conceit in regard to that. Those same persons, in the form realm and the formless realm, are without the latent tendencies of doubt, sensual lust, and aversion in regard to that, but they are not without the latent tendency of conceit in regard to that. Those same persons, in the unincluded, are without the latent tendency of doubt, and are without the latent tendencies of sensual lust, aversion, and conceit in regard to that. The non-returner, in the sense-sphere realm with respect to two feelings, in the form realm, and in the formless realm, is without the latent tendencies of doubt, sensual lust, and aversion in regard to that, but he is not without the latent tendency of conceit in regard to that. That same person, with respect to painful feeling and the unincluded, is without the latent tendency of doubt, and is without the latent tendencies of sensual lust, aversion, and conceit in regard to that. The Arahant is everywhere without the latent tendency of doubt, and is without the latent tendencies of sensual lust, aversion, and conceit.

(Ka) yo yato kāmarāgānusayena ca paṭighānusayena ca mānānusayena ca niranusayo so tato bhavarāgānusayena niranusayoti? Āmantā.

Is a person who is without the latent tendencies of sensual lust, aversion, and conceit in regard to a certain sphere thereby without the latent tendency of craving for existence in regard to that sphere? Yes.

(Kha) yo vā pana yato bhavarāgānusayena niranusayo so tato kāmarāgānusayena [T 1.0554] ca paṭighānusayena ca mānānusayena ca niranusayoti?

But is a person who is without the latent tendency of craving for existence in regard to a certain sphere thereby without the latent tendencies of sensual lust, aversion, and conceit in regard to that sphere?

Tayo puggalā dukkhāya vedanāya te tato bhavarāgānusayena ca kāmarāgānusayena ca mānānusayena ca niranusayā, no ca te tato paṭighānusayena niranusayā. Teva puggalā kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu te tato bhavarāgānusayena ca paṭighānusayena ca niranusayā, no ca te tato kāmarāgānusayena ca mānānusayena ca niranusayā. Teva puggalā apariyāpanne te tato bhavarāgānusayena ca niranusayā kāmarāgānusayena ca paṭighānusayena ca mānānusayena ca niranusayā. Anāgāmī kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu so tato bhavarāgānusayena ca kāmarāgānusayena ca paṭighānusayena ca niranusayo, no ca so tato mānānusayena niranusayo. Sveva puggalo dukkhāya vedanāya apariyāpanne so tato bhavarāgānusayena ca niranusayo kāmarāgānusayena ca paṭighānusayena ca mānānusayena ca niranusayo. Arahā sabbattha bhavarāgānusayena ca niranusayo kāmarāgānusayena ca paṭighānusayena ca mānānusayena ca niranusayo.

Three persons, with respect to painful feeling, are without the latent tendencies of craving for existence, sensual lust, and conceit that arise therefrom, but they are not without the latent tendency of aversion that arises therefrom. Those same persons, in the sense-sphere realm with respect to two feelings, are without the latent tendencies of craving for existence and aversion that arise therefrom, but they are not without the latent tendencies of sensual lust and conceit that arise therefrom. Those same persons, in the unincluded, are without the latent tendencies of craving for existence, sensual lust, aversion, and conceit that arise therefrom. The non-returner, in the sense-sphere realm with respect to two feelings, is without the latent tendencies of sensual lust and aversion that arise therefrom, but he is not without the latent tendency of conceit that arises therefrom. That same person, with respect to painful feeling and in the unincluded, is without the latent tendencies of craving for existence, sensual lust, aversion, and conceit that arise therefrom. The Arahant is everywhere without the latent tendencies of craving for existence, sensual lust, aversion, and conceit.

(Ka) yo yato kāmarāgānusayena ca paṭighānusayena ca mānānusayena ca niranusayo so tato avijjānusayena niranusayoti?

Is a person who, in regard to a certain sphere, is without the latent tendencies of sensual lust, aversion, and conceit, also without the latent tendency of ignorance in regard to that sphere?

Anāgāmī [M 2.0145] dukkhāya vedanāya so tato kāmarāgānusayena ca paṭighānusayena ca mānānusayena ca niranusayo, no ca so tato avijjānusayena niranusayo. Sveva puggalo apariyāpanne so tato kāmarāgānusayena [V 2.0187] ca paṭighānusayena ca mānānusayena ca niranusayo avijjānusayena [T 1.0555] ca niranusayo. Arahā sabbattha kāmarāgānusayena ca paṭighānusayena ca mānānusayena ca niranusayo avijjānusayena ca niranusayo.

A non-returner, with respect to painful feeling, is without the latent tendencies of sensual lust, aversion, and conceit that arise therefrom, but he is not without the latent tendency of ignorance that arises therefrom. That same person, in the unincluded, is without the latent tendencies of sensual lust, aversion, and conceit that arise therefrom, and is also without the latent tendency of ignorance. An Arahant, everywhere, is without the latent tendencies of sensual lust, aversion, and conceit, and is also without the latent tendency of ignorance.

(Kha) yo vā pana yato avijjānusayena niranusayo so tato kāmarāgānusayena ca paṭighānusayena ca mānānusayena ca niranusayoti? Āmantā. (Tikamūlakaṃ)

Or else, is a person who, in regard to a certain sphere, is without the latent tendency of ignorance, also without the latent tendencies of sensual lust, aversion, and conceit in regard to that sphere? Yes.

129. (Ka) yo yato kāmarāgānusayena ca paṭighānusayena ca mānānusayena ca diṭṭhānusayena ca niranusayo so tato vicikicchānusayena niranusayoti? Āmantā.

129. Is a person who, in regard to a certain sphere, is without the latent tendencies of sensual lust, aversion, conceit, and views, also without the latent tendency of doubt in regard to that sphere? Yes.

(Kha) yo vā pana yato vicikicchānusayena niranusayo so tato kāmarāgānusayena ca paṭighānusayena ca mānānusayena ca diṭṭhānusayena ca niranusayoti?

Or else, is a person who, in regard to a certain sphere, is without the latent tendency of doubt, also without the latent tendencies of sensual lust, aversion, conceit, and views in regard to that sphere?

Dve puggalā dukkhāya vedanāya te tato vicikicchānusayena ca kāmarāgānusayena ca mānānusayena ca diṭṭhānusayena ca niranusayā, no ca te tato paṭighānusayena niranusayā. Teva puggalā kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu te tato vicikicchānusayena ca paṭighānusayena ca diṭṭhānusayena ca niranusayā, no ca te tato kāmarāgānusayena ca mānānusayena ca niranusayā. Teva puggalā rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā te tato vicikicchānusayena ca kāmarāgānusayena ca paṭighānusayena ca diṭṭhānusayena ca niranusayā, no ca te tato mānānusayena niranusayā. Teva puggalā apariyāpanne te tato vicikicchānusayena ca niranusayā kāmarāgānusayena ca paṭighānusayena ca mānānusayena ca diṭṭhānusayena ca niranusayā. Anāgāmī kāmadhātuyā [T 1.0556] dvīsu vedanāsu rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā so tato vicikicchānusayena ca kāmarāgānusayena ca paṭighānusayena ca diṭṭhānusayena ca niranusayo, no ca so tato mānānusayena niranusayo. Sveva puggalo dukkhāya vedanāya apariyāpanne so tato vicikicchānusayena ca niranusayo kāmarāgānusayena ca paṭighānusayena [V 2.0188] ca mānānusayena ca diṭṭhānusayena ca niranusayo. Arahā sabbattha vicikicchānusayena ca niranusayo kāmarāgānusayena [M 2.0146] ca paṭighānusayena ca mānānusayena ca diṭṭhānusayena ca niranusayo …pe….

Two persons, with respect to painful feeling, are without the latent tendencies of doubt, sensual lust, conceit, and views that arise therefrom, but they are not without the latent tendency of aversion that arises therefrom. Those same persons, in the sense-sphere realm with respect to two feelings, are without the latent tendencies of doubt, aversion, and views that arise therefrom, but they are not without the latent tendencies of sensual lust and conceit that arise therefrom. Those same persons, in the form-sphere realm and the formless-sphere realm, are without the latent tendencies of doubt, sensual lust, aversion, and views that arise therefrom, but they are not without the latent tendency of conceit that arise therefrom. Those same persons, in the unincluded, are without the latent tendencies of doubt, sensual lust, aversion, conceit, and views that arise therefrom. A non-returner, in the sense-sphere realm, with respect to two feelings, in the form-sphere realm, and in the formless-sphere realm, is without the latent tendencies of doubt, sensual lust, aversion, and views that arise therefrom, but is not without the latent tendency of conceit that arises therefrom. That same person, with respect to painful feeling and in the unincluded, is without the latent tendencies of doubt, sensual lust, aversion, conceit, and views that arise therefrom. An Arahant, everywhere, is without the latent tendencies of doubt, sensual lust, aversion, conceit, and views... and so on...

130. (Ka) yo yato kāmarāgānusayena ca paṭighānusayena ca mānānusayena ca diṭṭhānusayena ca vicikicchānusayena ca niranusayo so tato bhavarāgānusayena niranusayoti? Āmantā.

130. Is a person who, in regard to a certain sphere, is without the latent tendencies of sensual lust, aversion, conceit, views, and doubt, also without the latent tendency of craving for existence in regard to that sphere? Yes.

(Kha) yo vā pana yato bhavarāgānusayena niranusayo so tato kāmarāgānusayena ca paṭighānusayena ca mānānusayena ca diṭṭhānusayena ca vicikicchānusayena ca niranusayoti?

Or else, is a person who, in regard to a certain sphere, is without the latent tendency of craving for existence, also without the latent tendencies of sensual lust, aversion, conceit, views, and doubt in regard to that sphere?

Puthujjano dukkhāya vedanāya so tato bhavarāgānusayena ca kāmarāgānusayena ca mānānusayena ca niranusayo, no ca so tato paṭighānusayena ca diṭṭhānusayena ca vicikicchānusayena ca niranusayo. Sveva puggalo kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu so tato bhavarāgānusayena ca paṭighānusayena ca niranusayo, no ca so tato kāmarāgānusayena ca mānānusayena ca diṭṭhānusayena ca vicikicchānusayena ca niranusayo. Sveva puggalo apariyāpanne so tato bhavarāgānusayena ca niranusayo kāmarāgānusayena [T 1.0557] ca paṭighānusayena ca mānānusayena ca diṭṭhānusayena ca vicikicchānusayena ca niranusayo. Dve puggalā dukkhāya vedanāya te tato bhavarāgānusayena ca kāmarāgānusayena ca mānānusayena ca diṭṭhānusayena ca vicikicchānusayena ca niranusayā, no ca te tato paṭighānusayena niranusayā. Teva puggalā kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu te tato bhavarāgānusayena ca paṭighānusayena ca diṭṭhānusayena ca vicikicchānusayena ca niranusayā, no ca te tato kāmarāgānusayena ca mānānusayena ca niranusayā. Teva puggalā apariyāpanne te tato bhavarāgānusayena ca niranusayā kāmarāgānusayena ca paṭighānusayena ca mānānusayena ca diṭṭhānusayena ca vicikicchānusayena ca niranusayā. Anāgāmī [V 2.0189] kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu so tato bhavarāgānusayena ca kāmarāgānusayena ca paṭighānusayena ca diṭṭhānusayena ca vicikicchānusayena ca niranusayo, no ca so tato mānānusayena niranusayo. Sveva puggalo dukkhāya vedanāya ariyāpanne so tato bhavarāgānusayena ca niranusayo kāmarāgānusayena ca paṭighānusayena ca mānānusayena ca diṭṭhānusayena ca vicikicchānusayena [M 2.0147] ca niranusayo. Arahā sabbattha bhavarāgānusayena ca niranusayo kāmarāgānusayena ca paṭighānusayena ca mānānusayena ca diṭṭhānusayena ca vicikicchānusayena ca niranusayo.

A worldling, in regard to painful feeling, is free from the underlying tendency to lust for becoming, sensual lust, and conceit, but is not free from the underlying tendency to aversion, views, and doubt. That same person, in regard to two feelings in the sense-sphere, is free from the underlying tendency to lust for becoming and aversion, but is not free from the underlying tendency to sensual lust, conceit, views, and doubt. That same person, in regard to the unincluded, is free from the underlying tendencies to lust for becoming, sensual lust, aversion, conceit, views, and doubt. Two persons, in regard to painful feeling, are free from the underlying tendencies to lust for becoming, sensual lust, conceit, views, and doubt, but they are not free from the underlying tendency to aversion. Those same persons, in regard to two feelings in the sense-sphere, are free from the underlying tendencies to lust for becoming, aversion, views, and doubt, but they are not free from the underlying tendencies to sensual lust and conceit. Those same persons, in regard to the unincluded, are free from the underlying tendencies to lust for becoming, sensual lust, aversion, conceit, views, and doubt. A non-returner, in regard to two feelings in the sense-sphere, is free from the underlying tendencies to lust for becoming, sensual lust, aversion, views, and doubt, but is not free from the underlying tendency to conceit. That same person, in regard to painful feeling and the unincluded, is free from the underlying tendencies to lust for becoming, sensual lust, aversion, conceit, views, and doubt. An arahant is everywhere free from the underlying tendencies to lust for becoming, sensual lust, aversion, conceit, views, and doubt.

(Ka) yo yato kāmarāgānusayena ca paṭighānusayena ca mānānusayena ca diṭṭhānusayena ca vicikicchānusayena [T 1.0558] ca niranusayo so tato avijjānusayena niranusayoti?

Is a person who, in regard to something, is without the underlying tendencies to sensual lust, aversion, conceit, views, and doubt, also without the underlying tendency to ignorance in regard to it?

Anāgāmī dukkhāya vedanāya so tato kāmarāgānusayena ca paṭighānusayena ca mānānusayena ca diṭṭhānusayena ca vicikicchānusayena ca niranusayo, no ca so tato avijjānusayena niranusayo. Sveva puggalo apariyāpanne so tato kāmarāgānusayena ca paṭighānusayena ca mānānusayena ca diṭṭhānusayena ca vicikicchānusayena ca niranusayo avijjānusayena ca niranusayo. Arahā sabbattha kāmarāgānusayena ca paṭighānusayena ca mānānusayena ca diṭṭhānusayena ca vicikicchānusayena ca niranusayo avijjānusayena ca niranusayo.

A non-returner, in regard to painful feeling, is free from the underlying tendencies to sensual lust, aversion, conceit, views, and doubt, but is not free from the underlying tendency to ignorance. That same person, in regard to the unincluded, is free from the underlying tendencies to sensual lust, aversion, conceit, views, and doubt, and also from the underlying tendency to ignorance. An arahant is everywhere free from the underlying tendencies to sensual lust, aversion, conceit, views, and doubt, and also from the underlying tendency to ignorance.

(Kha) yo vā pana yato avijjānusayena niranusayo so tato kāmarāgānusayena ca paṭighānusayena ca mānānusayena ca diṭṭhānusayena ca vicikicchānusayena ca niranusayoti? Āmantā. (Pañcakamūlakaṃ)

Or again, is a person who, in regard to something, is without the underlying tendency to ignorance, also without the underlying tendencies to sensual lust, aversion, conceit, views, and doubt in regard to it? Yes.

131. (Ka) yo yato kāmarāgānusayena ca paṭighānusayena ca mānānusayena ca diṭṭhānusayena ca vicikicchānusayena ca bhavarāgānusayena ca niranusayo so tato avijjānusayena niranusayoti?

131. Is a person who, in regard to something, is without the underlying tendencies to sensual lust, aversion, conceit, views, doubt, and lust for becoming, also without the underlying tendency to ignorance in regard to it?

Anāgāmī dukkhāya vedanāya so tato kāmarāgānusayena ca paṭighānusayena [V 2.0190] ca mānānusayena ca diṭṭhānusayena ca vicikicchānusayena ca bhavarāgānusayena ca niranusayo, no ca so tato avijjānusayena niranusayo. Sveva puggalo apariyāpanne so tato kāmarāgānusayena ca paṭighānusayena ca mānānusayena ca diṭṭhānusayena ca vicikicchānusayena ca bhavarāgānusayena ca niranusayo avijjānusayena ca niranusayo. Arahā sabbattha kāmarāgānusayena [T 1.0559] ca paṭighānusayena ca mānānusayena ca diṭṭhānusayena ca vicikicchānusayena ca bhavarāgānusayena ca niranusayo avijjānusayena ca niranusayo.

A non-returner, in regard to painful feeling, is free from the underlying tendencies to sensual lust, aversion, conceit, views, doubt, and lust for becoming, but is not free from the underlying tendency to ignorance. That same person, in regard to the unincluded, is free from the underlying tendencies to sensual lust, aversion, conceit, views, doubt, and lust for becoming, and also from the underlying tendency to ignorance. An arahant is everywhere free from the underlying tendencies to sensual lust, aversion, conceit, views, doubt, and lust for becoming, and also from the underlying tendency to ignorance.

(Kha) yo vā pana yato avijjānusayena niranusayo so tato kāmarāgānusayena ca paṭighānusayena ca mānānusayena ca diṭṭhānusayena ca [M 2.0148] vicikicchānusayena ca bhavarāgānusayena ca niranusayoti? Āmantā. (Chakkamūlakaṃ)

Or again, is a person who, in regard to something, is without the underlying tendency to ignorance, also without the underlying tendencies to sensual lust, aversion, conceit, views, doubt, and lust for becoming in regard to it? Yes.

Sānusayavāre paṭilomaṃ.

The Reverse Section in the Chapter on Latent Tendencies.

Sānusayavāro.

The Chapter on Latent Tendencies.

3. Pajahanavāro

The Section on Abandoning

(Ka) anulomapuggalo

(Ka) The Positive Person

132. (Ka) yo kāmarāgānusayaṃ pajahati so paṭighānusayaṃ pajahatīti? Āmantā.

3. (a) Does a person who is abandoning the underlying tendency to sensual lust also abandon the underlying tendency to aversion? Yes.

(Kha) yo vā pana paṭighānusayaṃ pajahati so kāmarāgānusayaṃ pajahatīti? Āmantā.

(b) Or, does a person who is abandoning the underlying tendency to aversion also abandon the underlying tendency to sensual lust? Yes.

(Ka) yo kāmarāgānusayaṃ pajahati so mānānusayaṃ pajahatīti?

132. (a) Does a person who is abandoning the underlying tendency to sensual lust also abandon the underlying tendency to conceit?

Tadekaṭṭhaṃ pajahati.

One partially abandons it.

(Kha) yo [V 2.0191] vā pana mānānusayaṃ pajahati so kāmarāgānusayaṃ pajahatīti? No.

(b) Or, does a person who is abandoning the underlying tendency to conceit also abandon the underlying tendency to sensual lust? No.

Yo kāmarāgānusayaṃ pajahati so diṭṭhānusayaṃ…pe… vicikicchānusayaṃ pajahatīti? No.

Does a person who is abandoning the underlying tendency to sensual lust also abandon the underlying tendency to views… the underlying tendency to doubt? No.

Yo vā pana vicikicchānusayaṃ pajahati so kāmarāgānusayaṃ pajahatīti?

Or, does a person who is abandoning the underlying tendency to doubt also abandon the underlying tendency to sensual lust?

Tadekaṭṭhaṃ pajahati.

One abandons it in part.

Yo kāmarāgānusayaṃ pajahati so bhavarāgānusayaṃ…pe… avijjānusayaṃ pajahatīti?

Does a person who is abandoning the underlying tendency to sensual lust also abandon the underlying tendency to craving for existence… the underlying tendency to ignorance?

Tadekaṭṭhaṃ pajahati.

One abandons them in part.

Yo vā pana avijjānusayaṃ pajahati so kāmarāgānusayaṃ pajahatīti? No.

Or, does a person who is abandoning the underlying tendency to ignorance also abandon the underlying tendency to sensual lust? No.

Does a person who is abandoning the underlying tendency to aversion also abandon the underlying tendency to craving for existence… the underlying tendency to ignorance?

One abandons them in part.

Or, does a person who is abandoning the underlying tendency to ignorance also abandon the underlying tendency to aversion? No.

134. Yo mānānusayaṃ pajahati so diṭṭhānusayaṃ…pe… vicikicchānusayaṃ pajahatīti? No.

One abandons it in part.

Yo mānānusayaṃ pajahati so bhavarāgānusayaṃ…pe… avijjānusayaṃ pajahatīti? Āmantā.

Does a person who is abandoning the underlying tendency to conceit also abandon the underlying tendency to craving for existence… the underlying tendency to ignorance? Yes.

135. (a) Does a person who is abandoning the underlying tendency to views also abandon the underlying tendency to doubt? Yes.

(Kha) yo vā pana vicikicchānusayaṃ pajahati so diṭṭhānusayaṃ pajahatīti? Āmantā …pe….

138. (a) Does a person who is abandoning the underlying tendencies to sensual lust and aversion also abandon the underlying tendency to conceit?

Tadekaṭṭhaṃ pajahati.

One abandons it in part.

Yo [V 2.0193] kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca pajahati so diṭṭhānusayaṃ…pe… vicikicchānusayaṃ pajahatīti? No.

Or, does a person who is abandoning the underlying tendency to doubt also abandon the underlying tendencies to sensual lust and aversion?

Tadekaṭṭhaṃ pajahati.

Yo kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca pajahati so bhavarāgānusayaṃ…pe… avijjānusayaṃ pajahatīti?

139. Yo [M 2.0150] kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca pajahati so diṭṭhānusayaṃ…pe… vicikicchānusayaṃ pajahatīti? Natthi.

139. Does a person who is abandoning the underlying tendencies to sensual lust, aversion, and conceit also abandon the underlying tendency to views… the underlying tendency to doubt? This does not occur.

Yo vā pana vicikicchānusayaṃ pajahati so kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca pajahatīti?

Or, does a person who is abandoning the underlying tendency to doubt also abandon the underlying tendencies to sensual lust, aversion, and conceit?

Tadekaṭṭhaṃ pajahati.

One abandons them in part.

Yo kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca pajahati so bhavarāgānusayaṃ…pe… avijjānusayaṃ pajahatīti? Natthi.

Does a person who is abandoning the underlying tendencies to sensual lust, aversion, and conceit also abandon the underlying tendency to craving for existence… the underlying tendency to ignorance? This does not occur.

Yo vā pana avijjānusayaṃ pajahati so kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca pajahatīti?

Mānānusayaṃ pajahati. (Tikamūlakaṃ)

One is abandoning the underlying tendency to conceit. (Three-Root Section)

140. (Ka) yo kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca diṭṭhānusayañca pajahati so vicikicchānusayaṃ pajahatīti? Natthi.

140. (a) Does a person who abandons the underlying tendency to sensual desire, the underlying tendency to aversion, the underlying tendency to conceit, and the underlying tendency to views also abandon the underlying tendency to doubt? No.

(Kha) yo [V 2.0194] vā pana vicikicchānusayaṃ pajahati so kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca [T 1.0562] mānānusayañca diṭṭhānusayañca pajahatīti?

(b) Or, does a person who abandons the underlying tendency to doubt also abandon the underlying tendency to sensual desire, the underlying tendency to aversion, the underlying tendency to conceit, and the underlying tendency to views?

Diṭṭhānusayaṃ pajahati kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca tadekaṭṭhaṃ pajahati …pe…. (Catukkamūlakaṃ)

One abandons the underlying tendency to views, and in the same context, one begins to abandon the underlying tendency to sensual desire, the underlying tendency to aversion, and the underlying tendency to conceit. …pe…. (Four-Root Section)

141. Yo kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca diṭṭhānusayañca vicikicchānusayañca pajahati so bhavarāgānusayaṃ…pe… avijjānusayaṃ pajahatīti? Natthi.

141. Does a person who abandons the underlying tendency to sensual desire, the underlying tendency to aversion, the underlying tendency to conceit, the underlying tendency to views, and the underlying tendency to doubt also abandon the underlying tendency to craving for existence … the underlying tendency to ignorance? No.

Yo vā pana avijjānusayaṃ pajahati so kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca diṭṭhānusayañca vicikicchānusayañca pajahatīti?

Or, does a person who abandons the underlying tendency to ignorance also abandon the underlying tendency to sensual desire, the underlying tendency to aversion, the underlying tendency to conceit, the underlying tendency to views, and the underlying tendency to doubt?

Mānānusayaṃ pajahati. (Pañcakamūlakaṃ)

One abandons the underlying tendency to conceit. (Five-Root Section)

142. (Ka) yo kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca diṭṭhānusayañca vicikicchānusayañca bhavarāgānusayañca pajahati so avijjānusayaṃ pajahatīti? Natthi.

142. (a) Does a person who abandons the underlying tendency to sensual desire, the underlying tendency to aversion, the underlying tendency to conceit, the underlying tendency to views, the underlying tendency to doubt, and the underlying tendency to craving for existence also abandon the underlying tendency to ignorance? No.

(Kha) yo vā pana avijjānusayaṃ pajahati so kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca diṭṭhānusayañca vicikicchānusayañca bhavarāgānusayañca pajahatīti?

(b) Or, does a person who abandons the underlying tendency to ignorance also abandon the underlying tendency to sensual desire, the underlying tendency to aversion, the underlying tendency to conceit, the underlying tendency to views, the underlying tendency to doubt, and the underlying tendency to craving for existence?

Mānānusayañca bhavarāgānusayañca pajahati. (Chakkamūlakaṃ)

One abandons the underlying tendency to conceit and the underlying tendency to craving for existence. (Six-Root Section)

(Kha) anulomaokāso

(b) The Positive Opportunity

143. (Ka) yato kāmarāgānusayaṃ pajahati tato paṭighānusayaṃ pajahatīti? No.

143. (a) Where one abandons the underlying tendency to sensual desire, does one there abandon the underlying tendency to aversion? No.

(Kha) yato vā pana paṭighānusayaṃ pajahati tato kāmarāgānusayaṃ pajahatīti? No.

(b) Or, where one abandons the underlying tendency to aversion, does one there abandon the underlying tendency to sensual desire? No.

(Ka) yato [M 2.0151][V 2.0195] kāmarāgānusayaṃ pajahati tato mānānusayaṃ pajahatīti? Āmantā.

(a) Where one abandons the underlying tendency to sensual desire, does one there abandon the underlying tendency to conceit? Yes.

(Kha) yato vā pana mānānusayaṃ pajahati tato kāmarāgānusayaṃ pajahatīti?

(b) Or, where one abandons the underlying tendency to conceit, does one there abandon the underlying tendency to sensual desire?

Rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā tato mānānusayaṃ pajahati, no ca tato kāmarāgānusayaṃ pajahati. Kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu tato mānānusayañca [T 1.0563] pajahati kāmarāgānusayañca pajahati.

In the form realm and in the formless realm, one there abandons the underlying tendency to conceit, but one does not there abandon the underlying tendency to sensual desire. In the sense-sphere realm, in two feelings, one there abandons both the underlying tendency to conceit and the underlying tendency to sensual desire.

Yato kāmarāgānusayaṃ pajahati tato diṭṭhānusayaṃ…pe… vicikicchānusayaṃ pajahatīti? Āmantā.

Where one abandons the underlying tendency to sensual desire, does one there abandon the underlying tendency to views… the underlying tendency to doubt? Yes.

Yato vā pana vicikicchānusayaṃ pajahati tato kāmarāgānusayaṃ pajahatīti?

Or, where one abandons the underlying tendency to doubt, does one there abandon the underlying tendency to sensual desire?

Dukkhāya vedanāya rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā tato vicikicchānusayaṃ pajahati, no ca tato kāmarāgānusayaṃ pajahati. Kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu tato vicikicchānusayañca pajahati kāmarāgānusayañca pajahati.

With respect to painful feeling, in the form realm, and in the formless realm, one there abandons the underlying tendency to doubt, but one does not there abandon the underlying tendency to sensual desire. In the sense-sphere realm, in two feelings, one there abandons both the underlying tendency to doubt and the underlying tendency to sensual desire.

(Ka) yato kāmarāgānusayaṃ pajahati tato bhavarāgānusayaṃ pajahatīti? No.

(a) Where one abandons the underlying tendency to sensual desire, does one there abandon the underlying tendency to craving for existence? No.

(Kha) yato vā pana bhavarāgānusayaṃ pajahati tato kāmarāgānusayaṃ pajahatīti? No.

(b) Or, where one abandons the underlying tendency to craving for existence, does one there abandon the underlying tendency to sensual desire? No.

(Ka) yato kāmarāgānusayaṃ pajahati tato avijjānusayaṃ pajahatīti? Āmantā.

(a) Where one abandons the underlying tendency to sensual desire, does one there abandon the underlying tendency to ignorance? Yes.

(Kha) yato vā pana avijjānusayaṃ pajahati tato kāmarāgānusayaṃ pajahatīti?

(b) Or, where one abandons the underlying tendency to ignorance, does one there abandon the underlying tendency to sensual desire?

Dukkhāya vedanāya rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā tato avijjānusayaṃ pajahati, no ca tato kāmarāgānusayaṃ pajahati. Kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu tato avijjānusayañca pajahati kāmarāgānusayañca pajahati.

With respect to painful feeling, in the form realm, and in the formless realm, one there abandons the underlying tendency to ignorance, but one does not there abandon the underlying tendency to sensual desire. In the sense-sphere realm, in two feelings, one there abandons both the underlying tendency to ignorance and the underlying tendency to sensual desire.

144. (Ka) yato [V 2.0196] paṭighānusayaṃ pajahati tato mānānusayaṃ pajahatīti? No.

144. (a) Where one abandons the underlying tendency to aversion, does one there abandon the underlying tendency to conceit? No.

(Kha) yato vā pana mānānusayaṃ pajahati tato paṭighānusayaṃ pajahatīti? No.

(b) Or, where one abandons the underlying tendency to conceit, does one there abandon the underlying tendency to aversion? No.

Yato paṭighānusayaṃ pajahati tato diṭṭhānusayaṃ…pe… vicikicchānusayaṃ pajahatīti? Āmantā.

Where one abandons the underlying tendency to aversion, does one there abandon the underlying tendency to views… the underlying tendency to doubt? Yes.

Yato vā pana vicikicchānusayaṃ pajahati tato paṭighānusayaṃ pajahatīti?

Or, where one abandons the underlying tendency to doubt, does one there abandon the underlying tendency to aversion?

Kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā tato vicikicchānusayaṃ pajahati, no ca tato paṭighānusayaṃ pajahati[T 1.0564]. Dukkhāya vedanāya tato vicikicchānusayañca pajahati paṭighānusayañca pajahati.

In the sense-sphere realm, in two feelings, in the form realm, and in the formless realm, one there abandons the underlying tendency to doubt, but one does not there abandon the underlying tendency to aversion. With respect to painful feeling, one there abandons both the underlying tendency to doubt and the underlying tendency to aversion.

(Ka) yato [M 2.0152] paṭighānusayaṃ pajahati tato bhavarāgānusayaṃ pajahatīti? No.

(a) Where one abandons the underlying tendency to aversion, does one there abandon the underlying tendency to craving for existence? No.

(Kha) yato vā pana bhavarāgānusayaṃ pajahati tato paṭighānusayaṃ pajahatīti? No.

(b) Or, where one abandons the underlying tendency to craving for existence, does one there abandon the underlying tendency to aversion? No.

(Ka) yato paṭighānusayaṃ pajahati tato avijjānusayaṃ pajahatīti? Āmantā.

(a) Where one abandons the underlying tendency to aversion, does one there abandon the underlying tendency to ignorance? Yes.

(Kha) yato vā pana avijjānusayaṃ pajahati tato paṭighānusayaṃ pajahatīti?

(b) Or, where one abandons the underlying tendency to ignorance, does one there abandon the underlying tendency to aversion?

Kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā tato avijjānusayaṃ pajahati, no ca tato paṭighānusayaṃ pajahati. Dukkhāya vedanāya tato avijjānusayañca pajahati paṭighānusayañca pajahati.

In the sense-sphere realm, in two feelings, in the form realm, and in the formless realm, one there abandons the underlying tendency to ignorance, but one does not there abandon the underlying tendency to aversion. With respect to painful feeling, one there abandons both the underlying tendency to ignorance and the underlying tendency to aversion.

145. Yato mānānusayaṃ pajahati tato diṭṭhānusayaṃ…pe… vicikicchānusayaṃ pajahatīti? Āmantā.

145. Where one abandons the underlying tendency to conceit, does one there abandon the underlying tendency to views… the underlying tendency to doubt? Yes.

Yato vā pana vicikicchānusayaṃ pajahati tato mānānusayaṃ pajahatīti?

Or, where one abandons the underlying tendency to doubt, does one there abandon the underlying tendency to conceit?

Dukkhāya vedanāya tato vicikicchānusayaṃ pajahati, no ca tato mānānusayaṃ [V 2.0197] pajahati. Kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā tato vicikicchānusayañca pajahati mānānusayañca pajahati.

With respect to painful feeling, one there abandons the underlying tendency to doubt, but one does not there abandon the underlying tendency to conceit. In the sense-sphere realm, in two feelings, in the form realm, and in the formless realm, one there abandons both the underlying tendency to doubt and the underlying tendency to conceit.

(Ka) yato mānānusayaṃ pajahati tato bhavarāgānusayaṃ pajahatīti?

(a) Where one abandons the underlying tendency to conceit, does one there abandon the underlying tendency to craving for existence?

Kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu tato mānānusayaṃ pajahati, no ca tato bhavarāgānusayaṃ pajahati. Rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā tato mānānusayañca pajahati bhavarāgānusayañca pajahati.

In the sense-sphere realm, in two feelings, one there abandons the underlying tendency to conceit, but one does not there abandon the underlying tendency to craving for existence. In the form realm and in the formless realm, one there abandons both the underlying tendency to conceit and the underlying tendency to craving for existence.

(Kha) yato vā pana bhavarāgānusayaṃ pajahati tato mānānusayaṃ pajahatīti? Āmantā.

(B) Or again, from where one abandons the underlying tendency to lust for existence, from there does one abandon the underlying tendency to conceit? Yes.

(Ka) yato mānānusayaṃ pajahati tato avijjānusayaṃ pajahatīti? Āmantā.

(A) From where one abandons the underlying tendency to conceit, from there does one abandon the underlying tendency to ignorance? Yes.

(Kha) yato vā [T 1.0565] pana avijjānusayaṃ pajahati tato mānānusayaṃ pajahatīti?

(B) Or again, from where one abandons the underlying tendency to ignorance, from there does one abandon the underlying tendency to conceit?

Dukkhāya vedanāya tato avijjānusayaṃ pajahati, no ca tato mānānusayaṃ pajahati. Kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā tato avijjānusayañca pajahati mānānusayañca pajahati.

In regard to painful feeling, from there one abandons the underlying tendency to ignorance, but from there one does not abandon the underlying tendency to conceit. In the sensual realm in regard to two feelings, in the form realm, and in the formless realm, from there one abandons both the underlying tendency to ignorance and the underlying tendency to conceit.

146. (Ka) yato diṭṭhānusayaṃ pajahati tato vicikicchānusayaṃ pajahatīti? Āmantā.

146. (A) From where one abandons the underlying tendency to views, from there does one abandon the underlying tendency to doubt? Yes.

(Kha) yato vā pana vicikicchānusayaṃ pajahati tato diṭṭhānusayaṃ pajahatīti? Āmantā …pe….

(B) Or again, from where one abandons the underlying tendency to doubt, from there does one abandon the underlying tendency to views? Yes. …pe…

147. (Ka) yato [M 2.0153] vicikicchānusayaṃ pajahati tato bhavarāgānusayaṃ pajahatīti?

147. (A) From where one abandons the underlying tendency to doubt, from there does one abandon the underlying tendency to lust for existence?

Kāmadhātuyā tīsu vedanāsu tato vicikicchānusayaṃ pajahati, no ca tato bhavarāgānusayaṃ pajahati. Rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā tato vicikicchānusayañca pajahati bhavarāgānusayañca pajahati.

In the sensual realm in regard to the three feelings, from there one abandons the underlying tendency to doubt, but from there one does not abandon the underlying tendency to lust for existence. In the form realm and the formless realm, from there one abandons both the underlying tendency to doubt and the underlying tendency to lust for existence.

(Kha) yato vā pana bhavarāgānusayaṃ pajahati tato vicikicchānusayaṃ pajahatīti? Āmantā.

(B) Or again, from where one abandons the underlying tendency to lust for existence, from there does one abandon the underlying tendency to doubt? Yes.

(Ka) yato vicikicchānusayaṃ pajahati tato avijjānusayaṃ pajahatīti? Āmantā.

(A) From where one abandons the underlying tendency to doubt, from there does one abandon the underlying tendency to ignorance? Yes.

(Kha) yato [V 2.0198] vā pana avijjānusayaṃ pajahati tato vicikicchānusayaṃ pajahatīti? Āmantā.

(B) Or again, from where one abandons the underlying tendency to ignorance, from there does one abandon the underlying tendency to doubt? Yes.

148. (Ka) yato bhavarāgānusayaṃ pajahati tato avijjānusayaṃ pajahatīti? Āmantā.

148. (A) From where one abandons the underlying tendency to lust for existence, from there does one abandon the underlying tendency to ignorance? Yes.

(Kha) yato vā pana avijjānusayaṃ pajahati tato bhavarāgānusayaṃ pajahatīti?

(B) Or again, from where one abandons the underlying tendency to ignorance, from there does one abandon the underlying tendency to lust for existence?

Kāmadhātuyā tīsu vedanāsu tato avijjānusayaṃ pajahati no ca tato bhavarāgānusayaṃ pajahati. Rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā tato avijjānusayañca pajahati bhavarāgānusayañca pajahati. (Ekamūlakaṃ)

In the sensual realm in regard to the three feelings, from there one abandons the underlying tendency to ignorance but from there one does not abandon the underlying tendency to lust for existence. In the form realm and the formless realm, from there one abandons both the underlying tendency to ignorance and the underlying tendency to lust for existence. (The Single-Root Section)

149. (Ka) yato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca pajahati tato mānānusayaṃ [T 1.0566] pajahatīti? Natthi.

149. (A) From where one abandons the underlying tendency to sensual lust and the underlying tendency to aversion, from there does one abandon the underlying tendency to conceit? There is no case.

(Kha) yato vā pana mānānusayaṃ pajahati tato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca pajahatīti?

(B) Or again, from where one abandons the underlying tendency to conceit, from there does one abandon the underlying tendencies to sensual lust and aversion?

Rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā tato mānānusayaṃ pajahati, no ca tato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca pajahati. Kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu tato mānānusayañca kāmarāgānusayañca pajahati, no ca tato paṭighānusayaṃ pajahati.

In the form realm and the formless realm, from there one abandons the underlying tendency to conceit, but from there one does not abandon the underlying tendencies to sensual lust and aversion. In the sensual realm in regard to two feelings, from there one abandons the underlying tendency to conceit and the underlying tendency to sensual lust, but from there one does not abandon the underlying tendency to aversion.

Yato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca pajahati tato diṭṭhānusayaṃ…pe… vicikicchānusayaṃ pajahatīti? Natthi.

From where one abandons the underlying tendency to sensual lust and the underlying tendency to aversion, from there does one abandon the underlying tendency to views …pe… the underlying tendency to doubt? There is no case.

Yato vā pana vicikicchānusayaṃ pajahati tato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca pajahatīti?

Or again, from where one abandons the underlying tendency to doubt, from there does one abandon the underlying tendencies to sensual lust and aversion?

Rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā tato vicikicchānusayaṃ pajahati, no ca tato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca pajahati. Kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu tato vicikicchānusayañca kāmarāgānusayañca pajahati, no ca tato paṭighānusayaṃ pajahati. Dukkhāya vedanāya tato vicikicchānusayañca [V 2.0199] paṭighānusayañca pajahati, no ca tato kāmarāgānusayaṃ pajahati.

In the form realm and the formless realm, from there one abandons the underlying tendency to doubt, but from there one does not abandon the underlying tendencies to sensual lust and aversion. In the sensual realm in regard to two feelings, from there one abandons the underlying tendency to doubt and the underlying tendency to sensual lust, but from there one does not abandon the underlying tendency to aversion. In regard to painful feeling, from there one abandons the underlying tendency to doubt and the underlying tendency to aversion, but from there one does not abandon the underlying tendency to sensual lust.

(Ka) yato [M 2.0154] kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca pajahati tato bhavarāgānusayaṃ pajahatīti? Natthi.
