(Kha) yato vā pana avijjānusayaṃ pajahati tato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca pajahatīti?

(B) Or again, from where one abandons the underlying tendency to ignorance, from there does one abandon the underlying tendencies to sensual lust and aversion?

Rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā tato avijjānusayaṃ pajahati, no ca tato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca pajahati. Kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu tato [T 1.0567] avijjānusayañca kāmarāgānusayañca pajahati, no ca tato paṭighānusayaṃ pajahati. Dukkhāya vedanāya tato avijjānusayañca paṭighānusayañca pajahati, no ca tato kāmarāgānusayaṃ pajahati. (Dukamūlakaṃ)

In the form realm and the formless realm, from there one abandons the underlying tendency to ignorance, but from there one does not abandon the underlying tendencies to sensual lust and aversion. In the sensual realm in regard to two feelings, from there one abandons the underlying tendency to ignorance and the underlying tendency to sensual lust, but from there one does not abandon the underlying tendency to aversion. In regard to painful feeling, from there one abandons the underlying tendency to ignorance and the underlying tendency to aversion, but from there one does not abandon the underlying tendency to sensual lust. (The Pair-Root Section)

150. Yato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca pajahati tato diṭṭhānusayaṃ…pe… vicikicchānusayaṃ pajahatīti? Natthi.

150. From where one abandons the underlying tendency to sensual lust, the underlying tendency to aversion, and the underlying tendency to conceit, from there does one abandon the underlying tendency to views…pe… the underlying tendency to doubt? There is no case.

Yato vā pana vicikicchānusayaṃ pajahati tato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca pajahatīti?

Or again, from where one abandons the underlying tendency to doubt, from there does one abandon the underlying tendencies to sensual lust, aversion, and conceit?

Rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā tato vicikicchānusayañca mānānusayañca pajahati, no ca tato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca pajahati. Kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu tato vicikicchānusayañca kāmarāgānusayañca mānānusayañca pajahati, no ca tato paṭighānusayaṃ pajahati. Dukkhāya vedanāya tato vicikicchānusayañca paṭighānusayañca pajahati, no ca tato kāmarāgānusayañca mānānusayañca pajahati.

In the form realm and the formless realm, from there one abandons the underlying tendency to doubt and the underlying tendency to conceit, but from there one does not abandon the underlying tendencies to sensual lust and aversion. In the sensual realm in regard to two feelings, from there one abandons the underlying tendency to doubt, the underlying tendency to sensual lust, and the underlying tendency to conceit, but from there one does not abandon the underlying tendency to aversion. In regard to painful feeling, from there one abandons the underlying tendency to doubt and the underlying tendency to aversion, but from there one does not abandon the underlying tendencies to sensual lust and conceit.

(Ka) yato [V 2.0200] kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca pajahati tato bhavarāgānusayaṃ pajahatīti? Natthi.

(A) From where one abandons the underlying tendency to sensual lust, the underlying tendency to aversion, and the underlying tendency to conceit, from there does one abandon the underlying tendency to lust for existence? There is no case.

(Kha) yato vā pana bhavarāgānusayaṃ pajahati tato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca pajahatīti?

(B) Or again, from where one abandons the underlying tendency to lust for existence, from there does one abandon the underlying tendencies to sensual lust, aversion, and conceit?

Mānānusayaṃ pajahati.

One abandons the underlying tendency to conceit.

(Ka) yato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca pajahati tato avijjānusayaṃ pajahatīti? Natthi.

(Ka) When one abandons the underlying tendency to sensual desire, the underlying tendency to aversion, and the underlying tendency to conceit, does one then abandon the underlying tendency to ignorance? No.

(Kha) yato vā pana avijjānusayaṃ pajahati tato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca pajahatīti?

(Kha) Or when one abandons the underlying tendency to ignorance, does one then abandon the underlying tendency to sensual desire, the underlying tendency to aversion, and the underlying tendency to conceit?

Rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā tato avijjānusayañca mānānusayañca pajahati, no ca tato kāmarāgānusayañca [T 1.0568] paṭighānusayañca pajahati[M 2.0155]. Kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu tato avijjānusayañca kāmarāgānusayañca mānānusayañca pajahati, no ca tato paṭighānusayaṃ pajahati. Dukkhāya vedanāya tato avijjānusayañca paṭighānusayañca pajahati, no ca tato kāmarāgānusayañca mānānusayañca pajahati. (Tikamūlakaṃ)

In the form realm and the formless realm, one abandons the underlying tendency to ignorance and the underlying tendency to conceit, but one does not then abandon the underlying tendency to sensual desire and the underlying tendency to aversion. In the desire realm, in regard to two feelings, one abandons the underlying tendency to ignorance, the underlying tendency to sensual desire, and the underlying tendency to conceit, but one does not then abandon the underlying tendency to aversion. In regard to painful feeling, one abandons the underlying tendency to ignorance and the underlying tendency to aversion, but one does not then abandon the underlying tendency to sensual desire and the underlying tendency to conceit. (The Triad Section)

151. (Ka) yato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca diṭṭhānusayañca pajahati tato vicikicchānusayaṃ pajahatīti? Natthi.

151. (Ka) When one abandons the underlying tendency to sensual desire, the underlying tendency to aversion, the underlying tendency to conceit, and the underlying tendency to views, does one then abandon the underlying tendency to doubt? No.

(Kha) yato vā pana vicikicchānusayaṃ pajahati tato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca diṭṭhānusayañca pajahatīti?

(Kha) Or when one abandons the underlying tendency to doubt, does one then abandon the underlying tendency to sensual desire, the underlying tendency to aversion, the underlying tendency to conceit, and the underlying tendency to views?

Rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā tato vicikicchānusayañca mānānusayañca diṭṭhānusayañca pajahati, no ca tato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca pajahati. Kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu tato vicikicchānusayañca kāmarāgānusayañca mānānusayañca diṭṭhānusayañca pajahati, no ca tato paṭighānusayaṃ pajahati. Dukkhāya vedanāya tato vicikicchānusayañca paṭighānusayañca diṭṭhānusayañca pajahati, no ca tato kāmarāgānusayañca mānānusayañca pajahati …pe…. (Catukkamūlakaṃ)

In the form realm and the formless realm, one abandons the underlying tendency to doubt, the underlying tendency to conceit, and the underlying tendency to views, but one does not then abandon the underlying tendency to sensual desire and the underlying tendency to aversion. In the desire realm, in regard to two feelings, one abandons the underlying tendency to doubt, the underlying tendency to sensual desire, the underlying tendency to conceit, and the underlying tendency to views, but one does not then abandon the underlying tendency to aversion. In regard to painful feeling, one abandons the underlying tendency to doubt, the underlying tendency to aversion, and the underlying tendency to views, but one does not then abandon the underlying tendency to sensual desire and the underlying tendency to conceit. (The Tetrad Section)

152. (Ka) yato [V 2.0201] kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca diṭṭhānusayañca vicikicchānusayañca pajahati tato bhavarāgānusayaṃ pajahatīti? Natthi.

152. (Ka) When one abandons the underlying tendency to sensual desire, the underlying tendency to aversion, the underlying tendency to conceit, the underlying tendency to views, and the underlying tendency to doubt, does one then abandon the underlying tendency to craving for existence? No.

(Kha) yato vā pana bhavarāgānusayaṃ pajahati tato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca diṭṭhānusayañca vicikicchānusayañca [T 1.0569] pajahatīti?

(Kha) Or when one abandons the underlying tendency to craving for existence, does one then abandon the underlying tendency to sensual desire, the underlying tendency to aversion, the underlying tendency to conceit, the underlying tendency to views, and the underlying tendency to doubt?

Mānānusayañca diṭṭhānusayañca vicikicchānusayañca pajahati.

One abandons the underlying tendency to conceit, the underlying tendency to views, and the underlying tendency to doubt.

(Ka) yato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca diṭṭhānusayañca vicikicchānusayañca pajahati tato avijjānusayaṃ pajahatīti? Natthi.

(Ka) When one abandons the underlying tendency to sensual desire, the underlying tendency to aversion, the underlying tendency to conceit, the underlying tendency to views, and the underlying tendency to doubt, does one then abandon the underlying tendency to ignorance? No.

(Kha) yato vā pana avijjānusayaṃ pajahati tato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca diṭṭhānusayañca vicikicchānusayañca pajahatīti?

(Kha) Or when one abandons the underlying tendency to ignorance, does one then abandon the underlying tendency to sensual desire, the underlying tendency to aversion, the underlying tendency to conceit, the underlying tendency to views, and the underlying tendency to doubt?

Rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā tato avijjānusayañca mānānusayañca diṭṭhānusayañca vicikicchānusayañca pajahati, no ca tato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca pajahati. Kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu tato avijjānusayañca kāmarāgānusayañca mānānusayañca diṭṭhānusayañca vicikicchānusayañca pajahati, no ca tato paṭighānusayaṃ pajahati. Dukkhāya vedanāya [M 2.0156] tato avijjānusayañca paṭighānusayañca diṭṭhānusayañca vicikicchānusayañca pajahati, no ca tato kāmarāgānusayañca mānānusayañca pajahati. (Pañcakamūlakaṃ)

In the form realm and the formless realm, one abandons the underlying tendency to ignorance, the underlying tendency to conceit, the underlying tendency to views, and the underlying tendency to doubt, but one does not then abandon the underlying tendency to sensual desire and the underlying tendency to aversion. In the desire realm, in regard to two feelings, one abandons the underlying tendency to ignorance, the underlying tendency to sensual desire, the underlying tendency to conceit, the underlying tendency to views, and the underlying tendency to doubt, but one does not then abandon the underlying tendency to aversion. In regard to painful feeling, one abandons the underlying tendency to ignorance, the underlying tendency to aversion, the underlying tendency to views, and the underlying tendency to doubt, but one does not then abandon the underlying tendency to sensual desire and the underlying tendency to conceit. (The Pentad Section)

153. (Ka) yato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca diṭṭhānusayañca vicikicchānusayañca bhavarāgānusayañca pajahati tato avijjānusayaṃ pajahatīti? Natthi.

153. (Ka) When one abandons the underlying tendency to sensual desire, the underlying tendency to aversion, the underlying tendency to conceit, the underlying tendency to views, the underlying tendency to doubt, and the underlying tendency to craving for existence, does one then abandon the underlying tendency to ignorance? No.

(Kha) yato vā pana avijjānusayaṃ pajahati tato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca diṭṭhānusayañca vicikicchānusayañca bhavarāgānusayañca pajahatīti?

(Kha) Or when one abandons the underlying tendency to ignorance, does one then abandon the underlying tendency to sensual desire, the underlying tendency to aversion, the underlying tendency to conceit, the underlying tendency to views, the underlying tendency to doubt, and the underlying tendency to craving for existence?

Rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā tato avijjānusayañca mānānusayañca diṭṭhānusayañca vicikicchānusayañca bhavarāgānusayañca pajahati, no ca tato [V 2.0202] kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca pajahati. Kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu tato avijjānusayañca [T 1.0570] kāmarāgānusayañca mānānusayañca diṭṭhānusayañca vicikicchānusayañca pajahati, no ca tato paṭighānusayañca bhavarāgānusayañca pajahati. Dukkhāya vedanāya tato avijjānusayañca paṭighānusayañca diṭṭhānusayañca vicikicchānusayañca pajahati, no ca tato kāmarāgānusayañca mānānusayañca bhavarāgānusayañca pajahati. (Chakkamūlakaṃ)

In the form realm and the formless realm, one abandons the underlying tendency to ignorance, the underlying tendency to conceit, the underlying tendency to views, the underlying tendency to doubt, and the underlying tendency to craving for existence, but one does not then abandon the underlying tendency to sensual desire and the underlying tendency to aversion. In the desire realm, in regard to two feelings, one abandons the underlying tendency to ignorance, the underlying tendency to sensual desire, the underlying tendency to conceit, the underlying tendency to views, and the underlying tendency to doubt, but one does not then abandon the underlying tendency to aversion and the underlying tendency to craving for existence. In regard to painful feeling, one abandons the underlying tendency to ignorance, the underlying tendency to aversion, the underlying tendency to views, and the underlying tendency to doubt, but one does not then abandon the underlying tendency to sensual desire, the underlying tendency to conceit, and the underlying tendency to craving for existence. (The Hexad Section)

(Ga) anulomapuggalokāsā

(C) The Occasions for the Person in Conformity

154. (Ka) yo yato kāmarāgānusayaṃ pajahati so tato paṭighānusayaṃ pajahatīti? No.

154. Does a person who abandons the underlying tendency to sensual desire from a certain sphere, abandon the underlying tendency to aversion from that sphere? No.

(Kha) yo vā pana yato paṭighānusayaṃ pajahati so tato kāmarāgānusayaṃ pajahatīti? No.

Or, does a person who abandons the underlying tendency to aversion from a certain sphere, abandon the underlying tendency to sensual desire from that sphere? No.

(Ka) yo yato kāmarāgānusayaṃ pajahati so tato mānānusayaṃ pajahatīti?

Does a person who abandons the underlying tendency to sensual desire from a certain sphere, abandon the underlying tendency to conceit from that sphere?

Tadekaṭṭhaṃ pajahati.

He abandons that which has the same locus, but not without remainder.

(Kha) yo vā pana yato mānānusayaṃ pajahati so tato kāmarāgānusayaṃ pajahatīti? No.

Or, does a person who abandons the underlying tendency to conceit from a certain sphere, abandon the underlying tendency to sensual desire from that sphere? No.

Yo yato kāmarāgānusayaṃ pajahati so tato diṭṭhānusayaṃ…pe… vicikicchānusayaṃ pajahatīti? No.

Does a person who abandons the underlying tendency to sensual desire from a certain sphere, abandon the underlying tendency to views... the underlying tendency to doubt from that sphere? No.

Yo vā pana yato vicikicchānusayaṃ pajahati so tato kāmarāgānusayaṃ pajahatīti?

Or, does a person who abandons the underlying tendency to doubt from a certain sphere, abandon the underlying tendency to sensual desire from that sphere?

Aṭṭhamako dukkhāya vedanāya rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā so tato vicikicchānusayaṃ pajahati, no ca so tato kāmarāgānusayaṃ pajahati. Sveva puggalo [M 2.0157] kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu so tato vicikicchānusayaṃ pajahati kāmarāgānusayaṃ tadekaṭṭhaṃ pajahati.

The eighth person, in painful feeling, the form element, and the formless element, from that sphere abandons the underlying tendency to doubt, but from that sphere does not abandon the underlying tendency to sensual lust. That same person, in the sense-desire element and in the two feelings, from that sphere abandons the underlying tendency to doubt and partially abandons the underlying tendency to sensual lust, which has the same locus.

(Ka) yo [V 2.0203] yato kāmarāgānusayaṃ pajahati so tato bhavarāgānusayaṃ pajahatīti? No.

Does a person who abandons the underlying tendency to sensual lust from a certain sphere, abandon the underlying tendency to craving for existence from that sphere? No.

(Kha) yo vā pana yato bhavarāgānusayaṃ pajahati so tato kāmarāgānusayaṃ pajahatīti? No.

Or, does a person who abandons the underlying tendency to craving for existence from a certain sphere, abandon the underlying tendency to sensual lust from that sphere? No.

(Ka) yo yato kāmarāgānusayaṃ pajahati so tato avijjānusayaṃ pajahatīti?

Does a person who abandons the underlying tendency to sensual lust from a certain sphere, abandon the underlying tendency to ignorance from that sphere?

Tadekaṭṭhaṃ pajahati.

He partially abandons that which has the same locus.

(Kha) yo vā pana yato [T 1.0571] avijjānusayaṃ pajahati so tato kāmarāgānusayaṃ pajahatīti? No.

Or, does a person who abandons the underlying tendency to ignorance from a certain sphere, abandon the underlying tendency to sensual lust from that sphere? No.

155. (Ka) yo yato paṭighānusayaṃ pajahati so tato mānānusayaṃ pajahatīti? No.

155. Does a person who abandons the underlying tendency to aversion from a certain sphere, abandon the underlying tendency to conceit from that sphere? No.

(Kha) yo vā pana yato mānānusayaṃ pajahati so tato paṭighānusayaṃ pajahatīti? No.

Or, does a person who abandons the underlying tendency to conceit from a certain sphere, abandon the underlying tendency to aversion from that sphere? No.

Yo yato paṭighānusayaṃ pajahati so tato diṭṭhānusayaṃ…pe… vicikicchānusayaṃ pajahatīti? No.

Does a person who abandons the underlying tendency to aversion from a certain sphere, abandon the underlying tendency to views... the underlying tendency to doubt from that sphere? No.

Yo vā pana yato vicikicchānusayaṃ pajahati so tato paṭighānusayaṃ pajahatīti?

Or, does a person who abandons the underlying tendency to doubt from a certain sphere, abandon the underlying tendency to aversion from that sphere?

Aṭṭhamako kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā so tato vicikicchānusayaṃ pajahati, no ca so tato paṭighānusayaṃ pajahati. Sveva puggalo dukkhāya vedanāya so tato vicikicchānusayaṃ pajahati paṭighānusayaṃ tadekaṭṭhaṃ pajahati.

The eighth person, in the sense-desire element, in the two feelings, the form element, and the formless element, from that sphere abandons the underlying tendency to doubt, but from that sphere does not abandon the underlying tendency to aversion. That same person, in painful feeling, from that sphere abandons the underlying tendency to doubt and partially abandons the underlying tendency to aversion, which has the same locus.

(Ka) yo yato paṭighānusayaṃ pajahati so tato bhavarāgānusayaṃ pajahatīti? No.

Does a person who abandons the underlying tendency to aversion from a certain sphere, abandon the underlying tendency to craving for existence from that sphere? No.

(Kha) yo vā pana yato bhavarāgānusayaṃ pajahati so tato paṭighānusayaṃ pajahatīti? No.

Or, does a person who abandons the underlying tendency to craving for existence from a certain sphere, abandon the underlying tendency to aversion from that sphere? No.

(Ka) yo yato paṭighānusayaṃ pajahati so tato avijjānusayaṃ pajahatīti?

Does a person who abandons the underlying tendency to aversion from a certain sphere, abandon the underlying tendency to ignorance from that sphere?

Tadekaṭṭhaṃ pajahati.

He partially abandons that which has the same locus.

(Kha) yo vā pana yato avijjānusayaṃ pajahati so tato paṭighānusayaṃ pajahatīti? No.

Or, does a person who abandons the underlying tendency to ignorance from a certain sphere, abandon the underlying tendency to aversion from that sphere? No.

156. Yo [V 2.0204] yato mānānusayaṃ pajahati so tato diṭṭhānusayaṃ…pe… vicikicchānusayaṃ pajahatīti? No.

156. Does a person who abandons the underlying tendency to conceit from a certain sphere, abandon the underlying tendency to views... the underlying tendency to doubt from that sphere? No.

Yo vā pana yato vicikicchānusayaṃ pajahati so tato mānānusayaṃ pajahatīti?

Or, does a person who abandons the underlying tendency to doubt from a certain sphere, abandon the underlying tendency to conceit from that sphere?

Aṭṭhamako dukkhāya vedanāya so tato vicikicchānusayaṃ pajahati, no [M 2.0158] ca so tato mānānusayaṃ pajahati. Sveva puggalo kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā [T 1.0572] so tato vicikicchānusayaṃ pajahati mānānusayaṃ tadekaṭṭhaṃ pajahati.

The eighth person, in painful feeling, from that sphere abandons the underlying tendency to doubt, but from that sphere does not abandon the underlying tendency to conceit. That same person, in the sense-desire element, in the two feelings, the form element, and the formless element, from that sphere abandons the underlying tendency to doubt and partially abandons the underlying tendency to conceit, which has the same locus.

(Ka) yo yato mānānusayaṃ pajahati so tato bhavarāgānusayaṃ pajahatīti?

Does a person who abandons the underlying tendency to conceit from a certain sphere, abandon the underlying tendency to craving for existence from that sphere?

Aggamaggasamaṅgī kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu so tato mānānusayaṃ pajahati, no ca so tato bhavarāgānusayaṃ pajahati. Sveva puggalo rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā so tato mānānusayañca pajahati bhavarāgānusayañca pajahati.

One endowed with the highest path, in the sense-desire element and in the two feelings, from that sphere abandons the underlying tendency to conceit, but from that sphere does not abandon the underlying tendency to craving for existence. That same person, in the form element and the formless element, from that sphere abandons both the underlying tendency to conceit and the underlying tendency to craving for existence.

(Kha) yo vā pana yato bhavarāgānusayaṃ pajahati so tato mānānusayaṃ pajahatīti? Āmantā.

Or, does a person who abandons the underlying tendency to craving for existence from a certain sphere, abandon the underlying tendency to conceit from that sphere? Yes.

(Ka) yo yato mānānusayaṃ pajahati so tato avijjānusayaṃ pajahatīti? Āmantā.

(Ka) Does a person who abandons the underlying tendency to conceit from a certain sphere, abandon the underlying tendency to ignorance from that sphere? Yes.

(Kha) yo vā pana yato avijjānusayaṃ pajahati so tato mānānusayaṃ pajahatīti?

(Kha) Or, does a person who abandons the underlying tendency to ignorance from a certain sphere, abandon the underlying tendency to conceit from that sphere?

Aggamaggasamaṅgī dukkhāya vedanāya so tato avijjānusayaṃ pajahati, no ca so tato mānānusayaṃ pajahati. Sveva puggalo kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā so tato avijjānusayañca pajahati mānānusayañca pajahati.

One endowed with the highest path, in painful feeling, from that sphere abandons the underlying tendency to ignorance, but from that sphere does not abandon the underlying tendency to conceit. That same person, in the sense-desire element, in the two feelings, the form element, and the formless element, from that sphere abandons both the underlying tendency to ignorance and the underlying tendency to conceit.

157. (Ka) yo yato diṭṭhānusayaṃ pajahati so tato vicikicchānusayaṃ pajahatīti? Āmantā.

157. (Ka) Does a person who abandons the underlying tendency to views from a certain sphere, abandon the underlying tendency to doubt from that sphere? Yes.

(Kha) yo [V 2.0205] vā pana yato vicikicchānusayaṃ pajahati so tato diṭṭhānusayaṃ pajahatīti? Āmantā…pe….

(Kha) Or, does a person who abandons the underlying tendency to doubt from a certain sphere, abandon the underlying tendency to views from that sphere? Yes. …pe….

158. (Ka) yo yato vicikicchānusayaṃ pajahati so tato bhavarāgānusayaṃ pajahatīti?

158. (Ka) Does a person who abandons the underlying tendency to doubt from a certain sphere, abandon the underlying tendency to craving for existence from that sphere?

Aṭṭhamako kāmadhātuyā tīsu vedanāsu so tato vicikicchānusayaṃ pajahati, no ca so tato bhavarāgānusayaṃ pajahati. Sveva puggalo rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā so tato vicikicchānusayaṃ pajahati bhavarāgānusayaṃ [T 1.0573] tadekaṭṭhaṃ pajahati.

The eighth person, in the sense-desire element and in the three feelings, from that sphere abandons the underlying tendency to doubt, but from that sphere does not abandon the underlying tendency to craving for existence. That same person, in the form element and the formless element, from that sphere abandons the underlying tendency to doubt and partially abandons the underlying tendency to craving for existence, which has the same locus.

(Kha) yo vā pana yato bhavarāgānusayaṃ pajahati so tato vicikicchānusayaṃ pajahatīti? No.

(Kha) Or, does a person who abandons the underlying tendency to craving for existence from a certain sphere, abandon the underlying tendency to doubt from that sphere? No.

(Ka) yo yato vicikicchānusayaṃ pajahati so tato avijjānusayaṃ pajahatīti?

(Ka) Whoever abandons the latent tendency of doubt in a certain respect, does he abandon the latent tendency of ignorance in that same respect?

Tadekaṭṭhaṃ pajahati.

He abandons them on the same basis.

(Kha) yo vā pana yato avijjānusayaṃ pajahati so tato vicikicchānusayaṃ pajahatīti? No.

(Kha) Or conversely, whoever abandons the latent tendency of ignorance in a certain respect, does he abandon the latent tendency of doubt in that same respect? No.

159. (Ka) yo [M 2.0159] yato bhavarāgānusayaṃ pajahati so tato avijjānusayaṃ pajahatīti? Āmantā.

(Ka) Does a person who abandons the underlying tendency to craving for existence from a certain sphere, abandon the underlying tendency to ignorance from that sphere? Yes.

(Kha) yo vā pana yato avijjānusayaṃ pajahati so tato bhavarāgānusayaṃ pajahatīti?

(Kha) Or, does a person who abandons the underlying tendency to ignorance from a certain sphere, abandon the underlying tendency to craving for existence from that sphere?

Aggamaggasamaṅgī kāmadhātuyā tīsu vedanāsu so tato avijjānusayaṃ pajahati, no ca so tato bhavarāgānusayaṃ pajahati. Sveva puggalo rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā so tato avijjānusayañca pajahati bhavarāgānusayañca pajahati. (Ekamūlakaṃ)

One endowed with the highest path, in the sense-desire element and in the three feelings, from that sphere abandons the underlying tendency to ignorance, but from that sphere does not abandon the underlying tendency to craving for existence. That same person, in the form element and the formless element, from that sphere abandons both the underlying tendency to ignorance and the underlying tendency to craving for existence. (Ekamūlaka)

160. (Ka) yo yato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca pajahati so tato mānānusayaṃ pajahatīti? Natthi.

159. (Ka) Does a person who abandons both the underlying tendency to sensual lust and the underlying tendency to aversion from a certain sphere, abandon the underlying tendency to conceit from that sphere? There is no such case.

(Kha) yo [V 2.0206] vā pana yato mānānusayaṃ pajahati so tato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca pajahatīti? No.

(Kha) Or, does a person who abandons the underlying tendency to conceit from a certain sphere, abandon both the underlying tendency to sensual lust and the underlying tendency to aversion from that sphere? No.

Yo yato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca pajahati so tato diṭṭhānusayaṃ…pe… vicikicchānusayaṃ pajahatīti? Natthi.

Wherever a person abandons the latent tendency of sensual desire and the latent tendency of aversion, does he from that sphere abandon the latent tendency of views …pe… the latent tendency of doubt? There is no such case.

Yo vā pana yato vicikicchānusayaṃ pajahati so tato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca pajahatīti?

Or again, wherever a person abandons the latent tendency of doubt, does he there abandon the latent tendency of sensual desire and the latent tendency of aversion?

Aṭṭhamako rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā so tato vicikicchānusayaṃ pajahati, no ca so tato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca pajahati. Sveva puggalo kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu so tato vicikicchānusayaṃ pajahati kāmarāgānusayaṃ tadekaṭṭhaṃ pajahati, no ca so tato paṭighānusayaṃ pajahati. Sveva puggalo dukkhāya vedanāya so tato vicikicchānusayaṃ pajahati paṭighānusayaṃ tadekaṭṭhaṃ pajahati, no ca so [T 1.0574] tato kāmarāgānusayaṃ pajahati.

The eighth person, in the form-sphere and the formless-sphere, from that sphere abandons the latent tendency of doubt, but from that sphere does not abandon the latent tendency of sensual desire and the latent tendency of aversion. That same person, in the sense-sphere in regard to the two feelings, from that sphere abandons the latent tendency of doubt, and makes a mere abandoning of the latent tendency of sensual desire that has a common basis with it, but does not abandon it without remainder; however, from that sphere he does not abandon the latent tendency of aversion. That same person, in regard to painful feeling, from that sphere abandons the latent tendency of doubt, and makes a mere abandoning of the latent tendency of aversion that has a common basis with it, but does not abandon it without remainder; however, from that sphere he does not abandon the latent tendency of sensual desire.

(Ka) yo yato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca pajahati so tato bhavarāgānusayaṃ pajahatīti? Natthi.

(A) Wherever a person abandons the latent tendency of sensual desire and the latent tendency of aversion, does he there abandon the latent tendency of craving for existence? There is no such case.

(Kha) yo vā pana yato bhavarāgānusayaṃ pajahati so tato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca pajahatīti? No.

(B) Or again, wherever a person abandons the latent tendency of craving for existence, does he there abandon the latent tendency of sensual desire and the latent tendency of aversion? No.

(Ka) yo yato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca pajahati so tato avijjānusayaṃ pajahatīti? Natthi.

(A) Wherever a person abandons the latent tendency of sensual desire and the latent tendency of aversion, does he there abandon the latent tendency of ignorance? There is no such case.

(Kha) yo vā pana yato avijjānusayaṃ pajahati so tato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca pajahatīti? No. (Dukamūlakaṃ)

(B) Or again, wherever a person abandons the latent tendency of ignorance, does he there abandon the latent tendency of sensual desire and the latent tendency of aversion? No. (Section on Double Roots)

161. Yo [M 2.0160] yato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca pajahati so tato diṭṭhānusayaṃ…pe… vicikicchānusayaṃ pajahatīti? Natthi.

161. Wherever a person abandons the latent tendency of sensual desire, the latent tendency of aversion, and the latent tendency of conceit, does he from that sphere abandon the latent tendency of views …pe… the latent tendency of doubt? There is no such case.

Yo vā pana yato vicikicchānusayaṃ pajahati so tato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca pajahatīti?

Or again, wherever a person abandons the latent tendency of doubt, does he there abandon the latent tendency of sensual desire, the latent tendency of aversion, and the latent tendency of conceit?

Aṭṭhamako [V 2.0207] rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā so tato vicikicchānusayaṃ pajahati mānānusayaṃ tadekaṭṭhaṃ pajahati, no ca so tato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca pajahati. Sveva puggalo kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu so tato vicikicchānusayaṃ pajahati kāmarāgānusayañca mānānusayañca tadekaṭṭhaṃ pajahati, no ca so tato paṭighānusayaṃ pajahati. Sveva puggalo dukkhāya vedanāya so tato vicikicchānusayaṃ pajahati paṭighānusayaṃ tadekaṭṭhaṃ pajahati, no ca so tato kāmarāgānusayañca mānānusayañca pajahati.

The eighth person, in the form-sphere and the formless-sphere, from that sphere abandons the latent tendency of doubt, and makes a mere abandoning of the latent tendency of conceit that has a common basis with it, but does not abandon it without remainder; however, from that sphere he does not abandon the latent tendency of sensual desire and the latent tendency of aversion. That same person, in the sense-sphere in regard to the two feelings, from that sphere abandons the latent tendency of doubt, and makes a mere abandoning of both the latent tendency of sensual desire and the latent tendency of conceit that have a common basis with it, but does not abandon them without remainder; however, from that sphere he does not abandon the latent tendency of aversion. That same person, in regard to painful feeling, from that sphere abandons the latent tendency of doubt, and makes a mere abandoning of the latent tendency of aversion that has a common basis with it, but does not abandon it without remainder; however, from that sphere he does not abandon the latent tendency of sensual desire and the latent tendency of conceit.

(Ka) yo yato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca pajahati so tato bhavarāgānusayaṃ pajahatīti? Natthi.

(A) Wherever a person abandons the latent tendency of sensual desire, the latent tendency of aversion, and the latent tendency of conceit, does he there abandon the latent tendency of craving for existence? There is no such case.

(Kha) yo vā pana yato [T 1.0575] bhavarāgānusayaṃ pajahati so tato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca pajahatīti?

(B) Or again, wherever a person abandons the latent tendency of craving for existence, does he there abandon the latent tendency of sensual desire, the latent tendency of aversion, and the latent tendency of conceit?

Mānānusayaṃ pajahati.

He abandons the latent tendency of conceit.

(Ka) yo yato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca pajahati so tato avijjānusayaṃ pajahatīti? Natthi.

(A) Wherever a person abandons the latent tendency of sensual desire, the latent tendency of aversion, and the latent tendency of conceit, does he there abandon the latent tendency of ignorance? There is no such case.

(Kha) yo vā pana yato avijjānusayaṃ pajahati so tato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca pajahatīti?

(B) Or again, wherever a person abandons the latent tendency of ignorance, does he there abandon the latent tendency of sensual desire, the latent tendency of aversion, and the latent tendency of conceit?

Aggamaggasamaṅgī dukkhāya vedanāya so tato avijjānusayaṃ pajahati, no ca so tato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca pajahati. Sveva puggalo kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā so tato avijjānusayañca mānānusayañca pajahati, no ca so tato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca pajahati. (Tikamūlakaṃ)

One endowed with the supreme path, in regard to painful feeling, from that sphere abandons the latent tendency of ignorance, but from that sphere does not abandon the latent tendencies of sensual desire, aversion, and conceit. That same person, in the sense-sphere in regard to the two feelings, and in the form-sphere and the formless-sphere, from that sphere abandons the latent tendency of ignorance and the latent tendency of conceit, but from that sphere does not abandon the latent tendency of sensual desire and the latent tendency of aversion. (Section on Triple Roots)

162. (Ka) yo yato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca diṭṭhānusayañca pajahati so tato vicikicchānusayaṃ pajahatīti? Natthi.

162. (A) Wherever a person abandons the latent tendency of sensual desire, the latent tendency of aversion, the latent tendency of conceit, and the latent tendency of views, does he from that sphere abandon the latent tendency of doubt? There is no such case.

(Kha) yo [V 2.0208] vā pana yato vicikicchānusayaṃ pajahati so tato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca diṭṭhānusayañca pajahatīti?

(B) Or again, wherever a person abandons the latent tendency of doubt, does he there abandon the latent tendency of sensual desire, the latent tendency of aversion, the latent tendency of conceit, and the latent tendency of views?

Aṭṭhamako rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā so tato vicikicchānusayañca diṭṭhānusayañca [M 2.0161] pajahati mānānusayaṃ tadekaṭṭhaṃ pajahati, no ca so tato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca pajahati. Sveva puggalo kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu so tato vicikicchānusayañca diṭṭhānusayañca pajahati kāmarāgānusayañca mānānusayañca tadekaṭṭhaṃ pajahati, no ca so tato [T 1.0576] paṭighānusayaṃ pajahati. Sveva puggalo dukkhāya vedanāya so tato vicikicchānusayañca diṭṭhānusayañca pajahati paṭighānusayaṃ tadekaṭṭhaṃ pajahati, no ca so tato kāmarāgānusayañca mānānusayañca pajahati…pe…. (Catukkamūlakaṃ)

The eighth person, in the form-sphere and the formless-sphere, from that sphere abandons the latent tendency of doubt and the latent tendency of views, and makes a mere abandoning of the latent tendency of conceit that has a common basis with them, but does not abandon it without remainder; however, from that sphere he does not abandon the latent tendency of sensual desire and the latent tendency of aversion. That same person, in the sense-sphere in regard to the two feelings, from that sphere abandons the latent tendency of doubt and the latent tendency of views, and makes a mere abandoning of the latent tendency of sensual desire and the latent tendency of conceit that have a common basis with them, but does not abandon them without remainder; however, from that sphere he does not abandon the latent tendency of aversion. That same person, in regard to painful feeling, from that sphere abandons the latent tendency of doubt and the latent tendency of views, and makes a mere abandoning of the latent tendency of aversion that has a common basis with them, but does not abandon it without remainder; however, from that sphere he does not abandon the latent tendency of sensual desire and the latent tendency of conceit. (Section on Fourfold Roots)

163. (Ka) yo yato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca diṭṭhānusayañca vicikicchānusayañca pajahati so tato bhavarāgānusayaṃ pajahatīti? Natthi.

163. (A) Wherever a person abandons the latent tendency of sensual desire, the latent tendency of aversion, the latent tendency of conceit, the latent tendency of views, and the latent tendency of doubt, does he there abandon the latent tendency of craving for existence? There is no such case.

(Kha) yo vā pana yato bhavarāgānusayaṃ pajahati so tato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca diṭṭhānusayañca vicikicchānusayañca pajahatīti?

(B) Or again, wherever a person abandons the latent tendency of craving for existence, does he there abandon the latent tendency of sensual desire, the latent tendency of aversion, the latent tendency of conceit, the latent tendency of views, and the latent tendency of doubt?

Mānānusayaṃ pajahati.

He abandons the latent tendency of conceit.

(Ka) yo yato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca diṭṭhānusayañca vicikicchānusayañca pajahati so tato avijjānusayaṃ pajahatīti? Natthi.

(A) Wherever a person abandons the latent tendency of sensual desire, the latent tendency of aversion, the latent tendency of conceit, the latent tendency of views, and the latent tendency of doubt, does he there abandon the latent tendency of ignorance? There is no such case.

(Kha) yo vā pana yato avijjānusayaṃ pajahati so tato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca diṭṭhānusayañca vicikicchānusayañca pajahatīti?

(b) Or again, one who abandons the underlying tendency to ignorance—does he thereby abandon the underlying tendency to sensual desire, the underlying tendency to aversion, the underlying tendency to conceit, the underlying tendency to views, and the underlying tendency to doubt?

Aggamaggasamaṅgī dukkhāya vedanāya so tato avijjānusayaṃ pajahati, no ca so tato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca diṭṭhānusayañca vicikicchānusayañca pajahati. Sveva puggalo [V 2.0209] kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā so tato avijjānusayañca mānānusayañca pajahati, no ca so tato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca diṭṭhānusayañca vicikicchānusayañca pajahati. (Pañcakamūlakaṃ)

One endowed with the supreme path, in regard to painful feeling, abandons the underlying tendency to ignorance, but he does not thereby abandon the underlying tendencies to sensual desire, aversion, conceit, views, and doubt. That same person, in regard to the two feelings in the sensual realm and in regard to the form realm and the formless realm, abandons the underlying tendency to ignorance and the underlying tendency to conceit, but he does not thereby abandon the underlying tendencies to sensual desire, aversion, views, and doubt.

164. (Ka) yo yato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca diṭṭhānusayañca vicikicchānusayañca bhavarāgānusayañca pajahati so [T 1.0577] tato avijjānusayaṃ pajahatīti? Natthi.

164. (a) One who abandons the underlying tendency to sensual desire, the underlying tendency to aversion, the underlying tendency to conceit, the underlying tendency to views, the underlying tendency to doubt, and the underlying tendency to craving for existence—does he thereby abandon the underlying tendency to ignorance? There is no such case.

(Kha) yo vā pana yato avijjānusayaṃ pajahati so tato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca diṭṭhānusayañca vicikicchānusayañca bhavarāgānusayañca pajahatīti?

(b) Or again, one who abandons the underlying tendency to ignorance—does he thereby abandon the underlying tendency to sensual desire, the underlying tendency to aversion, the underlying tendency to conceit, the underlying tendency to views, the underlying tendency to doubt, and the underlying tendency to craving for existence?

Aggamaggasamaṅgī dukkhāya vedanāya so tato avijjānusayaṃ pajahati, no ca so tato [M 2.0162] kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca diṭṭhānusayañca vicikicchānusayañca bhavarāgānusayañca pajahati. Sveva puggalo kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu so tato avijjānusayañca mānānusayañca pajahati, no ca so tato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca diṭṭhānusayañca vicikicchānusayañca bhavarāgānusayañca pajahati. Sveva puggalo rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā so tato avijjānusayañca mānānusayañca bhavarāgānusayañca pajahati, no ca so tato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca diṭṭhānusayañca vicikicchānusayañca pajahati. (Chakkamūlakaṃ)

One endowed with the supreme path, in regard to painful feeling, abandons the underlying tendency to ignorance, but he does not thereby abandon the underlying tendencies to sensual desire, aversion, conceit, views, doubt, and craving for existence. That same person, in regard to the two feelings in the sensual realm, abandons the underlying tendency to ignorance and the underlying tendency to conceit, but he does not thereby abandon the underlying tendencies to sensual desire, aversion, views, doubt, and craving for existence. That same person, in regard to the form realm and the formless realm, abandons the underlying tendency to ignorance, the underlying tendency to conceit, and the underlying tendency to craving for existence, but he does not thereby abandon the underlying tendencies to sensual desire, aversion, views, and doubt.

Pajahanavāre anulomaṃ.

Here ends the Positive Section of the Chapter on Abandoning.

3. Pajahanavāra

3. Chapter on Abandoning: Negative Section

(Gha) paṭilomapuggalo

(Gha) The Reverse Person

165. (Ka) yo [V 2.0210] kāmarāgānusayaṃ nappajahati so paṭighānusayaṃ nappajahatīti? Āmantā.

(a) One who does not abandon the underlying tendency of sensual desire, does he not abandon the underlying tendency of aversion? Yes.

(Kha) yo vā pana paṭighānusayaṃ nappajahati so kāmarāgānusayaṃ nappajahatīti? Āmantā.

165. (b) Or again, one who does not abandon the underlying tendency of aversion, does he not abandon the underlying tendency of sensual desire? Yes.

(Ka) yo kāmarāgānusayaṃ nappajahati so mānānusayaṃ nappajahatīti?

(a) One who does not abandon the underlying tendency of sensual desire, does he not abandon the underlying tendency of conceit?

Aggamaggasamaṅgī kāmarāgānusayaṃ nappajahati, no ca so mānānusayaṃ nappajahati. Dvinnaṃ maggasamaṅgīnaṃ ṭhapetvā avasesā puggalā kāmarāgānusayañca nappajahanti mānānusayañca [T 1.0578] nappajahanti.

One endowed with the supreme path is not abandoning the underlying tendency of sensual desire, but is abandoning the underlying tendency of conceit. Setting aside the two persons endowed with the path of stream-entry and the path of once-returning, the remaining persons do not abandon the underlying tendency of sensual desire and do not abandon the underlying tendency of conceit.

(Kha) yo vā pana mānānusayaṃ nappajahati so kāmarāgānusayaṃ nappajahatīti?

(b) Or again, one who does not abandon the underlying tendency of conceit, does he not abandon the underlying tendency of sensual desire?

Anāgāmimaggasamaṅgī mānānusayaṃ nappajahati, no ca so kāmarāgānusayaṃ nappajahati. Dvinnaṃ maggasamaṅgīnaṃ ṭhapetvā avasesā puggalā mānānusayañca nappajahanti kāmarāgānusayañca nappajahanti.

One endowed with the path of non-returning is not abandoning the underlying tendency of conceit, but is abandoning the underlying tendency of sensual desire. Setting aside the two persons endowed with the path of stream-entry and the path of once-returning, the remaining persons do not abandon the underlying tendency of conceit and do not abandon the underlying tendency of sensual desire.

Yo kāmarāgānusayaṃ nappajahati so diṭṭhānusayaṃ…pe… vicikicchānusayaṃ nappajahatīti?

One who does not abandon the underlying tendency of sensual desire, does he not abandon the underlying tendency of views... the underlying tendency of doubt?

Aṭṭhamako kāmarāgānusayaṃ nappajahati, no ca so vicikicchānusayaṃ nappajahati. Anāgāmimaggasamaṅgiñca aṭṭhamakañca ṭhapetvā avasesā puggalā kāmarāgānusayañca nappajahanti vicikicchānusayañca nappajahanti.

The person on the path of stream-entry is not abandoning the underlying tendency of sensual desire, but is abandoning the underlying tendency of doubt. Setting aside the person endowed with the path of non-returning and the person on the path of stream-entry, the remaining persons do not abandon the underlying tendency of sensual desire and do not abandon the underlying tendency of doubt.

Yo vā pana vicikicchānusayaṃ nappajahati so kāmarāgānusayaṃ nappajahatīti[M 2.0163]?

Or again, one who does not abandon the underlying tendency of doubt, does he not abandon the underlying tendency of sensual desire?

Anāgāmimaggasamaṅgī vicikicchānusayaṃ nappajahati, no ca so kāmarāgānusayaṃ nappajahati. Anāgāmimaggasamaṅgiñca aṭṭhamakañca ṭhapetvā avasesā puggalā vicikicchānusayañca nappajahanti kāmarāgānusayañca nappajahanti.

One endowed with the path of non-returning is not abandoning the underlying tendency of doubt, but is abandoning the underlying tendency of sensual desire. Setting aside the person endowed with the path of non-returning and the person on the path of stream-entry, the remaining persons do not abandon the underlying tendency of doubt and do not abandon the underlying tendency of sensual desire.

Yo [V 2.0211] kāmarāgānusayaṃ nappajahati so bhavarāgānusayaṃ…pe… avijjānusayaṃ nappajahatīti?

One who does not abandon the underlying tendency of sensual desire, does he not abandon the underlying tendency of craving for existence... the underlying tendency of ignorance?

Aggamaggasamaṅgī kāmarāgānusayaṃ nappajahati, no ca so avijjānusayaṃ nappajahati. Dvinnaṃ maggasamaṅgīnaṃ ṭhapetvā avasesā puggalā kāmarāgānusayañca nappajahanti avijjānusayañca nappajahanti.

One endowed with the supreme path is not abandoning the underlying tendency of sensual desire, but is abandoning the underlying tendency of ignorance. Setting aside the two persons endowed with the path of stream-entry and the path of once-returning, the remaining persons do not abandon the underlying tendency of sensual desire and do not abandon the underlying tendency of ignorance.

Yo vā pana avijjānusayaṃ nappajahati so kāmarāgānusayaṃ nappajahatīti?

Or again, one who does not abandon the underlying tendency of ignorance, does he not abandon the underlying tendency of sensual desire?

Anāgāmimaggasamaṅgī avijjānusayaṃ nappajahati, no ca so kāmarāgānusayaṃ nappajahati. Dvinnaṃ maggasamaṅgīnaṃ ṭhapetvā avasesā [T 1.0579] puggalā avijjānusayañca nappajahanti kāmarāgānusayañca nappajahanti.

One endowed with the path of non-returning is not abandoning the underlying tendency of ignorance, but is abandoning the underlying tendency of sensual desire. Setting aside the two persons endowed with the path of non-returning and the path of Arahantship, the remaining persons do not abandon the underlying tendency of ignorance and do not abandon the underlying tendency of sensual desire.

166. (Ka) yo paṭighānusayaṃ nappajahati so mānānusayaṃ nappajahatīti?

(a) One who does not abandon the underlying tendency of aversion, does he not abandon the underlying tendency of conceit?

Aggamaggasamaṅgī paṭighānusayaṃ nappajahati, no ca so mānānusayaṃ nappajahati. Dvinnaṃ maggasamaṅgīnaṃ ṭhapetvā avasesā puggalā paṭighānusayañca nappajahanti mānānusayañca nappajahanti.

166. One endowed with the supreme path is not abandoning the underlying tendency of aversion, but is abandoning the underlying tendency of conceit. Setting aside the two persons endowed with the path of stream-entry and the path of once-returning, the remaining persons do not abandon the underlying tendency of aversion and do not abandon the underlying tendency of conceit.

(Kha) yo vā pana mānānusayaṃ nappajahati so paṭighānusayaṃ nappajahatīti?

(b) Or again, one who does not abandon the underlying tendency of conceit, does he not abandon the underlying tendency of aversion?

Anāgāmimaggasamaṅgī mānānusayaṃ nappajahati, no ca so paṭighānusayaṃ nappajahati. Dvinnaṃ maggasamaṅgīnaṃ ṭhapetvā avasesā puggalā mānānusayañca nappajahanti paṭighānusayañca nappajahanti.

One endowed with the path of non-returning is not abandoning the underlying tendency of conceit, but is abandoning the underlying tendency of aversion. Setting aside the two persons endowed with the path of stream-entry and the path of once-returning, the remaining persons do not abandon the underlying tendency of conceit and do not abandon the underlying tendency of aversion.

One who does not abandon the underlying tendency of aversion, does he not abandon the underlying tendency of views... the underlying tendency of doubt?

Aṭṭhamako paṭighānusayaṃ nappajahati, no ca so vicikicchānusayaṃ nappajahati. Anāgāmimaggasamaṅgiñca aṭṭhamakañca ṭhapetvā avasesā puggalā paṭighānusayañca nappajahanti vicikicchānusayañca nappajahanti.

The person standing on the path of stream-entry does not abandon the underlying tendency of aversion, but he does abandon the underlying tendency of doubt. Setting aside the person endowed with the path of non-returning and the person standing on the path of stream-entry, the remaining persons do not abandon the underlying tendency of aversion and do not abandon the underlying tendency of doubt.
