Or again, does a person who does not abandon the underlying tendency of doubt not abandon the underlying tendency of aversion?

Anāgāmimaggasamaṅgī vicikicchānusayaṃ nappajahati, no ca so paṭighānusayaṃ nappajahati. Anāgāmimaggasamaṅgiñca aṭṭhamakañca ṭhapetvā avasesā [V 2.0212] puggalā vicikicchānusayañca nappajahanti paṭighānusayañca nappajahanti.

A person endowed with the path of non-returning does not abandon the underlying tendency of doubt, but he does abandon the underlying tendency of aversion. Setting aside the person endowed with the path of non-returning and the person standing on the path of stream-entry, the remaining persons do not abandon the underlying tendency of doubt and do not abandon the underlying tendency of aversion.

Yo paṭighānusayaṃ nappajahati so bhavarāgānusayaṃ…pe… avijjānusayaṃ nappajahatīti?

Does a person who does not abandon the underlying tendency of aversion not abandon the underlying tendency of craving for existence... and the underlying tendency of ignorance?

Aggamaggasamaṅgī paṭighānusayaṃ nappajahati, no ca so avijjānusayaṃ [T 1.0580][M 2.0164] nappajahati. Dvinnaṃ maggasamaṅgīnaṃ ṭhapetvā avasesā puggalā paṭighānusayañca nappajahanti avijjānusayañca nappajahanti.

A person endowed with the highest path does not abandon the underlying tendency of aversion, but he does abandon the underlying tendency of ignorance. Setting aside the two persons endowed with the paths of stream-entry and once-returning, the remaining persons do not abandon the underlying tendency of aversion and do not abandon the underlying tendency of ignorance.

Yo vā pana avijjānusayaṃ nappajahati so paṭighānusayaṃ nappajahatīti?

Or again, does a person who does not abandon the underlying tendency of ignorance not abandon the underlying tendency of aversion?

Anāgāmimaggasamaṅgī avijjānusayaṃ nappajahati, no ca so paṭighānusayaṃ nappajahati. Dvinnaṃ maggasamaṅgīnaṃ ṭhapetvā avasesā puggalā avijjānusayañca nappajahanti paṭighānusayañca nappajahanti.

A person endowed with the path of non-returning does not abandon the underlying tendency of ignorance, but he does abandon the underlying tendency of aversion. Setting aside the two persons endowed with the paths of non-returning and Arahantship, the remaining persons do not abandon the underlying tendency of ignorance and do not abandon the underlying tendency of aversion.

167. Yo mānānusayaṃ nappajahati so diṭṭhānusayaṃ…pe… vicikicchānusayaṃ nappajahatīti?

167. Does a person who does not abandon the underlying tendency of conceit not abandon the underlying tendency of views... and the underlying tendency of doubt?

Aṭṭhamako mānānusayaṃ nappajahati, no ca so vicikicchānusayaṃ nappajahati. Aggamaggasamaṅgiñca aṭṭhamakañca ṭhapetvā avasesā puggalā mānānusayañca nappajahanti vicikicchānusayañca nappajahanti.

The person standing on the path of stream-entry does not abandon the underlying tendency of conceit, but he does abandon the underlying tendency of doubt. Setting aside the person endowed with the highest path and the person standing on the path of stream-entry, the remaining persons do not abandon the underlying tendency of conceit and do not abandon the underlying tendency of doubt.

Yo vā pana vicikicchānusayaṃ nappajahati so mānānusayaṃ nappajahatīti?

Or again, does a person who does not abandon the underlying tendency of doubt not abandon the underlying tendency of conceit?

Aggamaggasamaṅgī vicikicchānusayaṃ nappajahati, no ca so mānānusayaṃ nappajahati. Aggamaggasamaṅgiñca aṭṭhamakañca ṭhapetvā avasesā puggalā vicikicchānusayañca nappajahanti mānānusayañca nappajahanti.

A person endowed with the highest path does not abandon the underlying tendency of doubt, but he does abandon the underlying tendency of conceit. Setting aside the person endowed with the highest path and the person standing on the path of stream-entry, the remaining persons do not abandon the underlying tendency of doubt and do not abandon the underlying tendency of conceit.

Yo [V 2.0213] mānānusayaṃ nappajahati so bhavarāgānusayaṃ…pe… avijjānusayaṃ nappajahatīti? Āmantā.

Does a person who does not abandon the underlying tendency of conceit not abandon the underlying tendency of craving for existence... and the underlying tendency of ignorance? Yes.

Yo vā pana avijjānusayaṃ nappajahati so mānānusayaṃ nappajahatīti? Āmantā.

Or again, does a person who does not abandon the underlying tendency of ignorance not abandon the underlying tendency of conceit? Yes.

168. (Ka) yo diṭṭhānusayaṃ nappajahati so vicikicchānusayaṃ nappajahatīti? Āmantā.

168. (a) Does a person who does not abandon the underlying tendency of wrong views not abandon the underlying tendency of doubt? Yes.

(Kha) yo vā pana vicikicchānusayaṃ nappajahati so diṭṭhānusayaṃ nappajahatīti? Āmantā …pe….

(b) Or again, does a person who does not abandon the underlying tendency of doubt not abandon the underlying tendency of wrong views? Yes... and so on.

169. Yo [T 1.0581] vicikicchānusayaṃ nappajahati so bhavarāgānusayaṃ…pe… avijjānusayaṃ nappajahatīti?

169. Does a person who does not abandon the underlying tendency of doubt not abandon the underlying tendency of craving for existence... and the underlying tendency of ignorance?

Aggamaggasamaṅgī vicikicchānusayaṃ nappajahati, no ca so avijjānusayaṃ nappajahati. Aggamaggasamaṅgiñca aṭṭhamakañca ṭhapetvā avasesā puggalā vicikicchānusayañca nappajahanti avijjānusayañca nappajahanti.

A person endowed with the highest path does not abandon the underlying tendency of doubt, but he does abandon the underlying tendency of ignorance. Setting aside the person endowed with the highest path and the person standing on the path of stream-entry, the remaining persons do not abandon the underlying tendency of doubt and do not abandon the underlying tendency of ignorance.

Yo vā pana avijjānusayaṃ nappajahati so vicikicchānusayaṃ nappajahatīti?

Or again, does a person who does not abandon the underlying tendency of ignorance not abandon the underlying tendency of doubt?

Aṭṭhamako avijjānusayaṃ nappajahati, no ca so vicikicchānusayaṃ nappajahati. Aggamaggasamaṅgiñca aṭṭhamakañca ṭhapetvā avasesā puggalā avijjānusayañca nappajahanti vicikicchānusayañca nappajahanti.

The person standing on the path of stream-entry does not abandon the underlying tendency of ignorance, but he does abandon the underlying tendency of doubt. Setting aside the person endowed with the highest path and the person standing on the path of stream-entry, the remaining persons do not abandon the underlying tendency of ignorance and do not abandon the underlying tendency of doubt.

170. (Ka) yo [M 2.0165] bhavarāgānusayaṃ nappajahati so avijjānusayaṃ nappajahatīti? Āmantā.

170. (a) Does a person who does not abandon the underlying tendency of craving for existence not abandon the underlying tendency of ignorance? Yes.

(Kha) yo vā pana avijjānusayaṃ nappajahati so bhavarāgānusayaṃ nappajahatīti? Āmantā. (Ekamūlakaṃ)

(b) Or again, does a person who does not abandon the underlying tendency of ignorance not abandon the underlying tendency of craving for existence? Yes. (The section on the single root)

171. (Ka) yo [V 2.0214] kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca nappajahati so mānānusayaṃ nappajahatīti?

171. (a) Does a person who does not abandon the underlying tendency of sensual lust and the underlying tendency of aversion not abandon the underlying tendency of conceit?

Aggamaggasamaṅgī kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca nappajahati, no ca so mānānusayaṃ nappajahati. Dvinnaṃ maggasamaṅgīnaṃ ṭhapetvā avasesā puggalā kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca nappajahanti mānānusayañca nappajahanti.

A person endowed with the highest path does not abandon the underlying tendency of sensual lust and the underlying tendency of aversion, but he does abandon the underlying tendency of conceit. Setting aside the two persons endowed with the paths of stream-entry and once-returning, the remaining persons do not abandon the underlying tendency of sensual lust and the underlying tendency of aversion, and do not abandon the underlying tendency of conceit.

(Kha) yo vā pana mānānusayaṃ nappajahati so kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca nappajahatīti?

(b) Or again, does a person who does not abandon the underlying tendency of conceit not abandon the underlying tendency of sensual lust and the underlying tendency of aversion?

Anāgāmimaggasamaṅgī mānānusayaṃ nappajahati, no ca so kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca nappajahati. Dvinnaṃ maggasamaṅgīnaṃ ṭhapetvā avasesā [T 1.0582] puggalā mānānusayañca nappajahanti kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca nappajahanti.

A person endowed with the path of non-returning does not abandon the underlying tendency of conceit, but he does abandon the underlying tendency of sensual lust and the underlying tendency of aversion. Setting aside the two persons endowed with the paths of non-returning and Arahantship, the remaining persons do not abandon the underlying tendency of conceit, and do not abandon the underlying tendency of sensual lust and the underlying tendency of aversion.

Yo kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca nappajahati so diṭṭhānusayaṃ…pe… vicikicchānusayaṃ nappajahatīti?

Does a person who does not abandon the underlying tendency of sensual lust and the underlying tendency of aversion not abandon the underlying tendency of wrong views... and the underlying tendency of doubt?

Aṭṭhamako kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca nappajahati, no ca so vicikicchānusayaṃ nappajahati. Anāgāmimaggasamaṅgiñca aṭṭhamakañca ṭhapetvā avasesā puggalā kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca nappajahanti vicikicchānusayañca nappajahanti.

The person standing on the path of stream-entry does not abandon the underlying tendency of sensual lust and the underlying tendency of aversion, but he does abandon the underlying tendency of doubt. Setting aside the person endowed with the path of non-returning and the person standing on the path of stream-entry, the remaining persons do not abandon the underlying tendency of sensual lust and the underlying tendency of aversion, and do not abandon the underlying tendency of doubt.

Yo vā pana vicikicchānusayaṃ nappajahati so kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca nappajahatīti?

Or again, does a person who does not abandon the underlying tendency of doubt not abandon the underlying tendency of sensual lust and the underlying tendency of aversion?

Anāgāmimaggasamaṅgī vicikicchānusayaṃ nappajahati, no ca so kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca nappajahati. Anāgāmimaggasamaṅgiñca aṭṭhamakañca ṭhapetvā avasesā puggalā vicikicchānusayañca nappajahanti kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca nappajahanti.

A person endowed with the path of non-returning does not abandon the underlying tendency of doubt, but he does abandon the underlying tendency of sensual lust and the underlying tendency of aversion. Setting aside the person endowed with the path of non-returning and the person standing on the path of stream-entry, the remaining persons do not abandon the underlying tendency of doubt, and do not abandon the underlying tendency of sensual lust and the underlying tendency of aversion.

Yo kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca nappajahati so bhavarāgānusayaṃ…pe… avijjānusayaṃ nappajahatīti?

Does a person who does not abandon the underlying tendency of sensual lust and the underlying tendency of aversion also not abandon the underlying tendency of lust for becoming... and the underlying tendency of ignorance?

Aggamaggasamaṅgī kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca nappajahati, no ca so avijjānusayaṃ nappajahati. Dvinnaṃ maggasamaṅgīnaṃ ṭhapetvā avasesā puggalā kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca nappajahanti avijjānusayañca nappajahanti.

One endowed with the highest path does not abandon the underlying tendency of sensual lust and the underlying tendency of aversion, but that person does abandon the underlying tendency of ignorance. Setting aside the two persons endowed with the path of stream-entry and the path of once-returning, the remaining persons do not abandon the underlying tendency of sensual lust and the underlying tendency of aversion, and they do not abandon the underlying tendency of ignorance.

Yo [V 2.0215] vā pana avijjānusayaṃ nappajahati so kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca nappajahatīti?

Or again, does a person who does not abandon the underlying tendency of ignorance also not abandon the underlying tendency of sensual lust and the underlying tendency of aversion?

Anāgāmimaggasamaṅgī avijjānusayaṃ nappajahati, no ca so kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca nappajahati. Dvinnaṃ maggasamaṅgīnaṃ ṭhapetvā [T 1.0583] avasesā [M 2.0166] puggalā avijjānusayañca nappajahanti kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca nappajahanti. (Dukamūlakaṃ)

One endowed with the path of non-returning does not abandon the underlying tendency of ignorance, but that person does abandon the underlying tendency of sensual lust and the underlying tendency of aversion. Setting aside the two persons endowed with the path of non-returning and the path of Arahantship, the remaining persons do not abandon the underlying tendency of ignorance, and they do not abandon the underlying tendency of sensual lust and the underlying tendency of aversion. (The Dyad Root Section)

172. Yo kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca nappajahati so diṭṭhānusayaṃ…pe… vicikicchānusayaṃ nappajahatīti?

172. Does a person who does not abandon the underlying tendency of sensual lust, the underlying tendency of aversion, and the underlying tendency of conceit also not abandon the underlying tendency of views... and the underlying tendency of doubt?

Aṭṭhamako kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca nappajahati, no ca so vicikicchānusayaṃ nappajahati. Dvinnaṃ maggasamaṅgīnañca aṭṭhamakañca ṭhapetvā avasesā puggalā kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca nappajahanti vicikicchānusayañca nappajahanti.

The person on the path of stream-entry does not abandon the underlying tendency of sensual lust, the underlying tendency of aversion, and the underlying tendency of conceit, but that person does abandon the underlying tendency of doubt. Setting aside the two persons endowed with the path of non-returning and the path of Arahantship, and the person on the path of stream-entry, the remaining persons do not abandon the underlying tendency of sensual lust, the underlying tendency of aversion, and the underlying tendency of conceit, and they do not abandon the underlying tendency of doubt.

Yo vā pana vicikicchānusayaṃ nappajahati so kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca nappajahatīti?

Or again, does a person who does not abandon the underlying tendency of doubt also not abandon the underlying tendency of sensual lust, the underlying tendency of aversion, and the underlying tendency of conceit?

Anāgāmimaggasamaṅgī vicikicchānusayañca mānānusayañca nappajahati, no ca so kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca nappajahati. Aggamaggasamaṅgī vicikicchānusayañca kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca nappajahati, no ca so mānānusayaṃ nappajahati. Dvinnaṃ maggasamaṅgīnañca aṭṭhamakañca ṭhapetvā avasesā puggalā vicikicchānusayañca nappajahanti kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca nappajahanti.

One endowed with the path of non-returning does not abandon the underlying tendency of doubt and the underlying tendency of conceit, but that person does abandon the underlying tendency of sensual lust and the underlying tendency of aversion. One endowed with the highest path does not abandon the underlying tendency of doubt, the underlying tendency of sensual lust, and the underlying tendency of aversion, but that person does abandon the underlying tendency of conceit. Setting aside the two persons endowed with the path of non-returning and the path of Arahantship, and the person on the path of stream-entry, the remaining persons do not abandon the underlying tendency of doubt, and they do not abandon the underlying tendencies of sensual lust, aversion, and conceit.

Yo kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca nappajahati so bhavarāgānusayaṃ…pe… avijjānusayaṃ nappajahatīti? Āmantā.

Does a person who does not abandon the underlying tendency of sensual lust, the underlying tendency of aversion, and the underlying tendency of conceit also not abandon the underlying tendency of lust for becoming... and the underlying tendency of ignorance? Yes.

Yo vā pana avijjānusayaṃ nappajahati so kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca nappajahatīti?

Or again, does a person who does not abandon the underlying tendency of ignorance also not abandon the underlying tendency of sensual lust, the underlying tendency of aversion, and the underlying tendency of conceit?

Anāgāmimaggasamaṅgī [V 2.0216] avijjānusayañca mānānusayañca nappajahati, no ca so [T 1.0584] kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca nappajahati. Dvinnaṃ maggasamaṅgīnaṃ ṭhapetvā avasesā puggalā avijjānusayañca nappajahanti kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca nappajahanti. (Tikamūlakaṃ)

One endowed with the path of non-returning does not abandon the underlying tendency of ignorance and the underlying tendency of conceit, but that person does abandon the underlying tendency of sensual lust and the underlying tendency of aversion. Setting aside the two persons endowed with the path of non-returning and the path of Arahantship, the remaining persons do not abandon the underlying tendency of ignorance, and they do not abandon the underlying tendencies of sensual lust, aversion, and conceit. (The Triad Root Section)

173. (Ka) yo kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca diṭṭhānusayañca nappajahati so vicikicchānusayaṃ nappajahatīti? Āmantā.

173. (a) Does a person who does not abandon the underlying tendency of sensual lust, the underlying tendency of aversion, the underlying tendency of conceit, and the underlying tendency of views also not abandon the underlying tendency of doubt? Yes.

(Kha) yo vā pana vicikicchānusayaṃ nappajahati so kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca diṭṭhānusayañca nappajahatīti?

(b) Or again, does a person who does not abandon the underlying tendency of doubt also not abandon the underlying tendency of sensual lust, the underlying tendency of aversion, the underlying tendency of conceit, and the underlying tendency of views?

Anāgāmimaggasamaṅgī vicikicchānusayañca mānānusayañca diṭṭhānusayañca nappajahati, no ca so kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca nappajahati. Aggamaggasamaṅgī vicikicchānusayañca kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca diṭṭhānusayañca nappajahati, no ca so mānānusayaṃ [M 2.0167] nappajahati. Dvinnaṃ maggasamaṅgīnañca aṭṭhamakañca ṭhapetvā avasesā puggalā vicikicchānusayañca nappajahanti kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca diṭṭhānusayañca nappajahanti …pe…. (Catukkamūlakaṃ)

One endowed with the path of non-returning does not abandon the underlying tendency of doubt, the underlying tendency of conceit, and the underlying tendency of views, but that person does abandon the underlying tendency of sensual lust and the underlying tendency of aversion. One endowed with the highest path does not abandon the underlying tendency of doubt, the underlying tendency of sensual lust, the underlying tendency of aversion, and the underlying tendency of views, but that person does abandon the underlying tendency of conceit. Setting aside the two persons endowed with the path of non-returning and the path of Arahantship, and the person on the path of stream-entry, the remaining persons do not abandon the underlying tendency of doubt, and they do not abandon the underlying tendencies of sensual lust, aversion, conceit, and views... and so on. (The Tetrad Root Section)

174. Yo kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca diṭṭhānusayañca vicikicchānusayañca nappajahati so bhavarāgānusayaṃ…pe… avijjānusayaṃ nappajahatīti? Āmantā.

174. Does a person who does not abandon the underlying tendency of sensual lust, the underlying tendency of aversion, the underlying tendency of conceit, the underlying tendency of views, and the underlying tendency of doubt also not abandon the underlying tendency of lust for becoming... and the underlying tendency of ignorance? Yes.

Yo vā pana avijjānusayaṃ nappajahati so kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca diṭṭhānusayañca vicikicchānusayañca nappajahatīti?

Or again, does a person who does not abandon the underlying tendency of ignorance also not abandon the underlying tendency of sensual lust, the underlying tendency of aversion, the underlying tendency of conceit, the underlying tendency of views, and the underlying tendency of doubt?

Aṭṭhamako avijjānusayañca kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca nappajahati, no ca so diṭṭhānusayañca [T 1.0585] vicikicchānusayañca nappajahati. Anāgāmimaggasamaṅgī avijjānusayañca mānānusayañca diṭṭhānusayañca vicikicchānusayañca nappajahati, no ca so [V 2.0217] kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca nappajahati. Dvinnaṃ maggasamaṅgīnañca aṭṭhamakañca ṭhapetvā avasesā puggalā avijjānusayañca nappajahanti kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca diṭṭhānusayañca vicikicchānusayañca nappajahanti. (Pañcakamūlakaṃ)

The person on the path of stream-entry does not abandon the underlying tendency of ignorance, the underlying tendency of sensual lust, the underlying tendency of aversion, and the underlying tendency of conceit, but that person does abandon the underlying tendency of views and the underlying tendency of doubt. One endowed with the path of non-returning does not abandon the underlying tendency of ignorance, the underlying tendency of conceit, the underlying tendency of views, and the underlying tendency of doubt, but that person does abandon the underlying tendency of sensual lust and the underlying tendency of aversion. Setting aside the two persons endowed with the path of non-returning and the path of Arahantship, and the person on the path of stream-entry, the remaining persons do not abandon the underlying tendency of ignorance, and they do not abandon the underlying tendencies of sensual lust, aversion, conceit, views, and doubt. (The Pentad Root Section)

175. (Ka) yo kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca diṭṭhānusayañca vicikicchānusayañca bhavarāgānusayañca nappajahati so avijjānusayaṃ nappajahatīti? Āmantā.

175. (a) Does a person who does not abandon the underlying tendency of sensual lust, the underlying tendency of aversion, the underlying tendency of conceit, the underlying tendency of views, the underlying tendency of doubt, and the underlying tendency of lust for becoming also not abandon the underlying tendency of ignorance? Yes.

(Kha) yo vā pana avijjānusayaṃ nappajahati so kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca diṭṭhānusayañca vicikicchānusayañca bhavarāgānusayañca nappajahatīti?

(b) Or again, does a person who does not abandon the underlying tendency of ignorance also not abandon the underlying tendency of sensual lust, the underlying tendency of aversion, the underlying tendency of conceit, the underlying tendency of views, the underlying tendency of doubt, and the underlying tendency of lust for becoming?

Aṭṭhamako avijjānusayañca kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca bhavarāgānusayañca nappajahati, no ca so diṭṭhānusayañca vicikicchānusayañca nappajahati. Anāgāmimaggasamaṅgī avijjānusayañca mānānusayañca diṭṭhānusayañca vicikicchānusayañca bhavarāgānusayañca nappajahati, no ca so kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca nappajahati. Dvinnaṃ maggasamaṅgīnañca aṭṭhamakañca ṭhapetvā avasesā puggalā avijjānusayañca nappajahanti kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca diṭṭhānusayañca vicikicchānusayañca bhavarāgānusayañca nappajahanti. (Chakkamūlakaṃ)

The eighth person does not abandon the underlying tendency to ignorance, the underlying tendency to sensual desire, the underlying tendency to aversion, the underlying tendency to conceit, and the underlying tendency to lust for becoming, but that person does abandon the underlying tendency to views and the underlying tendency to doubt. A person endowed with the non-returner path does not abandon the underlying tendency to ignorance, the underlying tendency to conceit, the underlying tendency to views, the underlying tendency to doubt, and the underlying tendency to lust for becoming, but that person does abandon the underlying tendency to sensual desire and the underlying tendency to aversion. Setting aside the two persons endowed with the paths and the eighth person, the remaining persons do not abandon the underlying tendency to ignorance, and they do not abandon the underlying tendencies to sensual desire, aversion, conceit, views, doubt, and lust for becoming.

(Ṅa) paṭilomaokāso

(Ṅa) Reversed Order

176. (Ka) yato [T 1.0586] kāmarāgānusayaṃ nappajahati tato paṭighānusayaṃ nappajahatīti?

176. Where one does not abandon the underlying tendency to sensual desire, does one there not abandon the underlying tendency to aversion?

Dukkhāya vedanāya tato kāmarāgānusayaṃ nappajahati, no ca [M 2.0168] tato paṭighānusayaṃ nappajahati. Rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā apariyāpanne tato kāmarāgānusayañca nappajahati paṭighānusayañca nappajahati.

In regard to painful feeling, one does not abandon the underlying tendency to sensual desire, but one does abandon the underlying tendency to aversion there. In the form realm, the formless realm, and in what is unincluded, one does not abandon the underlying tendency to sensual desire and one does not abandon the underlying tendency to aversion.

(Kha) yato [V 2.0218] vā pana paṭighānusayaṃ nappajahati tato kāmarāgānusayaṃ nappajahatīti?

Or again, where one does not abandon the underlying tendency to aversion, does one there not abandon the underlying tendency to sensual desire?

Kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu tato paṭighānusayaṃ nappajahati, no ca tato kāmarāgānusayaṃ nappajahati. Rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā apariyāpanne tato paṭighānusayañca nappajahati kāmarāgānusayañca nappajahati.

In the sense-sphere realm and in regard to two feelings, one does not abandon the underlying tendency to aversion, but one does abandon the underlying tendency to sensual desire there. In the form realm, the formless realm, and in what is unincluded, one does not abandon the underlying tendency to aversion and one does not abandon the underlying tendency to sensual desire.

(Ka) yato kāmarāgānusayaṃ nappajahati tato mānānusayaṃ nappajahatīti?

Where one does not abandon the underlying tendency to sensual desire, does one there not abandon the underlying tendency to conceit?

Rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā tato kāmarāgānusayaṃ nappajahati, no ca tato mānānusayaṃ nappajahati. Dukkhāya vedanāya apariyāpanne tato kāmarāgānusayañca nappajahati mānānusayañca nappajahati.

In the form realm and the formless realm, one does not abandon the underlying tendency to sensual desire, but one does abandon the underlying tendency to conceit there. In regard to painful feeling and in what is unincluded, one does not abandon the underlying tendency to sensual desire and one does not abandon the underlying tendency to conceit.

(Kha) yato vā pana mānānusayaṃ nappajahati tato kāmarāgānusayaṃ nappajahatīti? Āmantā.

Or again, where one does not abandon the underlying tendency to conceit, does one there not abandon the underlying tendency to sensual desire? Yes.

Yato kāmarāgānusayaṃ nappajahati tato diṭṭhānusayaṃ…pe… vicikicchānusayaṃ nappajahatīti?

Where one does not abandon the underlying tendency to sensual desire, does one there not abandon the underlying tendency to views … the underlying tendency to doubt?

Dukkhāya vedanāya rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā tato kāmarāgānusayaṃ nappajahati, no ca tato vicikicchānusayaṃ nappajahati. Apariyāpanne tato kāmarāgānusayañca nappajahati vicikicchānusayañca nappajahati.

In regard to painful feeling, in the form realm, and in the formless realm, one does not abandon the underlying tendency to sensual desire, but one does abandon the underlying tendency to doubt there. In what is unincluded, one does not abandon the underlying tendency to sensual desire and one does not abandon the underlying tendency to doubt.

Yato vā pana vicikicchānusayaṃ nappajahati tato kāmarāgānusayaṃ nappajahatīti? Āmantā.

Or again, where one does not abandon the underlying tendency to doubt, does one there not abandon the underlying tendency to sensual desire? Yes.

(Ka) yato kāmarāgānusayaṃ nappajahati tato bhavarāgānusayaṃ nappajahatīti?

Where one does not abandon the underlying tendency to sensual desire, does one there not abandon the underlying tendency to craving for existence?

Rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā tato kāmarāgānusayaṃ [T 1.0587] nappajahati, no ca tato bhavarāgānusayaṃ nappajahati. Dukkhāya vedanāya apariyāpanne tato kāmarāgānusayañca nappajahati bhavarāgānusayañca nappajahati.

In the form realm and the formless realm, one does not abandon the underlying tendency to sensual desire, but one does abandon the underlying tendency to craving for existence there. In regard to painful feeling and in what is unincluded, one does not abandon the underlying tendency to sensual desire and one does not abandon the underlying tendency to craving for existence.

(Kha) yato vā pana bhavarāgānusayaṃ nappajahati tato kāmarāgānusayaṃ nappajahatīti?

Or again, where one does not abandon the underlying tendency to craving for existence, does one there not abandon the underlying tendency to sensual desire?

Kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu tato bhavarāgānusayaṃ nappajahati, no ca tato kāmarāgānusayaṃ nappajahati. Dukkhāya vedanāya apariyāpanne tato bhavarāgānusayañca nappajahati kāmarāgānusayañca nappajahati.

In the sense-sphere realm and in regard to two feelings, one does not abandon the underlying tendency to craving for existence, but one does abandon the underlying tendency to sensual desire there. In regard to painful feeling and in what is unincluded, one does not abandon the underlying tendency to craving for existence and one does not abandon the underlying tendency to sensual desire.

(Ka) yato [V 2.0219] kāmarāgānusayaṃ nappajahati tato avijjānusayaṃ nappajahatīti?

Where one does not abandon the underlying tendency to sensual desire, does one there not abandon the underlying tendency to ignorance?

Dukkhāya vedanāya rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā tato kāmarāgānusayaṃ [M 2.0169] nappajahati, no ca tato avijjānusayaṃ nappajahati. Apariyāpanne tato kāmarāgānusayañca nappajahati avijjānusayañca nappajahati.

In regard to painful feeling, in the form realm, and in the formless realm, one does not abandon the underlying tendency to sensual desire, but one does abandon the underlying tendency to ignorance there. In what is unincluded, one does not abandon the underlying tendency to sensual desire and one does not abandon the underlying tendency to ignorance.

(Kha) yato vā pana avijjānusayaṃ nappajahati tato kāmarāgānusayaṃ nappajahatīti? Āmantā.

Or again, where one does not abandon the underlying tendency to ignorance, does one there not abandon the underlying tendency to sensual desire? Yes.

177. (Ka) yato paṭighānusayaṃ nappajahati tato mānānusayaṃ nappajahatīti?

177. Where one does not abandon the underlying tendency to aversion, does one there not abandon the underlying tendency to conceit?

Kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā tato paṭighānusayaṃ nappajahati, no ca tato mānānusayaṃ nappajahati. Apariyāpanne tato paṭighānusayañca nappajahati mānānusayañca nappajahati.

In the sense-sphere realm, in regard to two feelings, in the form realm, and in the formless realm, one does not abandon the underlying tendency to aversion, but one does abandon the underlying tendency to conceit there. In what is unincluded, one does not abandon the underlying tendency to aversion and one does not abandon the underlying tendency to conceit.

(Kha) yato vā pana mānānusayaṃ nappajahati tato paṭighānusayaṃ nappajahatīti?

Or again, where one does not abandon the underlying tendency to conceit, does one there not abandon the underlying tendency to aversion?

Dukkhāya vedanāya tato mānānusayaṃ nappajahati, no ca tato paṭighānusayaṃ nappajahati. Apariyāpanne tato mānānusayañca nappajahati paṭighānusayañca nappajahati.

In regard to painful feeling, one does not abandon the underlying tendency to conceit, but one does abandon the underlying tendency to aversion there. In what is unincluded, one does not abandon the underlying tendency to conceit and one does not abandon the underlying tendency to aversion.

Yato paṭighānusayaṃ nappajahati tato diṭṭhānusayaṃ…pe… vicikicchānusayaṃ [T 1.0588] nappajahatīti?

Where one does not abandon the underlying tendency to aversion, does one there not abandon the underlying tendency to views … the underlying tendency to doubt?

Kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā tato paṭighānusayaṃ nappajahati, no ca tato vicikicchānusayaṃ nappajahati. Apariyāpanne tato paṭighānusayañca nappajahati vicikicchānusayañca nappajahati.

In the sense-sphere realm, in regard to two feelings, in the form realm, and in the formless realm, one does not abandon the underlying tendency to aversion, but one does abandon the underlying tendency to doubt there. In what is unincluded, one does not abandon the underlying tendency to aversion and one does not abandon the underlying tendency to doubt.

Yato vā pana vicikicchānusayaṃ nappajahati tato paṭighānusayaṃ nappajahatīti? Āmantā.

Or again, where one does not abandon the underlying tendency to doubt, does one there not abandon the underlying tendency to aversion? Yes.

(Ka) yato paṭighānusayaṃ nappajahati tato bhavarāgānusayaṃ nappajahatīti?

Where one does not abandon the underlying tendency to aversion, does one there not abandon the underlying tendency to craving for existence?

Rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā tato paṭighānusayaṃ nappajahati, no ca tato bhavarāgānusayaṃ nappajahati. Kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu apariyāpanne tato paṭighānusayañca nappajahati bhavarāgānusayañca nappajahati.

In the form realm and the formless realm, one does not abandon the underlying tendency to aversion, but one does abandon the underlying tendency to craving for existence there. In the sense-sphere realm, in regard to two feelings, and in what is unincluded, one does not abandon the underlying tendency to aversion and one does not abandon the underlying tendency to craving for existence.

(Kha) yato [V 2.0220] vā pana bhavarāgānusayaṃ nappajahati tato paṭighānusayaṃ nappajahatīti?

Or again, where one does not abandon the underlying tendency to craving for existence, does one there not abandon the underlying tendency to aversion?

Dukkhāya vedanāya tato bhavarāgānusayaṃ nappajahati, no ca tato paṭighānusayaṃ nappajahati. Kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu apariyāpanne tato bhavarāgānusayañca nappajahati paṭighānusayañca nappajahati.

In regard to painful feeling, from there one does not abandon the underlying tendency to craving for existence, but one abandons the underlying tendency to aversion. In the sense-sphere realm, in two feelings, and in what is unincluded, from there one does not abandon the underlying tendency to craving for existence and one does not abandon the underlying tendency to aversion.

(Ka) yato paṭighānusayaṃ nappajahati tato avijjānusayaṃ nappajahatīti?

Where one does not abandon the underlying tendency to aversion, does one there not abandon the underlying tendency to ignorance?

Kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā tato paṭighānusayaṃ nappajahati, no ca tato avijjānusayaṃ nappajahati. Apariyāpanne [M 2.0170] tato paṭighānusayañca nappajahati avijjānusayañca nappajahati.

In the sense-sphere realm, in the two feelings, in the form realm, and in the formless realm, from there one does not abandon the underlying tendency to aversion, but one abandons the underlying tendency to ignorance. In what is unincluded, from there one does not abandon the underlying tendency to aversion and one does not abandon the underlying tendency to ignorance.

(Kha) yato vā pana avijjānusayaṃ nappajahati tato paṭighānusayaṃ nappajahatīti? Āmantā.

Or again, where one does not abandon the underlying tendency to ignorance, does one there not abandon the underlying tendency to aversion? Yes.

178. Yato mānānusayaṃ nappajahati tato diṭṭhānusayaṃ…pe… vicikicchānusayaṃ nappajahatīti?

178. Where one does not abandon the underlying tendency to conceit, does one there not abandon the underlying tendency to views … the underlying tendency to doubt?

Dukkhāya vedanāya tato mānānusayaṃ nappajahati[T 1.0589], no ca tato vicikicchānusayaṃ nappajahati. Apariyāpanne tato mānānusayañca nappajahati vicikicchānusayañca nappajahati. Yato vā pana vicikicchānusayaṃ nappajahati tato mānānusayaṃ nappajahatīti? Āmantā.

In regard to painful feeling, from there one does not abandon the underlying tendency to conceit, but one abandons the underlying tendency to doubt. In what is unincluded, from there one does not abandon the underlying tendency to conceit and one does not abandon the underlying tendency to doubt. Or again, where one does not abandon the underlying tendency to doubt, does one there not abandon the underlying tendency to conceit? Yes.

(Ka) yato mānānusayaṃ nappajahati tato bhavarāgānusayaṃ nappajahatīti? Āmantā.

Where one does not abandon the underlying tendency to conceit, does one there not abandon the underlying tendency to craving for existence? Yes.

(Kha) yato vā pana bhavarāgānusayaṃ nappajahati tato mānānusayaṃ nappajahatīti?

Or again, where one does not abandon the underlying tendency to craving for existence, does one there not abandon the underlying tendency to conceit?

Kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu tato bhavarāgānusayaṃ nappajahati, no ca tato mānānusayaṃ nappajahati. Dukkhāya vedanāya apariyāpanne tato bhavarāgānusayañca nappajahati mānānusayañca nappajahati.

In the sense-sphere realm and in the two feelings, from there one does not abandon the underlying tendency to craving for existence, but one abandons the underlying tendency to conceit. In regard to painful feeling and in what is unincluded, from there one does not abandon the underlying tendency to craving for existence and one does not abandon the underlying tendency to conceit.

(Ka) yato [V 2.0221] mānānusayaṃ nappajahati tato avijjānusayaṃ nappajahatīti?

Where one does not abandon the underlying tendency to conceit, does one there not abandon the underlying tendency to ignorance?

Dukkhāya vedanāya tato mānānusayaṃ nappajahati, no ca tato avijjānusayaṃ nappajahati. Apariyāpanne tato mānānusayañca nappajahati avijjānusayañca nappajahati.

In regard to painful feeling, from there one does not abandon the underlying tendency to conceit, but one abandons the underlying tendency to ignorance. In what is unincluded, from there one does not abandon the underlying tendency to conceit and one does not abandon the underlying tendency to ignorance.

(Kha) yato vā pana avijjānusayaṃ nappajahati tato mānānusayaṃ nappajahatīti? Āmantā.

Or again, where one does not abandon the underlying tendency to ignorance, does one there not abandon the underlying tendency to conceit? Yes.

179. (Ka) yato diṭṭhānusayaṃ nappajahati tato vicikicchānusayaṃ nappajahatīti? Āmantā.

179. Where one does not abandon the underlying tendency to views, does one there not abandon the underlying tendency to doubt? Yes.

(Kha) yato vā pana vicikicchānusayaṃ nappajahati tato diṭṭhānusayaṃ nappajahatīti? Āmantā.

Or again, where one does not abandon the underlying tendency to doubt, does one there not abandon the underlying tendency to views? Yes.

180. (Ka) yato vicikicchānusayaṃ nappajahati tato bhavarāgānusayaṃ nappajahatīti? Āmantā.

180. Where one does not abandon the underlying tendency to doubt, does one there not abandon the underlying tendency to craving for existence? Yes.

(Kha) yato vā pana bhavarāgānusayaṃ nappajahati tato vicikicchānusayaṃ nappajahatīti?

Or again, where one does not abandon the underlying tendency to craving for existence, does one there not abandon the underlying tendency to doubt?

Kāmadhātuyā tīsu vedanāsu tato bhavarāgānusayaṃ nappajahati, no ca tato vicikicchānusayaṃ nappajahati; apariyāpanne [T 1.0590] tato bhavarāgānusayañca nappajahati vicikicchānusayañca nappajahati.

In the sense-sphere realm and in the three feelings, from there one does not abandon the underlying tendency to craving for existence, but one abandons the underlying tendency to doubt; in what is unincluded, from there one does not abandon the underlying tendency to craving for existence and one does not abandon the underlying tendency to doubt.

(Ka) yato [M 2.0171] vicikicchānusayaṃ nappajahati tato avijjānusayaṃ nappajahatīti? Āmantā.

Where one does not abandon the underlying tendency to doubt, does one there not abandon the underlying tendency to ignorance? Yes.

(Kha) yato vā pana avijjānusayaṃ nappajahati tato vicikicchānusayaṃ nappajahatīti? Āmantā.

Or again, where one does not abandon the underlying tendency to ignorance, does one there not abandon the underlying tendency to doubt? Yes.

181. (Ka) yato bhavarāgānusayaṃ nappajahati tato avijjānusayaṃ nappajahatīti?

181. Where one does not abandon the underlying tendency to craving for existence, does one there not abandon the underlying tendency to ignorance?

Kāmadhātuyā tīsu vedanāsu tato bhavarāgānusayaṃ nappajahati, no ca tato avijjānusayaṃ nappajahati. Apariyāpanne tato bhavarāgānusayañca nappajahati avijjānusayañca nappajahati.

In the sense-sphere realm and in the three feelings, from there one does not abandon the underlying tendency to craving for existence, but one abandons the underlying tendency to ignorance. In what is unincluded, from there one does not abandon the underlying tendency to craving for existence and one does not abandon the underlying tendency to ignorance.

(Kha) yato [V 2.0222] vā pana avijjānusayaṃ nappajahati tato bhavarāgānusayaṃ nappajahatīti? Āmantā. (Ekamūlakaṃ)

Or again, where one does not abandon the underlying tendency to ignorance, does one there not abandon the underlying tendency to craving for existence? Yes. (Single-rooted.)

182. (Ka) yato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca nappajahati tato mānānusayaṃ nappajahatīti?

182. Where one does not abandon the underlying tendency to sensual desire and the underlying tendency to aversion, does one there not abandon the underlying tendency to conceit?

Rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā tato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca nappajahati, no ca tato mānānusayaṃ nappajahati. Apariyāpanne tato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca nappajahati mānānusayañca nappajahati.

In the form realm and in the formless realm, from there one does not abandon the underlying tendency to sensual desire and the underlying tendency to aversion, but one abandons the underlying tendency to conceit. In what is unincluded, from there one does not abandon the underlying tendency to sensual desire, the underlying tendency to aversion, and the underlying tendency to conceit.

(Kha) yato vā pana mānānusayaṃ nappajahati tato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca nappajahatīti?

Or again, where one does not abandon the underlying tendency to conceit, does one there not abandon the underlying tendency to sensual desire and the underlying tendency to aversion?

Dukkhāya vedanāya tato mānānusayañca kāmarāgānusayañca nappajahati, no ca tato paṭighānusayaṃ nappajahati. Apariyāpanne tato mānānusayañca nappajahati kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca nappajahati.

In regard to painful feeling, from there one does not abandon the underlying tendency to conceit and the underlying tendency to sensual desire, but one abandons the underlying tendency to aversion. In what is unincluded, from there one does not abandon the underlying tendency to conceit, the underlying tendency to sensual desire, and the underlying tendency to aversion.

Yato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca nappajahati tato diṭṭhānusayaṃ…pe… vicikicchānusayaṃ nappajahatīti?

Where one does not abandon the underlying tendency to sensual desire and the underlying tendency to aversion, does one there not abandon the underlying tendency to views … the underlying tendency to doubt?

Rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā tato kāmarāgānusayañca [T 1.0591] paṭighānusayañca nappajahati, no ca tato vicikicchānusayaṃ nappajahati. Apariyāpanne tato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca nappajahati vicikicchānusayañca nappajahati. Yato vā pana vicikicchānusayaṃ nappajahati tato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca nappajahatīti? Āmantā.

In the form realm and in the formless realm, from there one does not abandon the underlying tendency to sensual desire and the underlying tendency to aversion, but one abandons the underlying tendency to doubt. In what is unincluded, from there one does not abandon the underlying tendency to sensual desire, the underlying tendency to aversion, and the underlying tendency to doubt. Or again, where one does not abandon the underlying tendency to doubt, does one there not abandon the underlying tendency to sensual desire and the underlying tendency to aversion? Yes.

(Ka) yato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca nappajahati tato bhavarāgānusayaṃ nappajahatīti?

Where one does not abandon the underlying tendency to sensual desire and the underlying tendency to aversion, does one there not abandon the underlying tendency to craving for existence?

Rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā tato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca nappajahati, no ca tato bhavarāgānusayaṃ nappajahati. Apariyāpanne tato kāmarāgānusayañca [V 2.0223] paṭighānusayañca nappajahati bhavarāgānusayañca nappajahati.

In the form realm and in the formless realm, from there one does not abandon the underlying tendency to sensual desire and the underlying tendency to aversion, but one abandons the underlying tendency to craving for existence. In what is unincluded, from there one does not abandon the underlying tendency to sensual desire, the underlying tendency to aversion, and the underlying tendency to craving for existence.

(Kha) yato vā pana bhavarāgānusayaṃ nappajahati [M 2.0172] tato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca nappajahatīti?

Or again, where one does not abandon the underlying tendency to craving for existence, does one not abandon there the underlying tendency to sensual desire and the underlying tendency to aversion?

Dukkhāya vedanāya tato bhavarāgānusayañca kāmarāgānusayañca nappajahati, no ca tato paṭighānusayaṃ nappajahati. Kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu tato bhavarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca nappajahati, no ca tato kāmarāgānusayaṃ nappajahati. Apariyāpanne tato bhavarāgānusayañca nappajahati kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca nappajahati.

In painful feeling, from that occasion one does not abandon the underlying tendency to craving for existence and the underlying tendency to sensual desire, but one does abandon the underlying tendency to aversion. In the sense-sphere, in two feelings, from that occasion one does not abandon the underlying tendency to craving for existence and the underlying tendency to aversion, but one does abandon the underlying tendency to sensual desire. In the unincluded, from that occasion one does not abandon the underlying tendency to craving for existence, the underlying tendency to sensual desire, and the underlying tendency to aversion.

(Ka) yato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca nappajahati tato avijjānusayaṃ nappajahatīti?

Where one does not abandon the underlying tendency to sensual desire and the underlying tendency to aversion, does one not abandon there the underlying tendency to ignorance?

Rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā tato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca nappajahati, no ca tato avijjānusayaṃ nappajahati. Apariyāpanne tato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca nappajahati avijjānusayañca nappajahati.

In the form realm and the formless realm, from that occasion one does not abandon the underlying tendency to sensual desire and the underlying tendency to aversion, but one does abandon the underlying tendency to ignorance. In the unincluded, from that occasion one does not abandon the underlying tendency to sensual desire, the underlying tendency to aversion, and the underlying tendency to ignorance.

(Kha) yato vā pana avijjānusayaṃ nappajahati tato kāmarāgānusayañca [T 1.0592] paṭighānusayañca nappajahatīti? Āmantā. (Dukamūlakaṃ)

Or, where one does not abandon the underlying tendency to ignorance, does one not abandon there the underlying tendency to sensual desire and the underlying tendency to aversion? Yes. (The Dyad-Root)

183. Yato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca nappajahati tato diṭṭhānusayaṃ…pe… vicikicchānusayaṃ nappajahatīti? Āmantā.

183. Where one does not abandon the underlying tendency to sensual desire, the underlying tendency to aversion, and the underlying tendency to conceit, does one not abandon there the underlying tendency to views …pe… the underlying tendency to doubt? Yes.

Yato vā pana vicikicchānusayaṃ nappajahati tato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca nappajahatīti? Āmantā.

Or, where one does not abandon the underlying tendency to doubt, does one not abandon there the underlying tendency to sensual desire, the underlying tendency to aversion, and the underlying tendency to conceit? Yes.

(Ka) yato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca nappajahati tato bhavarāgānusayaṃ nappajahatīti? Āmantā.

Where one does not abandon the underlying tendency to sensual desire, the underlying tendency to aversion, and the underlying tendency to conceit, does one not abandon there the underlying tendency to craving for existence? Yes.

(Kha) yato vā pana bhavarāgānusayaṃ nappajahati tato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca nappajahatīti?

Or, where one does not abandon the underlying tendency to craving for existence, does one not abandon there the underlying tendency to sensual desire, the underlying tendency to aversion, and the underlying tendency to conceit?

Dukkhāya vedanāya tato bhavarāgānusayañca kāmarāgānusayañca mānānusayañca [V 2.0224] nappajahati, no ca tato paṭighānusayaṃ nappajahati. Kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu tato bhavarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca nappajahati, no ca tato kāmarāgānusayañca mānānusayañca nappajahati. Apariyāpanne tato bhavarāgānusayañca nappajahati kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca nappajahati.

In painful feeling, from that occasion one does not abandon the underlying tendency to craving for existence, the underlying tendency to sensual desire, and the underlying tendency to conceit, but one does abandon the underlying tendency to aversion. In the sense-sphere, in two feelings, from that occasion one does not abandon the underlying tendency to craving for existence and the underlying tendency to aversion, but one does abandon the underlying tendency to sensual desire and the underlying tendency to conceit. In the unincluded, from that occasion one does not abandon the underlying tendency to craving for existence, the underlying tendency to sensual desire, the underlying tendency to aversion, and the underlying tendency to conceit.

(Ka) yato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca nappajahati tato avijjānusayaṃ nappajahatīti? Āmantā.

Where one does not abandon the underlying tendency to sensual desire, the underlying tendency to aversion, and the underlying tendency to conceit, does one not abandon there the underlying tendency to ignorance? Yes.

(Kha) yato vā pana avijjānusayaṃ nappajahati tato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca nappajahatīti? Āmantā. (Tikamūlakaṃ)

Or, where one does not abandon the underlying tendency to ignorance, does one not abandon there the underlying tendency to sensual desire, the underlying tendency to aversion, and the underlying tendency to conceit? Yes. (The Triad-Root)

184. (Ka) yato [M 2.0173] kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca diṭṭhānusayañca nappajahati tato vicikicchānusayaṃ nappajahatīti? Āmantā.

184. Where one does not abandon the underlying tendency to sensual desire, the underlying tendency to aversion, the underlying tendency to conceit, and the underlying tendency to views, does one not abandon there the underlying tendency to doubt? Yes.

(Kha) yato [T 1.0593] vā pana vicikicchānusayaṃ nappajahati tato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca diṭṭhānusayañca nappajahatīti? Āmantā …pe…. (Catukkamūlakaṃ)

Or, where one does not abandon the underlying tendency to doubt, does one not abandon there the underlying tendency to sensual desire, the underlying tendency to aversion, the underlying tendency to conceit, and the underlying tendency to views? Yes. …pe… (The Tetrad-Root)

185. (Ka) yato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca diṭṭhānusayañca vicikicchānusayañca nappajahati tato bhavarāgānusayaṃ nappajahatīti? Āmantā.

185. Where one does not abandon the underlying tendency to sensual desire, the underlying tendency to aversion, the underlying tendency to conceit, the underlying tendency to views, and the underlying tendency to doubt, does one not abandon there the underlying tendency to craving for existence? Yes.

(Kha) yato vā pana bhavarāgānusayaṃ nappajahati tato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca diṭṭhānusayañca vicikicchānusayañca nappajahatīti?

Or, where one does not abandon the underlying tendency to craving for existence, does one not abandon there the underlying tendency to sensual desire, the underlying tendency to aversion, the underlying tendency to conceit, the underlying tendency to views, and the underlying tendency to doubt?

Dukkhāya vedanāya tato bhavarāgānusayañca kāmarāgānusayañca mānānusayañca nappajahati, no ca tato paṭighānusayañca diṭṭhānusayañca vicikicchānusayañca nappajahati. Kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu tato bhavarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca nappajahati, no ca tato kāmarāgānusayañca mānānusayañca diṭṭhānusayañca vicikicchānusayañca nappajahati[V 2.0225]. Apariyāpanne tato bhavarāgānusayañca nappajahati kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca diṭṭhānusayañca vicikicchānusayañca nappajahati.

In painful feeling, from that occasion one does not abandon the underlying tendency to craving for existence, the underlying tendency to sensual desire, and the underlying tendency to conceit; but one does abandon the underlying tendency to aversion, the underlying tendency to views, and the underlying tendency to doubt. In the sense-sphere, in two feelings, from that occasion one does not abandon the underlying tendency to craving for existence and the underlying tendency to aversion; but one does abandon the underlying tendency to sensual desire, the underlying tendency to conceit, the underlying tendency to views, and the underlying tendency to doubt. In the unincluded, from that occasion one does not abandon the underlying tendency to craving for existence, the underlying tendency to sensual desire, the underlying tendency to aversion, the underlying tendency to conceit, the underlying tendency to views, and the underlying tendency to doubt.

(Ka) yato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca diṭṭhānusayañca vicikicchānusayañca nappajahati tato avijjānusayaṃ nappajahatīti? Āmantā.

Where one does not abandon the underlying tendency to sensual desire, the underlying tendency to aversion, the underlying tendency to conceit, the underlying tendency to views, and the underlying tendency to doubt, does one not abandon there the underlying tendency to ignorance? Yes.

(Kha) yato vā pana avijjānusayaṃ nappajahati tato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca diṭṭhānusayañca vicikicchānusayañca nappajahatīti? Āmantā. (Pañcakamūlakaṃ)

Or, where one does not abandon the underlying tendency to ignorance, does one not abandon there the underlying tendency to sensual desire, the underlying tendency to aversion, the underlying tendency to conceit, the underlying tendency to views, and the underlying tendency to doubt? Yes. (The Pentad-Root)

186. (Ka) yato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca diṭṭhānusayañca vicikicchānusayañca bhavarāgānusayañca nappajahati tato avijjānusayaṃ [T 1.0594] nappajahatīti? Āmantā.

186. Where one does not abandon the underlying tendency to sensual desire, the underlying tendency to aversion, the underlying tendency to conceit, the underlying tendency to views, the underlying tendency to doubt, and the underlying tendency to craving for existence, does one not abandon there the underlying tendency to ignorance? Yes.

(Kha) yato vā pana avijjānusayaṃ nappajahati tato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca diṭṭhānusayañca vicikicchānusayañca bhavarāgānusayañca nappajahatīti? Āmantā. (Chakkamūlakaṃ)

Or, where one does not abandon the underlying tendency to ignorance, does one not abandon there the underlying tendency to sensual desire, the underlying tendency to aversion, the underlying tendency to conceit, the underlying tendency to views, the underlying tendency to doubt, and the underlying tendency to craving for existence? Yes. (The Hexad-Root)

(Ca) paṭilomapuggalokāsā

(Ca) Person and Sphere in Reverse Order

187. (Ka) yo yato kāmarāgānusayaṃ nappajahati so tato paṭighānusayaṃ nappajahatīti?

187. Does a person who does not abandon the underlying tendency to sensual desire from whatever sphere, from that sphere not abandon the underlying tendency to aversion?

Anāgāmimaggasamaṅgī dukkhāya vedanāya so tato [M 2.0174] kāmarāgānusayaṃ nappajahati, no ca so tato paṭighānusayaṃ nappajahati. Sveva puggalo rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā apariyāpanne so tato kāmarāgānusayañca nappajahati paṭighānusayañca nappajahati. Anāgāmimaggasamaṅgiṃ ṭhapetvā avasesā puggalā sabbattha kāmarāgānusayañca nappajahanti paṭighānusayañca nappajahanti.

A person endowed with the path of the non-returner, with respect to painful feeling, does not abandon the underlying tendency to sensual lust from that, but he does abandon the underlying tendency to aversion from that. That same person, with respect to the form realm, the formless realm, and the unincluded, does not abandon the underlying tendency to sensual lust from that and does not abandon the underlying tendency to aversion from that. Setting aside the person endowed with the path of the non-returner, the remaining persons do not abandon the underlying tendency to sensual lust and do not abandon the underlying tendency to aversion everywhere.

(Kha) yo [V 2.0226] vā pana yato paṭighānusayaṃ nappajahati so tato kāmarāgānusayaṃ nappajahatīti?

Or again, does a person who does not abandon the underlying tendency to aversion from whatever sphere, from that sphere not abandon the underlying tendency to sensual lust?

Anāgāmimaggasamaṅgī kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu so tato paṭighānusayaṃ nappajahati, no ca so tato kāmarāgānusayaṃ nappajahati. Sveva puggalo rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā apariyāpanne so tato paṭighānusayañca nappajahati kāmarāgānusayañca nappajahati. Anāgāmimaggasamaṅgiṃ ṭhapetvā avasesā puggalā sabbattha paṭighānusayañca nappajahanti kāmarāgānusayañca nappajahanti.

A person endowed with the path of the non-returner, with respect to the sense-sphere realm and the two feelings, does not abandon the underlying tendency to aversion from that, but he does abandon the underlying tendency to sensual lust from that. That same person, with respect to the form realm, the formless realm, and the unincluded, does not abandon the underlying tendency to aversion from that and does not abandon the underlying tendency to sensual lust from that. Setting aside the person endowed with the path of the non-returner, the remaining persons do not abandon the underlying tendency to aversion and do not abandon the underlying tendency to sensual lust everywhere.

(Ka) yo yato kāmarāgānusayaṃ nappajahati so tato mānānusayaṃ nappajahatīti?

Does a person who does not abandon the underlying tendency to sensual lust from whatever sphere, from that sphere not abandon the underlying tendency to conceit?

Aggamaggasamaṅgī kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā so tato kāmarāgānusayaṃ nappajahati, no ca so tato mānānusayaṃ nappajahati. Sveva [T 1.0595] puggalo dukkhāya vedanāya apariyāpanne so tato kāmarāgānusayañca nappajahati mānānusayañca nappajahati. Dvinnaṃ maggasamaṅgīnaṃ ṭhapetvā avasesā puggalā sabbattha kāmarāgānusayañca nappajahanti mānānusayañca nappajahanti.

A person endowed with the highest path, with respect to the sense-sphere realm, the two feelings, the form realm, and the formless realm, does not abandon the underlying tendency to sensual lust from that, but he does abandon the underlying tendency to conceit from that. That same person, with respect to painful feeling and the unincluded, does not abandon the underlying tendency to sensual lust from that and does not abandon the underlying tendency to conceit from that. Setting aside the two persons endowed with the paths, the remaining persons do not abandon the underlying tendency to sensual lust and do not abandon the underlying tendency to conceit everywhere.

(Kha) yo vā pana yato mānānusayaṃ nappajahati so tato kāmarāgānusayaṃ nappajahatīti?

Or again, does a person who does not abandon the underlying tendency to conceit from whatever sphere, from that sphere not abandon the underlying tendency to sensual lust?

Anāgāmimaggasamaṅgī kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu so tato mānānusayaṃ nappajahati, no ca so tato kāmarāgānusayaṃ nappajahati. Sveva puggalo dukkhāya vedanāya rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā apariyāpanne so tato mānānusayañca nappajahati kāmarāgānusayañca nappajahati. Dvinnaṃ maggasamaṅgīnaṃ ṭhapetvā avasesā puggalā sabbattha mānānusayañca nappajahanti kāmarāgānusayañca nappajahanti.

A person endowed with the path of the non-returner, with respect to the sense-sphere realm and the two feelings, does not abandon the underlying tendency to conceit from that, but he does abandon the underlying tendency to sensual lust from that. That same person, with respect to painful feeling, the form realm, the formless realm, and the unincluded, does not abandon the underlying tendency to conceit from that and does not abandon the underlying tendency to sensual lust from that. Setting aside the two persons endowed with the paths, the remaining persons do not abandon the underlying tendency to conceit and do not abandon the underlying tendency to sensual lust everywhere.

Yo yato kāmarāgānusayaṃ nappajahati so tato diṭṭhānusayaṃ…pe… vicikicchānusayaṃ nappajahatīti?

Does a person who does not abandon the underlying tendency to sensual lust from whatever sphere, from that sphere not abandon the underlying tendency to views... up to... the underlying tendency to skeptical doubt?

Aṭṭhamako kāmadhātuyā tīsu vedanāsu rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā so tato [V 2.0227] kāmarāgānusayaṃ nappajahati, no ca so tato vicikicchānusayaṃ nappajahati. Sveva puggalo apariyāpanne [M 2.0175] so tato kāmarāgānusayañca nappajahati vicikicchānusayañca nappajahati. Anāgāmimaggasamaṅgiñca aṭṭhamakañca ṭhapetvā avasesā puggalā sabbattha kāmarāgānusayañca nappajahanti vicikicchānusayañca nappajahanti.

The eighth person, with respect to the sense-sphere realm, the three feelings, the form realm, and the formless realm, does not abandon the underlying tendency to sensual lust from that, but he does abandon the underlying tendency to skeptical doubt from that. That same person, with respect to the unincluded, does not abandon the underlying tendency to sensual lust from that and does not abandon the underlying tendency to skeptical doubt from that. Setting aside the person endowed with the path of the non-returner and the eighth person, the remaining persons do not abandon the underlying tendency to sensual lust and do not abandon the underlying tendency to skeptical doubt everywhere.

Yo vā pana yato vicikicchānusayaṃ nappajahati so tato kāmarāgānusayaṃ nappajahatīti?

Or again, does a person who does not abandon the underlying tendency to skeptical doubt from whatever sphere, from that sphere not abandon the underlying tendency to sensual lust?

Anāgāmimaggasamaṅgī kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu so tato vicikicchānusayaṃ nappajahati, no [T 1.0596] ca so tato kāmarāgānusayaṃ nappajahati. Sveva puggalo dukkhāya vedanāya rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā apariyāpanne so tato vicikicchānusayañca nappajahati kāmarāgānusayañca nappajahati. Anāgāmimaggasamaṅgiñca aṭṭhamakañca ṭhapetvā avasesā puggalā sabbattha vicikicchānusayañca nappajahanti kāmarāgānusayañca nappajahanti.

A person endowed with the path of the non-returner, with respect to the sense-sphere realm and the two feelings, does not abandon the underlying tendency to skeptical doubt from that, but he does abandon the underlying tendency to sensual lust from that. That same person, with respect to painful feeling, the form realm, the formless realm, and the unincluded, does not abandon the underlying tendency to skeptical doubt from that and does not abandon the underlying tendency to sensual lust from that. Setting aside the person endowed with the path of the non-returner and the eighth person, the remaining persons do not abandon the underlying tendency to skeptical doubt and do not abandon the underlying tendency to sensual lust everywhere.

(Ka) yo yato kāmarāgānusayaṃ nappajahati so tato bhavarāgānusayaṃ nappajahatīti?

Does a person who does not abandon the underlying tendency to sensual lust from whatever sphere, from that sphere not abandon the underlying tendency to lust for existence?

Aggamaggasamaṅgī rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā so tato kāmarāgānusayaṃ nappajahati, no ca so tato bhavarāgānusayaṃ nappajahati. Sveva puggalo kāmadhātuyā tīsu vedanāsu apariyāpanne so tato kāmarāgānusayañca nappajahati bhavarāgānusayañca nappajahati. Dvinnaṃ maggasamaṅgīnaṃ ṭhapetvā avasesā puggalā sabbattha kāmarāgānusayañca nappajahanti bhavarāgānusayañca nappajahanti.

A person endowed with the highest path, with respect to the form realm and the formless realm, does not abandon the underlying tendency to sensual lust from that, but he does abandon the underlying tendency to lust for existence from that. That same person, with respect to the sense-sphere realm, the three feelings, and the unincluded, does not abandon the underlying tendency to sensual lust from that and does not abandon the underlying tendency to lust for existence from that. Setting aside the two persons endowed with the paths, the remaining persons do not abandon the underlying tendency to sensual lust and do not abandon the underlying tendency to lust for existence everywhere.

(Kha) yo vā pana yato bhavarāgānusayaṃ nappajahati so tato kāmarāgānusayaṃ nappajahatīti?

(Ka) yo yato kāmarāgānusayaṃ nappajahati so tato avijjānusayaṃ nappajahatīti?
