Aggamaggasamaṅgiñca aṭṭhamakañca ṭhapetvā avasesā puggalā sabbattha vicikicchānusayañca nappajahanti avijjānusayañca nappajahanti.

A person endowed with the highest path, in the sense-sphere, in the three feelings, in the form-sphere, and in the formless-sphere, does not abandon the underlying tendency to doubt from there, but that person does abandon the underlying tendency to ignorance from there. That same person, in the supramundane, does not abandon the underlying tendency to doubt from there and does not abandon the underlying tendency to ignorance from there. Except for the person endowed with the highest path and the eighth person, the remaining persons do not abandon the underlying tendency to doubt and do not abandon the underlying tendency to ignorance everywhere.

(Kha) yo vā pana yato avijjānusayaṃ nappajahati so tato vicikicchānusayaṃ nappajahatīti?

Or, as for a person who does not abandon the underlying tendency to ignorance from a certain sphere, does that person not abandon the underlying tendency to doubt from that sphere?

Aṭṭhamako kāmadhātuyā [T 1.0603] tīsu vedanāsu rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā so tato avijjānusayaṃ nappajahati, no ca so tato vicikicchānusayaṃ nappajahati[M 2.0180]. Sveva puggalo apariyāpanne so tato avijjānusayañca nappajahati vicikicchānusayañca nappajahati. Aggamaggasamaṅgiñca aṭṭhamakañca ṭhapetvā avasesā puggalā sabbattha avijjānusayañca nappajahanti vicikicchānusayañca nappajahanti.

The eighth person, in the sense-sphere, in the three feelings, in the form-sphere, and in the formless-sphere, does not abandon the underlying tendency to ignorance from there, but that person does abandon the underlying tendency to doubt from there. That same person, in the supramundane, does not abandon the underlying tendency to ignorance from there and does not abandon the underlying tendency to doubt from there. Except for the person endowed with the highest path and the eighth person, the remaining persons do not abandon the underlying tendency to ignorance and do not abandon the underlying tendency to doubt everywhere.

192. (Ka) yo yato bhavarāgānusayaṃ nappajahati so tato avijjānusayaṃ nappajahatīti?

192. Does a person who does not abandon the underlying tendency to lust for becoming from a certain sphere not abandon the underlying tendency to ignorance from that sphere?

Aggamaggasamaṅgī kāmadhātuyā tīsu vedanāsu so tato bhavarāgānusayaṃ nappajahati, no ca so tato avijjānusayaṃ nappajahati. Sveva puggalo apariyāpanne so tato bhavarāgānusayañca nappajahati avijjānusayañca [V 2.0234] nappajahati. Aggamaggasamaṅgiṃ ṭhapetvā avasesā puggalā sabbattha bhavarāgānusayañca nappajahanti avijjānusayañca nappajahanti.

A person endowed with the highest path, in the sense-sphere and in the three feelings, does not abandon the underlying tendency to lust for becoming from there, but that person does abandon the underlying tendency to ignorance from there. That same person, in the supramundane, does not abandon the underlying tendency to lust for becoming from there and does not abandon the underlying tendency to ignorance from there. Except for the person endowed with the highest path, the remaining persons do not abandon the underlying tendency to lust for becoming and do not abandon the underlying tendency to ignorance everywhere.

(Kha) yo vā pana yato avijjānusayaṃ nappajahati so tato bhavarāgānusayaṃ nappajahatīti? Āmantā. (Ekamūlakaṃ)

Or, as for a person who does not abandon the underlying tendency to ignorance from a certain sphere, does that person not abandon the underlying tendency to lust for becoming from that sphere? Yes.

193. (Ka) yo yato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca nappajahati so tato mānānusayaṃ nappajahatīti?

193. Does a person who does not abandon the underlying tendency to sensual lust and the underlying tendency to aversion from a certain sphere not abandon the underlying tendency to conceit from that sphere?

Aggamaggasamaṅgī kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā so tato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca nappajahati, no ca so tato mānānusayaṃ nappajahati. Sveva puggalo dukkhāya vedanāya apariyāpanne so tato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca nappajahati mānānusayañca nappajahati[T 1.0604]. Dvinnaṃ maggasamaṅgīnaṃ ṭhapetvā avasesā puggalā sabbattha kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca nappajahanti mānānusayañca nappajahanti.

A person endowed with the highest path, in the sense-sphere, in the two feelings, in the form-sphere, and in the formless-sphere, does not abandon the underlying tendency to sensual lust and the underlying tendency to aversion from there, but that person does abandon the underlying tendency to conceit from there. That same person, in painful feeling and in the supramundane, does not abandon the underlying tendency to sensual lust, the underlying tendency to aversion, and the underlying tendency to conceit from there. Except for the two persons endowed with the path, the remaining persons do not abandon the underlying tendency to sensual lust, the underlying tendency to aversion, and the underlying tendency to conceit everywhere.

(Kha) yo vā pana yato mānānusayaṃ nappajahati so tato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca nappajahatīti?

Or, as for a person who does not abandon the underlying tendency to conceit from a certain sphere, does that person not abandon the underlying tendency to sensual lust and the underlying tendency to aversion from that sphere?

Anāgāmimaggasamaṅgī dukkhāya vedanāya so tato mānānusayañca kāmarāgānusayañca nappajahati, no ca so tato paṭighānusayaṃ nappajahati. Sveva puggalo kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu so tato mānānusayañca paṭighānusayañca nappajahati, no ca so tato kāmarāgānusayaṃ nappajahati. Sveva puggalo rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā apariyāpanne so tato mānānusayañca nappajahati kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca nappajahati. Dvinnaṃ maggasamaṅgīnaṃ ṭhapetvā avasesā puggalā sabbattha mānānusayañca nappajahanti kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca nappajahanti.

A person endowed with the non-returner's path, in painful feeling, does not abandon the underlying tendency to conceit and the underlying tendency to sensual lust from there, but that person does abandon the underlying tendency to aversion from there. That same person, in the sense-sphere and in the two feelings, does not abandon the underlying tendency to conceit and the underlying tendency to aversion from there, but that person does abandon the underlying tendency to sensual lust from there. That same person, in the form-sphere, in the formless-sphere, and in the supramundane, does not abandon the underlying tendency to conceit, the underlying tendency to sensual lust, and the underlying tendency to aversion from there. Except for the two persons endowed with the path, the remaining persons do not abandon the underlying tendency to conceit, and do not abandon the underlying tendency to sensual lust and the underlying tendency to aversion everywhere.

Yo [M 2.0181] yato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca nappajahati so tato diṭṭhānusayaṃ…pe… vicikicchānusayaṃ nappajahatīti?

Does a person who does not abandon the underlying tendency to sensual lust and the underlying tendency to aversion from a certain sphere not abandon the underlying tendency to wrong view... the underlying tendency to doubt from that sphere?

Aṭṭhamako [V 2.0235] kāmadhātuyā tīsu vedanāsu rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā so tato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca nappajahati, no ca so tato vicikicchānusayaṃ nappajahati. Sveva puggalo apariyāpanne so tato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca nappajahati, vicikicchānusayañca nappajahati. Anāgāmimaggasamaṅgiñca aṭṭhamakañca ṭhapetvā avasesā puggalā sabbattha kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca nappajahanti vicikicchānusayañca nappajahanti[T 1.0605].

The eighth person, in the sense-sphere, in the three feelings, in the form-sphere, and in the formless-sphere, does not abandon the underlying tendency to sensual lust and the underlying tendency to aversion from there, but that person does abandon the underlying tendency to doubt from there. That same person, in the supramundane, does not abandon the underlying tendency to sensual lust and the underlying tendency to aversion from there, and does not abandon the underlying tendency to doubt from there. Except for the person endowed with the non-returner's path and the eighth person, the remaining persons do not abandon the underlying tendency to sensual lust, the underlying tendency to aversion, and the underlying tendency to doubt everywhere.

Yo vā pana yato vicikicchānusayaṃ nappajahati so tato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca nappajahatīti?

Or, as for a person who does not abandon the underlying tendency to doubt from a certain sphere, does that person not abandon the underlying tendency to sensual lust and the underlying tendency to aversion from that sphere?

Anāgāmimaggasamaṅgī dukkhāya vedanāya so tato vicikicchānusayañca kāmarāgānusayañca nappajahati, no ca so tato paṭighānusayaṃ nappajahati. Sveva puggalo kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu so tato vicikicchānusayañca paṭighānusayañca nappajahati, no ca so tato kāmarāgānusayaṃ nappajahati. Sveva puggalo rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā apariyāpanne so tato vicikicchānusayañca nappajahati kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca nappajahati. Anāgāmimaggasamaṅgiñca aṭṭhamakañca ṭhapetvā avasesā puggalā sabbattha vicikicchānusayañca nappajahanti kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca nappajahanti.

A person endowed with the non-returner's path, in painful feeling, does not abandon the underlying tendency to doubt and the underlying tendency to sensual lust from there, but that person does abandon the underlying tendency to aversion from there. That same person, in the sense-sphere and in the two feelings, does not abandon the underlying tendency to doubt and the underlying tendency to aversion from there, but that person does abandon the underlying tendency to sensual lust from there. That same person, in the form-sphere, in the formless-sphere, and in the supramundane, does not abandon the underlying tendency to doubt, the underlying tendency to sensual lust, and the underlying tendency to aversion from there. Except for the person endowed with the non-returner's path and the eighth person, the remaining persons do not abandon the underlying tendency to doubt, and do not abandon the underlying tendency to sensual lust and the underlying tendency to aversion everywhere.

(Ka) yo yato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca nappajahati so tato bhavarāgānusayaṃ nappajahatīti?

Does a person who does not abandon the underlying tendency to sensual lust and the underlying tendency to aversion from a certain sphere not abandon the underlying tendency to lust for becoming from that sphere?

Aggamaggasamaṅgī rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā so tato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca nappajahati, no ca so tato bhavarāgānusayaṃ nappajahati. Sveva puggalo kāmadhātuyā tīsu vedanāsu apariyāpanne so tato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca nappajahati bhavarāgānusayañca nappajahati. Dvinnaṃ maggasamaṅgīnaṃ ṭhapetvā avasesā puggalā sabbattha kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca nappajahanti bhavarāgānusayañca nappajahanti.

A person endowed with the highest path, in the form element and in the formless element, is not abandoning the underlying tendency to sensual lust and the underlying tendency to aversion from that sphere; but that person is abandoning the underlying tendency to craving for existence from that sphere. That very person, in the sense-sphere element, in the three feelings, and in the unincluded, is not abandoning the underlying tendency to sensual lust, the underlying tendency to aversion, and the underlying tendency to craving for existence from that sphere. Setting aside the two persons endowed with the path, the remaining persons are not abandoning the underlying tendency to sensual lust, the underlying tendency to aversion, and the underlying tendency to craving for existence in all spheres.

(Kha) yo vā pana yato bhavarāgānusayaṃ nappajahati so tato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca nappajahatīti?

Or again, whichever person is not abandoning the underlying tendency to craving for existence from whichever sphere, is that person not abandoning the underlying tendency to sensual lust and the underlying tendency to aversion from that sphere?

Anāgāmimaggasamaṅgī dukkhāya [T 1.0606] vedanāya so tato bhavarāgānusayañca kāmarāgānusayañca nappajahati, no ca so tato paṭighānusayaṃ [V 2.0236] nappajahati. Sveva puggalo kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu [M 2.0182] so tato bhavarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca nappajahati, no ca so tato kāmarāgānusayaṃ nappajahati. Sveva puggalo rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā apariyāpanne so tato bhavarāgānusayañca nappajahati kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca nappajahati. Dvinnaṃ maggasamaṅgīnaṃ ṭhapetvā avasesā puggalā sabbattha bhavarāgānusayañca nappajahanti kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca nappajahanti.

A person endowed with the non-returner's path, in painful feeling, is not abandoning the underlying tendency to craving for existence and the underlying tendency to sensual lust from that sphere; but that person is abandoning the underlying tendency to aversion from that sphere. That very person, in the sense-sphere element and in the two feelings, is not abandoning the underlying tendency to craving for existence and the underlying tendency to aversion from that sphere; but that person is abandoning the underlying tendency to sensual lust from that sphere. That very person, in the form element, in the formless element, and in the unincluded, is not abandoning the underlying tendency to craving for existence, the underlying tendency to sensual lust, and the underlying tendency to aversion from that sphere. Setting aside the two persons endowed with the path, the remaining persons are not abandoning the underlying tendency to craving for existence, the underlying tendency to sensual lust, and the underlying tendency to aversion in all spheres.

(Ka) yo yato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca nappajahati so tato avijjānusayaṃ nappajahatīti?

Whichever person is not abandoning the underlying tendency to sensual lust and the underlying tendency to aversion from whichever sphere, is that person not abandoning the underlying tendency to ignorance from that sphere?

Aggamaggasamaṅgī kāmadhātuyā tīsu vedanāsu rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā so tato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca nappajahati, no ca so tato avijjānusayaṃ nappajahati. Sveva puggalo apariyāpanne so tato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca nappajahati avijjānusayañca nappajahati. Dvinnaṃ maggasamaṅgīnaṃ ṭhapetvā avasesā puggalā sabbattha kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca nappajahanti avijjānusayañca nappajahanti.

A person endowed with the highest path, in the sense-sphere element, in the three feelings, in the form element, and in the formless element, is not abandoning the underlying tendency to sensual lust and the underlying tendency to aversion from that sphere; but that person is abandoning the underlying tendency to ignorance from that sphere. That very person, in the unincluded, is not abandoning the underlying tendency to sensual lust, the underlying tendency to aversion, and the underlying tendency to ignorance from that sphere. Setting aside the two persons endowed with the path, the remaining persons are not abandoning the underlying tendency to sensual lust, the underlying tendency to aversion, and the underlying tendency to ignorance in all spheres.

(Kha) yo vā pana yato avijjānusayaṃ nappajahati so tato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca nappajahatīti?

Or again, whichever person is not abandoning the underlying tendency to ignorance from whichever sphere, is that person not abandoning the underlying tendency to sensual lust and the underlying tendency to aversion from that sphere?

Anāgāmimaggasamaṅgī dukkhāya vedanāya so tato avijjānusayañca kāmarāgānusayañca nappajahati, no ca so tato paṭighānusayaṃ nappajahati. Sveva puggalo kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu so tato avijjānusayañca paṭighānusayañca [T 1.0607] nappajahati, no ca so tato kāmarāgānusayaṃ nappajahati. Sveva puggalo rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā apariyāpanne so tato avijjānusayañca nappajahati kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca nappajahati. Dvinnaṃ maggasamaṅgīnaṃ ṭhapetvā avasesā puggalā sabbattha avijjānusayañca nappajahanti kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca nappajahanti. (Dukamūlakaṃ)

A person endowed with the non-returner's path, in painful feeling, is not abandoning the underlying tendency to ignorance and the underlying tendency to sensual lust from that sphere; but that person is abandoning the underlying tendency to aversion from that sphere. That very person, in the sense-sphere element and in the two feelings, is not abandoning the underlying tendency to ignorance and the underlying tendency to aversion from that sphere; but that person is abandoning the underlying tendency to sensual lust from that sphere. That very person, in the form element, in the formless element, and in the unincluded, is not abandoning the underlying tendency to ignorance, the underlying tendency to sensual lust, and the underlying tendency to aversion from that sphere. Setting aside the two persons endowed with the path, the remaining persons are not abandoning the underlying tendency to ignorance, the underlying tendency to sensual lust, and the underlying tendency to aversion in all spheres. (The Dyad Root.)

194. Yo [V 2.0237] yato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca nappajahati so tato diṭṭhānusayaṃ…pe… vicikicchānusayaṃ nappajahatīti?

194. Whichever person is not abandoning the underlying tendency to sensual lust, the underlying tendency to aversion, and the underlying tendency to conceit from whichever sphere, is that person not abandoning the underlying tendency to views... the underlying tendency to doubt from that sphere?

Aṭṭhamako kāmadhātuyā tīsu vedanāsu rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā so tato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca nappajahati, no ca so tato vicikicchānusayaṃ nappajahati. Sveva puggalo apariyāpanne so tato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca nappajahati vicikicchānusayañca nappajahati. Dvinnaṃ maggasamaṅgīnañca aṭṭhamakañca [M 2.0183] ṭhapetvā avasesā puggalā sabbattha kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca nappajahanti vicikicchānusayañca nappajahanti.

The eighth person, in the sense-sphere element, in the three feelings, in the form element, and in the formless element, is not abandoning the underlying tendency to sensual lust, the underlying tendency to aversion, and the underlying tendency to conceit from that sphere; but that person is abandoning the underlying tendency to doubt from that sphere. That very person, in the unincluded, is not abandoning the underlying tendency to sensual lust, the underlying tendency to aversion, the underlying tendency to conceit, and the underlying tendency to doubt from that sphere. Setting aside the two persons endowed with the path and the eighth person, the remaining persons are not abandoning the underlying tendency to sensual lust, the underlying tendency to aversion, the underlying tendency to conceit, and the underlying tendency to doubt in all spheres.

Yo vā pana yato vicikicchānusayaṃ nappajahati so tato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca nappajahatīti?

Or again, whichever person is not abandoning the underlying tendency to doubt from whichever sphere, is that person not abandoning the underlying tendency to sensual lust, the underlying tendency to aversion, and the underlying tendency to conceit from that sphere?

Anāgāmimaggasamaṅgī dukkhāya vedanāya so tato vicikicchānusayañca kāmarāgānusayañca mānānusayañca nappajahati, no ca so tato paṭighānusayaṃ nappajahati. Sveva puggalo kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu so [T 1.0608] tato vicikicchānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca nappajahati, no ca so tato kāmarāgānusayaṃ nappajahati. Sveva puggalo rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā apariyāpanne so tato vicikicchānusayañca nappajahati kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca nappajahati. Aggamaggasamaṅgī kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā so tato vicikicchānusayañca kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca nappajahati, no ca so tato mānānusayaṃ nappajahati. Sveva puggalo dukkhāya vedanāya apariyāpanne so tato vicikicchānusayañca nappajahati kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca nappajahati. Dvinnaṃ maggasamaṅgīnañca aṭṭhamakañca ṭhapetvā avasesā puggalā sabbattha vicikicchānusayañca nappajahanti kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca nappajahanti.

A person endowed with the non-returner's path, in painful feeling, is not abandoning the underlying tendency to doubt, the underlying tendency to sensual lust, and the underlying tendency to conceit from that sphere; but that person is abandoning the underlying tendency to aversion from that sphere. That very person, in the sense-sphere element and in the two feelings, is not abandoning the underlying tendency to doubt, the underlying tendency to aversion, and the underlying tendency to conceit from that sphere; but that person is abandoning the underlying tendency to sensual lust from that sphere. That very person, in the form element, in the formless element, and in the unincluded, is not abandoning the underlying tendency to doubt, the underlying tendency to sensual lust, the underlying tendency to aversion, and the underlying tendency to conceit from that sphere. A person endowed with the highest path, in the sense-sphere element, in the two feelings, in the form element, and in the formless element, is not abandoning the underlying tendency to doubt, the underlying tendency to sensual lust, and the underlying tendency to aversion from that sphere; but that person is abandoning the underlying tendency to conceit from that sphere. That very person, in painful feeling and in the unincluded, is not abandoning the underlying tendency to doubt, the underlying tendency to sensual lust, the underlying tendency to aversion, and the underlying tendency to conceit from that sphere. Setting aside the two persons endowed with the path and the eighth person, the remaining persons are not abandoning the underlying tendency to doubt, the underlying tendency to sensual lust, the underlying tendency to aversion, and the underlying tendency to conceit in all spheres.

(Ka) yo [V 2.0238] yato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca nappajahati so tato bhavarāgānusayaṃ nappajahatīti? Āmantā.

The person who, from whichever sphere, does not abandon the underlying tendency to sensual lust, the underlying tendency to aversion, and the underlying tendency to conceit, does that person, from that sphere, not abandon the underlying tendency to lust for existence? Yes, that is so.

(Kha) yo vā pana yato bhavarāgānusayaṃ nappajahati so tato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca nappajahatīti?

Or again, the person who, from whichever sphere, does not abandon the underlying tendency to lust for existence, does that person, from that sphere, not abandon the underlying tendency to sensual lust, the underlying tendency to aversion, and the underlying tendency to conceit?

Anāgāmimaggasamaṅgī dukkhāya vedanāya so tato bhavarāgānusayañca kāmarāgānusayañca mānānusayañca nappajahati, no ca so tato paṭighānusayaṃ nappajahati. Sveva puggalo kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu so tato bhavarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca nappajahati, no ca so tato kāmarāgānusayaṃ nappajahati. Sveva puggalo rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā [T 1.0609] apariyāpanne so tato bhavarāgānusayañca nappajahati kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca nappajahati. Aggamaggasamaṅgī kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu so tato bhavarāgānusayañca kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca nappajahati, no ca so tato mānānusayaṃ [M 2.0184] nappajahati. Sveva puggalo dukkhāya vedanāya apariyāpanne so tato bhavarāgānusayañca nappajahati kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca nappajahati. Dvinnaṃ maggasamaṅgīnaṃ ṭhapetvā avasesā puggalā sabbattha bhavarāgānusayañca nappajahanti kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca nappajahanti.

A person endowed with the path of non-returning, in respect to painful feeling, does not abandon from that sphere the underlying tendency to lust for existence, the underlying tendency to sensual lust, and the underlying tendency to conceit, but does abandon from that sphere the underlying tendency to aversion. That same person, in the sense-sphere and in respect to two feelings, does not abandon from that sphere the underlying tendency to lust for existence, the underlying tendency to aversion, and the underlying tendency to conceit, but does abandon from that sphere the underlying tendency to sensual lust. That same person, in the form-sphere, the formless-sphere, and in the unincluded, does not abandon from that sphere the underlying tendency to lust for existence, and does not abandon the underlying tendency to sensual lust, the underlying tendency to aversion, and the underlying tendency to conceit. A person endowed with the highest path, in the sense-sphere and in respect to two feelings, does not abandon from that sphere the underlying tendency to lust for existence, the underlying tendency to sensual lust, and the underlying tendency to aversion, but does abandon from that sphere the underlying tendency to conceit. That same person, in respect to painful feeling and in the unincluded, does not abandon from that sphere the underlying tendency to lust for existence, and does not abandon the underlying tendency to sensual lust, the underlying tendency to aversion, and the underlying tendency to conceit. Setting aside the two persons endowed with the paths, the remaining persons, in all spheres, do not abandon the underlying tendency to lust for existence, and do not abandon the underlying tendency to sensual lust, the underlying tendency to aversion, and the underlying tendency to conceit.

(Ka) yo yato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca nappajahati so tato avijjānusayaṃ nappajahatīti?

The person who, from whichever sphere, does not abandon the underlying tendency to sensual lust, the underlying tendency to aversion, and the underlying tendency to conceit, does that person, from that sphere, not abandon the underlying tendency to ignorance?

Aggamaggasamaṅgī dukkhāya vedanāya so tato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca nappajahati, no ca so tato avijjānusayaṃ nappajahati. Sveva puggalo apariyāpanne so tato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca nappajahati avijjānusayañca nappajahati. Dvinnaṃ maggasamaṅgīnaṃ ṭhapetvā avasesā puggalā sabbattha kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca nappajahanti avijjānusayañca nappajahanti.

A person endowed with the highest path, in respect to painful feeling, does not abandon from that sphere the underlying tendency to sensual lust, the underlying tendency to aversion, and the underlying tendency to conceit, but does abandon from that sphere the underlying tendency to ignorance. That same person, in the unincluded, does not abandon from that sphere the underlying tendency to sensual lust, the underlying tendency to aversion, the underlying tendency to conceit, and the underlying tendency to ignorance. Setting aside the two persons endowed with the paths, the remaining persons, in all spheres, do not abandon the underlying tendency to sensual lust, the underlying tendency to aversion, and the underlying tendency to conceit, and do not abandon the underlying tendency to ignorance.

(Kha) yo [V 2.0239] vā pana yato avijjānusayaṃ nappajahati so tato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca nappajahatīti?

Or again, the person who, from whichever sphere, does not abandon the underlying tendency to ignorance, does that person, from that sphere, not abandon the underlying tendency to sensual lust, the underlying tendency to aversion, and the underlying tendency to conceit?

Anāgāmimaggasamaṅgī dukkhāya vedanāya so tato avijjānusayañca kāmarāgānusayañca mānānusayañca nappajahati[T 1.0610], no ca so tato paṭighānusayaṃ nappajahati. Sveva puggalo kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu so tato avijjānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca nappajahati, no ca so tato kāmarāgānusayaṃ nappajahati. Sveva puggalo rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā apariyāpanne so tato avijjānusayañca nappajahati kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca nappajahati. Dvinnaṃ maggasamaṅgīnaṃ ṭhapetvā avasesā puggalā sabbattha avijjānusayañca nappajahanti kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca nappajahanti. (Tikamūlakaṃ)

A person endowed with the path of non-returning, in respect to painful feeling, does not abandon from that sphere the underlying tendency to ignorance, the underlying tendency to sensual lust, and the underlying tendency to conceit, but does abandon from that sphere the underlying tendency to aversion. That same person, in the sense-sphere and in respect to two feelings, does not abandon from that sphere the underlying tendency to ignorance, the underlying tendency to aversion, and the underlying tendency to conceit, but does abandon from that sphere the underlying tendency to sensual lust. That same person, in the form-sphere, the formless-sphere, and in the unincluded, does not abandon from that sphere the underlying tendency to ignorance, and does not abandon the underlying tendency to sensual lust, the underlying tendency to aversion, and the underlying tendency to conceit. Setting aside the two persons endowed with the paths, the remaining persons, in all spheres, do not abandon the underlying tendency to ignorance, and do not abandon the underlying tendency to sensual lust, the underlying tendency to aversion, and the underlying tendency to conceit. (Rooted in the Triad)

195. (Ka) yo yato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca diṭṭhānusayañca nappajahati so tato vicikicchānusayaṃ nappajahatīti? Āmantā.

195. The person who, from whichever sphere, does not abandon the underlying tendency to sensual lust, the underlying tendency to aversion, the underlying tendency to conceit, and the underlying tendency to wrong views, does that person, from that sphere, not abandon the underlying tendency to doubt? Yes, that is so.

(Kha) yo vā pana yato vicikicchānusayaṃ nappajahati so tato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca diṭṭhānusayañca nappajahatīti?

Or again, the person who, from whichever sphere, does not abandon the underlying tendency to doubt, does that person, from that sphere, not abandon the underlying tendency to sensual lust, the underlying tendency to aversion, the underlying tendency to conceit, and the underlying tendency to wrong views?

Anāgāmimaggasamaṅgī dukkhāya vedanāya so tato vicikicchānusayañca kāmarāgānusayañca mānānusayañca diṭṭhānusayañca nappajahati, no ca so tato paṭighānusayaṃ nappajahati. Sveva puggalo kāmadhātuyā [M 2.0185] dvīsu vedanāsu so tato vicikicchānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca diṭṭhānusayañca nappajahati, no ca so tato kāmarāgānusayaṃ nappajahati. Sveva puggalo rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā apariyāpanne so tato vicikicchānusayañca nappajahati kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca diṭṭhānusayañca nappajahati[T 1.0611]. Aggamaggasamaṅgī kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā [V 2.0240] so tato vicikicchānusayañca kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca diṭṭhānusayañca nappajahati, no ca so tato mānānusayaṃ nappajahati. Sveva puggalo dukkhāya vedanāya apariyāpanne so tato vicikicchānusayañca nappajahati kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca diṭṭhānusayañca nappajahati. Dvinnaṃ maggasamaṅgīnañca aṭṭhamakañca ṭhapetvā avasesā puggalā sabbattha vicikicchānusayañca nappajahanti kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca diṭṭhānusayañca nappajahanti …pe…. (Catukkamūlakaṃ)

A person endowed with the path of non-returning, in respect to painful feeling, does not abandon from that sphere the underlying tendency to doubt, the underlying tendency to sensual lust, the underlying tendency to conceit, and the underlying tendency to wrong views, but does abandon from that sphere the underlying tendency to aversion. That same person, in the sense-sphere and in respect to two feelings, does not abandon from that sphere the underlying tendency to doubt, the underlying tendency to aversion, the underlying tendency to conceit, and the underlying tendency to wrong views, but does abandon from that sphere the underlying tendency to sensual lust. That same person, in the form-sphere, the formless-sphere, and in the unincluded, does not abandon from that sphere the underlying tendency to doubt, and does not abandon the underlying tendency to sensual lust, the underlying tendency to aversion, the underlying tendency to conceit, and the underlying tendency to wrong views. A person endowed with the highest path, in the sense-sphere, in respect to two feelings, in the form-sphere, and in the formless-sphere, does not abandon from that sphere the underlying tendency to doubt, the underlying tendency to sensual lust, the underlying tendency to aversion, and the underlying tendency to wrong views, but does abandon from that sphere the underlying tendency to conceit. That same person, in respect to painful feeling and in the unincluded, does not abandon from that sphere the underlying tendency to doubt, and does not abandon the underlying tendency to sensual lust, the underlying tendency to aversion, the underlying tendency to conceit, and the underlying tendency to wrong views. Setting aside the two persons endowed with the paths and the eighth person, the remaining persons, in all spheres, do not abandon the underlying tendency to doubt, and do not abandon the underlying tendency to sensual lust, the underlying tendency to aversion, the underlying tendency to conceit, and the underlying tendency to wrong views. (Rooted in the Tetrad)

196. (Ka) yo yato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca diṭṭhānusayañca vicikicchānusayañca nappajahati so tato bhavarāgānusayaṃ nappajahatīti? Āmantā.

196. The person who, from whichever sphere, does not abandon the underlying tendency to sensual lust, the underlying tendency to aversion, the underlying tendency to conceit, the underlying tendency to wrong views, and the underlying tendency to doubt, does that person, from that sphere, not abandon the underlying tendency to lust for existence? Yes, that is so.

(Kha) yo vā pana yato bhavarāgānusayaṃ nappajahati so tato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca diṭṭhānusayañca vicikicchānusayañca nappajahatīti?

Or again, whichever person does not abandon the underlying tendency to lust for becoming from any sphere, does that person from that sphere not abandon the underlying tendency to sensual lust, the underlying tendency to aversion, the underlying tendency to conceit, the underlying tendency to views, and the underlying tendency to doubt?

Aṭṭhamako kāmadhātuyā tīsu vedanāsu rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā so tato bhavarāgānusayañca kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca nappajahati, no ca so tato diṭṭhānusayañca vicikicchānusayañca nappajahati. Sveva puggalo apariyāpanne so tato bhavarāgānusayañca nappajahati kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca diṭṭhānusayañca vicikicchānusayañca nappajahati. Anāgāmimaggasamaṅgī dukkhāya vedanāya [T 1.0612] so tato bhavarāgānusayañca kāmarāgānusayañca mānānusayañca diṭṭhānusayañca vicikicchānusayañca nappajahati, no ca so tato paṭighānusayaṃ nappajahati. Sveva puggalo kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu so tato bhavarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca diṭṭhānusayañca vicikicchānusayañca nappajahati, no ca so tato kāmarāgānusayaṃ nappajahati. Sveva puggalo rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā apariyāpanne so tato bhavarāgānusayañca nappajahati kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca [V 2.0241] mānānusayañca diṭṭhānusayañca vicikicchānusayañca [M 2.0186] nappajahati. Aggamaggasamaṅgī kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu so tato bhavarāgānusayañca kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca diṭṭhānusayañca vicikicchānusayañca nappajahati, no ca so tato mānānusayaṃ nappajahati. Sveva puggalo dukkhāya vedanāya apariyāpanne so tato bhavarāgānusayañca nappajahati kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca diṭṭhānusayañca vicikicchānusayañca nappajahati. Dvinnaṃ maggasamaṅgīnañca aṭṭhamakañca ṭhapetvā avasesā puggalā sabbattha bhavarāgānusayañca nappajahanti kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca diṭṭhānusayañca vicikicchānusayañca nappajahanti.

The person on the path of stream-entry, in the sense-sphere, in the three feelings, in the fine-material sphere, and in the immaterial sphere, from those spheres does not abandon the underlying tendency to lust for becoming, the underlying tendency to sensual lust, the underlying tendency to aversion, and the underlying tendency to conceit, but from those spheres does abandon the underlying tendency to views and the underlying tendency to doubt. That same person, in the supramundane sphere, from that sphere does not abandon the underlying tendency to lust for becoming, and does not abandon the underlying tendency to sensual lust, the underlying tendency to aversion, the underlying tendency to conceit, the underlying tendency to views, and the underlying tendency to doubt. The person endowed with the path of non-returning, with respect to painful feeling, from that sphere does not abandon the underlying tendency to lust for becoming, the underlying tendency to sensual lust, the underlying tendency to conceit, the underlying tendency to views, and the underlying tendency to doubt, but from that sphere does abandon the underlying tendency to aversion. That same person, in the sense-sphere and in two feelings, from those spheres does not abandon the underlying tendency to lust for becoming, the underlying tendency to aversion, the underlying tendency to conceit, the underlying tendency to views, and the underlying tendency to doubt, but from those spheres does abandon the underlying tendency to sensual lust. That same person, in the fine-material sphere, in the immaterial sphere, and in the supramundane sphere, from those spheres does not abandon the underlying tendency to lust for becoming, and does not abandon the underlying tendency to sensual lust, the underlying tendency to aversion, the underlying tendency to conceit, the underlying tendency to views, and the underlying tendency to doubt. The person endowed with the supreme path, in the sense-sphere and in two feelings, from those spheres does not abandon the underlying tendency to lust for becoming, the underlying tendency to sensual lust, the underlying tendency to aversion, the underlying tendency to views, and the underlying tendency to doubt, but from those spheres does abandon the underlying tendency to conceit. That same person, with respect to painful feeling and in the supramundane sphere, from those spheres does not abandon the underlying tendency to lust for becoming, and does not abandon the underlying tendency to sensual lust, the underlying tendency to aversion, the underlying tendency to conceit, the underlying tendency to views, and the underlying tendency to doubt. Excluding the two persons endowed with the paths and the person on the path of stream-entry, the remaining persons everywhere do not abandon the underlying tendency to lust for becoming, and do not abandon the underlying tendency to sensual lust, the underlying tendency to aversion, the underlying tendency to conceit, the underlying tendency to views, and the underlying tendency to doubt.

(Ka) yo yato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca diṭṭhānusayañca vicikicchānusayañca nappajahati so tato avijjānusayaṃ nappajahatīti?

Whichever person does not abandon from any sphere the underlying tendency to sensual lust, the underlying tendency to aversion, the underlying tendency to conceit, the underlying tendency to views, and the underlying tendency to doubt, does that person from that sphere not abandon the underlying tendency to ignorance?

Aggamaggasamaṅgī dukkhāya vedanāya so tato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca [T 1.0613] diṭṭhānusayañca vicikicchānusayañca nappajahati, no ca so tato avijjānusayaṃ nappajahati. Sveva puggalo apariyāpanne so tato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca diṭṭhānusayañca vicikicchānusayañca nappajahati avijjānusayañca nappajahati. Dvinnaṃ maggasamaṅgīnañca aṭṭhamakañca ṭhapetvā avasesā puggalā sabbattha kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca diṭṭhānusayañca vicikicchānusayañca nappajahanti avijjānusayañca nappajahanti.

The person endowed with the supreme path, with respect to painful feeling, from that sphere does not abandon the underlying tendency to sensual lust, the underlying tendency to aversion, the underlying tendency to conceit, the underlying tendency to views, and the underlying tendency to doubt, but from that sphere does abandon the underlying tendency to ignorance. That same person, in the supramundane sphere, from that sphere does not abandon the underlying tendency to sensual lust, the underlying tendency to aversion, the underlying tendency to conceit, the underlying tendency to views, and the underlying tendency to doubt, and does not abandon the underlying tendency to ignorance. Excluding the two persons endowed with the paths and the person on the path of stream-entry, the remaining persons everywhere do not abandon the underlying tendency to sensual lust, the underlying tendency to aversion, the underlying tendency to conceit, the underlying tendency to views, and the underlying tendency to doubt, and do not abandon the underlying tendency to ignorance.

(Kha) yo vā pana yato avijjānusayaṃ nappajahati so tato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca diṭṭhānusayañca vicikicchānusayañca nappajahatīti?

Or again, whichever person does not abandon the underlying tendency to ignorance from any sphere, does that person from that sphere not abandon the underlying tendency to sensual lust, the underlying tendency to aversion, the underlying tendency to conceit, the underlying tendency to views, and the underlying tendency to doubt?

Aṭṭhamako kāmadhātuyā tīsu vedanāsu rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā so tato avijjānusayañca kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca nappajahati, no ca so tato diṭṭhānusayañca vicikicchānusayañca nappajahati. Sveva puggalo apariyāpanne so tato avijjānusayañca [V 2.0242] nappajahati kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca diṭṭhānusayañca vicikicchānusayañca nappajahati. Anāgāmimaggasamaṅgī dukkhāya vedanāya so tato avijjānusayañca kāmarāgānusayañca mānānusayañca diṭṭhānusayañca vicikicchānusayañca nappajahati, no ca so tato paṭighānusayaṃ nappajahati. Sveva puggalo kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu so tato avijjānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca diṭṭhānusayañca vicikicchānusayañca [M 2.0187] nappajahati, no ca so [T 1.0614] tato kāmarāgānusayaṃ nappajahati. Sveva puggalo rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā apariyāpanne so tato avijjānusayañca nappajahati kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca diṭṭhānusayañca vicikicchānusayañca nappajahati. Dvinnaṃ maggasamaṅgīnañca aṭṭhamakañca ṭhapetvā avasesā puggalā sabbattha avijjānusayañca nappajahanti kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca diṭṭhānusayañca vicikicchānusayañca nappajahanti. (Pañcakamūlakaṃ)

The person on the path of stream-entry, in the sense-sphere, in the three feelings, in the fine-material sphere, and in the immaterial sphere, from those spheres does not abandon the underlying tendency to ignorance, the underlying tendency to sensual lust, the underlying tendency to aversion, and the underlying tendency to conceit, but from those spheres does abandon the underlying tendency to views and the underlying tendency to doubt. That same person, in the supramundane sphere, from that sphere does not abandon the underlying tendency to ignorance, and does not abandon the underlying tendency to sensual lust, the underlying tendency to aversion, the underlying tendency to conceit, the underlying tendency to views, and the underlying tendency to doubt. The person endowed with the path of non-returning, with respect to painful feeling, from that sphere does not abandon the underlying tendency to ignorance, the underlying tendency to sensual lust, the underlying tendency to conceit, the underlying tendency to views, and the underlying tendency to doubt, but from that sphere does abandon the underlying tendency to aversion. That same person, in the sense-sphere and in two feelings, from those spheres does not abandon the underlying tendency to ignorance, the underlying tendency to aversion, the underlying tendency to conceit, the underlying tendency to views, and the underlying tendency to doubt, but from those spheres does abandon the underlying tendency to sensual lust. That same person, in the fine-material sphere, in the immaterial sphere, and in the supramundane sphere, from those spheres does not abandon the underlying tendency to ignorance, and does not abandon the underlying tendency to sensual lust, the underlying tendency to aversion, the underlying tendency to conceit, the underlying tendency to views, and the underlying tendency to doubt. Excluding the two persons endowed with the paths and the person on the path of stream-entry, the remaining persons everywhere do not abandon the underlying tendency to ignorance, and do not abandon the underlying tendency to sensual lust, the underlying tendency to aversion, the underlying tendency to conceit, the underlying tendency to views, and the underlying tendency to doubt. (The Five-Rooted Section)

197. (Ka) yo yato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca diṭṭhānusayañca vicikicchānusayañca bhavarāgānusayañca nappajahati so tato avijjānusayaṃ nappajahatīti?

197. Whichever person does not abandon from any sphere the underlying tendency to sensual lust, the underlying tendency to aversion, the underlying tendency to conceit, the underlying tendency to views, the underlying tendency to doubt, and the underlying tendency to lust for becoming, does that person from that sphere not abandon the underlying tendency to ignorance?

Aggamaggasamaṅgī dukkhāya vedanāya so tato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca diṭṭhānusayañca vicikicchānusayañca bhavarāgānusayañca nappajahati, no ca so tato avijjānusayaṃ nappajahati. Sveva puggalo apariyāpanne so tato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca diṭṭhānusayañca vicikicchānusayañca bhavarāgānusayañca nappajahati avijjānusayañca nappajahati. Dvinnaṃ maggasamaṅgīnañca aṭṭhamakañca ṭhapetvā avasesā puggalā sabbattha kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca diṭṭhānusayañca vicikicchānusayañca bhavarāgānusayañca nappajahanti avijjānusayañca nappajahanti.

A person endowed with the supreme path, in painful feeling, is not abandoning from that sphere the underlying tendency to sensual desire, the underlying tendency to aversion, the underlying tendency to conceit, the underlying tendency to views, the underlying tendency to doubt, and the underlying tendency to craving for existence; but he is abandoning from that sphere the underlying tendency to ignorance. That same person, in the supramundane states, is not abandoning from that sphere the underlying tendency to sensual desire, the underlying tendency to aversion, the underlying tendency to conceit, the underlying tendency to views, the underlying tendency to doubt, the underlying tendency to craving for existence, and the underlying tendency to ignorance. Setting aside the two persons endowed with the path and the eighth person, the remaining persons are not abandoning in all spheres the underlying tendency to sensual desire, the underlying tendency to aversion, the underlying tendency to conceit, the underlying tendency to views, the underlying tendency to doubt, the underlying tendency to craving for existence, and the underlying tendency to ignorance.

(Kha) yo [V 2.0243] vā pana yato avijjānusayaṃ nappajahati so tato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca diṭṭhānusayañca [T 1.0615] vicikicchānusayañca bhavarāgānusayañca nappajahatīti?

Or, does a person who is not abandoning the underlying tendency to ignorance from a certain sphere not abandon from that sphere the underlying tendency to sensual desire, the underlying tendency to aversion, the underlying tendency to conceit, the underlying tendency to views, the underlying tendency to doubt, and the underlying tendency to craving for existence?

Aṭṭhamako kāmadhātuyā tīsu vedanāsu rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā so tato avijjānusayañca kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca bhavarāgānusayañca nappajahati, no ca so tato diṭṭhānusayañca vicikicchānusayañca nappajahati. Sveva puggalo apariyāpanne so tato avijjānusayañca nappajahati kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca diṭṭhānusayañca vicikicchānusayañca bhavarāgānusayañca nappajahati. Anāgāmimaggasamaṅgī dukkhāya vedanāya so tato avijjānusayañca kāmarāgānusayañca mānānusayañca diṭṭhānusayañca vicikicchānusayañca bhavarāgānusayañca nappajahati, no ca so tato paṭighānusayaṃ nappajahati. Sveva puggalo kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu so tato avijjānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca diṭṭhānusayañca vicikicchānusayañca bhavarāgānusayañca nappajahati, no ca so tato [M 2.0188] kāmarāgānusayaṃ nappajahati. Sveva puggalo rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā apariyāpanne so tato avijjānusayañca nappajahati kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca diṭṭhānusayañca vicikicchānusayañca bhavarāgānusayañca nappajahati. Dvinnaṃ maggasamaṅgīnañca aṭṭhamakañca ṭhapetvā avasesā puggalā sabbattha avijjānusayañca nappajahanti kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca diṭṭhānusayañca vicikicchānusayañca bhavarāgānusayañca nappajahanti. (Chakkamūlakaṃ)

The eighth person, in the sense-sphere, in the three feelings, in the form-sphere, and in the formless-sphere, is not abandoning from that sphere the underlying tendency to ignorance, the underlying tendency to sensual desire, the underlying tendency to aversion, the underlying tendency to conceit, and the underlying tendency to craving for existence; but he is abandoning from that sphere the underlying tendency to views and the underlying tendency to doubt. That same person, in the supramundane states, is not abandoning from that sphere the underlying tendency to ignorance, the underlying tendency to sensual desire, the underlying tendency to aversion, the underlying tendency to conceit, the underlying tendency to views, the underlying tendency to doubt, and the underlying tendency to craving for existence. A person endowed with the path of non-returning, in painful feeling, is not abandoning from that sphere the underlying tendency to ignorance, the underlying tendency to sensual desire, the underlying tendency to conceit, the underlying tendency to views, the underlying tendency to doubt, and the underlying tendency to craving for existence; but he is abandoning from that sphere the underlying tendency to aversion. That same person, in the sense-sphere and in two feelings, is not abandoning from that sphere the underlying tendency to ignorance, the underlying tendency to aversion, the underlying tendency to conceit, the underlying tendency to views, the underlying tendency to doubt, and the underlying tendency to craving for existence; but he is abandoning from that sphere the underlying tendency to sensual desire. That same person, in the form-sphere, the formless-sphere, and in the supramundane states, is not abandoning from that sphere the underlying tendency to ignorance, the underlying tendency to sensual desire, the underlying tendency to aversion, the underlying tendency to conceit, the underlying tendency to views, the underlying tendency to doubt, and the underlying tendency to craving for existence. Setting aside the two persons endowed with the path and the eighth person, the remaining persons are not abandoning in all spheres the underlying tendency to ignorance, the underlying tendency to sensual desire, the underlying tendency to aversion, the underlying tendency to conceit, the underlying tendency to views, the underlying tendency to doubt, and the underlying tendency to craving for existence. (The Six-Rooted Section)

Pajahanāvāre paṭilomaṃ.

Pajahanavāro.

213. (Ka) yato vicikicchānusayaṃ parijānāti tato bhavarāgānusayaṃ parijānātīti?

213. (a) Where one comprehends the latent tendency of doubt, does one there comprehend the latent tendency of lust for becoming?

Kāmadhātuyā tīsu vedanāsu tato vicikicchānusayaṃ parijānāti, no ca tato bhavarāgānusayaṃ parijānāti. Rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā tato vicikicchānusayañca parijānāti bhavarāgānusayañca parijānāti.

In the sense-sphere realm, in the three feelings, one there comprehends the latent tendency of doubt, but one does not there comprehend the latent tendency of lust for becoming. In the form realm and in the formless realm, one there comprehends both the latent tendency of doubt and the latent tendency of lust for becoming.

(Kha) yato vā pana bhavarāgānusayaṃ parijānāti tato vicikicchānusayaṃ parijānātīti? Āmantā.

(b) Or again, where one comprehends the latent tendency of lust for becoming, does one there comprehend the latent tendency of doubt? Yes.

(Ka) yato vicikicchānusayaṃ parijānāti tato avijjānusayaṃ parijānātīti? Āmantā.

(a) Where one comprehends the latent tendency of doubt, does one there comprehend the latent tendency of ignorance? Yes.

(Kha) yato [V 2.0252] vā pana avijjānusayaṃ parijānāti tato vicikicchānusayaṃ parijānātīti? Āmantā.

(b) Or again, where one comprehends the latent tendency of ignorance, does one there comprehend the latent tendency of doubt? Yes.

214. (Ka) yato bhavarāgānusayaṃ parijānāti tato avijjānusayaṃ parijānātīti? Āmantā.

214. (a) Where one comprehends the latent tendency of lust for becoming, does one there comprehend the latent tendency of ignorance? Yes.

(Kha) yato vā pana avijjānusayaṃ parijānāti tato bhavarāgānusayaṃ parijānātīti?

(b) Or again, where one comprehends the latent tendency of ignorance, does one there comprehend the latent tendency of lust for becoming?

Kāmadhātuyā tīsu vedanāsu tato avijjānusayaṃ parijānāti, no ca tato bhavarāgānusayaṃ parijānāti. Rūpadhātuyā [T 1.0623] arūpadhātuyā tato avijjānusayañca parijānāti bhavarāgānusayañca parijānāti. (Ekamūlakaṃ)

In the sense-sphere realm, in the three feelings, one there comprehends the latent tendency of ignorance, but one does not there comprehend the latent tendency of lust for becoming. In the form realm and in the formless realm, one there comprehends both the latent tendency of ignorance and the latent tendency of lust for becoming. (Single-rooted section)

215. (Ka) yato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca parijānāti tato mānānusayaṃ parijānātīti? Natthi.

215. (a) Where one comprehends both the latent tendency of sensual lust and the latent tendency of aversion, does one there comprehend the latent tendency of conceit? There is no such case.

(Kha) yato vā pana mānānusayaṃ parijānāti tato [M 2.0194] kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca parijānātīti?

(b) Or again, where one comprehends the latent tendency of conceit, does one there comprehend both the latent tendency of sensual lust and the latent tendency of aversion?

Rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā tato mānānusayaṃ parijānāti, no ca tato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca parijānāti. Kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu tato mānānusayañca kāmarāgānusayañca parijānāti, no ca tato paṭighānusayaṃ parijānāti.

In the form realm and in the formless realm, one there comprehends the latent tendency of conceit, but one does not there comprehend both the latent tendency of sensual lust and the latent tendency of aversion. In the sense-sphere realm, in the two feelings, one there comprehends both the latent tendency of conceit and the latent tendency of sensual lust, but one does not there comprehend the latent tendency of aversion.

Yato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca parijānāti tato diṭṭhānusayaṃ…pe… vicikicchānusayaṃ parijānātīti? Natthi.

Where one comprehends both the latent tendency of sensual lust and the latent tendency of aversion, does one there comprehend the latent tendency of views... the latent tendency of doubt? There is no such case.

Yato vā pana vicikicchānusayaṃ parijānāti tato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca parijānātīti?

Or again, where one comprehends the latent tendency of doubt, does one there comprehend both the latent tendency of sensual lust and the latent tendency of aversion?

Rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā tato vicikicchānusayaṃ parijānāti, no ca tato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca parijānāti. Kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu tato vicikicchānusayañca kāmarāgānusayañca parijānāti[V 2.0253], no ca tato paṭighānusayaṃ parijānāti. Dukkhāya vedanāya tato vicikicchānusayañca paṭighānusayañca parijānāti, no ca tato kāmarāgānusayaṃ parijānāti.

In the form element and in the formless element, one therefrom comprehends the latent tendency of doubt, but one does not therefrom comprehend both the latent tendency of sensual lust and the latent tendency of aversion. In the sense element, in two feelings, one therefrom comprehends both the latent tendency of doubt and the latent tendency of sensual lust, but one does not therefrom comprehend the latent tendency of aversion. In painful feeling, one therefrom comprehends both the latent tendency of doubt and the latent tendency of aversion, but one does not therefrom comprehend the latent tendency of sensual lust.

(Ka) yato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca parijānāti tato bhavarāgānusayaṃ parijānātīti? Natthi.

(a) Wherefrom one comprehends both the latent tendency of sensual lust and the latent tendency of aversion, does one therefrom comprehend the latent tendency of lust for becoming? There is no such case.

(Kha) yato vā pana bhavarāgānusayaṃ parijānāti tato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca parijānātīti? No.

(b) Or again, wherefrom one comprehends the latent tendency of lust for becoming, does one therefrom comprehend both the latent tendency of sensual lust and the latent tendency of aversion? No.

(Ka) yato kāmarāgānusayañca [T 1.0624] paṭighānusayañca parijānāti tato avijjānusayaṃ parijānātīti? Natthi.

(a) Wherefrom one comprehends both the latent tendency of sensual lust and the latent tendency of aversion, does one therefrom comprehend the latent tendency of ignorance? There is no such case.

(Kha) yato vā pana avijjānusayaṃ parijānāti tato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca parijānātīti?

(b) Or again, wherefrom one comprehends the latent tendency of ignorance, does one therefrom comprehend both the latent tendency of sensual lust and the latent tendency of aversion?

Rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā tato avijjānusayaṃ parijānāti, no ca tato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca parijānāti. Kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu tato avijjānusayañca kāmarāgānusayañca parijānāti, no ca tato paṭighānusayaṃ parijānāti. Dukkhāya vedanāya tato avijjānusayañca paṭighānusayañca parijānāti, no ca tato kāmarāgānusayaṃ parijānāti. (Dukamūlakaṃ)

In the form element and in the formless element, one therefrom comprehends the latent tendency of ignorance, but one does not therefrom comprehend both the latent tendency of sensual lust and the latent tendency of aversion. In the sense element, in two feelings, one therefrom comprehends both the latent tendency of ignorance and the latent tendency of sensual lust, but one does not therefrom comprehend the latent tendency of aversion. In painful feeling, one therefrom comprehends both the latent tendency of ignorance and the latent tendency of aversion, but one does not therefrom comprehend the latent tendency of sensual lust. (Double-rooted section)

216. Yato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca parijānāti tato diṭṭhānusayaṃ…pe… vicikicchānusayaṃ parijānātīti? Natthi[M 2.0195].

216. Wherefrom one comprehends the latent tendencies of sensual lust, aversion, and conceit, does one therefrom comprehend the latent tendency of views and the latent tendency of doubt? There is no such case.

Yato vā pana vicikicchānusayaṃ parijānāti tato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca parijānātīti?

Or again, wherefrom one comprehends the latent tendency of doubt, does one therefrom comprehend the latent tendencies of sensual lust, aversion, and conceit?

Rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā tato vicikicchānusayañca mānānusayañca parijānāti, no ca tato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca parijānāti. Kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu tato vicikicchānusayañca kāmarāgānusayañca mānānusayañca parijānāti, no ca tato paṭighānusayaṃ parijānāti. Dukkhāya vedanāya tato vicikicchānusayañca paṭighānusayañca [V 2.0254] parijānāti, no ca tato kāmarāgānusayañca mānānusayañca parijānāti.

In the sense element, in two feelings, one therefrom comprehends the latent tendencies of doubt, sensual lust, and conceit, but one does not therefrom comprehend the latent tendency of aversion. In painful feeling, one therefrom comprehends both the latent tendency of doubt and the latent tendency of aversion, but one does not therefrom comprehend both the latent tendency of sensual lust and the latent tendency of conceit.

(a) Wherefrom one comprehends the latent tendencies of sensual lust, aversion, and conceit, does one therefrom comprehend the latent tendency of lust for becoming? There is no such case.

(b) Or again, wherefrom one comprehends the latent tendency of lust for becoming, does one therefrom comprehend the latent tendencies of sensual lust, aversion, and conceit?

Rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā tato bhavarāgānusayañca mānānusayañca parijānāti, no ca tato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca parijānāti.

In the form element and the formless element, therefrom one comprehends the latent tendency of lust for becoming and the latent tendency of conceit, but therefrom one does not comprehend the latent tendency of sensual lust and the latent tendency of aversion.

(Ka) yato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca parijānāti tato avijjānusayaṃ parijānātīti? Natthi.

(a) Wherefrom one comprehends the latent tendency of sensual lust, the latent tendency of aversion, and the latent tendency of conceit, does one therefrom comprehend the latent tendency of ignorance? There is no such case.

(b) Or again, wherefrom one comprehends the latent tendency of ignorance, does one therefrom comprehend the latent tendency of sensual lust, the latent tendency of aversion, and the latent tendency of conceit?

Kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu tato avijjānusayañca kāmarāgānusayañca mānānusayañca parijānāti, no ca tato paṭighānusayaṃ parijānāti. Dukkhāya vedanāya tato avijjānusayañca paṭighānusayañca parijānāti, no ca tato kāmarāgānusayañca mānānusayañca parijānāti. (Tikamūlakaṃ)

In the form element and the formless element, therefrom one comprehends the latent tendency of ignorance and the latent tendency of conceit, but therefrom one does not comprehend the latent tendency of sensual lust and the latent tendency of aversion. In the sense element, in two feelings, therefrom one comprehends the latent tendency of ignorance, the latent tendency of sensual lust, and the latent tendency of conceit, but therefrom one does not comprehend the latent tendency of aversion. In painful feeling, therefrom one comprehends the latent tendency of ignorance and the latent tendency of aversion, but therefrom one does not comprehend the latent tendency of sensual lust and the latent tendency of conceit. (Triple-rooted section)

217. (Ka) yato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca diṭṭhānusayañca parijānāti tato vicikicchānusayaṃ parijānātīti? Natthi.

Kāmadhātuyā [M 2.0196] dvīsu vedanāsu tato vicikicchānusayañca kāmarāgānusayañca mānānusayañca diṭṭhānusayañca parijānāti, no ca tato [T 1.0626] paṭighānusayaṃ parijānāti. Dukkhāya vedanāya tato vicikicchānusayañca paṭighānusayañca diṭṭhānusayañca parijānāti, no ca tato kāmarāgānusayañca mānānusayañca parijānāti …pe…. (Catukkamūlakaṃ)

In the form element and the formless element, therefrom one comprehends the latent tendency of doubt, the latent tendency of conceit, and the latent tendency of views, but therefrom one does not comprehend the latent tendency of sensual lust and the latent tendency of aversion. 218. (Ka) yato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca diṭṭhānusayañca vicikicchānusayañca parijānāti tato bhavarāgānusayaṃ parijānātīti? Natthi.

218. (a) Wherefrom one comprehends the latent tendency of sensual lust, the latent tendency of aversion, the latent tendency of conceit, the latent tendency of views, and the latent tendency of doubt, does one therefrom comprehend the latent tendency of lust for becoming? There is no such case.

Rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā tato bhavarāgānusayañca mānānusayañca diṭṭhānusayañca vicikicchānusayañca parijānāti, no ca tato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca parijānāti.

In the form element and the formless element, therefrom one comprehends the latent tendency of lust for becoming, the latent tendency of conceit, the latent tendency of views, and the latent tendency of doubt, but therefrom one does not comprehend the latent tendency of sensual lust and the latent tendency of aversion.

(Ka) yato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca diṭṭhānusayañca vicikicchānusayañca parijānāti tato avijjānusayaṃ parijānātīti? Natthi.

(Ka) Wherefrom one comprehends the latent tendency to sensual lust, the latent tendency to aversion, the latent tendency to conceit, the latent tendency to views, and the latent tendency to doubt, does one therefrom comprehend the latent tendency to ignorance? No.

(Kha) yato vā pana avijjānusayaṃ parijānāti tato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca diṭṭhānusayañca vicikicchānusayañca parijānātīti?

(Kha) Or again, wherefrom one comprehends the latent tendency to ignorance, does one therefrom comprehend the latent tendency to sensual lust, the latent tendency to aversion, the latent tendency to conceit, the latent tendency to views, and the latent tendency to doubt?

Rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā tato avijjānusayañca mānānusayañca diṭṭhānusayañca vicikicchānusayañca parijānāti, no ca tato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca parijānāti. Kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu tato avijjānusayañca kāmarāgānusayañca mānānusayañca diṭṭhānusayañca vicikicchānusayañca parijānāti, no ca tato paṭighānusayaṃ parijānāti. Dukkhāya vedanāya tato avijjānusayañca paṭighānusayañca [T 1.0627][V 2.0256] diṭṭhānusayañca vicikicchānusayañca parijānāti, no ca tato kāmarāgānusayañca mānānusayañca parijānāti. (Pañcakamūlakaṃ)

In the form realm and the formless realm, therefrom one comprehends the latent tendency to ignorance, the latent tendency to conceit, the latent tendency to views, and the latent tendency to doubt, but therefrom one does not comprehend the latent tendency to sensual lust and the latent tendency to aversion. In the sensual realm, in two feelings, therefrom one comprehends the latent tendency to ignorance, the latent tendency to sensual lust, the latent tendency to conceit, the latent tendency to views, and the latent tendency to doubt, but therefrom one does not comprehend the latent tendency to aversion. With painful feeling, therefrom one comprehends the latent tendency to ignorance, the latent tendency to aversion, the latent tendency to views, and the latent tendency to doubt, but therefrom one does not comprehend the latent tendency to sensual lust and the latent tendency to conceit.

219. (Ka) yato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca diṭṭhānusayañca vicikicchānusayañca bhavarāgānusayañca parijānāti tato avijjānusayaṃ parijānātīti? Natthi.

219. (Ka) Wherefrom one comprehends the latent tendency to sensual lust, the latent tendency to aversion, the latent tendency to conceit, the latent tendency to views, the latent tendency to doubt, and the latent tendency to lust for becoming, does one therefrom comprehend the latent tendency to ignorance? No.

(Kha) yato vā pana avijjānusayaṃ parijānāti tato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca diṭṭhānusayañca vicikicchānusayañca bhavarāgānusayañca parijānātīti?

(Kha) Or again, wherefrom one comprehends the latent tendency to ignorance, does one therefrom comprehend the latent tendency to sensual lust, the latent tendency to aversion, the latent tendency to conceit, the latent tendency to views, the latent tendency to doubt, and the latent tendency to lust for becoming?

Rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā tato avijjānusayañca mānānusayañca diṭṭhānusayañca [M 2.0197] vicikicchānusayañca bhavarāgānusayañca parijānāti, no ca tato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca parijānāti. Kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu tato avijjānusayañca kāmarāgānusayañca mānānusayañca diṭṭhānusayañca vicikicchānusayañca parijānāti, no ca tato paṭighānusayañca bhavarāgānusayañca parijānāti. Dukkhāya vedanāya tato avijjānusayañca paṭighānusayañca diṭṭhānusayañca vicikicchānusayañca parijānāti, no ca tato kāmarāgānusayañca mānānusayañca bhavarāgānusayañca parijānāti. (Chakkamūlakaṃ)

In the form realm and the formless realm, therefrom one comprehends the latent tendency to ignorance, the latent tendency to conceit, the latent tendency to views, the latent tendency to doubt, and the latent tendency to lust for becoming, but therefrom one does not comprehend the latent tendency to sensual lust and the latent tendency to aversion. In the sensual realm, in two feelings, therefrom one comprehends the latent tendency to ignorance, the latent tendency to sensual lust, the latent tendency to conceit, the latent tendency to views, and the latent tendency to doubt, but therefrom one does not comprehend the latent tendency to aversion and the latent tendency to lust for becoming. With painful feeling, therefrom one comprehends the latent tendency to ignorance, the latent tendency to aversion, the latent tendency to views, and the latent tendency to doubt, but therefrom one does not comprehend the latent tendency to sensual lust, the latent tendency to conceit, and the latent tendency to lust for becoming.
