(Ga) Forward Order: Person and Occasion

220. (Ka) yo yato kāmarāgānusayaṃ parijānāti so tato paṭighānusayaṃ parijānātīti? No.

220. (Ka) Does a person who comprehends the latent tendency of sensual lust in any sphere, therefrom comprehend the latent tendency of aversion in that sphere? No.

(Kha) yo vā pana yato paṭighānusayaṃ parijānāti so tato kāmarāgānusayaṃ parijānātīti? No.

(Kha) Or conversely, does a person who comprehends the latent tendency of aversion in any sphere, therefrom comprehend the latent tendency of sensual lust in that sphere? No.

(Ka) yo yato kāmarāgānusayaṃ parijānāti so tato mānānusayaṃ parijānātīti?

(Ka) Does a person who comprehends the latent tendency of sensual lust in any sphere, therefrom comprehend the latent tendency of conceit in that sphere?

Tadekaṭṭhaṃ parijānāti[T 1.0628].

He comprehends it in part, as it shares the same basis.

(Kha) yo [V 2.0257] vā pana yato mānānusayaṃ parijānāti so tato kāmarāgānusayaṃ parijānātīti? No.

(Kha) Or conversely, does a person who comprehends the latent tendency of conceit in any sphere, therefrom comprehend the latent tendency of sensual lust in that sphere? No.

Yo yato kāmarāgānusayaṃ parijānāti so tato diṭṭhānusayaṃ…pe… vicikicchānusayaṃ parijānātīti? No.

Does a person who comprehends the latent tendency of sensual lust in any sphere, therefrom comprehend the latent tendency of views... the latent tendency of doubt in that sphere? No.

Yo vā pana yato vicikicchānusayaṃ parijānāti so tato kāmarāgānusayaṃ parijānātīti?

Or conversely, does a person who comprehends the latent tendency of doubt in any sphere, therefrom comprehend the latent tendency of sensual lust in that sphere?

Aṭṭhamako dukkhāya vedanāya rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā so tato vicikicchānusayaṃ parijānāti, no ca so tato kāmarāgānusayaṃ parijānāti. Sveva puggalo kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu so tato vicikicchānusayaṃ parijānāti, kāmarāgānusayaṃ tadekaṭṭhaṃ parijānāti.

The eighth person (the one on the path of stream-entry), in regard to painful feeling, the form realm, and the formless realm, comprehends the latent tendency of doubt, but does not therefrom comprehend the latent tendency of sensual lust. That same person, in regard to the sensual realm and two feelings, comprehends the latent tendency of doubt, and comprehends in part the latent tendency of sensual lust, as it shares the same basis.

(Ka) yo yato kāmarāgānusayaṃ parijānāti so tato bhavarāgānusayaṃ parijānātīti? No.

(Ka) Does a person who comprehends the latent tendency of sensual lust in any sphere, therefrom comprehend the latent tendency of craving for existence in that sphere? No.

(Kha) yo vā pana yato bhavarāgānusayaṃ parijānāti so tato kāmarāgānusayaṃ parijānātīti? No.

(Kha) Or conversely, does a person who comprehends the latent tendency of craving for existence in any sphere, therefrom comprehend the latent tendency of sensual lust in that sphere? No.

(Ka) yo yato kāmarāgānusayaṃ parijānāti so tato avijjānusayaṃ parijānātīti?

(Ka) Does a person who comprehends the latent tendency of sensual lust in any sphere, therefrom comprehend the latent tendency of ignorance in that sphere?

Tadekaṭṭhaṃ parijānāti.

He comprehends it in part, as it shares the same basis.

(Kha) yo vā pana yato [M 2.0198] avijjānusayaṃ parijānāti so tato kāmarāgānusayaṃ parijānātīti? No.

(Kha) Or conversely, does a person who comprehends the latent tendency of ignorance in any sphere, therefrom comprehend the latent tendency of sensual lust in that sphere? No.

221. (Ka) yo yato paṭighānusayaṃ parijānāti so tato mānānusayaṃ parijānātīti? No.

221. (Ka) Does a person who comprehends the latent tendency of aversion in any sphere, therefrom comprehend the latent tendency of conceit in that sphere? No.

(Kha) yo vā pana yato mānānusayaṃ parijānāti so tato paṭighānusayaṃ parijānātīti? No.

(Kha) Or conversely, does a person who comprehends the latent tendency of conceit in any sphere, therefrom comprehend the latent tendency of aversion in that sphere? No.

Yo yato paṭighānusayaṃ parijānāti so tato diṭṭhānusayaṃ…pe… vicikicchānusayaṃ parijānātīti? No.

Does a person who comprehends the latent tendency of aversion in any sphere, therefrom comprehend the latent tendency of views... the latent tendency of doubt in that sphere? No.

Yo [V 2.0258] vā pana yato vicikicchānusayaṃ parijānāti so tato paṭighānusayaṃ parijānātīti?

Or conversely, does a person who comprehends the latent tendency of doubt in any sphere, therefrom comprehend the latent tendency of aversion in that sphere?

Aṭṭhamako kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu rūpadhātuyā [T 1.0629] arūpadhātuyā so tato vicikicchānusayaṃ parijānāti, no ca so tato paṭighānusayaṃ parijānāti. Sveva puggalo dukkhāya vedanāya so tato vicikicchānusayaṃ parijānāti, paṭighānusayaṃ tadekaṭṭhaṃ parijānāti.

The eighth person (the one on the path of stream-entry), in regard to the sensual realm, two feelings, the form realm, and the formless realm, comprehends the latent tendency of doubt, but does not therefrom comprehend the latent tendency of aversion. That same person, in regard to painful feeling, comprehends the latent tendency of doubt, and comprehends in part the latent tendency of aversion, as it shares the same basis.

(Ka) yo yato paṭighānusayaṃ parijānāti so tato bhavarāgānusayaṃ parijānātīti? No.

(Ka) Does a person who comprehends the latent tendency of aversion in any sphere, therefrom comprehend the latent tendency of craving for existence in that sphere? No.

(Kha) yo vā pana yato bhavarāgānusayaṃ parijānāti so tato paṭighānusayaṃ parijānātīti? No.

(Kha) Or conversely, does a person who comprehends the latent tendency of craving for existence in any sphere, therefrom comprehend the latent tendency of aversion in that sphere? No.

(Ka) yo yato paṭighānusayaṃ parijānāti so tato avijjānusayaṃ parijānātīti?

(Ka) Does a person who comprehends the latent tendency of aversion in any sphere, therefrom comprehend the latent tendency of ignorance in that sphere?

Tadekaṭṭhaṃ parijānāti.

He comprehends it in part, as it shares the same basis.

(Kha) yo vā pana yato avijjānusayaṃ parijānāti so tato paṭighānusayaṃ parijānātīti? No.

(Kha) Or conversely, does a person who comprehends the latent tendency of ignorance in any sphere, therefrom comprehend the latent tendency of aversion in that sphere? No.

222. Yo yato mānānusayaṃ parijānāti so tato diṭṭhānusayaṃ…pe… vicikicchānusayaṃ parijānātīti? No.

222. Does a person who comprehends the latent tendency of conceit in any sphere, therefrom comprehend the latent tendency of views... the latent tendency of doubt in that sphere? No.

Yo vā pana yato vicikicchānusayaṃ parijānāti so tato mānānusayaṃ parijānātīti?

Or conversely, does a person who comprehends the latent tendency of doubt in any sphere, therefrom comprehend the latent tendency of conceit in that sphere?

Aṭṭhamako dukkhāya vedanāya so tato vicikicchānusayaṃ parijānāti, no ca so tato mānānusayaṃ parijānāti. Sveva puggalo kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā so tato vicikicchānusayaṃ parijānāti, mānānusayaṃ tadekaṭṭhaṃ parijānāti.

The eighth person, with respect to painful feeling, from that fully comprehends the latent tendency of doubt, but from that does not fully comprehend the latent tendency of conceit. That same person, with respect to the sensual realm, two feelings, the form realm, and the formless realm, from that fully comprehends the latent tendency of doubt, and partially comprehends the latent tendency of conceit which has the same object.

(Ka) yo yato mānānusayaṃ parijānāti so tato bhavarāgānusayaṃ parijānātīti?

Does a person who, from a certain sphere, fully comprehends the latent tendency of conceit, from that sphere also fully comprehend the latent tendency of craving for existence?

Aggamaggasamaṅgī [V 2.0259] kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu so [M 2.0199] tato mānānusayaṃ parijānāti, no ca so tato bhavarāgānusayaṃ parijānāti. Sveva puggalo rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā so tato mānānusayañca parijānāti bhavarāgānusayañca parijānāti.

One endowed with the highest path, with respect to the sensual realm and two feelings, from that fully comprehends the latent tendency of conceit, but from that does not fully comprehend the latent tendency of craving for existence. That same person, with respect to the form realm and the formless realm, from that fully comprehends both the latent tendency of conceit and the latent tendency of craving for existence.

(Kha) yo [T 1.0630] vā pana yato bhavarāgānusayaṃ parijānāti so tato mānānusayaṃ parijānātīti? Āmantā.

Or again, does a person who, from a certain sphere, fully comprehends the latent tendency of craving for existence, from that sphere also fully comprehend the latent tendency of conceit? Yes.

(Ka) yo yato mānānusayaṃ parijānāti so tato avijjānusayaṃ parijānātīti? Āmantā.

Does a person who, from a certain sphere, fully comprehends the latent tendency of conceit, from that sphere also fully comprehend the latent tendency of ignorance? Yes.

(Kha) yo vā pana yato avijjānusayaṃ parijānāti so tato mānānusayaṃ parijānātīti?

Or again, does a person who, from a certain sphere, fully comprehends the latent tendency of ignorance, from that sphere also fully comprehend the latent tendency of conceit?

Aggamaggasamaṅgī dukkhāya vedanāya so tato avijjānusayaṃ parijānāti, no ca so tato mānānusayaṃ parijānāti. Sveva puggalo kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā so tato avijjānusayañca parijānāti mānānusayañca parijānāti.

One endowed with the highest path, with respect to painful feeling, from that fully comprehends the latent tendency of ignorance, but from that does not fully comprehend the latent tendency of conceit. That same person, with respect to the sensual realm, two feelings, the form realm, and the formless realm, from that fully comprehends both the latent tendency of ignorance and the latent tendency of conceit.

223. (Ka) yo yato diṭṭhānusayaṃ parijānāti so tato vicikicchānusayaṃ parijānātīti? Āmantā.

223. Does a person who, from a certain sphere, fully comprehends the latent tendency of views, from that sphere also fully comprehend the latent tendency of doubt? Yes.

(Kha) yo vā pana yato vicikicchānusayaṃ parijānāti so tato diṭṭhānusayaṃ parijānātīti? Āmantā …pe….

Or again, does a person who, from a certain sphere, fully comprehends the latent tendency of doubt, from that sphere also fully comprehend the latent tendency of views? Yes. …

224. (Ka) yo yato vicikicchānusayaṃ parijānāti so tato bhavarāgānusayaṃ parijānātīti?

224. Does a person who, from a certain sphere, fully comprehends the latent tendency of doubt, from that sphere also fully comprehend the latent tendency of craving for existence?

Aṭṭhamako kāmadhātuyā tīsu vedanāsu so tato vicikicchānusayaṃ parijānāti, no ca so tato bhavarāgānusayaṃ parijānāti. Sveva puggalo rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā so tato vicikicchānusayaṃ parijānāti, bhavarāgānusayaṃ tadekaṭṭhaṃ parijānāti.

The eighth person, with respect to the sensual realm and the three feelings, from that fully comprehends the latent tendency of doubt, but from that does not fully comprehend the latent tendency of craving for existence. That same person, with respect to the form realm and the formless realm, from that fully comprehends the latent tendency of doubt, and partially comprehends the latent tendency of craving for existence which has the same object.

(Kha) yo vā pana yato bhavarāgānusayaṃ parijānāti so tato vicikicchānusayaṃ parijānātīti? No.

Or again, does a person who, from a certain sphere, fully comprehends the latent tendency of craving for existence, from that sphere also fully comprehend the latent tendency of doubt? No.

(Ka) yo [V 2.0260] yato vicikicchānusayaṃ parijānāti so tato avijjānusayaṃ parijānātīti?

Does a person who, from a certain sphere, fully comprehends the latent tendency of doubt, from that sphere also fully comprehend the latent tendency of ignorance?

Tadekaṭṭhaṃ parijānāti.

He partially comprehends that which has the same object.

(Kha) yo vā pana yato avijjānusayaṃ parijānāti so tato vicikicchānusayaṃ parijānātīti? No.

Or again, does a person who, from a certain sphere, fully comprehends the latent tendency of ignorance, from that sphere also fully comprehend the latent tendency of doubt? No.

225. (Ka) yo [T 1.0631] yato bhavarāgānusayaṃ parijānāti so tato avijjānusayaṃ parijānātīti? Āmantā.

225. Does a person who, from a certain sphere, fully comprehends the latent tendency of craving for existence, from that sphere also fully comprehend the latent tendency of ignorance? Yes.

(Kha) yo vā pana yato avijjānusayaṃ parijānāti so tato bhavarāgānusayaṃ parijānātīti?

Or again, does a person who, from a certain sphere, fully comprehends the latent tendency of ignorance, from that sphere also fully comprehend the latent tendency of craving for existence?

Aggamaggasamaṅgī [M 2.0200] kāmadhātuyā tīsu vedanāsu so tato avijjānusayaṃ parijānāti, no ca so tato bhavarāgānusayaṃ parijānāti. Sveva puggalo rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā so tato avijjānusayañca parijānāti bhavarāgānusayañca parijānāti. (Ekamūlakaṃ)

One endowed with the highest path, with respect to the sensual realm and the three feelings, from that fully comprehends the latent tendency of ignorance, but from that does not fully comprehend the latent tendency of craving for existence. That same person, with respect to the form realm and the formless realm, from that fully comprehends both the latent tendency of ignorance and the latent tendency of craving for existence. (Single-rooted section)

226. (Ka) yo yato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca parijānāti so tato mānānusayaṃ parijānātīti? Natthi.

226. Does a person who, from a certain sphere, fully comprehends both the latent tendency of sensual desire and the latent tendency of aversion, from that sphere also fully comprehend the latent tendency of conceit? There is not.

(Kha) yo vā pana yato mānānusayaṃ parijānāti so tato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca parijānātīti? No.

Or again, does a person who, from a certain sphere, fully comprehends the latent tendency of conceit, from that sphere also fully comprehend both the latent tendency of sensual desire and the latent tendency of aversion? No.

Yo yato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca parijānāti so tato diṭṭhānusayaṃ…pe… vicikicchānusayaṃ parijānātīti? Natthi.

Does a person who, from a certain sphere, fully comprehends both the latent tendency of sensual desire and the latent tendency of aversion, from that sphere also fully comprehend the latent tendency of views… the latent tendency of doubt? There is not.

Yo vā pana yato vicikicchānusayaṃ parijānāti so tato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca parijānātīti?

Or again, does a person who, from a certain sphere, fully comprehends the latent tendency of doubt, from that sphere also fully comprehend both the latent tendency of sensual desire and the latent tendency of aversion?

Aṭṭhamako rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā so tato vicikicchānusayaṃ parijānāti, no ca so tato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca parijānāti. Sveva puggalo kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu so tato vicikicchānusayañca [V 2.0261] parijānāti kāmarāgānusayañca tadekaṭṭhaṃ parijānāti, no ca so tato paṭighānusayaṃ parijānāti. Sveva puggalo dukkhāya vedanāya so tato vicikicchānusayañca parijānāti paṭighānusayañca tadekaṭṭhaṃ parijānāti, no [T 1.0632] ca so tato kāmarāgānusayaṃ parijānāti.

The eighth person, with respect to the form realm and the formless realm, from that fully comprehends the latent tendency of doubt, but from that does not fully comprehend both the latent tendency of sensual desire and the latent tendency of aversion. That same person, with respect to the sensual realm and two feelings, from that fully comprehends the latent tendency of doubt and partially comprehends the latent tendency of sensual desire which has the same object, but from that does not fully comprehend the latent tendency of aversion. That same person, with respect to painful feeling, from that fully comprehends the latent tendency of doubt and partially comprehends the latent tendency of aversion which has the same object, but from that does not fully comprehend the latent tendency of sensual desire.

(Ka) yo yato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca parijānāti so tato bhavarāgānusayaṃ parijānātīti? Natthi.

Does a person who, from a certain sphere, fully comprehends both the latent tendency of sensual desire and the latent tendency of aversion, from that sphere also fully comprehend the latent tendency of craving for existence? There is not.

(Kha) yo vā pana yato bhavarāgānusayaṃ parijānāti so tato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca parijānātīti? No.

Or again, does a person who, from a certain sphere, fully comprehends the latent tendency of craving for existence, from that sphere also fully comprehend both the latent tendency of sensual desire and the latent tendency of aversion? No.

(Ka) yo yato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca parijānāti so tato avijjānusayaṃ parijānātīti? Natthi.

Does a person who, from a certain sphere, fully comprehends both the latent tendency of sensual desire and the latent tendency of aversion, from that sphere also fully comprehend the latent tendency of ignorance? There is not.

(Kha) yo vā pana yato avijjānusayaṃ parijānāti so tato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca parijānātīti? No. (Dukamūlakaṃ)

Or again, does a person who, from a certain sphere, fully comprehends the latent tendency of ignorance, from that sphere also fully comprehend both the latent tendency of sensual desire and the latent tendency of aversion? No. (Section on Pairs)

227. Yo yato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca parijānāti so tato diṭṭhānusayaṃ…pe… vicikicchānusayaṃ parijānātīti? Natthi[M 2.0201].

227. Does a person who, from a certain sphere, fully comprehends the latent tendency of sensual desire, the latent tendency of aversion, and the latent tendency of conceit, from that sphere also fully comprehend the latent tendency of views… the latent tendency of doubt? There is not.

Yo vā pana yato vicikicchānusayaṃ parijānāti so tato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca parijānātīti?

Or again, does a person who, from a certain sphere, fully comprehends the latent tendency of doubt, from that sphere also fully comprehend the latent tendency of sensual desire, the latent tendency of aversion, and the latent tendency of conceit?

Aṭṭhamako rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā so tato vicikicchānusayañca parijānāti mānānusayañca tadekaṭṭhaṃ parijānāti, no ca so tato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca parijānāti. Sveva puggalo kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu so tato vicikicchānusayañca parijānāti kāmarāgānusayañca mānānusayañca tadekaṭṭhaṃ parijānāti, no ca so tato paṭighānusayaṃ parijānāti. Sveva puggalo dukkhāya vedanāya so tato vicikicchānusayañca parijānāti paṭighānusayañca tadekaṭṭhaṃ parijānāti, no ca so tato kāmarāgānusayañca mānānusayañca parijānāti.

The person on the path of stream-entry, in the form realm and the formless realm, fully understands from that the underlying tendency to doubt and partially understands the underlying tendency to conceit which has the same basis, but does not from that fully understand both the underlying tendency to sensual desire and the underlying tendency to aversion. That same person, in the sensual realm, in regard to two feelings, fully understands from that the underlying tendency to doubt and partially understands both the underlying tendency to sensual desire and the underlying tendency to conceit which have the same basis, but does not from that fully understand the underlying tendency to aversion. That same person, in regard to painful feeling, fully understands from that the underlying tendency to doubt and partially understands the underlying tendency to aversion which has the same basis, but does not from that fully understand both the underlying tendency to sensual desire and the underlying tendency to conceit.

(Ka) yo [V 2.0262] yato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca [T 1.0633] parijānāti so tato bhavarāgānusayaṃ parijānātīti? Natthi.

(Ka) Does a person who, in a certain sphere, fully understands the underlying tendency to sensual desire, the underlying tendency to aversion, and the underlying tendency to conceit, also from that sphere fully understand the underlying tendency to craving for existence? There is no such case.

(Kha) yo vā pana yato bhavarāgānusayaṃ parijānāti so tato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca parijānātīti?

(Kha) Or, does a person who, in a certain sphere, fully understands the underlying tendency to craving for existence, also from that sphere fully understand the underlying tendency to sensual desire, the underlying tendency to aversion, and the underlying tendency to conceit?

Mānānusayaṃ parijānāti.

One fully understands the underlying tendency to conceit.

(Ka) yo yato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca parijānāti so tato avijjānusayaṃ parijānātīti? Natthi.

(Ka) Does a person who, in a certain sphere, fully understands the underlying tendency to sensual desire, the underlying tendency to aversion, and the underlying tendency to conceit, also from that sphere fully understand the underlying tendency to ignorance? No.

(Kha) yo vā pana yato avijjānusayaṃ parijānāti so tato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca parijānātīti?

(Kha) Or again, does a person who, in a certain sphere, fully understands the underlying tendency to ignorance, also from that sphere fully understand the underlying tendency to sensual desire, the underlying tendency to aversion, and the underlying tendency to conceit?

Aggamaggasamaṅgī dukkhāya vedanāya so tato avijjānusayaṃ parijānāti, no ca so tato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca parijānāti. Sveva puggalo kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā so tato avijjānusayañca mānānusayañca parijānāti, no ca so tato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca parijānāti. (Tikamūlakaṃ)

One who is endowed with the supreme path, in respect of painful feeling, fully understands from that the underlying tendency to ignorance, but does not from that fully understand the underlying tendencies to sensual desire, aversion, and conceit. That same person, in the sense-sphere realm in respect of two feelings, in the form realm, and in the formless realm, fully understands from that the underlying tendencies to ignorance and conceit, but does not from that fully understand the underlying tendencies to sensual desire and aversion. (Rooted in three)

228. (Ka) yo yato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca diṭṭhānusayañca parijānāti so tato vicikicchānusayaṃ parijānātīti? Natthi.

228. (Ka) Does a person who, in a certain sphere, fully understands the underlying tendency to sensual desire, the underlying tendency to aversion, the underlying tendency to conceit, and the underlying tendency to views, also from that sphere fully understand the underlying tendency to doubt? No.

(Kha) yo vā pana yato vicikicchānusayaṃ parijānāti so tato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca diṭṭhānusayañca parijānātīti?

(Kha) Or again, does a person who, in a certain sphere, fully understands the underlying tendency to doubt, also from that sphere fully understand the underlying tendency to sensual desire, the underlying tendency to aversion, the underlying tendency to conceit, and the underlying tendency to views?

Aṭṭhamako rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā so tato vicikicchānusayañca diṭṭhānusayañca parijānāti mānānusayañca tadekaṭṭhaṃ parijānāti, no [M 2.0202] ca so tato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca parijānāti. Sveva puggalo kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu so tato vicikicchānusayañca [T 1.0634] diṭṭhānusayañca parijānāti kāmarāgānusayañca mānānusayañca tadekaṭṭhaṃ parijānāti, no ca so tato paṭighānusayaṃ parijānāti. Sveva puggalo dukkhāya vedanāya so [V 2.0263] tato vicikicchānusayañca diṭṭhānusayañca parijānāti paṭighānusayañca tadekaṭṭhaṃ parijānāti, no ca so tato kāmarāgānusayañca mānānusayañca parijānāti …pe…. (Catukkamūlakaṃ)

The person on the path of stream-entry, in the form realm and in the formless realm, fully understands from that the underlying tendencies of doubt and views, and partially understands the underlying tendency of conceit which has the same basis, but does not from that fully understand the underlying tendencies of sensual desire and aversion. That same person, in the sense-sphere realm in regard to two feelings, fully understands from that the underlying tendencies of doubt and views, and partially understands the underlying tendencies of sensual desire and conceit which have the same basis, but does not from that fully understand the underlying tendency of aversion. That same person, in regard to painful feeling, fully understands from that the underlying tendencies of doubt and views, and partially understands the underlying tendency of aversion which has the same basis, but does not from that fully understand the underlying tendencies of sensual desire and conceit. (Rooted in four)

229. (Ka) yo yato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca diṭṭhānusayañca vicikicchānusayañca parijānāti so tato bhavarāgānusayaṃ parijānātīti? Natthi.

229. (Ka) Does a person who, in a certain sphere, fully understands the underlying tendency to sensual desire, the underlying tendency to aversion, the underlying tendency to conceit, the underlying tendency to views, and the underlying tendency to doubt, also from that sphere fully understand the underlying tendency to craving for existence? No.

(Kha) yo vā pana yato bhavarāgānusayaṃ parijānāti so tato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca diṭṭhānusayañca vicikicchānusayañca parijānātīti?

(Kha) Or again, does a person who, in a certain sphere, fully understands the underlying tendency to craving for existence, also from that sphere fully understand the underlying tendency to sensual desire, the underlying tendency to aversion, the underlying tendency to conceit, the underlying tendency to views, and the underlying tendency to doubt?

Mānānusayaṃ parijānāti.

He fully understands the underlying tendency to conceit.

(Ka) yo yato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca diṭṭhānusayañca vicikicchānusayañca parijānāti so tato avijjānusayaṃ parijānātīti? Natthi.

(Ka) Does a person who, in a certain sphere, fully understands the underlying tendency to sensual desire, the underlying tendency to aversion, the underlying tendency to conceit, the underlying tendency to views, and the underlying tendency to doubt, also from that sphere fully understand the underlying tendency to ignorance? No.

(Kha) yo vā pana yato avijjānusayaṃ parijānāti so tato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca diṭṭhānusayañca vicikicchānusayañca parijānātīti?

(Kha) Or again, does a person who, in a certain sphere, fully understands the underlying tendency to ignorance, also from that sphere fully understand the underlying tendency to sensual desire, the underlying tendency to aversion, the underlying tendency to conceit, the underlying tendency to views, and the underlying tendency to doubt?

Aggamaggasamaṅgī dukkhāya vedanāya so tato avijjānusayaṃ parijānāti, no ca so tato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca diṭṭhānusayañca vicikicchānusayañca parijānāti. Sveva puggalo kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā so tato avijjānusayañca mānānusayañca parijānāti, no ca so tato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca [T 1.0635] diṭṭhānusayañca vicikicchānusayañca parijānāti. (Pañcakamūlakaṃ)

One who is endowed with the supreme path, in respect of painful feeling, fully understands from that the underlying tendency to ignorance, but does not from that fully understand the underlying tendencies to sensual desire, aversion, conceit, views, and doubt. That same person, in the sense-sphere realm in respect of two feelings, in the form realm, and in the formless realm, fully understands from that the underlying tendencies to ignorance and conceit, but does not from that fully understand the underlying tendencies to sensual desire, aversion, views, and doubt. (Rooted in five)

230. (Ka) yo yato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca diṭṭhānusayañca vicikicchānusayañca bhavarāgānusayañca parijānāti so tato avijjānusayaṃ parijānātīti? Natthi.

230. (Ka) Does a person who, in a certain sphere, fully understands the underlying tendency to sensual desire, the underlying tendency to aversion, the underlying tendency to conceit, the underlying tendency to views, the underlying tendency to doubt, and the underlying tendency to craving for existence, also from that sphere fully understand the underlying tendency to ignorance? No.

(Kha) yo vā pana yato avijjānusayaṃ parijānāti so tato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca diṭṭhānusayañca vicikicchānusayañca bhavarāgānusayañca parijānātīti?

(Kha) Or again, does a person who, in a certain sphere, fully understands the underlying tendency to ignorance, also from that sphere fully understand the underlying tendency to sensual desire, the underlying tendency to aversion, the underlying tendency to conceit, the underlying tendency to views, the underlying tendency to doubt, and the underlying tendency to craving for existence?

Aggamaggasamaṅgī [V 2.0264] dukkhāya vedanāya so tato avijjānusayaṃ parijānāti, no ca so tato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca [M 2.0203] mānānusayañca diṭṭhānusayañca vicikicchānusayañca bhavarāgānusayañca parijānāti. Sveva puggalo kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu so tato avijjānusayañca mānānusayañca parijānāti, no ca so tato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca diṭṭhānusayañca vicikicchānusayañca bhavarāgānusayañca parijānāti. Sveva puggalo rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā so tato avijjānusayañca mānānusayañca bhavarāgānusayañca parijānāti, no ca so tato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca diṭṭhānusayañca vicikicchānusayañca parijānāti. (Chakkamūlakaṃ)

One who is endowed with the supreme path, in respect of painful feeling, fully understands from that the underlying tendency to ignorance, but does not from that fully understand the underlying tendencies to sensual desire, aversion, conceit, views, doubt, and craving for existence. That same person, in the sense-sphere realm in respect of two feelings, fully understands from that the underlying tendencies to ignorance and conceit, but does not from that fully understand the underlying tendencies to sensual desire, aversion, views, doubt, and craving for existence. That same person, in the form realm and in the formless realm, fully understands from that the underlying tendencies to ignorance, conceit, and craving for existence, but does not from that fully understand the underlying tendencies to sensual desire, aversion, views, and doubt.

Pariññāvāre anulomaṃ.

The Forward Section of the Chapter on Full Understanding.

4. Pariññāvāra

4. 7. Underlying Tendencies, Chapter on Full Understanding, Negative.

(Gha) paṭilomapuggalo

(d) The Person (Reverse Questioning)

231. (Ka) yo kāmarāgānusayaṃ na parijānāti so paṭighānusayaṃ na parijānātīti? Āmantā.

231. (a) Does a person who does not fully comprehend the underlying tendency to sensual desire also not fully comprehend the underlying tendency to aversion? Yes.

(Kha) yo vā pana paṭighānusayaṃ na parijānāti so kāmarāgānusayaṃ na parijānātīti? Āmantā.

(b) Or again, does a person who does not fully comprehend the underlying tendency to aversion also not fully comprehend the underlying tendency to sensual desire? Yes.

(Ka) yo kāmarāgānusayaṃ [T 1.0636] na parijānāti so mānānusayaṃ na parijānātīti?

(a) Does a person who does not fully comprehend the underlying tendency to sensual desire also not fully comprehend the underlying tendency to conceit?

Aggamaggasamaṅgī kāmarāgānusayaṃ na parijānāti, no ca so mānānusayaṃ na parijānāti. Dvinnaṃ maggasamaṅgīnaṃ ṭhapetvā avasesā puggalā kāmarāgānusayañca na parijānanti mānānusayañca na parijānanti.

A person endowed with the supreme path does not fully comprehend the underlying tendency to sensual desire, but they do fully comprehend the underlying tendency to conceit. Setting aside the two persons endowed with the path (of the non-returner and of Arahantship), the remaining persons do not fully comprehend either the underlying tendency to sensual desire or the underlying tendency to conceit.

(Kha) yo vā pana mānānusayaṃ na parijānāti so kāmarāgānusayaṃ na parijānātīti?

Anāgāmimaggasamaṅgī [V 2.0265] mānānusayaṃ na parijānāti, no ca so kāmarāgānusayaṃ na parijānāti. Dvinnaṃ maggasamaṅgīnaṃ ṭhapetvā avasesā puggalā mānānusayañca na parijānanti kāmarāgānusayañca na parijānanti.

A person endowed with the path of the non-returner does not fully comprehend the underlying tendency to conceit, but they do fully comprehend the underlying tendency to sensual desire. Setting aside the two persons endowed with the path (of the non-returner and of Arahantship), the remaining persons do not fully comprehend either the underlying tendency to conceit or the underlying tendency to sensual desire.

Yo kāmarāgānusayaṃ na parijānāti so diṭṭhānusayaṃ…pe… vicikicchānusayaṃ na parijānātīti?

Does a person who does not fully comprehend the underlying tendency to sensual desire also not fully comprehend the underlying tendency to views... up to... the underlying tendency to doubt?

Aṭṭhamako kāmarāgānusayaṃ na parijānāti, no ca so vicikicchānusayaṃ na parijānāti. Anāgāmimaggasamaṅgiñca aṭṭhamakañca ṭhapetvā avasesā puggalā kāmarāgānusayañca na parijānanti vicikicchānusayañca na parijānanti.

Setting aside the person endowed with the path of the non-returner and the person on the path of stream-entry, the remaining persons do not fully comprehend either the underlying tendency to sensual desire or the underlying tendency to doubt.

(The Dyad-Root Section)

238. Yo kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca na parijānāti so diṭṭhānusayaṃ…pe… vicikicchānusayaṃ na parijānātīti?

238. Does a person who does not fully comprehend the latent tendency of sensual lust, the latent tendency of aversion, and the latent tendency of conceit, also not fully comprehend the latent tendency of wrong views... and the latent tendency of doubt?

Aṭṭhamako kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca na parijānāti, no ca so vicikicchānusayaṃ na parijānāti. Dvinnaṃ maggasamaṅgīnañca aṭṭhamakañca ṭhapetvā avasesā puggalā kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca na parijānanti vicikicchānusayañca na parijānanti.

The person at the stage of the path of stream-entry does not fully comprehend the latent tendency of sensual lust, the latent tendency of aversion, and the latent tendency of conceit, but it is not that this person does not fully comprehend the latent tendency of doubt. Setting aside the two persons endowed with the path of the non-returner and the path of Arahantship, and the person at the stage of the path of stream-entry, the remaining persons do not fully comprehend the latent tendency of sensual lust, the latent tendency of aversion, and the latent tendency of conceit, and do not fully comprehend the latent tendency of doubt.

Yo vā pana vicikicchānusayaṃ na parijānāti so kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca na parijānātīti?

Or again, does a person who does not fully comprehend the latent tendency of doubt also not fully comprehend the latent tendency of sensual lust, the latent tendency of aversion, and the latent tendency of conceit?

Anāgāmimaggasamaṅgī vicikicchānusayañca mānānusayañca na parijānāti, no ca so kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca na parijānāti. Aggamaggasamaṅgī vicikicchānusayañca kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca na parijānāti, no ca so mānānusayaṃ na parijānāti. Dvinnaṃ [V 2.0271] maggasamaṅgīnañca aṭṭhamakañca ṭhapetvā [T 1.0642] avasesā puggalā vicikicchānusayañca na parijānanti kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca na parijānanti.

A person endowed with the path of the non-returner does not fully comprehend the latent tendency of doubt and the latent tendency of conceit, but it is not that this person does not fully comprehend the latent tendency of sensual lust and the latent tendency of aversion. A person endowed with the highest path does not fully comprehend the latent tendency of doubt, the latent tendency of sensual lust, and the latent tendency of aversion, but it is not that this person does not fully comprehend the latent tendency of conceit. Setting aside the two persons endowed with the path of the non-returner and the path of Arahantship, and the person at the stage of the path of stream-entry, the remaining persons do not fully comprehend the latent tendency of doubt, and do not fully comprehend the latent tendency of sensual lust, the latent tendency of aversion, and the latent tendency of conceit.

Yo kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca na parijānāti so bhavarāgānusayaṃ…pe… avijjānusayaṃ na parijānātīti? Āmantā.

Does a person who does not fully comprehend the latent tendency of sensual lust, the latent tendency of aversion, and the latent tendency of conceit, also not fully comprehend the latent tendency of lust for becoming... and the latent tendency of ignorance? Yes.

Yo vā pana avijjānusayaṃ na parijānāti so kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca na parijānātīti?

Or again, does a person who does not fully comprehend the latent tendency of ignorance also not fully comprehend the latent tendency of sensual lust, the latent tendency of aversion, and the latent tendency of conceit?

Anāgāmimaggasamaṅgī avijjānusayañca mānānusayañca na parijānāti, no ca so kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca na parijānāti. Dvinnaṃ maggasamaṅgīnaṃ ṭhapetvā avasesā puggalā avijjānusayañca na parijānanti kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca na parijānanti. (Tikamūlakaṃ)

A person endowed with the path of the non-returner does not fully comprehend the latent tendency of ignorance and the latent tendency of conceit, but it is not that this person does not fully comprehend the latent tendency of sensual lust and the latent tendency of aversion. Setting aside the two persons endowed with the path of the non-returner and the path of Arahantship, the remaining persons do not fully comprehend the latent tendency of ignorance, and do not fully comprehend the latent tendency of sensual lust, the latent tendency of aversion, and the latent tendency of conceit.

239. (Ka) yo kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca diṭṭhānusayañca na parijānāti so vicikicchānusayaṃ na parijānātīti? Āmantā.

239. Does a person who does not fully comprehend the latent tendency of sensual lust, the latent tendency of aversion, the latent tendency of conceit, and the latent tendency of wrong views, also not fully comprehend the latent tendency of doubt? Yes.

(Kha) yo [M 2.0208] vā pana vicikicchānusayaṃ na parijānāti so kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca diṭṭhānusayañca na parijānātīti?

Or again, does a person who does not fully comprehend the latent tendency of doubt also not fully comprehend the latent tendency of sensual lust, the latent tendency of aversion, the latent tendency of conceit, and the latent tendency of wrong views?

Anāgāmimaggasamaṅgī vicikicchānusayañca mānānusayañca diṭṭhānusayañca na parijānāti, no ca so kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca na parijānāti. Aggamaggasamaṅgī vicikicchānusayañca kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca diṭṭhānusayañca na parijānāti, no ca so mānānusayaṃ na parijānāti. Dvinnaṃ maggasamaṅgīnañca aṭṭhamakañca ṭhapetvā avasesā puggalā vicikicchānusayañca na parijānanti kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca [T 1.0643] mānānusayañca diṭṭhānusayañca na parijānanti …pe…. (Catukkamūlakaṃ)

A person endowed with the path of the non-returner does not fully comprehend the latent tendency of doubt, the latent tendency of conceit, and the latent tendency of wrong views, but it is not that this person does not fully comprehend the latent tendency of sensual lust and the latent tendency of aversion. A person endowed with the highest path does not fully comprehend the latent tendency of doubt, the latent tendency of sensual lust, the latent tendency of aversion, and the latent tendency of wrong views, but it is not that this person does not fully comprehend the latent tendency of conceit. Setting aside the two persons endowed with the path of the non-returner and the path of Arahantship, and the person at the stage of the path of stream-entry, the remaining persons do not fully comprehend the latent tendency of doubt, and do not fully comprehend the latent tendency of sensual lust, the latent tendency of aversion, the latent tendency of conceit, and the latent tendency of wrong views.

240. Yo [V 2.0272] kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca diṭṭhānusayañca vicikicchānusayañca na parijānāti so bhavarāgānusayaṃ…pe… avijjānusayaṃ na parijānātīti? Āmantā.

240. Does a person who does not fully comprehend the latent tendency of sensual lust, the latent tendency of aversion, the latent tendency of conceit, the latent tendency of wrong views, and the latent tendency of doubt, also not fully comprehend the latent tendency of lust for becoming... and the latent tendency of ignorance? Yes.

Yo vā pana avijjānusayaṃ na parijānāti so kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca diṭṭhānusayañca vicikicchānusayañca na parijānātīti?

Or again, does a person who does not fully comprehend the latent tendency of ignorance also not fully comprehend the latent tendency of sensual lust, the latent tendency of aversion, the latent tendency of conceit, the latent tendency of wrong views, and the latent tendency of doubt?

Aṭṭhamako avijjānusayañca kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca na parijānāti, no ca so diṭṭhānusayañca vicikicchānusayañca na parijānāti. Anāgāmimaggasamaṅgī avijjānusayañca mānānusayañca diṭṭhānusayañca vicikicchānusayañca na parijānāti, no ca so kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca na parijānāti. Dvinnaṃ maggasamaṅgīnañca aṭṭhamakañca ṭhapetvā avasesā puggalā avijjānusayañca na parijānanti kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca diṭṭhānusayañca vicikicchānusayañca na parijānanti. (Pañcakamūlakaṃ)

The person at the stage of the path of stream-entry does not fully comprehend the latent tendency of ignorance, the latent tendency of sensual lust, the latent tendency of aversion, and the latent tendency of conceit, but it is not that this person does not fully comprehend the latent tendency of wrong views and the latent tendency of doubt. A person endowed with the path of the non-returner does not fully comprehend the latent tendency of ignorance, the latent tendency of conceit, the latent tendency of wrong views, and the latent tendency of doubt, but it is not that this person does not fully comprehend the latent tendency of sensual lust and the latent tendency of aversion. Setting aside the two persons endowed with the path of the non-returner and the path of Arahantship, and the person at the stage of the path of stream-entry, the remaining persons do not fully comprehend the latent tendency of ignorance, and do not fully comprehend the latent tendency of sensual lust, the latent tendency of aversion, the latent tendency of conceit, the latent tendency of wrong views, and the latent tendency of doubt.

241. (Ka) yo kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca diṭṭhānusayañca vicikicchānusayañca bhavarāgānusayañca na parijānāti so avijjānusayaṃ na parijānātīti? Āmantā.

241. Does a person who does not fully comprehend the latent tendency of sensual lust, the latent tendency of aversion, the latent tendency of conceit, the latent tendency of wrong views, the latent tendency of doubt, and the latent tendency of lust for becoming, also not fully comprehend the latent tendency of ignorance? Yes.

(Kha) yo vā pana avijjānusayaṃ na parijānāti so kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca diṭṭhānusayañca vicikicchānusayañca bhavarāgānusayañca na parijānātīti?

Or again, does a person who does not fully comprehend the latent tendency of ignorance also not fully comprehend the latent tendency of sensual lust, the latent tendency of aversion, the latent tendency of conceit, the latent tendency of wrong views, the latent tendency of doubt, and the latent tendency of lust for becoming?

Aṭṭhamako avijjānusayañca kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca [T 1.0644] bhavarāgānusayañca na parijānāti, no ca so diṭṭhānusayañca vicikicchānusayañca na parijānāti. Anāgāmimaggasamaṅgī avijjānusayañca mānānusayañca diṭṭhānusayañca vicikicchānusayañca bhavarāgānusayañca na parijānāti, no ca so kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca na parijānāti. Dvinnaṃ maggasamaṅgīnañca [V 2.0273] aṭṭhamakañca [M 2.0209] ṭhapetvā avasesā puggalā avijjānusayañca na parijānanti kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca diṭṭhānusayañca vicikicchānusayañca bhavarāgānusayañca na parijānanti. (Chakkamūlakaṃ)

The person at the stage of the path of stream-entry does not fully comprehend the latent tendency of ignorance, the latent tendency of sensual lust, the latent tendency of aversion, the latent tendency of conceit, and the latent tendency of lust for becoming, but it is not that this person does not fully comprehend the latent tendency of wrong views and the latent tendency of doubt. A person endowed with the path of the non-returner does not fully comprehend the latent tendency of ignorance, the latent tendency of conceit, the latent tendency of wrong views, the latent tendency of doubt, and the latent tendency of lust for becoming, but it is not that this person does not fully comprehend the latent tendency of sensual lust and the latent tendency of aversion. Setting aside the two persons endowed with the path of the non-returner and the path of Arahantship, and the person at the stage of the path of stream-entry, the remaining persons do not fully comprehend the latent tendency of ignorance, and do not fully comprehend the latent tendency of sensual lust, the latent tendency of aversion, the latent tendency of conceit, the latent tendency of wrong views, the latent tendency of doubt, and the latent tendency of lust for becoming.

(Ṅa) paṭilomaokāso

(Ṅa) The Reverse Order.

242. (Ka) yato kāmarāgānusayaṃ na parijānāti tato paṭighānusayaṃ na parijānātīti?

242. Where one does not fully understand the underlying tendency to sensual desire, does one there not fully understand the underlying tendency to aversion?

Dukkhāya vedanāya tato kāmarāgānusayaṃ na parijānāti, no ca tato paṭighānusayaṃ na parijānāti. Rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā apariyāpanne tato kāmarāgānusayañca na parijānāti paṭighānusayañca na parijānāti.

With regard to painful feeling, one there does not fully understand the underlying tendency to sensual desire, but it is not that one there does not fully understand the underlying tendency to aversion. In the form realm, the formless realm, and in the supramundane, one there does not fully understand the underlying tendency to sensual desire, and one does not fully understand the underlying tendency to aversion.

(Kha) yato vā pana paṭighānusayaṃ na parijānāti tato kāmarāgānusayaṃ na parijānātīti?

Or where one does not fully understand the underlying tendency to aversion, does one there not fully understand the underlying tendency to sensual desire?

Kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu tato paṭighānusayaṃ na parijānāti, no ca tato kāmarāgānusayaṃ na parijānāti. Rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā apariyāpanne tato paṭighānusayañca na parijānāti kāmarāgānusayañca na parijānāti.

In the sensual realm, with regard to two feelings, one there does not fully understand the underlying tendency to aversion, but it is not that one there does not fully understand the underlying tendency to sensual desire. In the form realm, the formless realm, and in the supramundane, one there does not fully understand the underlying tendency to aversion, and one does not fully understand the underlying tendency to sensual desire.

(Ka) yato kāmarāgānusayaṃ na parijānāti tato mānānusayaṃ na parijānātīti?

Where one does not fully understand the underlying tendency to sensual desire, does one there not fully understand the underlying tendency to conceit?

Rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā tato kāmarāgānusayaṃ na parijānāti, no ca tato mānānusayaṃ na parijānāti. Dukkhāya vedanāya apariyāpanne tato kāmarāgānusayañca na parijānāti mānānusayañca [T 1.0645] na parijānāti.

In the form realm and the formless realm, one there does not fully understand the underlying tendency to sensual desire, but it is not that one there does not fully understand the underlying tendency to conceit. With regard to painful feeling and in the supramundane, one there does not fully understand the underlying tendency to sensual desire, and one does not fully understand the underlying tendency to conceit.

(Kha) yato vā pana mānānusayaṃ na parijānāti tato kāmarāgānusayaṃ na parijānātīti? Āmantā.

Or where one does not fully understand the underlying tendency to conceit, does one there not fully understand the underlying tendency to sensual desire? Yes.

Yato kāmarāgānusayaṃ na parijānāti tato diṭṭhānusayaṃ…pe… vicikicchānusayaṃ na parijānātīti?

Where one does not fully understand the underlying tendency to sensual desire, does one there not fully understand the underlying tendency to views… and so on… the underlying tendency to doubt?

Dukkhāya vedanāya rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā tato kāmarāgānusayaṃ na [V 2.0274] parijānāti, no ca tato vicikicchānusayaṃ na parijānāti. Apariyāpanne tato kāmarāgānusayañca na parijānāti vicikicchānusayañca na parijānāti.

With regard to painful feeling, the form realm, and the formless realm, one there does not fully understand the underlying tendency to sensual desire, but it is not that one there does not fully understand the underlying tendency to doubt. In the supramundane, one there does not fully understand the underlying tendency to sensual desire, and one does not fully understand the underlying tendency to doubt.

Yato vā pana vicikicchānusayaṃ na parijānāti tato kāmarāgānusayaṃ na parijānātīti? Āmantā.

Or where one does not fully understand the underlying tendency to doubt, does one there not fully understand the underlying tendency to sensual desire? Yes.

(Ka) yato kāmarāgānusayaṃ na parijānāti tato bhavarāgānusayaṃ na parijānātīti?

Where one does not fully understand the underlying tendency to sensual desire, does one there not fully understand the underlying tendency to craving for existence?

Rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā tato kāmarāgānusayaṃ na parijānāti, no ca tato bhavarāgānusayaṃ na parijānāti. Dukkhāya vedanāya [M 2.0210] apariyāpanne tato kāmarāgānusayañca na parijānāti bhavarāgānusayañca na parijānāti.

In the form realm and the formless realm, one there does not fully understand the underlying tendency to sensual desire, but it is not that one there does not fully understand the underlying tendency to craving for existence. With regard to painful feeling and in the supramundane, one there does not fully understand the underlying tendency to sensual desire, and one does not fully understand the underlying tendency to craving for existence.

(Kha) yato vā pana bhavarāgānusayaṃ na parijānāti tato kāmarāgānusayaṃ na parijānātīti?

Or where one does not fully understand the underlying tendency to craving for existence, does one there not fully understand the underlying tendency to sensual desire?

Kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu tato bhavarāgānusayaṃ na parijānāti, no ca tato kāmarāgānusayaṃ na parijānāti. Dukkhāya vedanāya apariyāpanne tato bhavarāgānusayañca na parijānāti kāmarāgānusayañca na parijānāti.

In the sensual realm, with regard to two feelings, one there does not fully understand the underlying tendency to craving for existence, but it is not that one there does not fully understand the underlying tendency to sensual desire. With regard to painful feeling and in the supramundane, one there does not fully understand the underlying tendency to craving for existence, and one does not fully understand the underlying tendency to sensual desire.

(Ka) yato kāmarāgānusayaṃ na parijānāti tato avijjānusayaṃ na parijānātīti?

Where one does not fully understand the underlying tendency to sensual desire, does one there not fully understand the underlying tendency to ignorance?

Dukkhāya vedanāya rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā tato kāmarāgānusayaṃ na parijānāti, no ca tato avijjānusayaṃ na parijānāti. Apariyāpanne tato kāmarāgānusayañca na parijānāti avijjānusayañca na parijānāti.

With regard to painful feeling, the form realm, and the formless realm, one there does not fully understand the underlying tendency to sensual desire, but it is not that one there does not fully understand the underlying tendency to ignorance. In the supramundane, one there does not fully understand the underlying tendency to sensual desire, and one does not fully understand the underlying tendency to ignorance.

(Kha) yato vā pana avijjānusayaṃ na [T 1.0646] parijānāti tato kāmarāgānusayaṃ na parijānātīti? Āmantā.

Or where one does not fully understand the underlying tendency to ignorance, does one there not fully understand the underlying tendency to sensual desire? Yes.

243. (Ka) yato [V 2.0275] paṭighānusayaṃ na parijānāti tato mānānusayaṃ parijānātīti?

243. Where one does not fully understand the underlying tendency to aversion, does one there not fully understand the underlying tendency to conceit?

Kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā tato paṭighānusayaṃ na parijānāti, no ca tato mānānusayaṃ na parijānāti. Apariyāpanne tato paṭighānusayañca na parijānāti mānānusayañca na parijānāti.

In the sensual realm with regard to two feelings, in the form realm, and in the formless realm, one there does not fully understand the underlying tendency to aversion, but it is not that one there does not fully understand the underlying tendency to conceit. In the supramundane, one there does not fully understand the underlying tendency to aversion, and one does not fully understand the underlying tendency to conceit.

(Kha) yato vā pana mānānusayaṃ na parijānāti tato paṭighānusayaṃ na parijānātīti?

Or where one does not fully understand the underlying tendency to conceit, does one there not fully understand the underlying tendency to aversion?

Dukkhāya vedanāya tato mānānusayaṃ na parijānāti, no ca tato paṭighānusayaṃ na parijānāti. Apariyāpanne tato mānānusayañca na parijānāti paṭighānusayañca na parijānāti.

With regard to painful feeling, one there does not fully understand the underlying tendency to conceit, but it is not that one there does not fully understand the underlying tendency to aversion. In the supramundane, one there does not fully understand the underlying tendency to conceit, and one does not fully understand the underlying tendency to aversion.

Yato paṭighānusayaṃ na parijānāti tato diṭṭhānusayaṃ…pe… vicikicchānusayaṃ na parijānātīti?

Where one does not fully understand the underlying tendency to aversion, does one there not fully understand the underlying tendency to views… and so on… the underlying tendency to doubt?

Kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā tato paṭighānusayaṃ na parijānāti, no ca tato vicikicchānusayaṃ na parijānāti. Apariyāpanne tato paṭighānusayañca na parijānāti vicikicchānusayañca na parijānāti.

In the sensual realm with regard to two feelings, in the form realm, and in the formless realm, one there does not fully understand the underlying tendency to aversion, but it is not that one there does not fully understand the underlying tendency to doubt. In the supramundane, one there does not fully understand the underlying tendency to aversion, and one does not fully understand the underlying tendency to doubt.

Yato vā pana vicikicchānusayaṃ na parijānāti tato paṭighānusayaṃ na parijānātīti? Āmantā.

Or where one does not fully understand the underlying tendency to doubt, does one there not fully understand the underlying tendency to aversion? Yes.

(Ka) yato paṭighānusayaṃ na parijānāti tato bhavarāgānusayaṃ na parijānātīti?

Where one does not fully understand the underlying tendency to aversion, does one there not fully understand the underlying tendency to craving for existence?

Rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā tato paṭighānusayaṃ na parijānāti[M 2.0211], no ca tato bhavarāgānusayaṃ na parijānāti. Kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu apariyāpanne tato paṭighānusayañca na parijānāti bhavarāgānusayañca na parijānāti.

In the form realm and the formless realm, one there does not fully understand the underlying tendency to aversion, but it is not that one there does not fully understand the underlying tendency to craving for existence. In the sensual realm with regard to two feelings, and in the supramundane, one there does not fully understand the underlying tendency to aversion, and one does not fully understand the underlying tendency to craving for existence.

(Kha) yato vā pana bhavarāgānusayaṃ na parijānāti tato paṭighānusayaṃ na parijānātīti?

Or where one does not fully understand the underlying tendency to craving for existence, does one there not fully understand the underlying tendency to aversion?

Dukkhāya [V 2.0276] vedanāya [T 1.0647] tato bhavarāgānusayaṃ na parijānāti, no ca tato paṭighānusayaṃ na parijānāti. Kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu apariyāpanne tato bhavarāgānusayañca na parijānāti paṭighānusayañca na parijānāti.

With regard to painful feeling, one there does not fully understand the underlying tendency to craving for existence, but it is not that one there does not fully understand the underlying tendency to aversion. In the sensual realm with regard to two feelings, and in the supramundane, one there does not fully understand the underlying tendency to craving for existence, and one does not fully understand the underlying tendency to aversion.

(Ka) yato paṭighānusayaṃ na parijānāti tato avijjānusayaṃ na parijānātīti?

Where one does not fully understand the underlying tendency to aversion, does one there not fully understand the underlying tendency to ignorance?

Kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā tato paṭighānusayaṃ na parijānāti, no ca tato avijjānusayaṃ na parijānāti. Apariyāpanne tato paṭighānusayañca na parijānāti avijjānusayañca na parijānāti.

In the sense-sphere, in the two feelings, in the form-sphere, and in the formless-sphere, from that, one does not yet comprehend the latent tendency to aversion, but one does indeed comprehend the latent tendency to ignorance. In the unincluded states, from that, one does not yet comprehend either the latent tendency to aversion or the latent tendency to ignorance.

(Kha) yato vā pana avijjānusayaṃ na parijānāti tato paṭighānusayaṃ na parijānātīti? Āmantā.

Or, from where one does not yet comprehend the latent tendency to ignorance, from there does one not yet comprehend the latent tendency to aversion? Yes.

244. Yato mānānusayaṃ na parijānāti tato diṭṭhānusayaṃ…pe… vicikicchānusayaṃ na parijānātīti?

244. From where one does not yet comprehend the latent tendency to conceit, from there does one not yet comprehend the latent tendency to wrong views… the latent tendency to doubt?

Dukkhāya vedanāya tato mānānusayaṃ na parijānāti, no ca tato vicikicchānusayaṃ na parijānāti. Apariyāpanne tato mānānusayañca na parijānāti vicikicchānusayañca na parijānāti.

In painful feeling, from that, one does not yet comprehend the latent tendency to conceit, but one does indeed comprehend the latent tendency to doubt. In the unincluded states, from that, one does not yet comprehend either the latent tendency to conceit or the latent tendency to doubt.

Yato vā pana vicikicchānusayaṃ na parijānāti tato mānānusayaṃ na parijānātīti? Āmantā.

Or, from where one does not yet comprehend the latent tendency to doubt, from there does one not yet comprehend the latent tendency to conceit? Yes.

(Ka) yato mānānusayaṃ na parijānāti tato bhavarāgānusayaṃ na parijānātīti? Āmantā.

From where one does not yet comprehend the latent tendency to conceit, from there does one not yet comprehend the latent tendency to craving for existence? Yes.

(Kha) yato vā pana bhavarāgānusayaṃ na parijānāti tato mānānusayaṃ na parijānātīti?

Or, from where one does not yet comprehend the latent tendency to craving for existence, from there does one not yet comprehend the latent tendency to conceit?

Kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu tato bhavarāgānusayaṃ na parijānāti, no ca tato mānānusayaṃ na parijānāti. Dukkhāya vedanāya apariyāpanne tato bhavarāgānusayañca na parijānāti mānānusayañca na parijānāti.

In the sense-sphere and in the two feelings, from that, one does not yet comprehend the latent tendency to craving for existence, but one does indeed comprehend the latent tendency to conceit. In painful feeling and in the unincluded states, from that, one does not yet comprehend either the latent tendency to craving for existence or the latent tendency to conceit.

(Ka) yato mānānusayaṃ na parijānāti [T 1.0648] tato avijjānusayaṃ na parijānātīti?

From where one does not yet comprehend the latent tendency to conceit, from there does one not yet comprehend the latent tendency to ignorance?

Dukkhāya vedanāya tato mānānusayaṃ na parijānāti, no ca tato avijjānusayaṃ [V 2.0277] na parijānāti. Apariyāpanne tato mānānusayañca na parijānāti avijjānusayañca na parijānāti.

In painful feeling, from that, one does not yet comprehend the latent tendency to conceit, but one does indeed comprehend the latent tendency to ignorance. In the unincluded states, from that, one does not yet comprehend either the latent tendency to conceit or the latent tendency to ignorance.

(Kha) yato vā [M 2.0212] pana avijjānusayaṃ na parijānāti tato mānānusayaṃ na parijānātīti? Āmantā.

Or, from where one does not yet comprehend the latent tendency to ignorance, from there does one not yet comprehend the latent tendency to conceit? Yes.

245. (Ka) yato diṭṭhānusayaṃ na parijānāti tato vicikicchānusayaṃ na parijānātīti? Āmantā.

245. From where one does not yet comprehend the latent tendency to wrong views, from there does one not yet comprehend the latent tendency to doubt? Yes.

(Kha) yato vā pana vicikicchānusayaṃ na parijānāti tato diṭṭhānusayaṃ na parijānātīti? Āmantā …pe….

Or, from where one does not yet comprehend the latent tendency to doubt, from there does one not yet comprehend the latent tendency to wrong views? Yes…

246. (Ka) yato vicikicchānusayaṃ na parijānāti tato bhavarāgānusayaṃ na parijānātīti? Āmantā.

246. From where one does not yet comprehend the latent tendency to doubt, from there does one not yet comprehend the latent tendency to craving for existence? Yes.

(Kha) yato vā pana bhavarāgānusayaṃ na parijānāti tato vicikicchānusayaṃ na parijānātīti?

Or, from where one does not yet comprehend the latent tendency to craving for existence, from there does one not yet comprehend the latent tendency to doubt?

Kāmadhātuyā tīsu vedanāsu tato bhavarāgānusayaṃ na parijānāti, no ca tato vicikicchānusayaṃ na parijānāti. Apariyāpanne tato bhavarāgānusayañca na parijānāti vicikicchānusayañca na parijānāti.

In the sense-sphere and in the three feelings, from that, one does not yet comprehend the latent tendency to craving for existence, but one does indeed comprehend the latent tendency to doubt. In the unincluded states, from that, one does not yet comprehend either the latent tendency to craving for existence or the latent tendency to doubt.

(Ka) yato vicikicchānusayaṃ na parijānāti tato avijjānusayaṃ na parijānātīti? Āmantā.

From where one does not yet comprehend the latent tendency to doubt, from there does one not yet comprehend the latent tendency to ignorance? Yes.

(Kha) yato vā pana avijjānusayaṃ na parijānāti tato vicikicchānusayaṃ na parijānātīti? Āmantā.

Or, from where one does not yet comprehend the latent tendency to ignorance, from there does one not yet comprehend the latent tendency to doubt? Yes.

247. (Ka) yato bhavarāgānusayaṃ na parijānāti tato avijjānusayaṃ na parijānātīti?

247. From where one does not yet comprehend the latent tendency to craving for existence, from there does one not yet comprehend the latent tendency to ignorance?

Kāmadhātuyā tīsu vedanāsu tato bhavarāgānusayaṃ na parijānāti, no ca tato avijjānusayaṃ na parijānāti. Apariyāpanne tato bhavarāgānusayañca na parijānāti avijjānusayañca na parijānāti.

In the sense-sphere and in the three feelings, from that, one does not yet comprehend the latent tendency to craving for existence, but one does indeed comprehend the latent tendency to ignorance. In the unincluded states, from that, one does not yet comprehend either the latent tendency to craving for existence or the latent tendency to ignorance.

(Kha) yato [T 1.0649][V 2.0278] vā pana avijjānusayaṃ na parijānāti tato bhavarāgānusayaṃ na parijānātīti? Āmantā. (Ekamūlakaṃ)

Or, from where one does not yet comprehend the latent tendency to ignorance, from there does one not yet comprehend the latent tendency to craving for existence? Yes.

248. (Ka) yato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca na parijānāti tato mānānusayaṃ na parijānātīti?

248. From where one does not yet comprehend both the latent tendency to sensual lust and the latent tendency to aversion, from there does one not yet comprehend the latent tendency to conceit?

Rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā tato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca na parijānāti, no ca tato mānānusayaṃ na parijānāti. Apariyāpanne tato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca na parijānāti mānānusayañca na parijānāti.

In the form-sphere and in the formless-sphere, from that, one does not yet comprehend either the latent tendency to sensual lust or the latent tendency to aversion, but one does indeed comprehend the latent tendency to conceit. In the unincluded states, from that, one does not yet comprehend the latent tendency to sensual lust, the latent tendency to aversion, or the latent tendency to conceit.

(Kha) yato vā pana mānānusayaṃ na parijānāti tato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca na parijānātīti?

Or, from where one does not yet comprehend the latent tendency to conceit, from there does one not yet comprehend both the latent tendency to sensual lust and the latent tendency to aversion?

Dukkhāya vedanāya tato mānānusayañca kāmarāgānusayañca [M 2.0213] na parijānāti, no ca tato paṭighānusayaṃ na parijānāti. Apariyāpanne tato mānānusayañca na parijānāti kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca na parijānāti.

In painful feeling, from that, one does not yet comprehend either the latent tendency to conceit or the latent tendency to sensual lust, but one does indeed comprehend the latent tendency to aversion. In the unincluded states, from that, one does not yet comprehend the latent tendency to conceit, the latent tendency to sensual lust, or the latent tendency to aversion.

Yato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca na parijānāti tato diṭṭhānusayaṃ…pe… vicikicchānusayaṃ na parijānātīti?

From where one does not yet comprehend both the latent tendency to sensual lust and the latent tendency to aversion, from there does one not yet comprehend the latent tendency to wrong views... the latent tendency to doubt?

Rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā tato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca na parijānāti, no ca tato vicikicchānusayaṃ na parijānāti. Apariyāpanne tato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca na parijānāti vicikicchānusayañca na parijānāti.

In the form-sphere and in the formless-sphere, from that, one does not yet comprehend either the latent tendency to sensual lust or the latent tendency to aversion, but one does indeed comprehend the latent tendency to doubt. In the unincluded states, from that, one does not yet comprehend the latent tendency to sensual lust, the latent tendency to aversion, or the latent tendency to doubt.

Yato vā pana vicikicchānusayaṃ na parijānāti tato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca na parijānātīti? Āmantā.

Or, from where one does not yet comprehend the latent tendency to doubt, from there does one not yet comprehend both the latent tendency to sensual lust and the latent tendency to aversion? Yes.

(Ka) yato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca na parijānāti tato bhavarāgānusayaṃ na parijānātīti?

From where one does not yet comprehend both the latent tendency to sensual lust and the latent tendency to aversion, from there does one not yet comprehend the latent tendency to craving for existence?

Rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā tato kāmarāgānusayañca [T 1.0650] paṭighānusayañca na parijānāti, no ca tato bhavarāgānusayaṃ na parijānāti. Apariyāpanne [V 2.0279] tato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca na parijānāti bhavarāgānusayañca na parijānāti.

In the form-sphere and in the formless-sphere, from that, one does not yet comprehend either the latent tendency to sensual lust or the latent tendency to aversion, but one does indeed comprehend the latent tendency to craving for existence. In the unincluded states, from that, one does not yet comprehend the latent tendency to sensual lust, the latent tendency to aversion, or the latent tendency to craving for existence.

(Kha) yato vā pana bhavarāgānusayaṃ na parijānāti tato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca na parijānātīti?

Or, from where one does not yet comprehend the latent tendency to craving for existence, from there does one not yet comprehend both the latent tendency to sensual lust and the latent tendency to aversion?

Dukkhāya vedanāya tato bhavarāgānusayañca kāmarāgānusayañca na parijānāti, no ca tato paṭighānusayaṃ na parijānāti. Kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu tato bhavarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca na parijānāti, no ca tato kāmarāgānusayaṃ na parijānāti. Apariyāpanne tato bhavarāgānusayañca na parijānāti kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca na parijānāti.

In painful feeling, therein one does not fully understand the underlying tendency to craving for existence and the underlying tendency to sensual desire, but it is not that one does not fully understand the underlying tendency to aversion. In the sense-sphere, in the two feelings, therein one does not fully understand the underlying tendency to craving for existence and the underlying tendency to aversion, but it is not that one does not fully understand the underlying tendency to sensual desire. In the unincluded, therein one does not fully understand the underlying tendency to craving for existence, and one does not fully understand the underlying tendency to sensual desire and the underlying tendency to aversion.

(Ka) yato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca na parijānāti tato avijjānusayaṃ na parijānātīti?

Where one does not fully understand the underlying tendency to sensual desire and the underlying tendency to aversion, does one then not fully understand the underlying tendency to ignorance?

Rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā tato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca na parijānāti, no ca tato avijjānusayaṃ na parijānāti. Apariyāpanne tato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca na parijānāti avijjānusayañca na parijānāti.

In the form realm and the formless realm, therein one does not fully understand the underlying tendency to sensual desire and the underlying tendency to aversion, but it is not that one does not fully understand the underlying tendency to ignorance. In the unincluded, therein one does not fully understand the underlying tendency to sensual desire and the underlying tendency to aversion, and one does not fully understand the underlying tendency to ignorance.

(Kha) yato vā pana avijjānusayaṃ na parijānāti tato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca na parijānātīti? Āmantā. (Dukamūlakaṃ)

Or again, where one does not fully understand the underlying tendency to ignorance, does one then not fully understand the underlying tendency to sensual desire and the underlying tendency to aversion? Yes.

249. Yato [M 2.0214] kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca na parijānāti tato diṭṭhānusayaṃ…pe… vicikicchānusayaṃ na parijānātīti? Āmantā.

249. Where one does not fully understand the underlying tendency to sensual desire, the underlying tendency to aversion, and the underlying tendency to conceit, does one then not fully understand the underlying tendency to views… and the underlying tendency to doubt? Yes.

Where one does not fully understand the underlying tendency to sensual desire, the underlying tendency to aversion, and the underlying tendency to conceit, does one then not fully understand the underlying tendency to craving for existence? Yes.

Or again, where one does not fully understand the underlying tendency to craving for existence, does one then not fully understand the underlying tendency to sensual desire, the underlying tendency to aversion, and the underlying tendency to conceit?

Dukkhāya vedanāya tato bhavarāgānusayañca kāmarāgānusayañca mānānusayañca na parijānāti, no ca tato paṭighānusayaṃ na parijānāti. Kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu tato bhavarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca na parijānāti, no ca tato kāmarāgānusayañca mānānusayañca na parijānāti. Apariyāpanne tato bhavarāgānusayañca na parijānāti kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca na parijānāti.

In painful feeling, therein one does not fully understand the underlying tendency to craving for existence, the underlying tendency to sensual desire, and the underlying tendency to conceit, but it is not that one does not fully understand the underlying tendency to aversion. In the sense-sphere, in the two feelings, therein one does not fully understand the underlying tendency to craving for existence and the underlying tendency to aversion, but it is not that one does not fully understand the underlying tendency to sensual desire and the underlying tendency to conceit. In the unincluded, therein one does not fully understand the underlying tendency to craving for existence, and one does not fully understand the underlying tendency to sensual desire, the underlying tendency to aversion, and the underlying tendency to conceit.

(Ka) yato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca na parijānāti tato avijjānusayaṃ na parijānātīti? Āmantā.

Where one does not fully understand the underlying tendency to sensual desire, the underlying tendency to aversion, and the underlying tendency to conceit, does one then not fully understand the underlying tendency to ignorance? Yes.

(Kha) yato vā pana avijjānusayaṃ na parijānāti tato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca na parijānātīti? Āmantā. (Tikamūlakaṃ)

Or again, where one does not fully understand the underlying tendency to ignorance, does one then not fully understand the underlying tendency to sensual desire, the underlying tendency to aversion, and the underlying tendency to conceit? Yes.

250. (Ka) yato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca diṭṭhānusayañca na parijānāti tato vicikicchānusayaṃ na [T 1.0652] parijānātīti? Āmantā.

250. Where one does not fully understand the underlying tendency to sensual desire, the underlying tendency to aversion, the underlying tendency to conceit, and the underlying tendency to views, does one then not fully understand the underlying tendency to doubt? Yes.

(Kha) yato vā pana vicikicchānusayaṃ na parijānāti tato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca diṭṭhānusayañca na parijānātīti? Āmantā …pe…. (Catukkamūlakaṃ)

Or again, where one does not fully understand the underlying tendency to doubt, does one then not fully understand the underlying tendency to sensual desire, the underlying tendency to aversion, the underlying tendency to conceit, and the underlying tendency to views? Yes. …

251. (Ka) yato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca diṭṭhānusayañca vicikicchānusayañca na parijānāti tato bhavarāgānusayaṃ na parijānātīti? Āmantā.

251. Where one does not fully understand the underlying tendency to sensual desire, the underlying tendency to aversion, the underlying tendency to conceit, the underlying tendency to views, and the underlying tendency to doubt, does one then not fully understand the underlying tendency to craving for existence? Yes.

(Kha) yato vā pana bhavarāgānusayaṃ na parijānāti tato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca diṭṭhānusayañca vicikicchānusayañca na parijānātīti?
