Dukkhāya vedanāya tato bhavarāgānusayañca kāmarāgānusayañca mānānusayañca na parijānāti, no ca [M 2.0215] tato paṭighānusayañca diṭṭhānusayañca [V 2.0281] vicikicchānusayañca na parijānāti. Kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu tato bhavarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca na parijānāti, no ca tato kāmarāgānusayañca mānānusayañca diṭṭhānusayañca vicikicchānusayañca na parijānāti. Apariyāpanne tato bhavarāgānusayañca na parijānāti kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca diṭṭhānusayañca vicikicchānusayañca na parijānāti.

In painful feeling, therein one does not fully understand the underlying tendency to craving for existence, the underlying tendency to sensual desire, and the underlying tendency to conceit, but it is not that one does not fully understand the underlying tendency to aversion, the underlying tendency to views, and the underlying tendency to doubt. In the sense-sphere, in the two feelings, therein one does not fully understand the underlying tendency to craving for existence and the underlying tendency to aversion, but it is not that one does not fully understand the underlying tendency to sensual desire, the underlying tendency to conceit, the underlying tendency to views, and the underlying tendency to doubt. In the unincluded, therein one does not fully understand the underlying tendency to craving for existence, and one does not fully understand the underlying tendency to sensual desire, the underlying tendency to aversion, the underlying tendency to conceit, the underlying tendency to views, and the underlying tendency to doubt.

(Ka) yato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca diṭṭhānusayañca vicikicchānusayañca na parijānāti tato avijjānusayaṃ na parijānātīti? Āmantā.

Where one does not fully understand the underlying tendency to sensual desire, the underlying tendency to aversion, the underlying tendency to conceit, the underlying tendency to views, and the underlying tendency to doubt, does one then not fully understand the underlying tendency to ignorance? Yes.

(Kha) yato vā pana avijjānusayaṃ na parijānāti tato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca diṭṭhānusayañca vicikicchānusayañca na parijānātīti? Āmantā. (Pañcakamūlakaṃ)

Or again, where one does not fully understand the underlying tendency to ignorance, does one then not fully understand the underlying tendency to sensual desire, the underlying tendency to aversion, the underlying tendency to conceit, the underlying tendency to views, and the underlying tendency to doubt? Yes.

252. (Ka) yato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca diṭṭhānusayañca vicikicchānusayañca bhavarāgānusayañca na parijānāti tato avijjānusayaṃ na parijānātīti? Āmantā.

252. Where one does not fully understand the underlying tendency to sensual desire, the underlying tendency to aversion, the underlying tendency to conceit, the underlying tendency to views, the underlying tendency to doubt, and the underlying tendency to craving for existence, does one then not fully understand the underlying tendency to ignorance? Yes.

(Kha) yato vā pana avijjānusayaṃ na parijānāti tato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca diṭṭhānusayañca vicikicchānusayañca bhavarāgānusayañca na parijānātīti[T 1.0653]? Āmantā. (Chakkamūlakaṃ)

Or again, where one does not fully understand the underlying tendency to ignorance, does one then not fully understand the underlying tendency to sensual desire, the underlying tendency to aversion, the underlying tendency to conceit, the underlying tendency to views, the underlying tendency to doubt, and the underlying tendency to craving for existence? Yes.

(Ca) paṭilomapuggalokāsā

(Ca) The Reverse Person-Plane

253. (Ka) yo yato kāmarāgānusayaṃ na parijānāti so tato paṭighānusayaṃ na parijānātīti?

Does the person who, in a certain basis, does not fully understand the underlying tendency to sensual desire, also, in that basis, not fully understand the underlying tendency to aversion?

Anāgāmimaggasamaṅgī dukkhāya vedanāya so tato kāmarāgānusayaṃ na parijānāti, no ca so tato paṭighānusayaṃ na parijānāti. Sveva puggalo rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā apariyāpanne so tato kāmarāgānusayañca na parijānāti paṭighānusayañca na parijānāti. Anāgāmimaggasamaṅgiṃ ṭhapetvā avasesā puggalā sabbattha kāmarāgānusayañca na parijānanti paṭighānusayañca na parijānanti.

A person endowed with the path of non-returning, in regard to painful feeling, does not fully comprehend the underlying tendency of sensual lust from that basis, but that person does fully comprehend the underlying tendency of aversion from that basis. That same person, in regard to the form realm, the formless realm, and the unincluded, does not fully comprehend either the underlying tendency of sensual lust or the underlying tendency of aversion from that basis. Except for the person endowed with the path of non-returning, the remaining persons do not fully comprehend either the underlying tendency of sensual lust or the underlying tendency of aversion in all circumstances.

(Kha) yo vā pana yato paṭighānusayaṃ na parijānāti so tato kāmarāgānusayaṃ na parijānātīti?

Or again, does a person who, in regard to a certain basis, does not fully comprehend the underlying tendency of aversion, also not fully comprehend the underlying tendency of sensual lust in regard to that basis?

Anāgāmimaggasamaṅgī [V 2.0282] kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu so tato paṭighānusayaṃ na parijānāti, no ca so tato kāmarāgānusayaṃ na parijānāti. Sveva puggalo rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā apariyāpanne so tato paṭighānusayañca na parijānāti kāmarāgānusayañca [M 2.0216] na parijānāti. Anāgāmimaggasamaṅgiṃ ṭhapetvā avasesā puggalā sabbattha paṭighānusayañca na parijānanti kāmarāgānusayañca na parijānanti.

A person endowed with the path of non-returning, in regard to the sense-sphere realm and the two feelings, does not fully comprehend the underlying tendency of aversion from that basis, but that person does fully comprehend the underlying tendency of sensual lust from that basis. That same person, in regard to the form realm, the formless realm, and the unincluded, does not fully comprehend either the underlying tendency of aversion or the underlying tendency of sensual lust from that basis. Except for the person endowed with the path of non-returning, the remaining persons do not fully comprehend either the underlying tendency of aversion or the underlying tendency of sensual lust in all circumstances.

(Ka) yo yato kāmarāgānusayaṃ na parijānāti so tato mānānusayaṃ na parijānātīti?

Does a person who, in regard to a certain basis, does not fully comprehend the underlying tendency of sensual lust, also not fully comprehend the underlying tendency of conceit in regard to that basis?

Aggamaggasamaṅgī kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā so tato kāmarāgānusayaṃ na parijānāti, no ca so tato mānānusayaṃ na parijānāti. Sveva puggalo dukkhāya vedanāya apariyāpanne so tato kāmarāgānusayañca na parijānāti mānānusayañca na parijānāti. Dvinnaṃ [T 1.0654] maggasamaṅgīnaṃ ṭhapetvā avasesā puggalā sabbattha kāmarāgānusayañca na parijānanti mānānusayañca na parijānanti.

A person endowed with the highest path, in regard to the sense-sphere realm, the two feelings, the form realm, and the formless realm, does not fully comprehend the underlying tendency of sensual lust from that basis, but that person does fully comprehend the underlying tendency of conceit from that basis. That same person, in regard to painful feeling and the unincluded, does not fully comprehend either the underlying tendency of sensual lust or the underlying tendency of conceit from that basis. Except for the two persons endowed with the paths, the remaining persons do not fully comprehend either the underlying tendency of sensual lust or the underlying tendency of conceit in all circumstances.

(Kha) yo vā pana yato mānānusayaṃ na parijānāti so tato kāmarāgānusayaṃ na parijānātīti?

Or again, does a person who, in regard to a certain basis, does not fully comprehend the underlying tendency of conceit, also not fully comprehend the underlying tendency of sensual lust in regard to that basis?

Anāgāmimaggasamaṅgī kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu so tato mānānusayaṃ na parijānāti, no ca so tato kāmarāgānusayaṃ na parijānāti. Sveva puggalo dukkhāya vedanāya rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā apariyāpanne so tato mānānusayañca na parijānāti kāmarāgānusayañca na parijānāti. Dvinnaṃ maggasamaṅgīnaṃ ṭhapetvā avasesā puggalā sabbattha mānānusayañca na parijānanti kāmarāgānusayañca na parijānanti.

A person endowed with the path of non-returning, in regard to the sense-sphere realm and the two feelings, does not fully comprehend the underlying tendency of conceit from that basis, but that person does fully comprehend the underlying tendency of sensual lust from that basis. That same person, in regard to painful feeling, the form realm, the formless realm, and the unincluded, does not fully comprehend either the underlying tendency of conceit or the underlying tendency of sensual lust from that basis. Except for the two persons endowed with the paths, the remaining persons do not fully comprehend either the underlying tendency of conceit or the underlying tendency of sensual lust in all circumstances.

Yo yato kāmarāgānusayaṃ na parijānāti so tato diṭṭhānusayaṃ…pe… vicikicchānusayaṃ na parijānātīti?

Does a person who, in regard to a certain basis, does not fully comprehend the underlying tendency of sensual lust, also not fully comprehend the underlying tendency of views… and the underlying tendency of doubt in regard to that basis?

Aṭṭhamako kāmadhātuyā tīsu vedanāsu rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā so tato kāmarāgānusayaṃ na parijānāti, no ca so tato vicikicchānusayaṃ na parijānāti. Sveva puggalo apariyāpanne so tato kāmarāgānusayañca [V 2.0283] na parijānāti vicikicchānusayañca na parijānāti. Anāgāmimaggasamaṅgiñca aṭṭhamakañca ṭhapetvā avasesā puggalā sabbattha kāmarāgānusayañca na parijānanti vicikicchānusayañca na parijānanti.

Except for the person endowed with the path of non-returning and the eighth person, the remaining persons do not fully comprehend either the underlying tendency of sensual lust or the underlying tendency of doubt in all circumstances.

Yo vā pana yato vicikicchānusayaṃ na parijānāti so tato kāmarāgānusayaṃ na parijānātīti?

(Ka) yo yato kāmarāgānusayaṃ na parijānāti so tato bhavarāgānusayaṃ na parijānātīti?

Does a person who, in regard to a certain basis, does not fully comprehend the underlying tendency of sensual lust, also not fully comprehend the underlying tendency of ignorance in regard to that basis?

254. (Ka) yo yato paṭighānusayaṃ na parijānāti so tato mānānusayaṃ na parijānātīti?

That same person, in the supramundane, does not comprehend the underlying tendency to conceit from that sphere and does not comprehend the underlying tendency to ignorance from that sphere. Setting aside the person endowed with the supreme path, the remaining persons do not comprehend the underlying tendency to conceit and do not comprehend the underlying tendency to ignorance in all spheres.

(Kha) yo vā pana yato avijjānusayaṃ na parijānāti so tato mānānusayaṃ na parijānātīti? Āmantā.

Or again, whoever from a certain sphere does not comprehend the underlying tendency to ignorance, does that person from that sphere not comprehend the underlying tendency to conceit? Yes.

256. (Ka) yo [T 1.0661] yato diṭṭhānusayaṃ na parijānāti so tato vicikicchānusayaṃ na parijānātīti? Āmantā.

256. Whoever from a certain sphere does not comprehend the underlying tendency to wrong views, does that person from that sphere not comprehend the underlying tendency to doubt? Yes.

(Kha) yo vā pana yato vicikicchānusayaṃ na parijānāti so tato diṭṭhānusayaṃ na parijānātīti? Āmantā …pe….

Or again, whoever from a certain sphere does not comprehend the underlying tendency to doubt, does that person from that sphere not comprehend the underlying tendency to wrong views? Yes… and so on.

257. (Ka) yo yato vicikicchānusayaṃ na parijānāti so tato bhavarāgānusayaṃ na parijānātīti?

257. Whoever from a certain sphere does not comprehend the underlying tendency to doubt, does that person from that sphere not comprehend the underlying tendency to lust for existence?

Aggamaggasamaṅgī rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā so tato vicikicchānusayaṃ na parijānāti, no ca so tato bhavarāgānusayaṃ na parijānāti. Sveva puggalo kāmadhātuyā tīsu vedanāsu, apariyāpanne so tato vicikicchānusayañca na parijānāti bhavarāgānusayañca na parijānāti. Aggamaggasamaṅgiñca aṭṭhamakañca ṭhapetvā avasesā puggalā sabbattha [V 2.0289] vicikicchānusayañca na parijānanti bhavarāgānusayañca na parijānanti.

A person endowed with the supreme path, in the form-sphere and in the formless-sphere, does not comprehend the underlying tendency to doubt from that sphere; but it is not that from that sphere he does not comprehend the underlying tendency to lust for existence. That same person, in the sense-sphere, in the three feelings, and in the supramundane, does not comprehend the underlying tendency to doubt from that sphere and does not comprehend the underlying tendency to lust for existence from that sphere. Setting aside the person endowed with the supreme path and the eighth person, the remaining persons do not comprehend the underlying tendency to doubt and do not comprehend the underlying tendency to lust for existence in all spheres.

(Kha) yo vā pana yato bhavarāgānusayaṃ na parijānāti so tato vicikicchānusayaṃ na parijānātīti?

Or again, whoever from a certain sphere does not comprehend the underlying tendency to lust for existence, does that person from that sphere not comprehend the underlying tendency to doubt?

Aṭṭhamako kāmadhātuyā tīsu vedanāsu rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā so tato bhavarāgānusayaṃ na parijānāti, no ca so tato vicikicchānusayaṃ na parijānāti. Sveva puggalo apariyāpanne so tato bhavarāgānusayañca na parijānāti vicikicchānusayañca na parijānāti. Aggamaggasamaṅgiñca aṭṭhamakañca ṭhapetvā avasesā puggalā sabbattha bhavarāgānusayañca na parijānanti vicikicchānusayañca na parijānanti.

The eighth person, in the sense-sphere, in the three feelings, in the form-sphere, and in the formless-sphere, does not comprehend the underlying tendency to lust for existence from that sphere; but it is not that from that sphere he does not comprehend the underlying tendency to doubt. That same person, in the supramundane, does not comprehend the underlying tendency to lust for existence from that sphere and does not comprehend the underlying tendency to doubt from that sphere. Setting aside the person endowed with the supreme path and the eighth person, the remaining persons do not comprehend the underlying tendency to lust for existence and do not comprehend the underlying tendency to doubt in all spheres.

(Ka) yo yato vicikicchānusayaṃ na parijānāti so tato avijjānusayaṃ na parijānātīti?

The person who, from a certain sphere, does not fully comprehend the latent tendency of doubt, does that person, from that sphere, also not fully comprehend the latent tendency of ignorance?

Aggamaggasamaṅgī kāmadhātuyā tīsu vedanāsu rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā so tato vicikicchānusayaṃ [T 1.0662] na parijānāti, no ca so tato avijjānusayaṃ na parijānāti. Sveva puggalo apariyāpanne so tato vicikicchānusayañca na parijānāti avijjānusayañca na parijānāti. Aggamaggasamaṅgiñca aṭṭhamakañca ṭhapetvā avasesā puggalā sabbattha vicikicchānusayañca na parijānanti avijjānusayañca [M 2.0222] na parijānanti.

A person endowed with the highest path, in the sense-sphere, in the three feelings, in the form-sphere, and in the formless-sphere, does not, from that sphere, fully comprehend the latent tendency of doubt, but it is not that this person, from that sphere, does not fully comprehend the latent tendency of ignorance. That very person, in the unincluded, does not, from that sphere, fully comprehend the latent tendency of doubt and does not fully comprehend the latent tendency of ignorance. Setting aside the person endowed with the highest path and the eighth person, the remaining persons, everywhere, do not fully comprehend the latent tendency of doubt and do not fully comprehend the latent tendency of ignorance.

(Kha) yo vā pana yato avijjānusayaṃ na parijānāti so tato vicikicchānusayaṃ na parijānātīti?

Or again, the person who, from a certain sphere, does not fully comprehend the latent tendency of ignorance, does that person, from that sphere, also not fully comprehend the latent tendency of doubt?

Aṭṭhamako kāmadhātuyā tīsu vedanāsu rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā so tato avijjānusayaṃ na parijānāti, no ca so tato vicikicchānusayaṃ na parijānāti. Sveva puggalo apariyāpanne so tato avijjānusayañca na parijānāti vicikicchānusayañca na parijānāti. Aggamaggasamaṅgiñca aṭṭhamakañca ṭhapetvā avasesā puggalā sabbattha avijjānusayañca na parijānanti vicikicchānusayañca na parijānanti.

The eighth person, in the sense-sphere, in the three feelings, in the form-sphere, and in the formless-sphere, does not, from that sphere, fully comprehend the latent tendency of ignorance, but it is not that this person, from that sphere, does not fully comprehend the latent tendency of doubt. That very person, in the unincluded, does not, from that sphere, fully comprehend the latent tendency of ignorance and does not fully comprehend the latent tendency of doubt. Setting aside the person endowed with the highest path and the eighth person, the remaining persons, everywhere, do not fully comprehend the latent tendency of ignorance and do not fully comprehend the latent tendency of doubt.

258. (Ka) yo [V 2.0290] yato bhavarāgānusayaṃ na parijānāti so tato avijjānusayaṃ na parijānātīti?

258. The person who, from a certain sphere, does not fully comprehend the latent tendency of lust for becoming, does that person, from that sphere, also not fully comprehend the latent tendency of ignorance?

Aggamaggasamaṅgī kāmadhātuyā tīsu vedanāsu so tato bhavarāgānusayaṃ na parijānāti, no ca so tato avijjānusayaṃ na parijānāti. Sveva puggalo apariyāpanne so tato bhavarāgānusayañca na parijānāti avijjānusayañca na parijānāti. Aggamaggasamaṅgiṃ ṭhapetvā avasesā puggalā sabbattha bhavarāgānusayañca na parijānanti avijjānusayañca na parijānanti.

A person endowed with the highest path, in the sense-sphere and in the three feelings, does not, from that sphere, fully comprehend the latent tendency of lust for becoming, but it is not that this person, from that sphere, does not fully comprehend the latent tendency of ignorance. That very person, in the unincluded, does not, from that sphere, fully comprehend the latent tendency of lust for becoming and does not fully comprehend the latent tendency of ignorance. Setting aside the person endowed with the highest path, the remaining persons, everywhere, do not fully comprehend the latent tendency of lust for becoming and do not fully comprehend the latent tendency of ignorance.

(Kha) yo vā pana yato avijjānusayaṃ na parijānāti so tato bhavarāgānusayaṃ na parijānātīti? Āmantā[T 1.0663]. (Ekamūlakaṃ)

Or again, the person who, from a certain sphere, does not fully comprehend the latent tendency of ignorance, does that person, from that sphere, also not fully comprehend the latent tendency of lust for becoming? Yes. (The Single-Rooted Section)

259. (Ka) yo yato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca na parijānāti so tato mānānusayaṃ na parijānātīti?

259. The person who, from a certain sphere, does not fully comprehend the latent tendency of sensual lust and the latent tendency of aversion, does that person, from that sphere, also not fully comprehend the latent tendency of conceit?

Aggamaggasamaṅgī kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā so tato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca na parijānāti, no ca so tato mānānusayaṃ na parijānāti. Sveva puggalo dukkhāya vedanāya apariyāpanne so tato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca na parijānāti mānānusayañca na parijānāti. Dvinnaṃ maggasamaṅgīnaṃ ṭhapetvā avasesā puggalā sabbattha kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca na parijānanti mānānusayañca na parijānanti.

A person endowed with the highest path, in the sense-sphere, in two feelings, in the form-sphere, and in the formless-sphere, does not, from that sphere, fully comprehend the latent tendency of sensual lust and the latent tendency of aversion, but it is not that this person, from that sphere, does not fully comprehend the latent tendency of conceit. That very person, in painful feeling and in the unincluded, does not, from that sphere, fully comprehend the latent tendency of sensual lust and the latent tendency of aversion, and does not fully comprehend the latent tendency of conceit. Setting aside the two persons endowed with the path, the remaining persons, everywhere, do not fully comprehend the latent tendency of sensual lust and the latent tendency of aversion, and do not fully comprehend the latent tendency of conceit.

(Kha) yo vā pana yato mānānusayaṃ na parijānāti so tato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca na parijānātīti?

Or again, the person who, from a certain sphere, does not fully comprehend the latent tendency of conceit, does that person, from that sphere, also not fully comprehend the latent tendency of sensual lust and the latent tendency of aversion?

Anāgāmimaggasamaṅgī dukkhāya vedanāya so tato mānānusayañca kāmarāgānusayañca na parijānāti, no ca so tato paṭighānusayaṃ na parijānāti. Sveva puggalo kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu [M 2.0223] so tato mānānusayañca paṭighānusayañca na parijānāti, no ca so tato kāmarāgānusayaṃ na parijānāti. Sveva puggalo rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā apariyāpanne so tato mānānusayañca na parijānāti kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca [V 2.0291] na parijānāti. Dvinnaṃ maggasamaṅgīnaṃ ṭhapetvā avasesā puggalā sabbattha mānānusayañca na parijānanti kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca na parijānanti.

A person endowed with the path of the non-returner, in painful feeling, does not, from that sphere, fully comprehend the latent tendency of conceit and the latent tendency of sensual lust, but it is not that this person, from that sphere, does not fully comprehend the latent tendency of aversion. That very person, in the sense-sphere and in two feelings, does not, from that sphere, fully comprehend the latent tendency of conceit and the latent tendency of aversion, but it is not that this person, from that sphere, does not fully comprehend the latent tendency of sensual lust. That very person, in the form-sphere, in the formless-sphere, and in the unincluded, does not, from that sphere, fully comprehend the latent tendency of conceit, and does not fully comprehend the latent tendency of sensual lust and the latent tendency of aversion. Setting aside the two persons endowed with the path, the remaining persons, everywhere, do not fully comprehend the latent tendency of conceit, and do not fully comprehend the latent tendency of sensual lust and the latent tendency of aversion.

Yo [T 1.0664] yato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca na parijānāti so tato diṭṭhānusayaṃ…pe… vicikicchānusayaṃ na parijānātīti?

The person who, from a certain sphere, does not fully comprehend the latent tendency of sensual lust and the latent tendency of aversion, does that person, from that sphere, also not fully comprehend the latent tendency of views... up to... the latent tendency of doubt?

Aṭṭhamako kāmadhātuyā tīsu vedanāsu rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā so tato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca na parijānāti, no ca so tato vicikicchānusayaṃ na parijānāti. Sveva puggalo apariyāpanne so tato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca na parijānāti vicikicchānusayañca na parijānāti. Anāgāmimaggasamaṅgiñca aṭṭhamakañca ṭhapetvā avasesā puggalā sabbattha kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca na parijānanti vicikicchānusayañca na parijānanti.

The eighth person, in the sense-sphere, in the three feelings, in the form-sphere, and in the formless-sphere, does not, from that sphere, fully comprehend the latent tendency of sensual lust and the latent tendency of aversion, but it is not that this person, from that sphere, does not fully comprehend the latent tendency of doubt. That very person, in the unincluded, does not, from that sphere, fully comprehend the latent tendency of sensual lust and the latent tendency of aversion, and does not fully comprehend the latent tendency of doubt. Setting aside the person endowed with the path of the non-returner and the eighth person, the remaining persons, everywhere, do not fully comprehend the latent tendency of sensual lust and the latent tendency of aversion, and do not fully comprehend the latent tendency of doubt.

Yo vā pana yato vicikicchānusayaṃ na parijānāti so tato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca na parijānātīti?

Or again, the person who, from a certain sphere, does not fully comprehend the latent tendency of doubt, does that person, from that sphere, also not fully comprehend the latent tendency of sensual lust and the latent tendency of aversion?

Anāgāmimaggasamaṅgī dukkhāya vedanāya so tato vicikicchānusayañca kāmarāgānusayañca na parijānāti, no ca so tato paṭighānusayaṃ na parijānāti. Sveva puggalo kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu so tato vicikicchānusayañca paṭighānusayañca na parijānāti, no ca so tato kāmarāgānusayaṃ na parijānāti. Sveva puggalo rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā apariyāpanne so tato vicikicchānusayañca na parijānāti kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca na parijānāti. Anāgāmimaggasamaṅgiñca aṭṭhamakañca ṭhapetvā avasesā puggalā sabbattha vicikicchānusayañca na parijānanti kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca na parijānanti.

A person endowed with the path of the non-returner, in painful feeling, does not, from that sphere, fully comprehend the latent tendency of doubt and the latent tendency of sensual lust, but it is not that this person, from that sphere, does not fully comprehend the latent tendency of aversion. That very person, in the sense-sphere and in two feelings, does not, from that sphere, fully comprehend the latent tendency of doubt and the latent tendency of aversion, but it is not that this person, from that sphere, does not fully comprehend the latent tendency of sensual lust. That very person, in the form-sphere, in the formless-sphere, and in the unincluded, does not, from that sphere, fully comprehend the latent tendency of doubt, and does not fully comprehend the latent tendency of sensual lust and the latent tendency of aversion. Setting aside the person endowed with the path of the non-returner and the eighth person, the remaining persons, everywhere, do not fully comprehend the latent tendency of doubt, and do not fully comprehend the latent tendency of sensual lust and the latent tendency of aversion.

(Ka) yo yato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca na parijānāti so tato bhavarāgānusayaṃ [T 1.0665] na parijānātīti?

Does a person who, from a certain sphere, does not yet fully comprehend the underlying tendency to sensual lust and the underlying tendency to aversion, from that sphere also not yet fully comprehend the underlying tendency to craving for existence?

Aggamaggasamaṅgī [V 2.0292] rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā so tato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca na parijānāti, no ca so tato bhavarāgānusayaṃ na parijānāti. Sveva puggalo kāmadhātuyā tīsu vedanāsu apariyāpanne so tato [M 2.0224] kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca na parijānāti bhavarāgānusayañca na parijānāti. Dvinnaṃ maggasamaṅgīnaṃ ṭhapetvā avasesā puggalā sabbattha kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca na parijānanti bhavarāgānusayañca na parijānanti.

A person endowed with the highest path, in the form element and in the formless element, from that sphere does not yet fully comprehend the underlying tendency to sensual lust and the underlying tendency to aversion, but that person from that sphere does fully comprehend the underlying tendency to craving for existence. That very person, in the sense-sphere element, in the three feelings, and in the supramundane, from that sphere does not yet fully comprehend the underlying tendency to sensual lust and the underlying tendency to aversion, and also does not yet fully comprehend the underlying tendency to craving for existence. Setting aside the two persons endowed with the paths, the remaining persons everywhere do not yet fully comprehend the underlying tendency to sensual lust and the underlying tendency to aversion, and also do not yet fully comprehend the underlying tendency to craving for existence.

(Kha) yo vā pana yato bhavarāgānusayaṃ na parijānāti so tato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca na parijānātīti?

Or again, does a person who, from a certain sphere, does not yet fully comprehend the underlying tendency to craving for existence, from that sphere also not yet fully comprehend the underlying tendency to sensual lust and the underlying tendency to aversion?

Anāgāmimaggasamaṅgī dukkhāya vedanāya so tato bhavarāgānusayañca kāmarāgānusayañca na parijānāti, no ca so tato paṭighānusayaṃ na parijānāti. Sveva puggalo kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu so tato bhavarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca na parijānāti, no ca so tato kāmarāgānusayaṃ na parijānāti. Sveva puggalo rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā apariyāpanne so tato bhavarāgānusayañca na parijānāti kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca na parijānāti. Dvinnaṃ maggasamaṅgīnaṃ ṭhapetvā avasesā puggalā sabbattha bhavarāgānusayañca na parijānanti kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca na parijānanti.

A person endowed with the path of the non-returner, in painful feeling, from that sphere does not yet fully comprehend the underlying tendency to craving for existence and the underlying tendency to sensual lust, but that person from that sphere does fully comprehend the underlying tendency to aversion. That very person, in the sense-sphere element and in the two feelings, from that sphere does not yet fully comprehend the underlying tendency to craving for existence and the underlying tendency to aversion, but that person from that sphere does fully comprehend the underlying tendency to sensual lust. That very person, in the form element, in the formless element, and in the supramundane, from that sphere does not yet fully comprehend the underlying tendency to craving for existence, and also does not yet fully comprehend the underlying tendency to sensual lust and the underlying tendency to aversion. Setting aside the two persons endowed with the paths, the remaining persons everywhere do not yet fully comprehend the underlying tendency to craving for existence, and also do not yet fully comprehend the underlying tendency to sensual lust and the underlying tendency to aversion.

(Ka) yo yato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca na parijānāti so tato avijjānusayaṃ na parijānātīti?

Does a person who, from a certain sphere, does not yet fully comprehend the underlying tendency to sensual lust and the underlying tendency to aversion, from that sphere also not yet fully comprehend the underlying tendency to ignorance?

Aggamaggasamaṅgī kāmadhātuyā tīsu vedanāsu rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā so tato [T 1.0666] kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca na parijānāti, no ca so tato avijjānusayaṃ na parijānāti. Sveva puggalo apariyāpanne so tato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca na parijānāti avijjānusayañca na parijānāti. Dvinnaṃ maggasamaṅgīnaṃ ṭhapetvā avasesā puggalā sabbattha kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca na parijānanti avijjānusayañca na parijānanti.

A person endowed with the highest path, in the sense-sphere element, in the three feelings, in the form element, and in the formless element, from that sphere does not yet fully comprehend the underlying tendency to sensual lust and the underlying tendency to aversion, but that person from that sphere does fully comprehend the underlying tendency to ignorance. That very person, in the supramundane, from that sphere does not yet fully comprehend the underlying tendency to sensual lust and the underlying tendency to aversion, and also does not yet fully comprehend the underlying tendency to ignorance. Setting aside the two persons endowed with the paths, the remaining persons everywhere do not yet fully comprehend the underlying tendency to sensual lust and the underlying tendency to aversion, and also do not yet fully comprehend the underlying tendency to ignorance.

(Kha) yo [V 2.0293] vā pana yato avijjānusayaṃ na parijānāti so tato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca na parijānātīti?

Or again, does a person who, from a certain sphere, does not yet fully comprehend the underlying tendency to ignorance, from that sphere also not yet fully comprehend the underlying tendency to sensual lust and the underlying tendency to aversion?

Anāgāmimaggasamaṅgī dukkhāya vedanāya so tato avijjānusayañca kāmarāgānusayañca na parijānāti, no ca so tato paṭighānusayaṃ na parijānāti. Sveva puggalo kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu so tato avijjānusayañca paṭighānusayañca na parijānāti, no ca so tato kāmarāgānusayaṃ na parijānāti. Sveva puggalo rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā apariyāpanne so tato avijjānusayañca na parijānāti kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca na parijānāti. Dvinnaṃ maggasamaṅgīnaṃ ṭhapetvā avasesā [M 2.0225] puggalā sabbattha avijjānusayañca na parijānanti kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca na parijānanti. (Dukamūlakaṃ)

A person endowed with the path of the non-returner, in painful feeling, from that sphere does not yet fully comprehend the underlying tendency to ignorance and the underlying tendency to sensual lust, but that person from that sphere does fully comprehend the underlying tendency to aversion. That very person, in the sense-sphere element and in the two feelings, from that sphere does not yet fully comprehend the underlying tendency to ignorance and the underlying tendency to aversion, but that person from that sphere does fully comprehend the underlying tendency to sensual lust. That very person, in the form element, in the formless element, and in the supramundane, from that sphere does not yet fully comprehend the underlying tendency to ignorance, and also does not yet fully comprehend the underlying tendency to sensual lust and the underlying tendency to aversion. Setting aside the two persons endowed with the paths, the remaining persons everywhere do not yet fully comprehend the underlying tendency to ignorance, and also do not yet fully comprehend the underlying tendency to sensual lust and the underlying tendency to aversion. (Rooted in the Dyad)

260. Yo yato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca na parijānāti so tato diṭṭhānusayaṃ…pe… vicikicchānusayaṃ na parijānātīti?

260. Does a person who, from a certain sphere, does not yet fully comprehend the underlying tendency to sensual lust, the underlying tendency to aversion, and the underlying tendency to conceit, from that sphere also not yet fully comprehend the underlying tendency to views... the underlying tendency to doubt?

Aṭṭhamako kāmadhātuyā tīsu vedanāsu rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā so tato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca [T 1.0667] na parijānāti, no ca so tato vicikicchānusayaṃ na parijānāti. Sveva puggalo apariyāpanne so tato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca na parijānāti vicikicchānusayañca na parijānāti. Dvinnaṃ maggasamaṅgīnañca aṭṭhamakañca ṭhapetvā avasesā puggalā sabbattha kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca na parijānanti vicikicchānusayañca na parijānanti.

The person on the path of stream-entry, in the sense-sphere element, in the three feelings, in the form element, and in the formless element, from that sphere does not yet fully comprehend the underlying tendency to sensual lust, the underlying tendency to aversion, and the underlying tendency to conceit, but that person from that sphere does fully comprehend the underlying tendency to doubt. That very person, in the supramundane, from that sphere does not yet fully comprehend the underlying tendency to sensual lust, the underlying tendency to aversion, and the underlying tendency to conceit, and also does not yet fully comprehend the underlying tendency to doubt. Setting aside the two persons endowed with the paths and the person on the path of stream-entry, the remaining persons everywhere do not yet fully comprehend the underlying tendency to sensual lust, the underlying tendency to aversion, and the underlying tendency to conceit, and also do not yet fully comprehend the underlying tendency to doubt.

Yo vā pana yato vicikicchānusayaṃ na parijānāti so tato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca na parijānātīti?

Or again, does a person who, from a certain sphere, does not yet fully comprehend the underlying tendency to doubt, from that sphere also not yet fully comprehend the underlying tendency to sensual lust, the underlying tendency to aversion, and the underlying tendency to conceit?

Anāgāmimaggasamaṅgī dukkhāya vedanāya so tato vicikicchānusayañca kāmarāgānusayañca mānānusayañca na parijānāti, no ca so tato paṭighānusayaṃ na parijānāti. Sveva puggalo kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu so tato vicikicchānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca na parijānāti, no ca so tato kāmarāgānusayaṃ na parijānāti. Sveva puggalo rūpadhātuyā [V 2.0294] arūpadhātuyā apariyāpanne so tato vicikicchānusayañca na parijānāti kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca na parijānāti. Aggamaggasamaṅgī kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā so tato vicikicchānusayañca kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca na parijānāti, no ca so tato mānānusayaṃ na parijānāti. Sveva puggalo dukkhāya vedanāya apariyāpanne so tato vicikicchānusayañca na parijānāti kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca na parijānāti. Dvinnaṃ maggasamaṅgīnañca [T 1.0668] aṭṭhamakañca ṭhapetvā avasesā puggalā sabbattha vicikicchānusayañca na parijānanti kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca na parijānanti.

A person endowed with the path of the non-returner, in regard to painful feeling, does not yet fully comprehend from that the latent tendency of doubt, the latent tendency of sensual lust, and the latent tendency of conceit, but it is not that he does not fully comprehend from that the latent tendency of aversion. That same person, in regard to the sense-sphere and the two feelings, does not yet fully comprehend from that the latent tendency of doubt, the latent tendency of aversion, and the latent tendency of conceit, but it is not that he does not fully comprehend from that the latent tendency of sensual lust. That same person, in regard to the fine-material sphere, the immaterial sphere, and the unincluded, does not yet fully comprehend from that the latent tendency of doubt, the latent tendency of sensual lust, the latent tendency of aversion, and the latent tendency of conceit. A person endowed with the highest path, in regard to the sense-sphere, the two feelings, the fine-material sphere, and the immaterial sphere, does not yet fully comprehend from that the latent tendency of doubt, the latent tendency of sensual lust, and the latent tendency of aversion, but it is not that he does not fully comprehend from that the latent tendency of conceit. That same person, in regard to painful feeling and the unincluded, does not yet fully comprehend from that the latent tendency of doubt, the latent tendency of sensual lust, the latent tendency of aversion, and the latent tendency of conceit. Setting aside the two persons endowed with the path and the eighth individual, the remaining persons do not yet fully comprehend anywhere the latent tendency of doubt, the latent tendency of sensual lust, the latent tendency of aversion, and the latent tendency of conceit.

(Ka) yo yato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca na parijānāti so tato bhavarāgānusayaṃ na parijānātīti? Āmantā.

Does a person who, in a certain respect, does not yet fully comprehend the latent tendency of sensual lust, the latent tendency of aversion, and the latent tendency of conceit, from that, also not yet fully comprehend the latent tendency of lust for becoming? Yes.

(Kha) yo [M 2.0226] vā pana yato bhavarāgānusayaṃ na parijānāti so tato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca na parijānātīti?

Or, does a person who, in a certain respect, does not yet fully comprehend the latent tendency of lust for becoming, from that, also not yet fully comprehend the latent tendency of sensual lust, the latent tendency of aversion, and the latent tendency of conceit?

Anāgāmimaggasamaṅgī dukkhāya vedanāya so tato bhavarāgānusayañca kāmarāgānusayañca mānānusayañca na parijānāti, no ca so tato paṭighānusayaṃ na parijānāti. Sveva puggalo kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu so tato bhavarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca na parijānāti, no ca so tato kāmarāgānusayaṃ na parijānāti. Sveva puggalo rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā apariyāpanne so tato bhavarāgānusayañca na parijānāti kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca na parijānāti. Aggamaggasamaṅgī kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu so tato bhavarāgānusayañca kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca na parijānāti, no ca so tato mānānusayaṃ na parijānāti. Sveva puggalo dukkhāya vedanāya apariyāpanne so tato bhavarāgānusayañca na parijānāti kāmarāgānusayañca [V 2.0295] paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca na parijānāti. Dvinnaṃ maggasamaṅgīnaṃ ṭhapetvā avasesā puggalā sabbattha bhavarāgānusayañca na parijānanti kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca [T 1.0669] mānānusayañca na parijānanti.

A person endowed with the path of the non-returner, in regard to painful feeling, does not yet fully comprehend from that the latent tendency of lust for becoming, the latent tendency of sensual lust, and the latent tendency of conceit, but it is not that he does not fully comprehend from that the latent tendency of aversion. That same person, in regard to the sense-sphere and the two feelings, does not yet fully comprehend from that the latent tendency of lust for becoming, the latent tendency of aversion, and the latent tendency of conceit, but it is not that he does not fully comprehend from that the latent tendency of sensual lust. That same person, in regard to the fine-material sphere, the immaterial sphere, and the unincluded, does not yet fully comprehend from that the latent tendency of lust for becoming, and he does not yet fully comprehend the latent tendency of sensual lust, the latent tendency of aversion, and the latent tendency of conceit. A person endowed with the highest path, in regard to the sense-sphere and the two feelings, does not yet fully comprehend from that the latent tendency of lust for becoming, the latent tendency of sensual lust, and the latent tendency of aversion, but it is not that he does not fully comprehend from that the latent tendency of conceit. That same person, in regard to painful feeling and the unincluded, does not yet fully comprehend from that the latent tendency of lust for becoming, and he does not yet fully comprehend the latent tendency of sensual lust, the latent tendency of aversion, and the latent tendency of conceit. Setting aside the two persons endowed with the path, the remaining persons do not yet fully comprehend anywhere the latent tendency of lust for becoming, and they do not yet fully comprehend the latent tendency of sensual lust, the latent tendency of aversion, and the latent tendency of conceit.

(Ka) yo yato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca na parijānāti so tato avijjānusayaṃ na parijānātīti?

Does a person who, in a certain respect, does not yet fully comprehend the latent tendency of sensual lust, the latent tendency of aversion, and the latent tendency of conceit, from that, also not yet fully comprehend the latent tendency of ignorance?

Aggamaggasamaṅgī dukkhāya vedanāya so tato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca na parijānāti, no ca so tato avijjānusayaṃ na parijānāti. Sveva puggalo apariyāpanne so tato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca na parijānāti avijjānusayañca na parijānāti. Dvinnaṃ maggasamaṅgīnaṃ ṭhapetvā avasesā puggalā sabbattha kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca na parijānanti avijjānusayañca na parijānanti.

A person endowed with the highest path, in regard to painful feeling, does not yet fully comprehend from that the latent tendency of sensual lust, the latent tendency of aversion, and the latent tendency of conceit, but it is not that he does not fully comprehend from that the latent tendency of ignorance. That same person, in regard to the unincluded, does not yet fully comprehend from that the latent tendency of sensual lust, the latent tendency of aversion, and the latent tendency of conceit, and he does not yet fully comprehend the latent tendency of ignorance. Setting aside the two persons endowed with the path, the remaining persons do not yet fully comprehend anywhere the latent tendency of sensual lust, the latent tendency of aversion, and the latent tendency of conceit, and they do not yet fully comprehend the latent tendency of ignorance.

(Kha) yo vā pana yato avijjānusayaṃ na parijānāti so tato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca na parijānātīti?

Or, does a person who, in a certain respect, does not yet fully comprehend the latent tendency of ignorance, from that, also not yet fully comprehend the latent tendency of sensual lust, the latent tendency of aversion, and the latent tendency of conceit?

Anāgāmimaggasamaṅgī dukkhāya vedanāya so tato avijjānusayañca kāmarāgānusayañca mānānusayañca na parijānāti, no ca so tato paṭighānusayaṃ na parijānāti. Sveva puggalo kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu so tato avijjānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca [M 2.0227] na parijānāti, no ca so tato kāmarāgānusayaṃ na parijānāti. Sveva puggalo rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā apariyāpanne so tato avijjānusayañca na parijānāti kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca na parijānāti. Dvinnaṃ maggasamaṅgīnaṃ ṭhapetvā avasesā puggalā sabbattha avijjānusayañca na parijānanti kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca [T 1.0670] na parijānanti. (Tikamūlakaṃ)

A person endowed with the path of the non-returner, in regard to painful feeling, does not yet fully comprehend from that the latent tendency of ignorance, the latent tendency of sensual lust, and the latent tendency of conceit, but it is not that he does not fully comprehend from that the latent tendency of aversion. That same person, in regard to the sense-sphere and the two feelings, does not yet fully comprehend from that the latent tendency of ignorance, the latent tendency of aversion, and the latent tendency of conceit, but it is not that he does not fully comprehend from that the latent tendency of sensual lust. That same person, in regard to the fine-material sphere, the immaterial sphere, and the unincluded, does not yet fully comprehend from that the latent tendency of ignorance, and he does not yet fully comprehend the latent tendency of sensual lust, the latent tendency of aversion, and the latent tendency of conceit. Setting aside the two persons endowed with the path, the remaining persons do not yet fully comprehend anywhere the latent tendency of ignorance, and they do not yet fully comprehend the latent tendency of sensual lust, the latent tendency of aversion, and the latent tendency of conceit. (Rooted in the Triad)

261. (Ka) yo [V 2.0296] yato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca diṭṭhānusayañca na parijānāti so tato vicikicchānusayaṃ na parijānātīti? Āmantā.

261. Does a person who, in a certain respect, does not yet fully comprehend the latent tendency of sensual lust, the latent tendency of aversion, the latent tendency of conceit, and the latent tendency of views, from that, also not yet fully comprehend the latent tendency of doubt? Yes.

(Kha) yo vā pana yato vicikicchānusayaṃ na parijānāti so tato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca diṭṭhānusayañca na parijānātīti?

Or, does a person who, in a certain respect, does not yet fully comprehend the latent tendency of doubt, from that, also not yet fully comprehend the latent tendency of sensual lust, the latent tendency of aversion, the latent tendency of conceit, and the latent tendency of views?

Anāgāmimaggasamaṅgī dukkhāya vedanāya so tato vicikicchānusayañca kāmarāgānusayañca mānānusayañca diṭṭhānusayañca na parijānāti, no ca so tato paṭighānusayaṃ na parijānāti. Sveva puggalo kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu so tato vicikicchānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca diṭṭhānusayañca na parijānāti, no ca so tato kāmarāgānusayaṃ na parijānāti. Sveva puggalo rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā apariyāpanne so tato vicikicchānusayañca na parijānāti kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca diṭṭhānusayañca na parijānāti. Aggamaggasamaṅgī kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā so tato vicikicchānusayañca kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca diṭṭhānusayañca na parijānāti, no ca so tato mānānusayaṃ na parijānāti. Sveva puggalo dukkhāya vedanāya apariyāpanne so tato vicikicchānusayañca [T 1.0671] na parijānāti kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca diṭṭhānusayañca na parijānāti. Dvinnaṃ maggasamaṅgīnañca aṭṭhamakañca ṭhapetvā avasesā puggalā sabbattha vicikicchānusayañca na parijānanti kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca diṭṭhānusayañca na parijānanti …pe…. (Catukkamūlakaṃ)

A person endowed with the path of non-returning, with respect to painful feeling, does not from that sphere fully comprehend the latent tendency of doubt, the latent tendency of sensual lust, the latent tendency of conceit, and the latent tendency of wrong views; but it is not that this person from that sphere does not fully comprehend the latent tendency of aversion. That same person, in the sense-sphere with respect to two feelings, does not from that sphere fully comprehend the latent tendency of doubt, the latent tendency of aversion, the latent tendency of conceit, and the latent tendency of wrong views; but it is not that this person from that sphere does not fully comprehend the latent tendency of sensual lust. That same person, in the form-sphere, the formless-sphere, and in the unincluded, does not from that sphere fully comprehend the latent tendency of doubt, and does not fully comprehend the latent tendency of sensual lust, the latent tendency of aversion, the latent tendency of conceit, and the latent tendency of wrong views. A person endowed with the highest path, in the sense-sphere with respect to two feelings, in the form-sphere, and in the formless-sphere, does not from that sphere fully comprehend the latent tendency of doubt, the latent tendency of sensual lust, the latent tendency of aversion, and the latent tendency of wrong views; but it is not that this person from that sphere does not fully comprehend the latent tendency of conceit. That same person, with respect to painful feeling and in the unincluded, does not from that sphere fully comprehend the latent tendency of doubt, and does not fully comprehend the latent tendency of sensual lust, the latent tendency of aversion, the latent tendency of conceit, and the latent tendency of wrong views. Setting aside the two persons endowed with the paths, the remaining persons do not in all instances fully comprehend the latent tendency of doubt, and do not fully comprehend the latent tendency of sensual lust, the latent tendency of aversion, the latent tendency of conceit, and the latent tendency of wrong views.

262. (Ka) yo yato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca diṭṭhānusayañca vicikicchānusayañca na parijānāti so tato bhavarāgānusayaṃ na parijānātīti? Āmantā.

262. Does a person who, from a certain sphere, does not fully comprehend the latent tendency of sensual lust, the latent tendency of aversion, the latent tendency of conceit, the latent tendency of wrong views, and the latent tendency of doubt, from that sphere also not fully comprehend the latent tendency of lust for existence? Yes.

(Kha) yo [V 2.0297] vā pana yato bhavarāgānusayaṃ [M 2.0228] na parijānāti so tato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca diṭṭhānusayañca vicikicchānusayañca na parijānātīti?

Or, does a person who, from a certain sphere, does not fully comprehend the latent tendency of lust for existence, from that sphere also not fully comprehend the latent tendency of sensual lust, the latent tendency of aversion, the latent tendency of conceit, the latent tendency of wrong views, and the latent tendency of doubt?

Aṭṭhamako kāmadhātuyā tīsu vedanāsu rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā so tato bhavarāgānusayañca kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca na parijānāti, no ca so tato diṭṭhānusayañca vicikicchānusayañca na parijānāti. Sveva puggalo apariyāpanne so tato bhavarāgānusayañca na parijānāti kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca diṭṭhānusayañca vicikicchānusayañca na parijānāti. Anāgāmimaggasamaṅgī dukkhāya vedanāya so tato bhavarāgānusayañca kāmarāgānusayañca mānānusayañca diṭṭhānusayañca vicikicchānusayañca na parijānāti, no ca so tato paṭighānusayaṃ na parijānāti. Sveva puggalo kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu so tato bhavarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca diṭṭhānusayañca vicikicchānusayañca na parijānāti, no ca so tato kāmarāgānusayaṃ na parijānāti. Sveva puggalo rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā apariyāpanne so tato bhavarāgānusayañca na parijānāti kāmarāgānusayañca [T 1.0672] paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca diṭṭhānusayañca vicikicchānusayañca na parijānāti. Aggamaggasamaṅgī kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu so tato bhavarāgānusayañca kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca diṭṭhānusayañca vicikicchānusayañca na parijānāti, no ca so tato mānānusayaṃ na parijānāti. Sveva puggalo dukkhāya vedanāya apariyāpanne so tato bhavarāgānusayañca na parijānāti kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca diṭṭhānusayañca vicikicchānusayañca na parijānāti. Dvinnaṃ maggasamaṅgīnañca aṭṭhamakañca ṭhapetvā avasesā puggalā sabbattha bhavarāgānusayañca na parijānanti kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca diṭṭhānusayañca vicikicchānusayañca na parijānanti.

The eighth person, in the sense-sphere with respect to three feelings, in the form-sphere, and in the formless-sphere, does not from that sphere fully comprehend the latent tendency of lust for existence, the latent tendency of sensual lust, the latent tendency of aversion, and the latent tendency of conceit; but it is not that this person from that sphere does not fully comprehend the latent tendency of wrong views and the latent tendency of doubt. That same person, in the unincluded, does not from that sphere fully comprehend the latent tendency of lust for existence, and does not fully comprehend the latent tendency of sensual lust, the latent tendency of aversion, the latent tendency of conceit, the latent tendency of wrong views, and the latent tendency of doubt. A person endowed with the path of non-returning, with respect to painful feeling, does not from that sphere fully comprehend the latent tendency of lust for existence, the latent tendency of sensual lust, the latent tendency of conceit, the latent tendency of wrong views, and the latent tendency of doubt; but it is not that this person from that sphere does not fully comprehend the latent tendency of aversion. That same person, in the sense-sphere with respect to two feelings, does not from that sphere fully comprehend the latent tendency of lust for existence, the latent tendency of aversion, the latent tendency of conceit, the latent tendency of wrong views, and the latent tendency of doubt; but it is not that this person from that sphere does not fully comprehend the latent tendency of sensual lust. That same person, in the form-sphere, the formless-sphere, and in the unincluded, does not from that sphere fully comprehend the latent tendency of lust for existence, and does not fully comprehend the latent tendency of sensual lust, the latent tendency of aversion, the latent tendency of conceit, the latent tendency of wrong views, and the latent tendency of doubt. A person endowed with the highest path, in the sense-sphere with respect to two feelings, does not from that sphere fully comprehend the latent tendency of lust for existence, the latent tendency of sensual lust, the latent tendency of aversion, the latent tendency of wrong views, and the latent tendency of doubt; but it is not that this person from that sphere does not fully comprehend the latent tendency of conceit. That same person, with respect to painful feeling and in the unincluded, does not from that sphere fully comprehend the latent tendency of lust for existence, and does not fully comprehend the latent tendency of sensual lust, the latent tendency of aversion, the latent tendency of conceit, the latent tendency of wrong views, and the latent tendency of doubt. Setting aside the two persons endowed with the paths and the eighth person, the remaining persons do not in all instances fully comprehend the latent tendency of lust for existence, and do not fully comprehend the latent tendency of sensual lust, the latent tendency of aversion, the latent tendency of conceit, the latent tendency of wrong views, and the latent tendency of doubt.

(Ka) yo yato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca diṭṭhānusayañca [V 2.0298] vicikicchānusayañca na parijānāti so tato avijjānusayaṃ na parijānātīti?

Does a person who, from a certain sphere, does not fully comprehend the latent tendency of sensual lust, the latent tendency of aversion, the latent tendency of conceit, the latent tendency of wrong views, and the latent tendency of doubt, from that sphere also not fully comprehend the latent tendency of ignorance?

Aggamaggasamaṅgī dukkhāya vedanāya so tato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca diṭṭhānusayañca vicikicchānusayañca na parijānāti, no ca so tato avijjānusayaṃ na parijānāti[M 2.0229]. Sveva puggalo apariyāpanne so tato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca diṭṭhānusayañca vicikicchānusayañca na parijānāti avijjānusayañca na parijānāti. Dvinnaṃ maggasamaṅgīnañca aṭṭhamakañca ṭhapetvā avasesā puggalā sabbattha kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca diṭṭhānusayañca vicikicchānusayañca [T 1.0673] na parijānanti avijjānusayañca na parijānanti.

A person endowed with the highest path, with respect to painful feeling, does not from that sphere fully comprehend the latent tendency of sensual lust, the latent tendency of aversion, the latent tendency of conceit, the latent tendency of wrong views, and the latent tendency of doubt; but it is not that this person from that sphere does not fully comprehend the latent tendency of ignorance. That same person, in the unincluded, does not from that sphere fully comprehend the latent tendency of sensual lust, the latent tendency of aversion, the latent tendency of conceit, the latent tendency of wrong views, and the latent tendency of doubt, and does not fully comprehend the latent tendency of ignorance. Setting aside the two persons endowed with the paths and the eighth person, the remaining persons do not in all instances fully comprehend the latent tendency of sensual lust, the latent tendency of aversion, the latent tendency of conceit, the latent tendency of wrong views, and the latent tendency of doubt, and do not fully comprehend the latent tendency of ignorance.

(Kha) yo vā pana yato avijjānusayaṃ na parijānāti so tato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca diṭṭhānusayañca vicikicchānusayañca na parijānātīti?

Or, does a person who, from a certain sphere, does not fully comprehend the latent tendency of ignorance, from that sphere also not fully comprehend the latent tendency of sensual lust, the latent tendency of aversion, the latent tendency of conceit, the latent tendency of wrong views, and the latent tendency of doubt?

Aṭṭhamako kāmadhātuyā tīsu vedanāsu rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā so tato avijjānusayañca kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca na parijānāti, no ca so tato diṭṭhānusayañca vicikicchānusayañca na parijānāti. Sveva puggalo apariyāpanne so tato avijjānusayañca na parijānāti kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca diṭṭhānusayañca vicikicchānusayañca na parijānāti. Anāgāmimaggasamaṅgī dukkhāya vedanāya so tato avijjānusayañca kāmarāgānusayañca mānānusayañca diṭṭhānusayañca vicikicchānusayañca na parijānāti, no ca so tato paṭighānusayaṃ na parijānāti. Sveva puggalo kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu so tato avijjānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca diṭṭhānusayañca vicikicchānusayañca na parijānāti, no ca so tato kāmarāgānusayaṃ na parijānāti. Sveva puggalo rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā apariyāpanne so tato avijjānusayañca na parijānāti kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca [V 2.0299] mānānusayañca diṭṭhānusayañca vicikicchānusayañca na parijānāti. Dvinnaṃ maggasamaṅgīnañca aṭṭhamakañca ṭhapetvā avasesā puggalā sabbattha avijjānusayañca na parijānanti kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca [T 1.0674] diṭṭhānusayañca vicikicchānusayañca na parijānanti. (Pañcakamūlakaṃ)

The eighth person—in the sense-sphere, in the three feelings, in the fine-material sphere, and in the immaterial sphere—that person from that sphere does not fully comprehend the underlying tendency of ignorance, the underlying tendency of sensual lust, the underlying tendency of aversion, and the underlying tendency of conceit; but it is not that that person from that sphere does not fully comprehend the underlying tendency of views and the underlying tendency of doubt. That same person—in the supramundane—that person from that sphere does not fully comprehend the underlying tendency of ignorance, and does not fully comprehend the underlying tendency of sensual lust, the underlying tendency of aversion, the underlying tendency of conceit, the underlying tendency of views, and the underlying tendency of doubt. The one endowed with the path of non-returning—in painful feeling—that person from that sphere does not fully comprehend the underlying tendency of ignorance, the underlying tendency of sensual lust, the underlying tendency of conceit, the underlying tendency of views, and the underlying tendency of doubt; but it is not that that person from that sphere does not fully comprehend the underlying tendency of aversion. That same person—in the sense-sphere, in two feelings—that person from that sphere does not fully comprehend the underlying tendency of ignorance, the underlying tendency of aversion, the underlying tendency of conceit, the underlying tendency of views, and the underlying tendency of doubt; but it is not that that person from that sphere does not fully comprehend the underlying tendency of sensual lust. That same person—in the fine-material sphere, in the immaterial sphere, and in the supramundane—that person from that sphere does not fully comprehend the underlying tendency of ignorance, and does not fully comprehend the underlying tendency of sensual lust, the underlying tendency of aversion, the underlying tendency of conceit, the underlying tendency of views, and the underlying tendency of doubt. Setting aside the two persons endowed with the paths and the eighth person, the remaining persons in all spheres do not fully comprehend the underlying tendency of ignorance, and do not fully comprehend the underlying tendency of sensual lust, the underlying tendency of aversion, the underlying tendency of conceit, the underlying tendency of views, and the underlying tendency of doubt.

263. (Ka) yo yato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca diṭṭhānusayañca vicikicchānusayañca bhavarāgānusayañca na parijānāti so tato avijjānusayaṃ na parijānātīti?

263. Does the person who from a certain sphere does not fully comprehend the underlying tendency of sensual lust, the underlying tendency of aversion, the underlying tendency of conceit, the underlying tendency of views, the underlying tendency of doubt, and the underlying tendency of lust for existence—does that person from that sphere not fully comprehend the underlying tendency of ignorance?

Aggamaggasamaṅgī dukkhāya vedanāya so tato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca diṭṭhānusayañca vicikicchānusayañca bhavarāgānusayañca na parijānāti, no ca so tato [M 2.0230] avijjānusayaṃ na parijānāti. Sveva puggalo apariyāpanne so tato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca diṭṭhānusayañca vicikicchānusayañca bhavarāgānusayañca na parijānāti avijjānusayañca na parijānāti. Dvinnaṃ maggasamaṅgīnañca aṭṭhamakañca ṭhapetvā avasesā puggalā sabbattha kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca diṭṭhānusayañca vicikicchānusayañca bhavarāgānusayañca na parijānanti avijjānusayañca na parijānanti.

The one endowed with the highest path—in painful feeling—that person from that sphere does not fully comprehend the underlying tendency of sensual lust, the underlying tendency of aversion, the underlying tendency of conceit, the underlying tendency of views, the underlying tendency of doubt, and the underlying tendency of lust for existence; but it is not that that person from that sphere does not fully comprehend the underlying tendency of ignorance. That same person—in the supramundane—that person from that sphere does not fully comprehend the underlying tendency of sensual lust, the underlying tendency of aversion, the underlying tendency of conceit, the underlying tendency of views, the underlying tendency of doubt, and the underlying tendency of lust for existence, and does not fully comprehend the underlying tendency of ignorance. Setting aside the two persons endowed with the paths and the eighth person, the remaining persons in all spheres do not fully comprehend the underlying tendency of sensual lust, the underlying tendency of aversion, the underlying tendency of conceit, the underlying tendency of views, the underlying tendency of doubt, and the underlying tendency of lust for existence, and they do not fully comprehend the underlying tendency of ignorance.

(Kha) yo vā pana yato avijjānusayaṃ na parijānāti so tato kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca diṭṭhānusayañca vicikicchānusayañca bhavarāgānusayañca na parijānātīti?

Or again, does the person who from a certain sphere does not fully comprehend the underlying tendency of ignorance—does that person from that sphere not fully comprehend the underlying tendency of sensual lust, the underlying tendency of aversion, the underlying tendency of conceit, the underlying tendency of views, the underlying tendency of doubt, and the underlying tendency of lust for existence?

Aṭṭhamako kāmadhātuyā tīsu vedanāsu rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā so tato avijjānusayañca kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca bhavarāgānusayañca na parijānāti, no ca so tato diṭṭhānusayañca vicikicchānusayañca na parijānāti. Sveva puggalo apariyāpanne so tato avijjānusayañca na parijānāti kāmarāgānusayañca [T 1.0675] paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca diṭṭhānusayañca vicikicchānusayañca [V 2.0300] bhavarāgānusayañca na parijānāti. Anāgāmimaggasamaṅgī dukkhāya vedanāya so tato avijjānusayañca kāmarāgānusayañca mānānusayañca diṭṭhānusayañca vicikicchānusayañca bhavarāgānusayañca na parijānāti, no ca so tato paṭighānusayaṃ na parijānāti. Sveva puggalo kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu so tato avijjānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca diṭṭhānusayañca vicikicchānusayañca bhavarāgānusayañca na parijānāti, no ca so tato kāmarāgānusayaṃ na parijānāti. Sveva puggalo rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā apariyāpanne so tato avijjānusayañca na parijānāti kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca diṭṭhānusayañca vicikicchānusayañca bhavarāgānusayañca na parijānāti. Dvinnaṃ maggasamaṅgīnañca aṭṭhamakañca ṭhapetvā avasesā puggalā sabbattha avijjānusayañca na parijānanti kāmarāgānusayañca paṭighānusayañca mānānusayañca diṭṭhānusayañca vicikicchānusayañca bhavarāgānusayañca na parijānanti. (Chakkamūlakaṃ)

The eighth person—in the sense-sphere, in the three feelings, in the fine-material sphere, and in the immaterial sphere—that person from that sphere does not fully comprehend the underlying tendency of ignorance, the underlying tendency of sensual lust, the underlying tendency of aversion, the underlying tendency of conceit, and the underlying tendency of lust for existence; but it is not that that person from that sphere does not fully comprehend the underlying tendency of views and the underlying tendency of doubt. That same person—in the supramundane—that person from that sphere does not fully comprehend the underlying tendency of ignorance, and does not fully comprehend the underlying tendency of sensual lust, the underlying tendency of aversion, the underlying tendency of conceit, the underlying tendency of views, the underlying tendency of doubt, and the underlying tendency of lust for existence. The one endowed with the path of non-returning—in painful feeling—that person from that sphere does not fully comprehend the underlying tendency of ignorance, the underlying tendency of sensual lust, the underlying tendency of conceit, the underlying tendency of views, the underlying tendency of doubt, and the underlying tendency of lust for existence; but it is not that that person from that sphere does not fully comprehend the underlying tendency of aversion. That same person—in the sense-sphere, in two feelings—that person from that sphere does not fully comprehend the underlying tendency of ignorance, the underlying tendency of aversion, the underlying tendency of conceit, the underlying tendency of views, the underlying tendency of doubt, and the underlying tendency of lust for existence; but it is not that that person from that sphere does not fully comprehend the underlying tendency of sensual lust. That same person—in the fine-material sphere, in the immaterial sphere, and in the supramundane—that person from that sphere does not fully comprehend the underlying tendency of ignorance, and does not fully comprehend the underlying tendency of sensual lust, the underlying tendency of aversion, the underlying tendency of conceit, the underlying tendency of views, the underlying tendency of doubt, and the underlying tendency of lust for existence. Setting aside the two persons endowed with the paths and the eighth person, the remaining persons in all spheres do not fully comprehend the underlying tendency of ignorance, and do not fully comprehend the underlying tendency of sensual lust, the underlying tendency of aversion, the underlying tendency of conceit, the underlying tendency of views, the underlying tendency of doubt, and the underlying tendency of lust for existence.

Pariññāvāre paṭilomaṃ.

The Reverse Section in the Chapter on Full Comprehension.

Pariññāvāro.

The Chapter on Full Comprehension is finished.

5. Pahīnavāro

The Chapter on Abandonment

(Ka) anulomapuggalo

(Ka) The Positive Person

264. (Ka) yassa [M 2.0231] kāmarāgānusayo pahīno tassa paṭighānusayo pahīnoti? Āmantā.

5. For a person by whom the underlying tendency of sensual lust has been abandoned, has the underlying tendency of aversion been abandoned? Yes.

(Kha) yassa [V 2.0301] vā pana paṭighānusayo pahīno tassa kāmarāgānusayo [T 1.0676] pahīnoti? Āmantā.

Or again, for a person by whom the underlying tendency of aversion has been abandoned, has the underlying tendency of sensual lust been abandoned? Yes.

(Ka) yassa kāmarāgānusayo pahīno tassa mānānusayo pahīnoti?

264. For a person by whom the underlying tendency of sensual lust has been abandoned, has the underlying tendency of conceit been abandoned?

Anāgāmissa kāmarāgānusayo pahīno, no ca tassa mānānusayo pahīno. Arahato kāmarāgānusayo ca pahīno mānānusayo ca pahīno.

For a non-returner, the underlying tendency of sensual lust has been abandoned, but for that person the underlying tendency of conceit has not been abandoned. For an Arahant, both the underlying tendency of sensual lust and the underlying tendency of conceit have been abandoned.

(Kha) yassa vā pana mānānusayo pahīno tassa kāmarāgānusayo pahīnoti? Āmantā.

Or again, for a person by whom the underlying tendency of conceit has been abandoned, has the underlying tendency of sensual lust been abandoned? Yes.

Yassa kāmarāgānusayo pahīno tassa diṭṭhānusayo…pe… vicikicchānusayo pahīnoti? Āmantā.

For a person by whom the underlying tendency of sensual lust has been abandoned, have the underlying tendency of views... the underlying tendency of doubt been abandoned? Yes.

Yassa vā pana vicikicchānusayo pahīno tassa kāmarāgānusayo pahīnoti?

Or again, for a person for whom the underlying tendency of doubt has been abandoned, has the underlying tendency of sensual lust been abandoned for him?

Dvinnaṃ puggalānaṃ vicikicchānusayo pahīno, no ca tesaṃ kāmarāgānusayo pahīno. Dvinnaṃ puggalānaṃ vicikicchānusayo ca pahīno kāmarāgānusayo ca pahīno.

For two individuals (the Stream-enterer and the Once-returner), the underlying tendency of doubt has been abandoned, but for them the underlying tendency of sensual lust has not been abandoned. For two individuals (the Non-returner and the Arahant), both the underlying tendency of doubt and the underlying tendency of sensual lust have been abandoned.

Yassa kāmarāgānusayo pahīno tassa bhavarāgānusayo…pe… avijjānusayo pahīnoti?

For a person for whom the underlying tendency of sensual lust has been abandoned, have the underlying tendency of lust for becoming... up to... the underlying tendency of ignorance been abandoned for him?

Anāgāmissa kāmarāgānusayo pahīno, no ca tassa avijjānusayo pahīno. Arahato kāmarāgānusayo ca pahīno avijjānusayo ca pahīno.

For a Non-returner, the underlying tendency of sensual lust has been abandoned, but for him the underlying tendency of ignorance has not been abandoned. For an Arahant, both the underlying tendency of sensual lust and the underlying tendency of ignorance have been abandoned.

Yassa vā pana avijjānusayo pahīno tassa kāmarāgānusayo pahīnoti? Āmantā.

Or again, for a person for whom the underlying tendency of ignorance has been abandoned, has the underlying tendency of sensual lust been abandoned for him? Yes.

265. (Ka) yassa paṭighānusayo pahīno tassa mānānusayo pahīnoti?

265. (A) For a person for whom the underlying tendency of aversion has been abandoned, has the underlying tendency of conceit been abandoned for him?

Anāgāmissa paṭighānusayo pahīno, no ca tassa mānānusayo pahīno. Arahato paṭighānusayo ca pahīno mānānusayo ca pahīno.

Dvinnaṃ puggalānaṃ vicikicchānusayo pahīno, no ca tesaṃ paṭighānusayo pahīno. Dvinnaṃ puggalānaṃ vicikicchānusayo ca pahīno paṭighānusayo ca pahīno.

For two individuals (the Stream-enterer and the Once-returner), the underlying tendency of doubt has been abandoned, but for them the underlying tendency of aversion has not been abandoned. Yassa paṭighānusayo pahīno tassa bhavarāgānusayo…pe… avijjānusayo pahīnoti?

For a person for whom the underlying tendency of aversion has been abandoned, have the underlying tendency of lust for becoming... up to... the underlying tendency of ignorance been abandoned for him?

Anāgāmissa paṭighānusayo pahīno, no ca tassa avijjānusayo pahīno. Arahato paṭighānusayo ca pahīno avijjānusayo ca pahīno.

For a Non-returner, the underlying tendency of aversion has been abandoned, but for him the underlying tendency of ignorance has not been abandoned. For an Arahant, both the underlying tendency of aversion and the underlying tendency of ignorance have been abandoned.

Yassa vā pana avijjānusayo pahīno tassa paṭighānusayo pahīnoti? Āmantā.

Or again, for a person for whom the underlying tendency of ignorance has been abandoned, has the underlying tendency of aversion been abandoned for him? Yes.

266. Yassa mānānusayo pahīno tassa diṭṭhānusayo…pe… vicikicchānusayo pahīnoti? Āmantā.

266. For a person for whom the underlying tendency of conceit has been abandoned, have the underlying tendency of views... up to... the underlying tendency of doubt been abandoned for him? Yes.

Yassa vā pana vicikicchānusayo pahīno tassa mānānusayo pahīnoti?

Or again, for a person for whom the underlying tendency of doubt has been abandoned, has the underlying tendency of conceit been abandoned for him?

Tiṇṇaṃ puggalānaṃ vicikicchānusayo pahīno, no ca tesaṃ mānānusayo pahīno. Arahato vicikicchānusayo ca pahīno mānānusayo ca pahīno.

For three individuals (the Stream-enterer, the Once-returner, and the Non-returner), the underlying tendency of doubt has been abandoned, but for them the underlying tendency of conceit has not been abandoned. For an Arahant, both the underlying tendency of doubt and the underlying tendency of conceit have been abandoned.

Yassa mānānusayo pahīno tassa bhavarāgānusayo…pe… avijjānusayo pahīnoti? Āmantā.

For a person for whom the underlying tendency of conceit has been abandoned, have the underlying tendency of lust for becoming... up to... the underlying tendency of ignorance been abandoned for him? Yes.

Yassa [V 2.0303] vā pana avijjānusayo pahīno tassa mānānusayo pahīnoti? Āmantā.

Or again, for a person for whom the underlying tendency of ignorance has been abandoned, has the underlying tendency of conceit been abandoned for him? Yes.

267. (Ka) yassa diṭṭhānusayo pahīno tassa vicikicchānusayo pahīnoti? Āmantā.

267. (A) For a person for whom the underlying tendency of views has been abandoned, has the underlying tendency of doubt been abandoned for him? Yes.

(Kha) yassa vā pana vicikicchānusayo pahīno tassa diṭṭhānusayo pahīnoti? Āmantā …pe….

(B) Or again, for a person for whom the underlying tendency of doubt has been abandoned, has the underlying tendency of views been abandoned for him? Yes... and so on.

268. Yassa [T 1.0678] vicikicchānusayo pahīno tassa bhavarāgānusayo…pe… avijjānusayo pahīnoti?

268. For a person for whom the underlying tendency of doubt has been abandoned, have the underlying tendency of lust for becoming... up to... the underlying tendency of ignorance been abandoned for him?

For three individuals (the Stream-enterer, the Once-returner, and the Non-returner), the underlying tendency of doubt has been abandoned, but for them the underlying tendency of ignorance has not been abandoned. For an Arahant, both the underlying tendency of doubt and the underlying tendency of ignorance have been abandoned.
