Or again, for a person for whom the underlying tendency of ignorance has been abandoned, has the underlying tendency of doubt been abandoned for him? Yes.

269. (Ka) yassa bhavarāgānusayo pahīno tassa avijjānusayo pahīnoti? Āmantā.

269. (A) For a person for whom the underlying tendency of lust for becoming has been abandoned, has the underlying tendency of ignorance been abandoned for him? Yes.

(Kha) yassa vā pana avijjānusayo pahīno tassa bhavarāgānusayo pahīnoti? Āmantā. (Ekamūlakaṃ)

(B) Or again, for a person for whom the underlying tendency of ignorance has been abandoned, has the underlying tendency of lust for becoming been abandoned for him? Yes. (The Single-Root Section)

270. (Ka) yassa [M 2.0233] kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca pahīnā pahīno (sī. ka.) anusayavārena pana na sameti tassa mānānusayo pahīnoti?

270. (A) For a person for whom both the underlying tendency of sensual lust and the underlying tendency of aversion have been abandoned, has the underlying tendency of conceit been abandoned for him?

Anāgāmissa kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca pahīnā, no ca tassa mānānusayo pahīno. Arahato kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca pahīnā mānānusayo ca pahīno.

For a Non-returner, both the underlying tendency of sensual lust and the underlying tendency of aversion have been abandoned, but for him the underlying tendency of conceit has not been abandoned. For an Arahant, both the underlying tendency of sensual lust and the underlying tendency of aversion have been abandoned, and the underlying tendency of conceit has also been abandoned.

(Kha) yassa vā pana mānānusayo pahīno tassa kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca pahīnāti? Āmantā.

(B) Or again, for a person for whom the underlying tendency of conceit has been abandoned, have both the underlying tendency of sensual lust and the underlying tendency of aversion been abandoned for him? Yes.

Yassa [V 2.0304] kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca pahīnā tassa diṭṭhānusayo…pe… vicikicchānusayo pahīnoti? Āmantā.

For a person for whom both the underlying tendency of sensual lust and the underlying tendency of aversion have been abandoned, have the underlying tendency of views... up to... the underlying tendency of doubt been abandoned for him? Yes.

Yassa vā pana vicikicchānusayo pahīno tassa kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca pahīnāti?

Or again, for a person for whom the underlying tendency of doubt has been abandoned, have both the underlying tendency of sensual lust and the underlying tendency of aversion been abandoned for him?

Dvinnaṃ puggalānaṃ vicikicchānusayo pahīno, no ca tesaṃ kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca pahīnā. Dvinnaṃ puggalānaṃ vicikicchānusayo ca pahīno kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca pahīnā.

For two individuals (the Stream-enterer and the Once-returner), the underlying tendency of doubt has been abandoned, but for them both the underlying tendency of sensual lust and the underlying tendency of aversion have not been abandoned. For two individuals (the Non-returner and the Arahant), the underlying tendency of doubt has been abandoned, and both the underlying tendency of sensual lust and the underlying tendency of aversion have also been abandoned.

Yassa kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo [T 1.0679] ca pahīnā tassa bhavarāgānusayo…pe… avijjānusayo pahīnoti?

For a person for whom both the underlying tendency of sensual lust and the underlying tendency of aversion have been abandoned, have the underlying tendency of lust for becoming... up to... the underlying tendency of ignorance been abandoned for him?

Anāgāmissa kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca pahīnā, no ca tassa avijjānusayo pahīno. Arahato kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca pahīnā avijjānusayo ca pahīno.

For a Non-returner, both the underlying tendency of sensual lust and the underlying tendency of aversion have been abandoned, but for him the underlying tendency of ignorance has not been abandoned. For an Arahant, both the underlying tendency of sensual lust and the underlying tendency of aversion have been abandoned, and the underlying tendency of ignorance has also been abandoned.

Yassa vā pana avijjānusayo pahīno tassa kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca pahīnāti? Āmantā. (Dukamūlakaṃ)

Or again, for a person for whom the underlying tendency of ignorance has been abandoned, have both the underlying tendency of sensual lust and the underlying tendency of aversion been abandoned for him? Yes. (The Dyad-Root Section)

271. Yassa kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca mānānusayo ca pahīnā tassa diṭṭhānusayo…pe… vicikicchānusayo pahīnoti? Āmantā.

271. For a person for whom the underlying tendencies of sensual lust, aversion, and conceit have been abandoned, have the underlying tendency of views... up to... the underlying tendency of doubt been abandoned for him? Yes.

Yassa vā pana vicikicchānusayo pahīno tassa kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca mānānusayo ca pahīnāti?

Or again, for a person for whom the underlying tendency of doubt has been abandoned, have the underlying tendencies of sensual lust, aversion, and conceit been abandoned for him?

Dvinnaṃ puggalānaṃ vicikicchānusayo pahīno, no ca tesaṃ kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca mānānusayo ca pahīnā. Anāgāmissa vicikicchānusayo ca kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca pahīnā, no ca tassa mānānusayo pahīno. Arahato vicikicchānusayo ca pahīno kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca mānānusayo ca pahīnā.

For two individuals (the Stream-enterer and the Once-returner), the underlying tendency of doubt has been abandoned, but for them the underlying tendencies of sensual lust, aversion, and conceit have not been abandoned. For a Non-returner, the underlying tendencies of doubt, sensual lust, and aversion have been abandoned, but for him the underlying tendency of conceit has not been abandoned. For an Arahant, the underlying tendency of doubt has been abandoned, and the underlying tendencies of sensual lust, aversion, and conceit have also been abandoned.

Yassa [M 2.0234][V 2.0305] kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca mānānusayo [T 1.0680] ca pahīnā tassa bhavarāgānusayo…pe… avijjānusayo pahīnoti? Āmantā.

For one who has abandoned the underlying tendencies of sensual desire, aversion, and conceit, have the underlying tendencies of craving for existence... up to... ignorance also been abandoned? Yes.

Yassa vā pana avijjānusayo pahīno tassa kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca mānānusayo ca pahīnāti? Āmantā. (Tikamūlakaṃ)

Or, for one who has abandoned the underlying tendency of ignorance, have the underlying tendencies of sensual desire, aversion, and conceit also been abandoned? Yes. (The Triad Root.)

272. (Ka) yassa kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca mānānusayo ca diṭṭhānusayo ca pahīnā tassa vicikicchānusayo pahīnoti? Āmantā.

272. (A) For one who has abandoned the underlying tendencies of sensual desire, aversion, conceit, and wrong view, has the underlying tendency of doubt also been abandoned? Yes.

(Kha) yassa vā pana vicikicchānusayo pahīno tassa kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca mānānusayo ca diṭṭhānusayo ca pahīnāti?

(B) Or, for one who has abandoned the underlying tendency of doubt, have the underlying tendencies of sensual desire, aversion, conceit, and wrong view also been abandoned?

Dvinnaṃ puggalānaṃ vicikicchānusayo ca diṭṭhānusayo ca pahīnā, no ca tesaṃ kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca mānānusayo ca pahīnā. Anāgāmissa vicikicchānusayo ca kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca diṭṭhānusayo ca pahīnā, no ca tassa mānānusayo pahīno. Arahato vicikicchānusayo ca pahīno kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca mānānusayo ca diṭṭhānusayo ca pahīnā …pe…. (Catukkamūlakaṃ)

For two individuals, the underlying tendencies of doubt and wrong view have been abandoned, but for them the underlying tendencies of sensual desire, aversion, and conceit have not been abandoned. For a non-returner, the underlying tendencies of doubt, sensual desire, aversion, and wrong view have been abandoned, but for that one the underlying tendency of conceit has not been abandoned. For an arahant, the underlying tendencies of doubt, sensual desire, aversion, conceit, and wrong view have been abandoned…pe…. (The Tetrad Root.)

273. Yassa kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca mānānusayo ca diṭṭhānusayo ca vicikicchānusayo ca pahīnā tassa bhavarāgānusayo…pe… avijjānusayo pahīnoti? Āmantā.

273. For one who has abandoned the underlying tendencies of sensual desire, aversion, conceit, wrong view, and doubt, have the underlying tendencies of craving for existence... up to... ignorance also been abandoned? Yes.

Yassa vā pana avijjānusayo pahīno tassa kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca mānānusayo ca diṭṭhānusayo ca vicikicchānusayo ca pahīnāti? Āmantā. (Pañcakamūlakaṃ)

Or, for one who has abandoned the underlying tendency of ignorance, have the underlying tendencies of sensual desire, aversion, conceit, wrong view, and doubt also been abandoned? Yes. (The Pentad Root.)

274. (Ka) yassa kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca mānānusayo ca diṭṭhānusayo ca vicikicchānusayo ca bhavarāgānusayo ca pahīnā tassa avijjānusayo pahīnoti? Āmantā.

274. (A) For one who has abandoned the underlying tendencies of sensual desire, aversion, conceit, wrong view, doubt, and craving for existence, has the underlying tendency of ignorance also been abandoned? Yes.

(Kha) yassa vā pana avijjānusayo pahīno tassa kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo [V 2.0306] ca mānānusayo ca diṭṭhānusayo ca vicikicchānusayo ca bhavarāgānusayo ca pahīnāti? Āmantā. (Chakkamūlakaṃ)

(B) Or, for one who has abandoned the underlying tendency of ignorance, have the underlying tendencies of sensual desire, aversion, conceit, wrong view, doubt, and craving for existence also been abandoned? Yes. (The Hexad Root.)

(Kha) anulomaokāso

(B) The Positive Method Section

275. (Ka) yattha [T 1.0681][M 2.0235] kāmarāgānusayo pahīno tattha paṭighānusayo pahīnoti?

275. (A) Where the underlying tendency to sensual lust is abandoned, is the underlying tendency to aversion also abandoned there?

Na vattabbo “pahīno”ti vā “appahīno”ti vā.

It should not be said ‘it is abandoned’ or ‘it is not abandoned’.

(Kha) yattha vā pana paṭighānusayo pahīno tattha kāmarāgānusayo pahīnoti?

(B) Or where the underlying tendency to aversion is abandoned, is the underlying tendency to sensual lust also abandoned there?

Na vattabbo “pahīno”ti vā “appahīno”ti vā.

It should not be said ‘it is abandoned’ or ‘it is not abandoned’.

(Ka) yattha kāmarāgānusayo pahīno tattha mānānusayo pahīnoti? Āmantā.

(A) Where the underlying tendency to sensual lust is abandoned, is the underlying tendency to conceit also abandoned there? Yes.

(Kha) yattha vā pana mānānusayo pahīno tattha kāmarāgānusayo pahīnoti?

(B) Or where the underlying tendency to conceit is abandoned, is the underlying tendency to sensual lust also abandoned there?

Rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā ettha mānānusayo pahīno; kāmarāgānusayo na vattabbo “pahīno”ti vā “appahīno”ti vā. Kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu ettha mānānusayo ca pahīno kāmarāgānusayo ca pahīno.

In the form-sphere and the formless-sphere, the underlying tendency to conceit is abandoned; regarding the underlying tendency to sensual lust, it should not be said ‘it is abandoned’ or ‘it is not abandoned’. In the sense-sphere, with regard to the two feelings, both the underlying tendency to conceit and the underlying tendency to sensual lust are abandoned.

Yattha kāmarāgānusayo pahīno tattha diṭṭhānusayo…pe… vicikicchānusayo pahīnoti? Āmantā.

Where the underlying tendency of sensual lust is abandoned, are the underlying tendencies of wrong view and doubt also abandoned there? Yes.

Yattha vā pana vicikicchānusayo pahīno tattha kāmarāgānusayo pahīnoti?

Or where the underlying tendency to doubt is abandoned, is the underlying tendency to sensual lust also abandoned there?

Dukkhāya vedanāya rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā ettha vicikicchānusayo pahīno; kāmarāgānusayo na vattabbo “pahīno”ti vā “appahīno”ti vā. Kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu ettha vicikicchānusayo ca pahīno kāmarāgānusayo ca pahīno.

With regard to painful feeling, in the form-sphere, and in the formless-sphere, the underlying tendency to doubt is abandoned; regarding the underlying tendency to sensual lust, it should not be said ‘it is abandoned’ or ‘it is not abandoned’. In the sense-sphere, with regard to the two feelings, both the underlying tendency to doubt and the underlying tendency to sensual lust are abandoned.

(Ka) yattha kāmarāgānusayo pahīno tattha bhavarāgānusayo pahīnoti?

(A) Where the underlying tendency to sensual lust is abandoned, is the underlying tendency to craving for existence also abandoned there?

Na vattabbo “pahīno”ti vā “appahīno”ti vā.

It should not be said ‘it is abandoned’ or ‘it is not abandoned’.

(Kha) yattha vā pana bhavarāgānusayo pahīno tattha kāmarāgānusayo pahīnoti?

(B) Or where the underlying tendency to craving for existence is abandoned, is the underlying tendency to sensual lust also abandoned there?

Na vattabbo “pahīno”ti vā “appahīno”ti vā.

It should not be said ‘it is abandoned’ or ‘it is not abandoned’.

(Ka) yattha [V 2.0307] kāmarāgānusayo pahīno tattha avijjānusayo pahīnoti? Āmantā.

(A) Where the underlying tendency to sensual lust is abandoned, is the underlying tendency to ignorance also abandoned there? Yes.

(Kha) yattha vā pana avijjānusayo pahīno tattha kāmarāgānusayo pahīnoti?

(B) Or where the underlying tendency to ignorance is abandoned, is the underlying tendency to sensual lust also abandoned there?

Dukkhāya vedanāya [T 1.0682] rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā ettha avijjānusayo pahīno; kāmarāgānusayo na vattabbo “pahīno”ti vā “appahīno”ti vā. Kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu ettha avijjānusayo ca pahīno kāmarāgānusayo ca pahīno.

With regard to painful feeling, in the form-sphere, and in the formless-sphere, the underlying tendency to ignorance is abandoned; regarding the underlying tendency to sensual lust, it should not be said ‘it is abandoned’ or ‘it is not abandoned’. In the sense-sphere, with regard to the two feelings, both the underlying tendency to ignorance and the underlying tendency to sensual lust are abandoned.

276. (Ka) yattha [M 2.0236] paṭighānusayo pahīno tattha mānānusayo pahīnoti?

276. (A) Where the underlying tendency to aversion is abandoned, is the underlying tendency to conceit also abandoned there?

Na vattabbo “pahīno”ti vā “appahīno”ti vā.

It should not be said ‘it is abandoned’ or ‘it is not abandoned’.

(Kha) yattha vā pana mānānusayo pahīno tattha paṭighānusayo pahīnoti?

(B) Or where the underlying tendency to conceit is abandoned, is the underlying tendency to aversion also abandoned there?

Na vattabbo “pahīno”ti vā “appahīno”ti vā.

It should not be said ‘it is abandoned’ or ‘it is not abandoned’.

Yattha paṭighānusayo pahīno tattha diṭṭhānusayo…pe… vicikicchānusayo pahīnoti? Āmantā.

Where the underlying tendency of aversion is abandoned, are the underlying tendencies of wrong view and doubt also abandoned there? Yes.

Yattha vā pana vicikicchānusayo pahīno tattha paṭighānusayo pahīnoti?

Or where the underlying tendency to doubt is abandoned, is the underlying tendency to aversion also abandoned there?

Kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā ettha vicikicchānusayo pahīno; paṭighānusayo na vattabbo “pahīno”ti vā “appahīno”ti vā. Dukkhāya vedanāya ettha vicikicchānusayo ca pahīno paṭighānusayo ca pahīno.

In the sense-sphere, with regard to the two feelings, in the form-sphere, and in the formless-sphere, the underlying tendency to doubt is abandoned; regarding the underlying tendency to aversion, it should not be said ‘it is abandoned’ or ‘it is not abandoned’. With regard to painful feeling, both the underlying tendency to doubt and the underlying tendency to aversion are abandoned.

(Ka) yattha paṭighānusayo pahīno tattha bhavarāgānusayo pahīnoti?

(A) Where the underlying tendency to aversion is abandoned, is the underlying tendency to craving for existence also abandoned there?

Na vattabbo “pahīno”ti vā “appahīno”ti vā.

It should not be said ‘it is abandoned’ or ‘it is not abandoned’.

(Kha) yattha vā pana bhavarāgānusayo pahīno tattha paṭighānusayo pahīnoti?

(B) Or where the underlying tendency to craving for existence is abandoned, is the underlying tendency to aversion also abandoned there?

Na vattabbo “pahīno”ti vā “appahīno”ti vā.

It should not be said ‘it is abandoned’ or ‘it is not abandoned’.

(Ka) yattha [V 2.0308] paṭighānusayo pahīno tattha avijjānusayo pahīnoti? Āmantā.

(A) Where the underlying tendency to aversion is abandoned, is the underlying tendency to ignorance also abandoned there? Yes.

(Kha) yattha vā pana avijjānusayo pahīno tattha paṭighānusayo pahīnoti?

Or where the underlying tendency to ignorance is abandoned, is the underlying tendency to aversion also abandoned there?

Kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā ettha avijjānusayo pahīno; paṭighānusayo na vattabbo “pahīno”ti vā “appahīno”ti vā. Dukkhāya [T 1.0683] vedanāya ettha avijjānusayo ca pahīno paṭighānusayo ca pahīno.

In the sense-sphere, in the two feelings, in the form-sphere, and in the formless-sphere, here the underlying tendency to ignorance is abandoned; but regarding the underlying tendency to aversion, it should not be said to be ‘abandoned’ or ‘not abandoned’. In painful feeling, here both the underlying tendency to ignorance and the underlying tendency to aversion are abandoned.

277. Yattha mānānusayo pahīno tattha diṭṭhānusayo…pe… vicikicchānusayo pahīnoti? Āmantā.

277. Where the underlying tendency to conceit is abandoned, is the underlying tendency to wrong view…pe… the underlying tendency to doubt also abandoned there? Yes.

Yattha vā pana vicikicchānusayo pahīno tattha mānānusayo pahīnoti?

Or where the underlying tendency to doubt is abandoned, is the underlying tendency to conceit also abandoned there?

Dukkhāya vedanāya ettha vicikicchānusayo pahīno; mānānusayo na vattabbo “pahīno”ti vā “appahīno”ti vā. Kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā ettha vicikicchānusayo ca pahīno mānānusayo ca pahīno.

In painful feeling, here the underlying tendency to doubt is abandoned; but regarding the underlying tendency to conceit, it should not be said to be ‘abandoned’ or ‘not abandoned’. In the sense-sphere, in the two feelings, in the form-sphere, and in the formless-sphere, here both the underlying tendency to doubt and the underlying tendency to conceit are abandoned.

(Ka) yattha mānānusayo pahīno tattha bhavarāgānusayo pahīnoti?

Where the underlying tendency to conceit is abandoned, is the underlying tendency to craving for existence also abandoned there?

Kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu ettha mānānusayo pahīno; bhavarāgānusayo na vattabbo “pahīno”ti vā “appahīno”ti vā. Rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā [M 2.0237] ettha mānānusayo ca pahīno bhavarāgānusayo ca pahīno.

In the sense-sphere and in the two feelings, here the underlying tendency to conceit is abandoned; but regarding the underlying tendency to craving for existence, it should not be said to be ‘abandoned’ or ‘not abandoned’. In the form-sphere and the formless-sphere, here both the underlying tendency to conceit and the underlying tendency to craving for existence are abandoned.

(Kha) yattha vā pana bhavarāgānusayo pahīno tattha mānānusayo pahīnoti? Āmantā.

Or where the underlying tendency to craving for existence is abandoned, is the underlying tendency to conceit also abandoned there? Yes.

(Ka) yattha mānānusayo pahīno tattha avijjānusayo pahīnoti? Āmantā.

Where the underlying tendency to conceit is abandoned, is the underlying tendency to ignorance also abandoned there? Yes.

(Kha) yattha vā pana avijjānusayo pahīno tattha mānānusayo pahīnoti?

Or where the underlying tendency to ignorance is abandoned, is the underlying tendency to conceit also abandoned there?

Dukkhāya vedanāya ettha avijjānusayo pahīno; mānānusayo na vattabbo “pahīno”ti vā “appahīno”ti vā. Kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu [V 2.0309] rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā ettha avijjānusayo ca pahīno mānānusayo ca pahīno.

In painful feeling, here the underlying tendency to ignorance is abandoned; but regarding the underlying tendency to conceit, it should not be said to be ‘abandoned’ or ‘not abandoned’. In the sense-sphere, in the two feelings, in the form-sphere, and in the formless-sphere, here both the underlying tendency to ignorance and the underlying tendency to conceit are abandoned.

278. (Ka) yattha diṭṭhānusayo pahīno tattha vicikicchānusayo pahīnoti[T 1.0684]? Āmantā.

278. Where the underlying tendency to wrong view is abandoned, is the underlying tendency to doubt also abandoned there? Yes.

(Kha) yattha vā pana vicikicchānusayo pahīno tattha diṭṭhānusayo pahīnoti? Āmantā …pe….

Or where the underlying tendency to doubt is abandoned, is the underlying tendency to wrong view also abandoned there? Yes…pe….

279. (Ka) yattha vicikicchānusayo pahīno tattha bhavarāgānusayo pahīnoti?

279. Where the underlying tendency to doubt is abandoned, is the underlying tendency to craving for existence also abandoned there?

Kāmadhātuyā tīsu vedanāsu ettha vicikicchānusayo pahīno; bhavarāgānusayo na vattabbo “pahīno”ti vā “appahīno”ti vā. Rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā ettha vicikicchānusayo ca pahīno bhavarāgānusayo ca pahīno.

In the sense-sphere and in the three feelings, here the underlying tendency to doubt is abandoned; but regarding the underlying tendency to craving for existence, it should not be said to be ‘abandoned’ or ‘not abandoned’. In the form-sphere and the formless-sphere, here both the underlying tendency to doubt and the underlying tendency to craving for existence are abandoned.

(Kha) yattha vā pana bhavarāgānusayo pahīno tattha vicikicchānusayo pahīnoti? Āmantā.

Or where the underlying tendency to craving for existence is abandoned, is the underlying tendency to doubt also abandoned there? Yes.

(Ka) yattha vicikicchānusayo pahīno tattha avijjānusayo pahīnoti? Āmantā.

Where the underlying tendency to doubt is abandoned, is the underlying tendency to ignorance also abandoned there? Yes.

(Kha) yattha vā pana avijjānusayo pahīno tattha vicikicchānusayo pahīnoti? Āmantā.

Or where the underlying tendency to ignorance is abandoned, is the underlying tendency to doubt also abandoned there? Yes.

280. (Ka) yattha bhavarāgānusayo pahīno tattha avijjānusayo pahīnoti? Āmantā.

280. Where the underlying tendency to craving for existence is abandoned, is the underlying tendency to ignorance also abandoned there? Yes.

(Kha) yattha vā pana avijjānusayo pahīno tattha bhavarāgānusayo pahīnoti?

Or where the underlying tendency to ignorance is abandoned, is the underlying tendency to craving for existence also abandoned there?

Kāmadhātuyā tīsu vedanāsu ettha avijjānusayo pahīno; bhavarāgānusayo na vattabbo “pahīno”ti vā “appahīno”ti vā. Rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā ettha avijjānusayo ca pahīno bhavarāgānusayo ca pahīno. (Ekamūlakaṃ)

In the sense-sphere and in the three feelings, here the underlying tendency to ignorance is abandoned; but regarding the underlying tendency to craving for existence, it should not be said to be 'abandoned' or 'not abandoned.' In the form-sphere and the formless-sphere, here both the underlying tendency to ignorance and the underlying tendency to craving for existence are abandoned. (Single Root)

281. (Ka) yattha [V 2.0310] kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca pahīnā tattha mānānusayo pahīnoti? Natthi.

281. Where both the underlying tendency to sensual lust and the underlying tendency to aversion are abandoned, is the underlying tendency to conceit abandoned there? There is not.

(Kha) yattha vā pana mānānusayo pahīno tattha [M 2.0238] kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca pahīnāti?

Or where the underlying tendency to conceit is abandoned, are both the underlying tendency to sensual lust and the underlying tendency to aversion also abandoned there?

Rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā ettha mānānusayo pahīno; kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca na [T 1.0685] vattabbā “pahīnā”ti vā “appahīnā”ti vā. Kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu ettha mānānusayo ca kāmarāgānusayo ca pahīnā; paṭighānusayo na vattabbo “pahīno”ti vā “appahīno”ti vā.

In the form-sphere and the formless-sphere, here the underlying tendency to conceit is abandoned; but regarding both the underlying tendency to sensual lust and the underlying tendency to aversion, it should not be said that 'they are abandoned' or 'they are not abandoned.' In the sense-sphere and in the two feelings, here both the underlying tendency to conceit and the underlying tendency to sensual lust are abandoned; but regarding the underlying tendency to aversion, it should not be said to be 'abandoned' or 'not abandoned.'

Yattha kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca pahīnā tattha diṭṭhānusayo…pe… vicikicchānusayo pahīnoti? Natthi.

Where both the underlying tendency to sensual lust and the underlying tendency to aversion are abandoned, is the underlying tendency to wrong view...pe...the underlying tendency to doubt abandoned there? There is not.

Yattha vā pana vicikicchānusayo pahīno tattha kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca pahīnāti?

Or where the underlying tendency to doubt is abandoned, are both the underlying tendency to sensual lust and the underlying tendency to aversion also abandoned there?

Rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā ettha vicikicchānusayo pahīno; kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca na vattabbā “pahīnā”ti vā “appahīnā”ti vā. Kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu ettha vicikicchānusayo ca kāmarāgānusayo ca pahīnā; paṭighānusayo na vattabbo “pahīno”ti vā “appahīno”ti vā. Dukkhāya vedanāya ettha vicikicchānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca pahīnā; kāmarāgānusayo na vattabbo “pahīno”ti vā “appahīno”ti vā.

In the form-sphere and the formless-sphere, here the underlying tendency to doubt is abandoned; but regarding both the underlying tendency to sensual lust and the underlying tendency to aversion, it should not be said that 'they are abandoned' or 'they are not abandoned.' In the sense-sphere and in the two feelings, here both the underlying tendency to doubt and the underlying tendency to sensual lust are abandoned; but regarding the underlying tendency to aversion, it should not be said to be 'abandoned' or 'not abandoned.' In painful feeling, here both the underlying tendency to doubt and the underlying tendency to aversion are abandoned; but regarding the underlying tendency to sensual lust, it should not be said to be 'abandoned' or 'not abandoned.'

(Ka) yattha kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca pahīnā tattha bhavarāgānusayo pahīnoti? Natthi.

Where both the underlying tendency to sensual lust and the underlying tendency to aversion are abandoned, is the underlying tendency to craving for existence abandoned there? There is not.

(Kha) yattha vā pana bhavarāgānusayo pahīno tattha kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca pahīnāti?

Or where the underlying tendency to craving for existence is abandoned, are both the underlying tendency to sensual lust and the underlying tendency to aversion also abandoned there?

Na vattabbā “pahīnā”ti vā “appahīnā”ti vā.

It should not be said that 'they are abandoned' or 'they are not abandoned.'

(Ka) yattha [V 2.0311] kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca pahīnā tattha avijjānusayo pahīnoti? Natthi.

Where both the underlying tendency to sensual lust and the underlying tendency to aversion are abandoned, is the underlying tendency to ignorance abandoned there? There is not.

(Kha) yattha vā pana avijjānusayo pahīno tattha kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca pahīnāti?

Or where the underlying tendency to ignorance is abandoned, are both the underlying tendency to sensual lust and the underlying tendency to aversion abandoned there?

Rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā ettha avijjānusayo pahīno; kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca na vattabbā “pahīnā”ti vā “appahīnā”ti [T 1.0686] vā. Kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu ettha avijjānusayo ca kāmarāgānusayo ca pahīnā; paṭighānusayo na vattabbo “pahīno”ti vā “appahīno”ti vā. Dukkhāya vedanāya ettha avijjānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca pahīnā; kāmarāgānusayo na vattabbo “pahīno”ti vā “appahīno”ti vā. (Dukamūlakaṃ)

In the form element and the formless element, here the underlying tendency to ignorance is abandoned; the underlying tendencies to sensual desire and aversion should not be spoken of as 'abandoned' or 'not abandoned.' In the sense-sphere element, with regard to two feelings, here the underlying tendencies to ignorance and sensual desire are abandoned; the underlying tendency to aversion should not be spoken of as 'abandoned' or 'not abandoned.' With painful feeling, here the underlying tendencies to ignorance and aversion are abandoned; the underlying tendency to sensual desire should not be spoken of as 'abandoned' or 'not abandoned.' (Duo-rooted)

282. Yattha [M 2.0239] kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca mānānusayo ca pahīnā tattha diṭṭhānusayo…pe… vicikicchānusayo pahīnoti? Natthi.

282. Where the underlying tendencies to sensual desire, aversion, and conceit are abandoned, is the underlying tendency to views... pe... the underlying tendency to doubt abandoned there? No.

Yattha vā pana vicikicchānusayo pahīno tattha kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca mānānusayo ca pahīnāti?

Or, where the underlying tendency to doubt is abandoned, are the underlying tendencies to sensual desire, aversion, and conceit abandoned there?

Rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā ettha vicikicchānusayo ca mānānusayo ca pahīnā; kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca na vattabbā “pahīnā”ti vā “appahīnā”ti vā. Kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu ettha vicikicchānusayo ca kāmarāgānusayo ca mānānusayo ca pahīnā; paṭighānusayo na vattabbo “pahīno”ti vā “appahīno”ti vā. Dukkhāya vedanāya ettha vicikicchānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca pahīnā; kāmarāgānusayo ca mānānusayo ca na vattabbā “pahīnā”ti vā “appahīnā”ti vā.

In the form element and the formless element, here the underlying tendencies to doubt and conceit are abandoned; the underlying tendencies to sensual desire and aversion should not be spoken of as 'abandoned' or 'not abandoned.' In the sense-sphere element, with regard to two feelings, here the underlying tendencies to doubt, sensual desire, and conceit are abandoned; the underlying tendency to aversion should not be spoken of as 'abandoned' or 'not abandoned.' With painful feeling, here the underlying tendencies to doubt and aversion are abandoned; the underlying tendencies to sensual desire and conceit should not be spoken of as 'abandoned' or 'not abandoned.'

(Ka) yattha kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca mānānusayo ca pahīnā tattha bhavarāgānusayo pahīnoti? Natthi.

(Ka) Where the underlying tendencies to sensual desire, aversion, and conceit are abandoned, is the underlying tendency to craving for existence abandoned there? No.

(Kha) yattha [V 2.0312] vā pana bhavarāgānusayo pahīno tattha kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca mānānusayo ca pahīnāti?

(Kha) Or, where the underlying tendency to craving for existence is abandoned, are the underlying tendencies to sensual desire, aversion, and conceit abandoned there?

Mānānusayo pahīno; kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca na vattabbā “pahīnā”ti vā “appahīnā”ti [T 1.0687] vā.

The underlying tendency to conceit is abandoned; the underlying tendencies to sensual desire and aversion should not be spoken of as 'abandoned' or 'not abandoned.'

(Ka) yattha kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca mānānusayo ca pahīnā tattha avijjānusayo pahīnoti? Natthi.

(Ka) Where the underlying tendencies to sensual desire, aversion, and conceit are abandoned, is the underlying tendency to ignorance abandoned there? No.

(Kha) yattha vā pana avijjānusayo pahīno tattha kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca mānānusayo ca pahīnāti?

(Kha) Or, where the underlying tendency to ignorance is abandoned, are the underlying tendencies to sensual desire, aversion, and conceit abandoned there?

Rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā ettha avijjānusayo ca mānānusayo ca pahīnā; kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca na vattabbā “pahīnā”ti vā “appahīnā”ti vā. Kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu ettha avijjānusayo ca kāmarāgānusayo ca mānānusayo ca pahīnā; paṭighānusayo na vattabbo “pahīno”ti vā “appahīno”ti vā. Dukkhāya vedanāya ettha avijjānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca pahīnā; kāmarāgānusayo ca mānānusayo ca na vattabbā “pahīnā”ti vā “appahīnā”ti vā. (Tikamūlakaṃ)

In the form element and the formless element, here the underlying tendencies to ignorance and conceit are abandoned; the underlying tendencies to sensual desire and aversion should not be spoken of as 'abandoned' or 'not abandoned.' In the sense-sphere element, with regard to two feelings, here the underlying tendencies to ignorance, sensual desire, and conceit are abandoned; the underlying tendency to aversion should not be spoken of as 'abandoned' or 'not abandoned.' With painful feeling, here the underlying tendencies to ignorance and aversion are abandoned; the underlying tendencies to sensual desire and conceit should not be spoken of as 'abandoned' or 'not abandoned.' (Trio-rooted)

283. (Ka) yattha kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca mānānusayo ca diṭṭhānusayo ca pahīnā tattha vicikicchānusayo pahīnoti? Natthi.

283. (Ka) Where the underlying tendencies to sensual desire, aversion, conceit, and views are abandoned, is the underlying tendency to doubt abandoned there? No.

(Kha) yattha vā pana vicikicchānusayo pahīno tattha kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo [M 2.0240] ca mānānusayo ca diṭṭhānusayo ca pahīnāti?

(Kha) Or, where the underlying tendency to doubt is abandoned, are the underlying tendencies to sensual desire, aversion, conceit, and views abandoned there?

Rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā ettha vicikicchānusayo ca mānānusayo ca diṭṭhānusayo ca pahīnā; kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca na vattabbā “pahīnā”ti vā “appahīnā”ti vā. Kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu ettha vicikicchānusayo ca kāmarāgānusayo ca mānānusayo ca diṭṭhānusayo ca pahīnā; paṭighānusayo na vattabbo “pahīno”ti vā “appahīno”ti vā. Dukkhāya vedanāya ettha vicikicchānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca diṭṭhānusayo [T 1.0688] ca pahīnā; kāmarāgānusayo ca mānānusayo [V 2.0313] ca na vattabbā “pahīnā”ti vā “appahīnā”ti vā …pe…. (Catukkamūlakaṃ)

In the form element and the formless element, here the underlying tendencies to doubt, conceit, and views are abandoned; the underlying tendencies to sensual desire and aversion should not be spoken of as 'abandoned' or 'not abandoned.' In the sense-sphere element, with regard to two feelings, here the underlying tendencies to doubt, sensual desire, conceit, and views are abandoned; the underlying tendency to aversion should not be spoken of as 'abandoned' or 'not abandoned.' With painful feeling, here the underlying tendencies to doubt, aversion, and views are abandoned; the underlying tendencies to sensual desire and conceit should not be spoken of as 'abandoned' or 'not abandoned.' …pe… (Quartet-rooted)

284. (Ka) yattha kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca mānānusayo ca diṭṭhānusayo ca vicikicchānusayo ca pahīnā tattha bhavarāgānusayo pahīnoti? Natthi.

284. (Ka) Where the underlying tendencies to sensual desire, aversion, conceit, views, and doubt are abandoned, is the underlying tendency to craving for existence abandoned there? No.

(Kha) yattha vā pana bhavarāgānusayo pahīno tattha kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca mānānusayo ca diṭṭhānusayo ca vicikicchānusayo ca pahīnāti?

(Kha) Or, where the underlying tendency to craving for existence is abandoned, are the underlying tendencies to sensual desire, aversion, conceit, views, and doubt abandoned there?

Rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā ettha bhavarāgānusayo ca mānānusayo ca diṭṭhānusayo ca vicikicchānusayo ca pahīnā; kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca na vattabbā “pahīnā”ti vā “appahīnā”ti vā.

In the form element and the formless element, here the underlying tendencies to craving for existence, conceit, views, and doubt are abandoned; the underlying tendencies to sensual desire and aversion should not be spoken of as 'abandoned' or 'not abandoned.'

(Ka) yattha kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca mānānusayo ca diṭṭhānusayo ca vicikicchānusayo ca pahīnā tattha avijjānusayo pahīnoti? Natthi.

(Ka) Where the underlying tendencies to sensual desire, aversion, conceit, views, and doubt are abandoned, is the underlying tendency to ignorance abandoned there? No.

(Kha) yattha vā pana avijjānusayo pahīno tattha kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca mānānusayo ca diṭṭhānusayo ca vicikicchānusayo ca pahīnāti?

(Kha) Or, where the underlying tendency to ignorance is abandoned, are the underlying tendencies to sensual desire, aversion, conceit, views, and doubt abandoned there?

Rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā ettha avijjānusayo ca mānānusayo ca diṭṭhānusayo ca vicikicchānusayo ca pahīnā; kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca na vattabbā “pahīnā”ti vā “appahīnā”ti vā. Kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu ettha avijjānusayo ca kāmarāgānusayo ca mānānusayo ca diṭṭhānusayo ca vicikicchānusayo ca pahīnā; paṭighānusayo na vattabbo “pahīno”ti vā “appahīno”ti vā. Dukkhāya vedanāya ettha avijjānusayo [T 1.0689] ca paṭighānusayo ca diṭṭhānusayo ca vicikicchānusayo ca pahīnā; kāmarāgānusayo ca mānānusayo ca na vattabbā “pahīnā”ti vā “appahīnā”ti vā. (Pañcakamūlakaṃ)

In the form realm and the formless realm, here the underlying tendencies of ignorance, conceit, views, and doubt are abandoned; the underlying tendencies of sensual desire and aversion should not be said to be 'abandoned' or 'not abandoned.' In the sensual realm, in two feelings, here the underlying tendencies of ignorance, sensual desire, conceit, views, and doubt are abandoned; the underlying tendency of aversion should not be said to be 'abandoned' or 'not abandoned.' In painful feeling, here the underlying tendencies of ignorance, aversion, views, and doubt are abandoned; the underlying tendencies of sensual desire and conceit should not be said to be 'abandoned' or 'not abandoned.' (The section rooted in five)

285. (Ka) yattha [M 2.0241] kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca mānānusayo ca diṭṭhānusayo ca [V 2.0314] vicikicchānusayo ca bhavarāgānusayo ca pahīnā tattha avijjānusayo pahīnoti? Natthi.

285. Where the underlying tendencies of sensual desire, aversion, conceit, views, doubt, and craving for existence are abandoned, is the underlying tendency of ignorance abandoned there? No.

(Kha) yattha vā pana avijjānusayo pahīno tattha kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca mānānusayo ca diṭṭhānusayo ca vicikicchānusayo ca bhavarāgānusayo ca pahīnāti?

Or where the underlying tendency of ignorance is abandoned, are the underlying tendencies of sensual desire, aversion, conceit, views, doubt, and craving for existence abandoned there?

Rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā ettha avijjānusayo ca mānānusayo ca diṭṭhānusayo ca vicikicchānusayo ca bhavarāgānusayo ca pahīnā; kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca na vattabbā “pahīnā”ti vā “appahīnā”ti vā. Kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu ettha avijjānusayo ca kāmarāgānusayo ca mānānusayo ca diṭṭhānusayo ca vicikicchānusayo ca pahīnā; paṭighānusayo ca bhavarāgānusayo ca na vattabbā “pahīnā”ti vā “appahīnā”ti vā. Dukkhāya vedanāya ettha avijjānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca diṭṭhānusayo ca vicikicchānusayo ca pahīnā; kāmarāgānusayo ca mānānusayo ca bhavarāgānusayo ca na vattabbā “pahīnā”ti vā “appahīnā”ti vā. (Chakkamūlakaṃ)

In the form realm and the formless realm, here the underlying tendencies of ignorance, conceit, views, doubt, and craving for existence are abandoned; the underlying tendencies of sensual desire and aversion should not be said to be 'abandoned' or 'not abandoned.' In the sensual realm, in two feelings, here the underlying tendencies of ignorance, sensual desire, conceit, views, and doubt are abandoned; the underlying tendencies of aversion and craving for existence should not be said to be 'abandoned' or 'not abandoned.' In painful feeling, here the underlying tendencies of ignorance, aversion, views, and doubt are abandoned; the underlying tendencies of sensual desire, conceit, and craving for existence should not be said to be 'abandoned' or 'not abandoned.' (The section rooted in six)

(Ga) anulomapuggalokāsā

(Ga) Scope of persons in progressive order.

286. (Ka) yassa yattha kāmarāgānusayo pahīno tassa tattha paṭighānusayo pahīnoti?

286. (Ka) For a person for whom the latent tendency to sensual lust is abandoned in a certain plane, for that person, is the latent tendency to aversion abandoned in that plane?

Na vattabbo “pahīno”ti vā “appahīno”ti vā.

It should not be said 'it is abandoned' or 'it is not abandoned.'

(Kha) yassa [T 1.0690] vā pana yattha paṭighānusayo pahīno tassa tattha kāmarāgānusayo pahīnoti?

(Kha) Or again, for a person for whom the latent tendency to aversion is abandoned in a certain plane, for that person, is the latent tendency to sensual lust abandoned in that plane?

Na vattabbo “pahīno”ti vā “appahīno”ti vā.

It should not be said 'it is abandoned' or 'it is not abandoned.'

(Ka) yassa yattha kāmarāgānusayo pahīno tassa tattha mānānusayo pahīnoti?

(Ka) For a person for whom the latent tendency to sensual lust is abandoned in a certain plane, for that person, is the latent tendency to conceit abandoned in that plane?

Anāgāmissa kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu tassa tattha kāmarāgānusayo pahīno, no ca tassa tattha mānānusayo pahīno. Arahato kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu tassa tattha kāmarāgānusayo ca pahīno mānānusayo ca pahīno.

For a non-returner, in the sense-sphere realm and with respect to two feelings, for that person, in that plane, the latent tendency to sensual lust is abandoned, but the latent tendency to conceit is not abandoned for them in that plane. For an Arahant, in the sense-sphere realm and with respect to two feelings, for that person, in that plane, both the latent tendency to sensual lust and the latent tendency to conceit are abandoned.

(Kha) yassa vā pana yattha mānānusayo pahīno tassa tattha kāmarāgānusayo pahīnoti?

(Kha) Or again, for a person for whom the latent tendency to conceit is abandoned in a certain plane, for that person, is the latent tendency to sensual lust abandoned in that plane?

Arahato rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā tassa tattha mānānusayo pahīno; kāmarāgānusayo [V 2.0315] na vattabbo “pahīno”ti vā “appahīno”ti vā. Tasseva puggalassa kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu tassa tattha mānānusayo ca pahīno kāmarāgānusayo ca pahīno.

For an Arahant, in the fine-material sphere and the immaterial sphere, for that person, in that plane, the latent tendency to conceit is abandoned; the latent tendency to sensual lust should not be said to be 'abandoned' or 'not abandoned.' For that same person, in the sense-sphere realm and with respect to two feelings, for that person, in that plane, both the latent tendency to conceit and the latent tendency to sensual lust are abandoned.

(Ka) yassa [M 2.0242] yattha kāmarāgānusayo pahīno tassa tattha diṭṭhānusayo pahīnoti? Āmantā.

(Ka) For a person for whom the latent tendency to sensual lust is abandoned in a certain plane, for that person, is the latent tendency to wrong views abandoned in that plane? Yes.

(Kha) yassa vā pana yattha diṭṭhānusayo pahīno tassa tattha kāmarāgānusayo pahīnoti?

(Kha) Or again, for a person for whom the latent tendency to wrong views is abandoned in a certain plane, for that person, is the latent tendency to sensual lust abandoned in that plane?

Dvinnaṃ puggalānaṃ dukkhāya vedanāya rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā tesaṃ tattha diṭṭhānusayo pahīno; kāmarāgānusayo na vattabbo “pahīno”ti vā “appahīno”ti vā. Tesaññeva puggalānaṃ kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu tesaṃ tattha diṭṭhānusayo pahīno, no ca tesaṃ tattha kāmarāgānusayo pahīno. Dvinnaṃ puggalānaṃ dukkhāya vedanāya rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā tesaṃ tattha diṭṭhānusayo pahīno; kāmarāgānusayo na vattabbo “pahīno”ti vā “appahīno”ti [T 1.0691] vā. Tesaññeva puggalānaṃ kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu tesaṃ tattha diṭṭhānusayo ca pahīno kāmarāgānusayo ca pahīno.

For two persons (the Stream-enterer and the Once-returner), with respect to painful feeling, in the fine-material sphere, and in the immaterial sphere, for them, in that plane, the latent tendency to wrong views is abandoned; the latent tendency to sensual lust should not be said to be 'abandoned' or 'not abandoned.' For those same persons, in the sense-sphere realm and with respect to two feelings, for them, in that plane, the latent tendency to wrong views is abandoned, but the latent tendency to sensual lust is not abandoned for them in that plane. For two persons, with respect to painful feeling, in the fine-material sphere, and in the immaterial sphere, for them, in that plane, the latent tendency to wrong views is abandoned; the latent tendency to sensual lust should not be said to be 'abandoned' or 'not abandoned.' For those same persons, in the sense-sphere realm and with respect to two feelings, for them, in that plane, both the latent tendency to wrong views and the latent tendency to sensual lust are abandoned.

(Ka) yassa yattha kāmarāgānusayo pahīno tassa tattha vicikicchānusayo pahīnoti? Āmantā.

(Ka) For a person for whom the latent tendency to sensual lust is abandoned in a certain plane, for that person, is the latent tendency to doubt abandoned in that plane? Yes.

(Kha) yassa vā pana yattha vicikicchānusayo pahīno tassa tattha kāmarāgānusayo pahīnoti?

(Kha) Or again, for a person for whom the latent tendency to doubt is abandoned in a certain plane, for that person, is the latent tendency to sensual lust abandoned in that plane?

Dvinnaṃ puggalānaṃ dukkhāya vedanāya rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā tesaṃ tattha vicikicchānusayo pahīno; kāmarāgānusayo na vattabbo “pahīno”ti vā “appahīno”ti vā. Tesaññeva puggalānaṃ kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu tesaṃ tattha vicikicchānusayo pahīno, no ca tesaṃ tattha kāmarāgānusayo pahīno. Dvinnaṃ puggalānaṃ dukkhāya vedanāya rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā tesaṃ tattha vicikicchānusayo pahīno; kāmarāgānusayo na vattabbo “pahīno”ti vā “appahīno”ti vā. Tesaññeva puggalānaṃ kāmadhātuyā [V 2.0316] dvīsu vedanāsu tesaṃ tattha vicikicchānusayo ca pahīno kāmarāgānusayo ca pahīno.

For two persons (the Stream-enterer and the Once-returner), with respect to painful feeling, in the fine-material sphere, and in the immaterial sphere, for them, in that plane, the latent tendency to doubt is abandoned; the latent tendency to sensual lust should not be said to be 'abandoned' or 'not abandoned.' For those same persons, in the sense-sphere realm and with respect to two feelings, for them, in that plane, the latent tendency to doubt is abandoned, but the latent tendency to sensual lust is not abandoned for them in that plane. For two persons, with respect to painful feeling, in the fine-material sphere, and in the immaterial sphere, for them, in that plane, the latent tendency to doubt is abandoned; the latent tendency to sensual lust should not be said to be 'abandoned' or 'not abandoned.' For those same persons, in the sense-sphere realm and with respect to two feelings, for them, in that plane, both the latent tendency to doubt and the latent tendency to sensual lust are abandoned.

(Ka) yassa yattha kāmarāgānusayo pahīno tassa tattha bhavarāgānusayo pahīnoti?

(Ka) For a person for whom the latent tendency to sensual lust is abandoned in a certain plane, for that person, is the latent tendency to lust for becoming abandoned in that plane?

Na vattabbo “pahīno”ti vā “appahīno”ti vā.

It should not be said 'it is abandoned' or 'it is not abandoned.'

(Kha) yassa vā pana yattha bhavarāgānusayo pahīno tassa tattha kāmarāgānusayo pahīnoti?

Or again, of a person of whom the latent tendency to lust for becoming is abandoned in a certain sphere, of that person, is the latent tendency to sensual lust abandoned in that sphere?

Na vattabbo “pahīno”ti vā “appahīno”ti vā.

It should not be said 'it is abandoned' or 'it is not abandoned.'

(Ka) yassa yattha kāmarāgānusayo pahīno tassa tattha avijjānusayo pahīnoti?

Of a person of whom the latent tendency to sensual lust is abandoned in a certain sphere, of that person, is the latent tendency to ignorance abandoned in that sphere?

Anāgāmissa kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu tassa tattha kāmarāgānusayo pahīno, no ca tassa tattha avijjānusayo pahīno[M 2.0243]. Arahato kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu tassa tattha kāmarāgānusayo [T 1.0692] ca pahīno avijjānusayo ca pahīno.

Of a non-returner, in the sense-sphere and with respect to two feelings, for that person, in that sphere, the latent tendency to sensual lust is abandoned, but the latent tendency to ignorance is not abandoned. Of an Arahant, in the sense-sphere and with respect to two feelings, for that person, in that sphere, both the latent tendency to sensual lust and the latent tendency to ignorance are abandoned.

(Kha) yassa vā pana yattha avijjānusayo pahīno tassa tattha kāmarāgānusayo pahīnoti?

Or again, of a person of whom the latent tendency to ignorance is abandoned in a certain sphere, of that person, is the latent tendency to sensual lust abandoned in that sphere?

Arahato dukkhāya vedanāya rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā tassa tattha avijjānusayo pahīno; kāmarāgānusayo na vattabbo “pahīno”ti vā “appahīno”ti vā. Tasseva puggalassa kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu tassa tattha avijjānusayo ca pahīno kāmarāgānusayo ca pahīno.

Of an Arahant, with respect to painful feeling, in the fine-material sphere, and in the immaterial sphere, for that person, in that sphere, the latent tendency to ignorance is abandoned; the latent tendency to sensual lust should not be said to be 'abandoned' or 'not abandoned.' For that same person, in the sense-sphere and with respect to two feelings, for that person, in that sphere, both the latent tendency to ignorance and the latent tendency to sensual lust are abandoned.

287. (Ka) yassa yattha paṭighānusayo pahīno tassa tattha mānānusayo pahīnoti?

287. Of a person of whom the latent tendency to aversion is abandoned in a certain sphere, of that person, is the latent tendency to conceit abandoned in that sphere?

Na vattabbo “pahīno”ti vā “appahīno”ti vā.

It should not be said 'it is abandoned' or 'it is not abandoned.'

(Kha) yassa vā pana yattha mānānusayo pahīno tassa tattha paṭighānusayo pahīnoti?

Or again, of a person of whom the latent tendency to conceit is abandoned in a certain sphere, of that person, is the latent tendency to aversion abandoned in that sphere?

Na vattabbo “pahīno”ti vā “appahīno”ti vā.

It should not be said 'it is abandoned' or 'it is not abandoned.'

Yassa [V 2.0317] yattha paṭighānusayo pahīno tassa tattha diṭṭhānusayo…pe… vicikicchānusayo pahīnoti? Āmantā.
