Yassa vā pana yattha vicikicchānusayo pahīno tassa tattha paṭighānusayo pahīnoti?

Or again, of a person of whom the latent tendency to doubt is abandoned in a certain sphere, of that person, is the latent tendency to aversion abandoned in that sphere?

Dvinnaṃ puggalānaṃ kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā tesaṃ tattha vicikicchānusayo pahīno; paṭighānusayo na vattabbo “pahīno”ti vā “appahīno”ti vā. Tesaññeva puggalānaṃ dukkhāya vedanāya tesaṃ tattha vicikicchānusayo pahīno, no ca tesaṃ tattha paṭighānusayo pahīno. Dvinnaṃ puggalānaṃ kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā tesaṃ tattha vicikicchānusayo pahīno; paṭighānusayo na vattabbo “pahīno”ti vā “appahīno”ti vā. Tesaññeva puggalānaṃ dukkhāya vedanāya tesaṃ tattha vicikicchānusayo [T 1.0693] ca pahīno paṭighānusayo ca pahīno.

Of the two individuals (the Stream-enterer and the Once-returner), in the sense-sphere, with respect to two feelings, in the fine-material sphere, and in the immaterial sphere, for them, in that sphere, the latent tendency to doubt is abandoned; the latent tendency to aversion should not be said to be 'abandoned' or 'not abandoned'. Of those same individuals, with respect to painful feeling, for them, in that sphere, the latent tendency to doubt is abandoned, but the latent tendency to aversion is not abandoned. Of the two individuals (the Non-returner and the Arahant), in the sense-sphere, with respect to two feelings, in the fine-material sphere, and in the immaterial sphere, for them, in that sphere, the latent tendency to doubt is abandoned; the latent tendency to aversion should not be said to be 'abandoned' or 'not abandoned'. Of those same individuals, with respect to painful feeling, for them, in that sphere, both the latent tendency to doubt and the latent tendency to aversion are abandoned.

(Ka) yassa yattha paṭighānusayo pahīno tassa tattha bhavarāgānusayo pahīnoti?

(Ka) Of a person of whom the latent tendency to aversion is abandoned in a certain sphere, of that person, is the latent tendency to lust for becoming abandoned in that sphere?

Na vattabbo “pahīno”ti vā “appahīno”ti vā.

It should not be said 'it is abandoned' or 'it is not abandoned.'

(Kha) yassa vā pana yattha bhavarāgānusayo pahīno tassa tattha paṭighānusayo pahīnoti?

(Kha) Or again, of a person of whom the latent tendency to lust for becoming is abandoned in a certain sphere, of that person, is the latent tendency to aversion abandoned in that sphere?

Na vattabbo “pahīno”ti vā “appahīno”ti vā.

It should not be said 'it is abandoned' or 'it is not abandoned.'

(Ka) yassa [M 2.0244] yattha paṭighānusayo pahīno tassa tattha avijjānusayo pahīnoti?

(Ka) Of a person of whom the latent tendency to aversion is abandoned in a certain sphere, of that person, is the latent tendency to ignorance abandoned in that sphere?

Anāgāmissa dukkhāya vedanāya tassa tattha paṭighānusayo pahīno, no ca tassa tattha avijjānusayo pahīno. Arahato dukkhāya vedanāya tassa tattha paṭighānusayo ca pahīno avijjānusayo ca pahīno.

Of a Non-returner, with respect to painful feeling, for that person, in that sphere, the latent tendency to aversion is abandoned, but the latent tendency to ignorance is not abandoned. Of an Arahant, with respect to painful feeling, for that person, in that sphere, both the latent tendency to aversion and the latent tendency to ignorance are abandoned.

(Kha) yassa vā pana yattha avijjānusayo pahīno tassa tattha paṭighānusayo pahīnoti?

(Kha) Or again, of a person of whom the latent tendency to ignorance is abandoned in a certain sphere, of that person, is the latent tendency to aversion abandoned in that sphere?

Arahato kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā tassa tattha avijjānusayo pahīno; paṭighānusayo na vattabbo “pahīno”ti vā “appahīno”ti [V 2.0318] vā. Tasseva puggalassa dukkhāya vedanāya tassa tattha avijjānusayo ca pahīno paṭighānusayo ca pahīno.

Of an Arahant, in the sense-sphere, with respect to two feelings, in the fine-material sphere, and in the immaterial sphere, for that person, in that sphere, the latent tendency to ignorance is abandoned; the latent tendency to aversion should not be said to be 'abandoned' or 'not abandoned'. For that same person, with respect to painful feeling, for that person, in that sphere, both the latent tendency to ignorance and the latent tendency to aversion are abandoned.

288. Yassa yattha mānānusayo pahīno tassa tattha diṭṭhānusayo…pe… vicikicchānusayo pahīnoti? Āmantā.

288. Of a person of whom the latent tendency to conceit is abandoned in a certain sphere, of that person, in that sphere, are the latent tendency to wrong views... and the latent tendency to doubt abandoned? Yes.

Yassa vā pana yattha vicikicchānusayo pahīno tassa tattha mānānusayo pahīnoti?

Or again, of a person of whom the latent tendency to doubt is abandoned in a certain sphere, of that person, is the latent tendency to conceit abandoned in that sphere?

Tiṇṇaṃ puggalānaṃ dukkhāya vedanāya tesaṃ tattha vicikicchānusayo pahīno; mānānusayo na vattabbo “pahīno”ti vā “appahīno”ti vā. Tesaññeva puggalānaṃ kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā tesaṃ [T 1.0694] tattha vicikicchānusayo pahīno, no ca tesaṃ tattha mānānusayo pahīno. Arahato dukkhāya vedanāya tassa tattha vicikicchānusayo pahīno; mānānusayo na vattabbo “pahīno”ti vā “appahīno”ti vā. Tasseva puggalassa kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā tassa tattha vicikicchānusayo ca pahīno mānānusayo ca pahīno.

Of the three individuals (the Stream-enterer, the Once-returner, and the Non-returner), with respect to painful feeling, for them, in that sphere, the latent tendency to doubt is abandoned; the latent tendency to conceit should not be said to be 'abandoned' or 'not abandoned'. Of those same individuals, in the sense-sphere, with respect to two feelings, in the fine-material sphere, and in the immaterial sphere, for them, in that sphere, the latent tendency to doubt is abandoned, but the latent tendency to conceit is not abandoned. Of an Arahant, with respect to painful feeling, for that person, in that sphere, the latent tendency to doubt is abandoned; the latent tendency to conceit should not be said to be 'abandoned' or 'not abandoned'. For that same individual, in the sense-sphere, with respect to two feelings, in the fine-material sphere, and in the immaterial sphere, for that person, in that sphere, both the latent tendency to doubt and the latent tendency to conceit are abandoned.

(Ka) yassa yattha mānānusayo pahīno tassa tattha bhavarāgānusayo pahīnoti?

(Ka) Of a person of whom the latent tendency to conceit is abandoned in a certain sphere, of that person, is the latent tendency to lust for becoming abandoned in that sphere?

Arahato kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu tassa tattha mānānusayo pahīno; bhavarāgānusayo na vattabbo “pahīno”ti vā “appahīno”ti vā. Tasseva puggalassa rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā tassa tattha mānānusayo ca pahīno bhavarāgānusayo ca pahīno.

Of an Arahant, in the sense-sphere and with respect to two feelings, for that person, in that sphere, the latent tendency to conceit is abandoned; the latent tendency to lust for becoming should not be said to be 'abandoned' or 'not abandoned'. For that same individual, in the fine-material sphere and in the immaterial sphere, for that person, in that sphere, both the latent tendency to conceit and the latent tendency to lust for becoming are abandoned.

(Kha) yassa vā pana yattha bhavarāgānusayo pahīno tassa tattha mānānusayo pahīnoti? Āmantā.

(Kha) Or again, of a person of whom the latent tendency to lust for becoming is abandoned in a certain sphere, of that person, is the latent tendency to conceit abandoned in that sphere? Yes.

(Ka) yassa [M 2.0245] yattha mānānusayo pahīno tassa tattha avijjānusayo pahīnoti? Āmantā.

(Ka) Of a person of whom the latent tendency to conceit is abandoned in a certain sphere, of that person, is the latent tendency to ignorance abandoned in that sphere? Yes.

(Kha) yassa vā pana yattha avijjānusayo pahīno tassa tattha mānānusayo pahīnoti?

(Kha) Or again, of a person of whom the latent tendency to ignorance is abandoned in a certain sphere, of that person, is the latent tendency to conceit abandoned in that sphere?

Arahato dukkhāya vedanāya tassa tattha avijjānusayo pahīno; mānānusayo [V 2.0319] na vattabbo “pahīno”ti vā “appahīno”ti vā. Tasseva puggalassa kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā tassa tattha avijjānusayo ca pahīno mānānusayo ca pahīno.

For an Arahant, in painful feeling, for them the latent tendency to ignorance is abandoned therein; the latent tendency to conceit should not be said to be 'abandoned' or 'not abandoned'. For that same individual, in the sense-sphere, in two feelings, in the form-sphere, and in the formless-sphere, for them both the latent tendency to ignorance and the latent tendency to conceit are abandoned therein.

289. (Ka) yassa yattha diṭṭhānusayo pahīno tassa tattha vicikicchānusayo pahīnoti? Āmantā.

289. For a person for whom the latent tendency to views is abandoned in a certain sphere, for that person, is the latent tendency to doubt abandoned in that sphere? Yes.

(Kha) yassa vā pana yattha vicikicchānusayo pahīno tassa tattha diṭṭhānusayo pahīnoti? Āmantā …pe….

Or again, for a person for whom the latent tendency to doubt is abandoned in a certain sphere, for that person, is the latent tendency to views abandoned in that sphere? Yes...

290. (Ka) yassa [T 1.0695] yattha vicikicchānusayo pahīno tassa tattha bhavarāgānusayo pahīnoti?

290. For a person for whom the latent tendency to doubt is abandoned in a certain sphere, for that person, is the latent tendency to lust for becoming abandoned in that sphere?

Tiṇṇaṃ puggalānaṃ kāmadhātuyā tīsu vedanāsu tesaṃ tattha vicikicchānusayo pahīno; bhavarāgānusayo na vattabbo “pahīno”ti vā “appahīno”ti vā. Tesaññeva puggalānaṃ rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā tesaṃ tattha vicikicchānusayo pahīno, no ca tesaṃ tattha bhavarāgānusayo pahīno. Arahato kāmadhātuyā tīsu vedanāsu tassa tattha vicikicchānusayo pahīno; bhavarāgānusayo na vattabbo “pahīno”ti vā “appahīno”ti vā. Tasseva puggalassa rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā tassa tattha vicikicchānusayo ca pahīno bhavarāgānusayo ca pahīno.

For three individuals, in the sense-sphere, in three feelings, for them the latent tendency to doubt is abandoned therein; the latent tendency to lust for becoming should not be said to be 'abandoned' or 'not abandoned'. For those same individuals, in the form-sphere and in the formless-sphere, for them the latent tendency to doubt is abandoned therein, but for them the latent tendency to lust for becoming is not abandoned therein. For an Arahant, in the sense-sphere, in three feelings, for them the latent tendency to doubt is abandoned therein; the latent tendency to lust for becoming should not be said to be 'abandoned' or 'not abandoned'. For that same individual, in the form-sphere and in the formless-sphere, for them both the latent tendency to doubt and the latent tendency to lust for becoming are abandoned therein.

(Kha) yassa vā pana yattha bhavarāgānusayo pahīno tassa tattha vicikicchānusayo pahīnoti? Āmantā.

Or again, for a person for whom the latent tendency to lust for becoming is abandoned in a certain sphere, for that person, is the latent tendency to doubt abandoned in that sphere? Yes.

(Ka) yassa yattha vicikicchānusayo pahīno tassa tattha avijjānusayo pahīnoti?

For a person for whom the latent tendency to doubt is abandoned in a certain sphere, for that person, is the latent tendency to ignorance abandoned in that sphere?

Tiṇṇaṃ puggalānaṃ kāmadhātuyā tīsu vedanāsu rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā tesaṃ tattha vicikicchānusayo pahīno, no ca tesaṃ tattha avijjānusayo pahīno. Arahato kāmadhātuyā tīsu vedanāsu rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā tassa tattha vicikicchānusayo ca pahīno avijjānusayo ca pahīno.

For the three individuals, in the sense-sphere, in the three feelings, in the form-sphere, and in the formless-sphere, for them the latent tendency to doubt is abandoned therein, but for them the latent tendency to ignorance is not abandoned therein. For the Arahant, in the sense-sphere, in the three feelings, in the form-sphere, and in the formless-sphere, for them both the latent tendency to doubt and the latent tendency to ignorance are abandoned therein.

(Kha) yassa vā pana yattha avijjānusayo pahīno tassa tattha vicikicchānusayo pahīnoti? Āmantā.

Or for whomever, wherever the latent tendency to ignorance is abandoned, for them, is the latent tendency to doubt abandoned therein? Yes.

291. (Ka) yassa [M 2.0246][V 2.0320] yattha bhavarāgānusayo pahīno tassa tattha avijjānusayo pahīnoti? Āmantā.

291. For whomever, wherever the latent tendency to lust for becoming is abandoned, for them, is the latent tendency to ignorance abandoned therein? Yes.

(Kha) yassa vā pana yattha avijjānusayo pahīno tassa tattha bhavarāgānusayo pahīnoti?

Or for whomever, wherever the latent tendency to ignorance is abandoned, for them, is the latent tendency to lust for becoming abandoned therein?

Arahato kāmadhātuyā tīsu [T 1.0696] vedanāsu tassa tattha avijjānusayo pahīno; bhavarāgānusayo na vattabbo “pahīno”ti vā “appahīno”ti vā. Tasseva puggalassa rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā tassa tattha avijjānusayo ca pahīno bhavarāgānusayo ca pahīno. (Ekamūlakaṃ)

For the Arahant, in the sense-sphere and in the three feelings, for them the latent tendency to ignorance is abandoned therein; the latent tendency to lust for becoming should not be spoken of as 'abandoned' or 'not abandoned'. For that same individual, in the form-sphere and in the formless-sphere, for them both the latent tendency to ignorance and the latent tendency to lust for becoming are abandoned therein. (Ekamūlakaṃ)

292. (Ka) yassa yattha kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca pahīnā tassa tattha mānānusayo pahīnoti? Natthi.

292. For whomever, wherever both the latent tendency to sensual lust and the latent tendency to aversion are abandoned, for them, is the latent tendency to conceit abandoned therein? No.

(Kha) yassa vā pana yattha mānānusayo pahīno tassa tattha kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca pahīnāti?

Or for whomever, wherever the latent tendency to conceit is abandoned, for them, are both the latent tendency to sensual lust and the latent tendency to aversion abandoned therein?

Arahato rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā tassa tattha mānānusayo pahīno; kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca na vattabbā “pahīnā”ti vā “appahīnā”ti vā. Tasseva puggalassa kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu tassa tattha mānānusayo ca kāmarāgānusayo ca pahīnā; paṭighānusayo na vattabbo “pahīno”ti vā “appahīno”ti vā.

For the Arahant, in the form-sphere and in the formless-sphere, for them the latent tendency to conceit is abandoned therein; both the latent tendency to sensual lust and the latent tendency to aversion should not be spoken of as 'abandoned' or 'not abandoned'. For that same individual, in the sense-sphere and in the two feelings, for them both the latent tendency to conceit and the latent tendency to sensual lust are abandoned therein; the latent tendency to aversion should not be spoken of as 'abandoned' or 'not abandoned'.

Yassa yattha kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca pahīnā tassa tattha diṭṭhānusayo…pe… vicikicchānusayo pahīnoti? Natthi.

For whomever, wherever both the latent tendency to sensual lust and the latent tendency to aversion are abandoned, for them, is the latent tendency to views… the latent tendency to doubt abandoned therein? No.

Yassa vā pana yattha vicikicchānusayo pahīno tassa tattha kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca pahīnāti?

Or for whomever, wherever the latent tendency to doubt is abandoned, for them, are both the latent tendency to sensual lust and the latent tendency to aversion abandoned therein?

Dvinnaṃ puggalānaṃ rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā tesaṃ tattha vicikicchānusayo pahīno; kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca na vattabbā “pahīnā”ti vā “appahīnā”ti vā. Tesaññeva puggalānaṃ kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu tesaṃ tattha vicikicchānusayo pahīno, no ca tesaṃ tattha kāmarāgānusayo pahīno; paṭighānusayo na vattabbo “pahīno”ti [V 2.0321] vā “appahīno”ti [T 1.0697] vā. Tesaññeva puggalānaṃ dukkhāya vedanāya tesaṃ tattha vicikicchānusayo pahīno, no ca tesaṃ tattha paṭighānusayo pahīno; kāmarāgānusayo na vattabbo “pahīno”ti vā “appahīno”ti vā. Dvinnaṃ puggalānaṃ rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā tesaṃ tattha vicikicchānusayo pahīno; kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca na vattabbā “pahīnā”ti vā “appahīnā”ti vā. Tesaññeva puggalānaṃ kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu tesaṃ tattha vicikicchānusayo [M 2.0247] ca kāmarāgānusayo ca pahīnā; paṭighānusayo na vattabbo “pahīno”ti vā “appahīno”ti vā. Tesaññeva puggalānaṃ dukkhāya vedanāya tesaṃ tattha vicikicchānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca pahīnā; kāmarāgānusayo na vattabbo “pahīno”ti vā “appahīno”ti vā.

For the two individuals, in the form-sphere and in the formless-sphere, for them the latent tendency to doubt is abandoned therein; both the latent tendency to sensual lust and the latent tendency to aversion should not be spoken of as 'abandoned' or 'not abandoned'. For those same individuals, in the sense-sphere and in the two feelings, for them the latent tendency to doubt is abandoned therein, but for them the latent tendency to sensual lust is not abandoned therein; the latent tendency to aversion should not be spoken of as 'abandoned' or 'not abandoned'. For those same individuals, in painful feeling, for them the latent tendency to doubt is abandoned therein, but for them the latent tendency to aversion is not abandoned therein; the latent tendency to sensual lust should not be spoken of as 'abandoned' or 'not abandoned'. For the two individuals, in the form-sphere and in the formless-sphere, for them the latent tendency to doubt is abandoned therein; both the latent tendency to sensual lust and the latent tendency to aversion should not be spoken of as 'abandoned' or 'not abandoned'. For those same individuals, in the sense-sphere and in the two feelings, for them both the latent tendency to doubt and the latent tendency to sensual lust are abandoned therein; the latent tendency to aversion should not be spoken of as 'abandoned' or 'not abandoned'. For those same individuals, in painful feeling, for them both the latent tendency to doubt and the latent tendency to aversion are abandoned therein; the latent tendency to sensual lust should not be spoken of as 'abandoned' or 'not abandoned'.

(Ka) yassa yattha kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca pahīnā tassa tattha bhavarāgānusayo pahīnoti? Natthi.

For whomever, wherever both the latent tendency to sensual lust and the latent tendency to aversion are abandoned, for them, is the latent tendency to lust for becoming abandoned therein? No.

(Kha) yassa vā pana yattha bhavarāgānusayo pahīno tassa tattha kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca pahīnāti?

Or for whomever, wherever the latent tendency to lust for becoming is abandoned, for them, are both the latent tendency to sensual lust and the latent tendency to aversion abandoned therein?

Na vattabbā “pahīnā”ti vā “appahīnā”ti vā.

They should not be spoken of as 'abandoned' or 'not abandoned'.

(Ka) yassa yattha kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca pahīnā tassa tattha avijjānusayo pahīnoti? Natthi.

For whomever, wherever both the latent tendency of sensual lust and the latent tendency of aversion are abandoned, for that person, is the latent tendency of ignorance abandoned therein? No.

(Kha) yassa vā pana yattha avijjānusayo pahīno tassa tattha kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca pahīnāti?

Or alternatively, for whomever, wherever the latent tendency of ignorance is abandoned, for that person, are both the latent tendency of sensual lust and the latent tendency of aversion abandoned therein?

Arahato rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā tassa tattha avijjānusayo pahīno; kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca na vattabbā “pahīnā”ti vā “appahīnā”ti vā. Tasseva puggalassa kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu tassa tattha avijjānusayo ca kāmarāgānusayo [T 1.0698] ca pahīnā; paṭighānusayo na vattabbo “pahīno”ti vā “appahīno”ti vā. Tasseva puggalassa dukkhāya vedanāya tassa tattha avijjānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca pahīnā[V 2.0322]; kāmarāgānusayo na vattabbo “pahīno”ti vā “appahīno”ti vā. (Dukamūlakaṃ)

For the Arahant, in the form sphere and in the formless sphere, for that person, the latent tendency of ignorance is abandoned therein; both the latent tendency of sensual lust and the latent tendency of aversion should not be spoken of as 'abandoned' or 'not abandoned'. For that same person, in the sense-desire sphere and in two feelings, for that person, both the latent tendency of ignorance and the latent tendency of sensual lust are abandoned therein; the latent tendency of aversion should not be spoken of as 'abandoned' or 'not abandoned'. For that same person, in painful feeling, for that person, both the latent tendency of ignorance and the latent tendency of aversion are abandoned therein; the latent tendency of sensual lust should not be spoken of as 'abandoned' or 'not abandoned'. (The section rooted in the pair)

293. Yassa yattha kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca mānānusayo ca pahīnā tassa tattha diṭṭhānusayo…pe… vicikicchānusayo pahīnoti? Natthi.

293. For whomever, wherever the latent tendency of sensual lust, the latent tendency of aversion, and the latent tendency of conceit are abandoned, for that person, is the latent tendency of views… the latent tendency of doubt abandoned therein? No.

Yassa vā pana yattha vicikicchānusayo pahīno tassa tattha kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca mānānusayo ca pahīnāti?

Or alternatively, for whomever, wherever the latent tendency of doubt is abandoned, for that person, are the latent tendency of sensual lust, the latent tendency of aversion, and the latent tendency of conceit abandoned therein?

Dvinnaṃ puggalānaṃ rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā tesaṃ tattha vicikicchānusayo pahīno, no ca tesaṃ tattha mānānusayo pahīno; kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca na vattabbā “pahīnā”ti vā “appahīnā”ti vā. Tesaññeva puggalānaṃ kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu tesaṃ tattha vicikicchānusayo pahīno, no ca tesaṃ tattha kāmarāgānusayo ca mānānusayo ca pahīnā; paṭighānusayo na vattabbo [M 2.0248] “pahīno”ti vā “appahīno”ti vā. Tesaññeva puggalānaṃ dukkhāya vedanāya tesaṃ tattha vicikicchānusayo pahīno, no ca tesaṃ tattha paṭighānusayo pahīno; kāmarāgānusayo ca mānānusayo ca na vattabbā “pahīnā”ti vā “appahīnā”ti vā. Anāgāmissa rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā tassa tattha vicikicchānusayo pahīno, no ca tassa tattha mānānusayo pahīno; kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca na vattabbā “pahīnā”ti vā “appahīnā”ti [T 1.0699] vā. Tasseva puggalassa kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu tassa tattha vicikicchānusayo ca kāmarāgānusayo ca pahīnā, no ca tassa tattha mānānusayo pahīno; paṭighānusayo na vattabbo “pahīno”ti vā “appahīno”ti vā. Tasseva puggalassa dukkhāya vedanāya tassa tattha vicikicchānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca pahīnā; kāmarāgānusayo ca mānānusayo ca na vattabbā “pahīnā”ti vā “appahīnā”ti vā. Arahato rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā tassa tattha vicikicchānusayo ca mānānusayo ca pahīnā; kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca na vattabbā “pahīnā”ti vā “appahīnā”ti vā. Tasseva puggalassa kāmadhātuyā dvīsu [V 2.0323] vedanāsu tassa tattha vicikicchānusayo ca kāmarāgānusayo ca mānānusayo ca pahīnā; paṭighānusayo na vattabbo “pahīno”ti vā “appahīno”ti vā. Tasseva puggalassa dukkhāya vedanāya tassa tattha vicikicchānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca pahīnā; kāmarāgānusayo ca mānānusayo ca na vattabbā “pahīnā”ti vā “appahīnā”ti vā.

For the two persons, in the form sphere and in the formless sphere, for those persons the latent tendency of doubt is abandoned therein, but for them the latent tendency of conceit is not abandoned therein; it should not be said of the latent tendency of sensual lust and the latent tendency of aversion that they are 'abandoned' or 'not abandoned'. For those same persons, in the sense-desire sphere and in two feelings, for them the latent tendency of doubt is abandoned therein, but for them the latent tendency of sensual lust and the latent tendency of conceit are not abandoned therein; it should not be said of the latent tendency of aversion that it is 'abandoned' or 'not abandoned'. For those same persons, in painful feeling, for them the latent tendency of doubt is abandoned therein, but for them the latent tendency of aversion is not abandoned therein; it should not be said of the latent tendency of sensual lust and the latent tendency of conceit that they are 'abandoned' or 'not abandoned'. For the Non-returner, in the form sphere and in the formless sphere, for that person the latent tendency of doubt is abandoned therein, but for that person the latent tendency of conceit is not abandoned therein; it should not be said of the latent tendency of sensual lust and the latent tendency of aversion that they are 'abandoned' or 'not abandoned'. For that same person, in the sense-desire sphere and in two feelings, for that person the latent tendency of doubt and the latent tendency of sensual lust are abandoned therein, but for that person the latent tendency of conceit is not abandoned therein; it should not be said of the latent tendency of aversion that it is 'abandoned' or 'not abandoned'. For that same person, in painful feeling, for that person the latent tendency of doubt and the latent tendency of aversion are abandoned therein; it should not be said of the latent tendency of sensual lust and the latent tendency of conceit that they are 'abandoned' or 'not abandoned'. For the Arahant, in the form sphere and in the formless sphere, for that person the latent tendency of doubt and the latent tendency of conceit are abandoned therein; it should not be said of the latent tendency of sensual lust and the latent tendency of aversion that they are 'abandoned' or 'not abandoned'. For that same person, in the sense-desire sphere and in two feelings, for that person the latent tendency of doubt, the latent tendency of sensual lust, and the latent tendency of conceit are abandoned therein; it should not be said of the latent tendency of aversion that it is 'abandoned' or 'not abandoned'. For that same person, in painful feeling, for that person the latent tendency of doubt and the latent tendency of aversion are abandoned therein; it should not be said of the latent tendency of sensual lust and the latent tendency of conceit that they are 'abandoned' or 'not abandoned'.

(Ka) yassa yattha kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca mānānusayo ca pahīnā tassa tattha bhavarāgānusayo pahīnoti? Natthi.

For whomever, wherever the latent tendency of sensual lust, the latent tendency of aversion, and the latent tendency of conceit are abandoned, for that person, is the latent tendency of lust for existence abandoned therein? No.

(Kha) yassa vā pana yattha bhavarāgānusayo pahīno tassa tattha kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca mānānusayo ca pahīnāti?

Or alternatively, for whomever, wherever the latent tendency of lust for existence is abandoned, for that person, are the latent tendency of sensual lust, the latent tendency of aversion, and the latent tendency of conceit abandoned therein?

Mānānusayo pahīno; kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca na vattabbā “pahīnā”ti vā “appahīnā”ti vā.

The latent tendency of conceit is abandoned; it should not be said of the latent tendency of sensual lust and the latent tendency of aversion that they are 'abandoned' or 'not abandoned'.

(Ka) yassa yattha kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca mānānusayo ca pahīnā tassa tattha avijjānusayo pahīnoti[T 1.0700]? Natthi.

For whomever, wherever the latent tendency of sensual lust, the latent tendency of aversion, and the latent tendency of conceit are abandoned, for that person, is the latent tendency of ignorance abandoned therein? No.

(Kha) yassa vā pana yattha avijjānusayo pahīno tassa tattha kāmarāgānusayo [M 2.0249] ca paṭighānusayo ca mānānusayo ca pahīnāti?

Or alternatively, for whomever, wherever the latent tendency of ignorance is abandoned, for that person, are the latent tendency of sensual lust, the latent tendency of aversion, and the latent tendency of conceit abandoned therein?

Arahato rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā tassa tattha avijjānusayo ca mānānusayo ca pahīnā; kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca na vattabbā “pahīnā”ti vā “appahīnā”ti vā. Tasseva puggalassa kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu tassa tattha avijjānusayo ca kāmarāgānusayo ca mānānusayo ca pahīnā; paṭighānusayo na vattabbo “pahīno”ti vā “appahīno”ti vā. Tasseva puggalassa dukkhāya vedanāya tassa tattha avijjānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca pahīnā; kāmarāgānusayo ca mānānusayo ca na vattabbā “pahīnā”ti vā “appahīnā”ti vā. (Tikamūlakaṃ)

For the Arahant, in the form sphere and in the formless sphere, for that person the latent tendency of ignorance and the latent tendency of conceit are abandoned therein; it should not be said of the latent tendency of sensual lust and the latent tendency of aversion that they are 'abandoned' or 'not abandoned'. For that same person, in the sense-desire sphere and in two feelings, for that person the latent tendency of ignorance, the latent tendency of sensual lust, and the latent tendency of conceit are abandoned therein; it should not be said of the latent tendency of aversion that it is 'abandoned' or 'not abandoned'. For that same person, in painful feeling, for that person the latent tendency of ignorance and the latent tendency of aversion are abandoned therein; it should not be said of the latent tendency of sensual lust and the latent tendency of conceit that they are 'abandoned' or 'not abandoned'. (The section rooted in the triplet)

294. (Ka) yassa yattha kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca mānānusayo ca diṭṭhānusayo ca pahīnā tassa tattha vicikicchānusayo pahīnoti? Natthi.

294. For whomever, wherever the latent tendency of sensual lust, the latent tendency of aversion, the latent tendency of conceit, and the latent tendency of views are abandoned, for that person, is the latent tendency of doubt abandoned therein? No.

(Kha) yassa [V 2.0324] vā pana yattha vicikicchānusayo pahīno tassa tattha kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca mānānusayo ca diṭṭhānusayo ca pahīnāti?

Or conversely, for whom, wherever the latent tendency of doubt is abandoned, are the latent tendency of sensual lust, the latent tendency of aversion, the latent tendency of conceit, and the latent tendency of wrong views abandoned for him therein?

Dvinnaṃ puggalānaṃ rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā tesaṃ tattha vicikicchānusayo ca diṭṭhānusayo ca pahīnā, no ca tesaṃ tattha mānānusayo pahīno; kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca na vattabbā “pahīnā”ti vā “appahīnā”ti vā. Tesaññeva puggalānaṃ kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu tesaṃ tattha vicikicchānusayo ca diṭṭhānusayo ca pahīnā, no ca tesaṃ tattha kāmarāgānusayo ca mānānusayo ca pahīnā; paṭighānusayo na [T 1.0701] vattabbo “pahīno”ti vā “appahīno”ti vā. Tesaññeva puggalānaṃ dukkhāya vedanāya tesaṃ tattha vicikicchānusayo ca diṭṭhānusayo ca pahīnā, no ca tesaṃ tattha paṭighānusayo pahīno; kāmarāgānusayo ca mānānusayo ca na vattabbā “pahīnā”ti vā “appahīnā”ti vā. Anāgāmissa rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā tassa tattha vicikicchānusayo ca diṭṭhānusayo ca pahīnā, no ca tassa tattha mānānusayo pahīno; kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca na vattabbā “pahīnā”ti vā “appahīnā”ti vā. Tasseva puggalassa kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu tassa tattha vicikicchānusayo ca kāmarāgānusayo ca diṭṭhānusayo ca pahīnā, no ca tassa tattha mānānusayo pahīno; paṭighānusayo na vattabbo “pahīno”ti [M 2.0250] vā “appahīno”ti vā. Tasseva puggalassa dukkhāya vedanāya tassa tattha vicikicchānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca diṭṭhānusayo ca pahīnā; kāmarāgānusayo ca mānānusayo ca na vattabbā “pahīnā”ti vā “appahīnā”ti vā. Arahato rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā tassa tattha vicikicchānusayo ca mānānusayo ca diṭṭhānusayo ca pahīnā; kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca na vattabbā “pahīnā”ti vā “appahīnā”ti vā. Tasseva puggalassa kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu tassa tattha vicikicchānusayo ca kāmarāgānusayo ca mānānusayo ca diṭṭhānusayo ca pahīnā[V 2.0325]; paṭighānusayo na vattabbo “pahīno”ti vā “appahīno”ti vā. Tasseva puggalassa dukkhāya vedanāya tassa tattha vicikicchānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca diṭṭhānusayo [T 1.0702] ca pahīnā; kāmarāgānusayo ca mānānusayo ca na vattabbā “pahīnā”ti vā “appahīnā”ti vā …pe…. (Catukkamūlakaṃ)

For two individuals, in the form realm and the formless realm, for them the latent tendency of doubt and the latent tendency of wrong views are abandoned there, but for them the latent tendency of conceit is not abandoned there; it should not be said that the latent tendency of sensual lust and the latent tendency of aversion are 'abandoned' or 'not abandoned'. For those same individuals, in the sensual realm, in two feelings, for them the latent tendency of doubt and the latent tendency of wrong views are abandoned there, but for them the latent tendency of sensual lust and the latent tendency of conceit are not abandoned there; it should not be said that the latent tendency of aversion is 'abandoned' or 'not abandoned'. For those same individuals, in painful feeling, for them the latent tendency of doubt and the latent tendency of wrong views are abandoned there, but for them the latent tendency of aversion is not abandoned there; it should not be said that the latent tendency of sensual lust and the latent tendency of conceit are 'abandoned' or 'not abandoned'. For a non-returner, in the form realm and the formless realm, for him the latent tendency of doubt and the latent tendency of wrong views are abandoned there, but for him the latent tendency of conceit is not abandoned there; it should not be said that the latent tendency of sensual lust and the latent tendency of aversion are 'abandoned' or 'not abandoned'. For that same individual, in the sensual realm, in two feelings, for him the latent tendency of doubt, the latent tendency of sensual lust, and the latent tendency of wrong views are abandoned there, but for him the latent tendency of conceit is not abandoned there; it should not be said that the latent tendency of aversion is 'abandoned' or 'not abandoned'. For that same individual, in painful feeling, for him the latent tendency of doubt, the latent tendency of aversion, and the latent tendency of wrong views are abandoned there; it should not be said that the latent tendency of sensual lust and the latent tendency of conceit are 'abandoned' or 'not abandoned'. For an Arahant, in the form realm and the formless realm, for him the latent tendency of doubt, the latent tendency of conceit, and the latent tendency of wrong views are abandoned there; it should not be said that the latent tendency of sensual lust and the latent tendency of aversion are 'abandoned' or 'not abandoned'. For that same individual, in the sensual realm, in two feelings, for him the latent tendency of doubt, the latent tendency of sensual lust, the latent tendency of conceit, and the latent tendency of wrong views are abandoned there; it should not be said that the latent tendency of aversion is 'abandoned' or 'not abandoned'. For that same individual, in painful feeling, for him the latent tendency of doubt, the latent tendency of aversion, and the latent tendency of wrong views are abandoned there; it should not be said that the latent tendency of sensual lust and the latent tendency of conceit are 'abandoned' or 'not abandoned'. (Rooted in the Quadruplet)

295. (Ka) yassa yattha kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca mānānusayo ca diṭṭhānusayo ca vicikicchānusayo ca pahīnā tassa tattha bhavarāgānusayo pahīnoti? Natthi.

295. (A) For whichever person in whichever sphere the latent tendencies of sensual lust, aversion, conceit, wrong view, and doubt are abandoned, for that person is the latent tendency of craving for existence abandoned there? No.

(Kha) yassa vā pana yattha bhavarāgānusayo pahīno tassa tattha kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca mānānusayo ca diṭṭhānusayo ca vicikicchānusayo ca pahīnāti?

(B) Or, for whichever person in whichever sphere the latent tendency of craving for existence is abandoned, for that person are the latent tendencies of sensual lust, aversion, conceit, wrong view, and doubt abandoned there?

Arahato rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā tassa tattha bhavarāgānusayo ca mānānusayo ca diṭṭhānusayo ca vicikicchānusayo ca pahīnā; kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca na vattabbā “pahīnā”ti vā “appahīnā”ti vā.

For an Arahant, in the form realm and the formless realm, for him the latent tendency of craving for existence, the latent tendency of conceit, the latent tendency of wrong view, and the latent tendency of doubt are abandoned there; it should not be said that the latent tendencies of sensual lust and aversion are 'abandoned' or 'not abandoned'.

(Ka) yassa yattha kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca mānānusayo ca diṭṭhānusayo ca vicikicchānusayo ca pahīnā tassa tattha avijjānusayo pahīnoti? Natthi.

(A) For whichever person in whichever sphere the latent tendencies of sensual lust, aversion, conceit, wrong view, and doubt are abandoned, for that person is the latent tendency of ignorance abandoned there? No.

(Kha) yassa vā pana yattha avijjānusayo pahīno tassa tattha kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca mānānusayo ca diṭṭhānusayo ca vicikicchānusayo ca pahīnāti?

(B) Or, for whichever person in whichever sphere the latent tendency of ignorance is abandoned, for that person are the latent tendencies of sensual lust, aversion, conceit, wrong view, and doubt abandoned there?

Arahato rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā tassa tattha avijjānusayo ca mānānusayo ca diṭṭhānusayo ca vicikicchānusayo ca pahīnā; kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca na vattabbā “pahīnā”ti vā “appahīnā”ti vā. Tasseva puggalassa kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu tassa tattha avijjānusayo ca kāmarāgānusayo ca mānānusayo ca diṭṭhānusayo [M 2.0251] ca vicikicchānusayo ca pahīnā; paṭighānusayo na vattabbo [V 2.0326] “pahīno”ti vā “appahīno”ti vā. Tasseva puggalassa [T 1.0703] dukkhāya vedanāya tassa tattha avijjānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca diṭṭhānusayo ca vicikicchānusayo ca pahīnā; kāmarāgānusayo ca mānānusayo ca na vattabbā “pahīnā”ti vā “appahīnā”ti vā. (Pañcakamūlakaṃ)

For an Arahant, in the form realm and the formless realm, for him the latent tendencies of ignorance, conceit, wrong view, and doubt are abandoned there; it should not be said that the latent tendencies of sensual lust and aversion are 'abandoned' or 'not abandoned'. For that same individual, in the sensual realm, in two feelings, for him the latent tendencies of ignorance, sensual lust, conceit, wrong view, and doubt are abandoned there; it should not be said that the latent tendency of aversion is 'abandoned' or 'not abandoned'. For that same individual, in painful feeling, for him the latent tendencies of ignorance, aversion, wrong view, and doubt are abandoned there; it should not be said that the latent tendencies of sensual lust and conceit are 'abandoned' or 'not abandoned'. (Rooted in the Quintuplet)

296. (Ka) yassa yattha kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca mānānusayo ca diṭṭhānusayo ca vicikicchānusayo ca bhavarāgānusayo ca pahīnā tassa tattha avijjānusayo pahīnoti? Natthi.

296. (A) For whichever person in whichever sphere the latent tendencies of sensual lust, aversion, conceit, wrong view, doubt, and craving for existence are abandoned, for that person is the latent tendency of ignorance abandoned there? No.

(Kha) yassa vā pana yattha avijjānusayo pahīno tassa tattha kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca mānānusayo ca diṭṭhānusayo ca vicikicchānusayo ca bhavarāgānusayo ca pahīnāti?

(B) Or, for whichever person in whichever sphere the latent tendency of ignorance is abandoned, for that person are the latent tendencies of sensual lust, aversion, conceit, wrong view, doubt, and craving for existence abandoned there?

Arahato rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā tassa tattha avijjānusayo ca mānānusayo ca diṭṭhānusayo ca vicikicchānusayo ca bhavarāgānusayo ca pahīnā; kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca na vattabbā “pahīnā”ti vā “appahīnā”ti vā. Tasseva puggalassa kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu tassa tattha avijjānusayo ca kāmarāgānusayo ca mānānusayo ca diṭṭhānusayo ca vicikicchānusayo ca pahīnā; paṭighānusayo ca bhavarāgānusayo ca na vattabbā “pahīnā”ti vā “appahīnā”ti vā. Tasseva puggalassa dukkhāya vedanāya tassa tattha avijjānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca diṭṭhānusayo ca vicikicchānusayo ca pahīnā; kāmarāgānusayo ca mānānusayo ca bhavarāgānusayo ca na vattabbā “pahīnā”ti vā “appahīnā”ti vā. (Chakkamūlakaṃ)

For an Arahant, in the form element and the formless element, for that person the latent tendencies of ignorance, conceit, views, doubt, and craving for existence are abandoned therein. The latent tendencies of sensual desire and aversion should not be said to be 'abandoned' or 'not abandoned'. For that same individual, in the sense-sphere element, in two feelings, for that person the latent tendencies of ignorance, sensual desire, conceit, views, and doubt are abandoned therein. The latent tendencies of aversion and craving for existence should not be said to be 'abandoned' or 'not abandoned'. For that same individual, in painful feeling, for that person the latent tendencies of ignorance, aversion, views, and doubt are abandoned therein. The latent tendencies of sensual desire, conceit, and craving for existence should not be said to be 'abandoned' or 'not abandoned'. (Sixfold Root)

Pahīnavāre anulomaṃ.

Section on Abandonment: Direct Method.

5. Pahīnavāra

5. The Section on Abandonment

(Gha) paṭilomapuggalo

(Gha) Reverse Method: The Individual

297. (Ka) yassa [T 1.0704] kāmarāgānusayo appahīno tassa paṭighānusayo appahīnoti? Āmantā.

297. (Ka) For an individual for whom the latent tendency of sensual desire is not abandoned, for that individual is the latent tendency of aversion not abandoned? Yes.

(Kha) yassa [V 2.0327] vā pana paṭighānusayo appahīno tassa kāmarāgānusayo appahīnoti? Āmantā.

(Kha) Or again, for an individual for whom the latent tendency of aversion is not abandoned, for that individual is the latent tendency of sensual desire not abandoned? Yes.

(Ka) yassa [M 2.0252] kāmarāgānusayo appahīno tassa mānānusayo appahīnoti? Āmantā.

(Ka) For an individual for whom the latent tendency of sensual desire is not abandoned, for that individual is the latent tendency of conceit not abandoned? Yes.

(Kha) yassa vā pana mānānusayo appahīno tassa kāmarāgānusayo appahīnoti?

(Kha) Or again, for an individual for whom the latent tendency of conceit is not abandoned, for that individual is the latent tendency of sensual desire not abandoned?

Anāgāmissa mānānusayo appahīno, no ca tassa kāmarāgānusayo appahīno. Tiṇṇaṃ puggalānaṃ mānānusayo ca appahīno kāmarāgānusayo ca appahīno.

For a non-returner, the latent tendency of conceit is not abandoned, but for that person the latent tendency of sensual desire is abandoned. For three individuals, both the latent tendency of conceit and the latent tendency of sensual desire are not abandoned.

Yassa kāmarāgānusayo appahīno tassa diṭṭhānusayo…pe… vicikicchānusayo appahīnoti?

For an individual for whom the latent tendency of sensual desire is not abandoned, for that individual are the latent tendency of views and the latent tendency of doubt not abandoned?

Dvinnaṃ puggalānaṃ kāmarāgānusayo appahīno, no ca tesaṃ vicikicchānusayo appahīno. Puthujjanassa kāmarāgānusayo ca appahīno vicikicchānusayo ca appahīno.

For two individuals, the latent tendency of sensual desire is not abandoned, but for them the latent tendency of doubt is abandoned. For a worldling, both the latent tendency of sensual desire and the latent tendency of doubt are not abandoned.

Yassa vā pana vicikicchānusayo appahīno tassa kāmarāgānusayo appahīnoti? Āmantā.

Or again, for an individual for whom the latent tendency of doubt is not abandoned, for that individual is the latent tendency of sensual desire not abandoned? Yes.

Yassa kāmarāgānusayo appahīno tassa bhavarāgānusayo…pe… avijjānusayo appahīnoti? Āmantā.

For an individual for whom the latent tendency of sensual desire is not abandoned, for that individual are the latent tendency of craving for existence and the latent tendency of ignorance not abandoned? Yes.

Yassa vā pana avijjānusayo appahīno tassa kāmarāgānusayo appahīnoti?

Or again, for an individual for whom the latent tendency of ignorance is not abandoned, for that individual is the latent tendency of sensual desire not abandoned?

Anāgāmissa avijjānusayo appahīno, no ca tassa kāmarāgānusayo appahīno. Tiṇṇaṃ puggalānaṃ avijjānusayo ca appahīno kāmarāgānusayo ca appahīno.

For a non-returner, the latent tendency of ignorance is not abandoned, but for that person the latent tendency of sensual desire is abandoned. For three individuals, both the latent tendency of ignorance and the latent tendency of sensual desire are not abandoned.

298. (Ka) yassa [V 2.0328] paṭighānusayo appahīno tassa mānānusayo appahīnoti? Āmantā.

298. (Ka) For an individual for whom the latent tendency of aversion is not abandoned, for that individual is the latent tendency of conceit not abandoned? Yes.

(Kha) yassa vā pana mānānusayo appahīno tassa [T 1.0705] paṭighānusayo appahīnoti?

(Kha) Or again, for an individual for whom the latent tendency of conceit is not abandoned, for that individual is the latent tendency of aversion not abandoned?

Anāgāmissa mānānusayo appahīno, no ca tassa paṭighānusayo appahīno. Tiṇṇaṃ puggalānaṃ mānānusayo ca appahīno paṭighānusayo ca appahīno.

For a non-returner, the latent tendency of conceit is not abandoned, but for that person the latent tendency of aversion is abandoned. For three individuals, both the latent tendency of conceit and the latent tendency of aversion are not abandoned.

Yassa paṭighānusayo appahīno tassa diṭṭhānusayo…pe… vicikicchānusayo appahīnoti?

For an individual for whom the latent tendency of aversion is not abandoned, for that individual are the latent tendency of views and the latent tendency of doubt not abandoned?

Dvinnaṃ puggalānaṃ paṭighānusayo appahīno, no ca tesaṃ vicikicchānusayo appahīno. Puthujjanassa paṭighānusayo ca appahīno vicikicchānusayo ca appahīno.

For two individuals, the latent tendency of aversion is not abandoned, but for them the latent tendency of doubt is abandoned. For a worldling, both the latent tendency of aversion and the latent tendency of doubt are not abandoned.

Yassa vā pana vicikicchānusayo appahīno tassa paṭighānusayo appahīnoti? Āmantā.

Or again, for an individual for whom the latent tendency of doubt is not abandoned, for that individual is the latent tendency of aversion not abandoned? Yes.

Yassa paṭighānusayo appahīno tassa bhavarāgānusayo…pe… avijjānusayo appahīnoti? Āmantā.

For an individual for whom the latent tendency of aversion is not abandoned, for that individual are the latent tendency of craving for existence and the latent tendency of ignorance not abandoned? Yes.

Yassa vā pana avijjānusayo appahīno tassa paṭighānusayo appahīnoti?

Or again, for an individual for whom the latent tendency of ignorance is not abandoned, for that individual is the latent tendency of aversion not abandoned?

Anāgāmissa avijjānusayo [M 2.0253] appahīno, no ca tassa paṭighānusayo appahīno. Tiṇṇaṃ puggalānaṃ avijjānusayo ca appahīno paṭighānusayo ca appahīno.

For a non-returner, the latent tendency of ignorance is not abandoned, but for that person the latent tendency of aversion is abandoned. For three individuals, both the latent tendency of ignorance and the latent tendency of aversion are not abandoned.

299. Yassa mānānusayo appahīno tassa diṭṭhānusayo…pe… vicikicchānusayo appahīnoti?

299. For an individual for whom the latent tendency of conceit is not abandoned, for that individual are the latent tendency of views and the latent tendency of doubt not abandoned?

Tiṇṇaṃ puggalānaṃ mānānusayo appahīno, no ca tesaṃ vicikicchānusayo [V 2.0329] appahīno. Puthujjanassa mānānusayo ca appahīno vicikicchānusayo ca appahīno.

For three individuals, the latent tendency of conceit is not abandoned, but for them the latent tendency of doubt is abandoned. For a worldling, both the latent tendency of conceit and the latent tendency of doubt are not abandoned.

Yassa vā pana vicikicchānusayo appahīno tassa mānānusayo appahīnoti? Āmantā.

Or again, for an individual for whom the latent tendency of doubt is not abandoned, for that individual is the latent tendency of conceit not abandoned? Yes.

Yassa mānānusayo appahīno tassa bhavarāgānusayo…pe… avijjānusayo appahīnoti? Āmantā.

For an individual for whom the latent tendency of conceit is not abandoned, for that individual are the latent tendency of craving for existence and the latent tendency of ignorance not abandoned? Yes.

Yassa vā pana avijjānusayo appahīno [T 1.0706] tassa mānānusayo appahīnoti? Āmantā.

Or again, for an individual for whom the latent tendency of ignorance is not abandoned, for that individual is the latent tendency of conceit not abandoned? Yes.

300. (Ka) yassa diṭṭhānusayo appahīno tassa vicikicchānusayo appahīnoti? Āmantā.

300. (Ka) For an individual for whom the latent tendency of views is not abandoned, for that individual is the latent tendency of doubt not abandoned? Yes.

(Kha) yassa vā pana vicikicchānusayo appahīno tassa diṭṭhānusayo appahīnoti? Āmantā …pe….

(Kha) Or again, for an individual for whom the latent tendency of doubt is not abandoned, for that individual is the latent tendency of views not abandoned? Yes... and so on...

301. Yassa vicikicchānusayo appahīno tassa bhavarāgānusayo…pe… avijjānusayo appahīnoti? Āmantā.

301. For an individual for whom the latent tendency of doubt is not abandoned, for that individual are the latent tendency of craving for existence and the latent tendency of ignorance not abandoned? Yes.

Yassa vā pana avijjānusayo appahīno tassa vicikicchānusayo appahīnoti?

Or again, for an individual for whom the latent tendency of ignorance is not abandoned, for that individual is the latent tendency of doubt not abandoned?

Tiṇṇaṃ puggalānaṃ avijjānusayo appahīno, no ca tesaṃ vicikicchānusayo appahīno. Puthujjanassa avijjānusayo ca appahīno vicikicchānusayo ca appahīno.

For three individuals, the latent tendency of ignorance is not abandoned, but for them the latent tendency of doubt is abandoned. For a worldling, both the latent tendency of ignorance and the latent tendency of doubt are not abandoned.

302. (Ka) yassa bhavarāgānusayo appahīno tassa avijjānusayo appahīnoti? Āmantā.

302. (Ka) For an individual for whom the latent tendency of craving for existence is not abandoned, for that individual is the latent tendency of ignorance not abandoned? Yes.

(Kha) yassa vā pana avijjānusayo appahīno tassa bhavarāgānusayo appahīnoti? Āmantā. (Ekamūlakaṃ)

(Kha) Or again, for an individual for whom the latent tendency of ignorance is not abandoned, for that individual is the latent tendency of craving for existence not abandoned? Yes. (Single Root Section)

303. (Ka) yassa kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca appahīnā tassa mānānusayo appahīnoti? Āmantā.

303. (Ka) For an individual for whom the latent tendencies of sensual desire and aversion are not abandoned, for that individual is the latent tendency of conceit not abandoned? Yes.

(Kha) yassa vā pana mānānusayo appahīno tassa kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca appahīnāti?

(Kha) Or again, for an individual for whom the latent tendency of conceit is not abandoned, for that individual are the latent tendencies of sensual desire and aversion not abandoned?

Anāgāmissa [V 2.0330] mānānusayo appahīno, no ca tassa [M 2.0254] kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca appahīnā. Tiṇṇaṃ puggalānaṃ mānānusayo ca appahīno kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca appahīnā.

For a non-returner, the latent tendency of conceit is not abandoned, but for that one the latent tendencies of sensual desire and aversion are abandoned. For the three individuals, the latent tendency of conceit is not abandoned, and the latent tendencies of sensual desire and aversion are not abandoned.

Yassa kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca appahīnā tassa [T 1.0707] diṭṭhānusayo…pe… vicikicchānusayo appahīnoti?

For one for whom the latent tendencies of sensual desire and aversion are not abandoned, is the latent tendency of views... the latent tendency of doubt also not abandoned?

Dvinnaṃ puggalānaṃ kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca appahīnā, no ca tesaṃ vicikicchānusayo appahīno. Puthujjanassa kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca appahīnā vicikicchānusayo ca appahīno.

For the two individuals, the latent tendencies of sensual desire and aversion are not abandoned, but for them the latent tendency of doubt is abandoned. For an ordinary person, the latent tendencies of sensual desire and aversion are not abandoned, and the latent tendency of doubt is not abandoned.

Yassa vā pana vicikicchānusayo appahīno tassa kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca appahīnāti? Āmantā.

Or, for one for whom the latent tendency of doubt is not abandoned, are the latent tendencies of sensual desire and aversion also not abandoned? Yes.

Yassa kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca appahīnā tassa bhavarāgānusayo…pe… avijjānusayo appahīnoti? Āmantā.

For one for whom the latent tendencies of sensual desire and aversion are not abandoned, is the latent tendency of craving for existence... the latent tendency of ignorance also not abandoned? Yes.

Yassa vā pana avijjānusayo appahīno tassa kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca appahīnāti?

Or, for one for whom the latent tendency of ignorance is not abandoned, are the latent tendencies of sensual desire and aversion also not abandoned?

Anāgāmissa avijjānusayo appahīno, no ca tassa kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca appahīnā. Tiṇṇaṃ puggalānaṃ avijjānusayo ca appahīno kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca appahīnā. (Dukamūlakaṃ)

For a non-returner, the latent tendency of ignorance is not abandoned, but for that one the latent tendencies of sensual desire and aversion are abandoned. For the three individuals, the latent tendency of ignorance is not abandoned, and the latent tendencies of sensual desire and aversion are not abandoned. (Based on a Pair)

304. Yassa kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca mānānusayo ca appahīnā tassa diṭṭhānusayo…pe… vicikicchānusayo appahīnoti?

304. For one for whom the latent tendencies of sensual desire, aversion, and conceit are not abandoned, is the latent tendency of views... the latent tendency of doubt also not abandoned?

Dvinnaṃ puggalānaṃ kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca mānānusayo ca appahīnā, no ca tesaṃ vicikicchānusayo appahīno. Puthujjanassa kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca mānānusayo ca appahīnā vicikicchānusayo ca appahīno.

For the two individuals, the latent tendencies of sensual desire, aversion, and conceit are not abandoned, but for them the latent tendency of doubt is abandoned. For an ordinary person, the latent tendencies of sensual desire, aversion, and conceit are not abandoned, and the latent tendency of doubt is not abandoned.

Yassa [V 2.0331] vā pana vicikicchānusayo appahīno tassa kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca mānānusayo ca appahīnāti? Āmantā.

Or, for one for whom the latent tendency of doubt is not abandoned, are the latent tendencies of sensual desire, aversion, and conceit also not abandoned? Yes.

Yassa kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca mānānusayo [T 1.0708] ca appahīnā tassa bhavarāgānusayo…pe… avijjānusayo appahīnoti? Āmantā.

For one for whom the latent tendencies of sensual desire, aversion, and conceit are not abandoned, is the latent tendency of craving for existence... the latent tendency of ignorance also not abandoned? Yes.

Yassa vā pana avijjānusayo appahīno tassa kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca mānānusayo ca appahīnāti?

Or, for one for whom the latent tendency of ignorance is not abandoned, are the latent tendencies of sensual desire, aversion, and conceit also not abandoned?

Anāgāmissa avijjānusayo ca mānānusayo ca appahīnā, no ca [M 2.0255] tassa kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca appahīnā. Tiṇṇaṃ puggalānaṃ avijjānusayo ca appahīno kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca mānānusayo ca appahīnā. (Tikamūlakaṃ)

For a non-returner, the latent tendencies of ignorance and conceit are not abandoned, but for that one the latent tendencies of sensual desire and aversion are abandoned. For the three individuals, the latent tendency of ignorance is not abandoned, and the latent tendencies of sensual desire, aversion, and conceit are not abandoned. (Based on a Triad)

305. (Ka) yassa kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca mānānusayo ca diṭṭhānusayo ca appahīnā tassa vicikicchānusayo appahīnoti? Āmantā.

305. (Ka) For one for whom the latent tendencies of sensual desire, aversion, conceit, and views are not abandoned, is the latent tendency of doubt also not abandoned? Yes.

(Kha) yassa vā pana vicikicchānusayo appahīno tassa kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca mānānusayo ca diṭṭhānusayo ca appahīnāti? Āmantā …pe…. (Catukkamūlakaṃ)

(Kha) Or, for one for whom the latent tendency of doubt is not abandoned, are the latent tendencies of sensual desire, aversion, conceit, and views also not abandoned? Yes. ... (Based on a Tetrad)

306. Yassa kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca mānānusayo ca diṭṭhānusayo ca vicikicchānusayo ca appahīnā tassa bhavarāgānusayo…pe… avijjānusayo appahīnoti? Āmantā.

306. For one for whom the latent tendencies of sensual desire, aversion, conceit, views, and doubt are not abandoned, is the latent tendency of craving for existence... the latent tendency of ignorance also not abandoned? Yes.

Yassa vā pana avijjānusayo appahīno tassa kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca mānānusayo ca diṭṭhānusayo ca vicikicchānusayo ca appahīnāti?

Or, for one for whom the latent tendency of ignorance is not abandoned, are the latent tendencies of sensual desire, aversion, conceit, views, and doubt also not abandoned?

Anāgāmissa avijjānusayo ca mānānusayo ca appahīnā, no ca tassa kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca diṭṭhānusayo ca vicikicchānusayo [V 2.0332] ca appahīnā. Dvinnaṃ puggalānaṃ avijjānusayo ca kāmarāgānusayo [T 1.0709] ca paṭighānusayo ca mānānusayo ca appahīnā, no ca tesaṃ diṭṭhānusayo ca vicikicchānusayo ca appahīnā. Puthujjanassa avijjānusayo ca appahīno; kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca mānānusayo ca diṭṭhānusayo ca vicikicchānusayo ca appahīnā. (Pañcakamūlakaṃ)

For a non-returner, the latent tendencies of ignorance and conceit are not abandoned, but for that one the latent tendencies of sensual desire, aversion, views, and doubt are abandoned. For the two individuals, the latent tendencies of ignorance, sensual desire, aversion, and conceit are not abandoned, but for them the latent tendencies of views and doubt are abandoned. For an ordinary person, the latent tendency of ignorance is not abandoned, and the latent tendencies of sensual desire, aversion, conceit, views, and doubt are not abandoned. (Based on a Pentad)

307. (Ka) yassa kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca mānānusayo ca diṭṭhānusayo ca vicikicchānusayo ca bhavarāgānusayo ca appahīnā tassa avijjānusayo appahīnoti? Āmantā.

307. (Ka) For one for whom the latent tendencies of sensual desire, aversion, conceit, views, doubt, and craving for existence are not abandoned, is the latent tendency of ignorance also not abandoned? Yes.

(Kha) yassa vā pana avijjānusayo appahīno tassa kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca mānānusayo ca diṭṭhānusayo ca vicikicchānusayo ca bhavarāgānusayo ca appahīnāti?

(Kha) Or, for one for whom the latent tendency of ignorance is not abandoned, are the latent tendencies of sensual desire, aversion, conceit, views, doubt, and craving for existence also not abandoned?

Anāgāmissa avijjānusayo ca mānānusayo ca bhavarāgānusayo ca appahīnā, no ca tassa kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca diṭṭhānusayo ca vicikicchānusayo ca appahīnā. Dvinnaṃ puggalānaṃ avijjānusayo ca kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo [M 2.0256] ca mānānusayo ca bhavarāgānusayo ca appahīnā, no ca tesaṃ diṭṭhānusayo ca vicikicchānusayo ca appahīnā. Puthujjanassa avijjānusayo ca appahīno, kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca mānānusayo ca diṭṭhānusayo ca vicikicchānusayo ca bhavarāgānusayo ca appahīnā. (Chakkamūlakaṃ)

For a non-returner, the latent tendencies of ignorance, conceit, and craving for existence are not abandoned, but for that one the latent tendencies of sensual desire, aversion, views, and doubt are abandoned. For the two individuals, the latent tendencies of ignorance, sensual desire, aversion, conceit, and craving for existence are not abandoned, but for them the latent tendencies of views and doubt are abandoned. For an ordinary person, the latent tendency of ignorance is not abandoned, and the latent tendencies of sensual desire, aversion, conceit, views, doubt, and craving for existence are not abandoned. (Based on a Hexad)

(Ṅa) paṭilomaokāso

(Ṅa) The Reverse Application

308. (Ka) yattha kāmarāgānusayo appahīno tattha paṭighānusayo appahīnoti?

308. (Ka) Where the latent tendency of sensual desire is not abandoned, is the latent tendency of aversion not abandoned there?

Na vattabbo “pahīno”ti vā “appahīno”ti vā.

It should not be said to be either 'abandoned' or 'not abandoned'.

(Kha) yattha [V 2.0333] vā pana paṭighānusayo appahīno tattha kāmarāgānusayo appahīnoti?

(Kha) Or where the latent tendency of aversion is not abandoned, is the latent tendency of sensual desire not abandoned there?

Na vattabbo [T 1.0710] “pahīno”ti vā “appahīno”ti vā.

It should not be said to be either 'abandoned' or 'not abandoned'.

(Ka) yattha kāmarāgānusayo appahīno tattha mānānusayo appahīnoti? Āmantā.

(Ka) Where the underlying tendency to sensual desire is unabandoned, is the underlying tendency to conceit unabandoned there? Yes.

(Kha) yattha vā pana mānānusayo appahīno tattha kāmarāgānusayo appahīnoti?

(Kha) Or where the underlying tendency to conceit is unabandoned, is the underlying tendency to sensual desire unabandoned there?

Rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā ettha mānānusayo appahīno; kāmarāgānusayo na vattabbo “pahīno”ti vā “appahīno”ti vā. Kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu ettha mānānusayo ca appahīno kāmarāgānusayo ca appahīno.

In the form realm and the formless realm, here the underlying tendency to conceit is unabandoned; the underlying tendency to sensual desire should not be said to be either 'abandoned' or 'unabandoned.' In the sense-sphere realm and in the two feelings, here both the underlying tendency to conceit is unabandoned and the underlying tendency to sensual desire is unabandoned.

Yattha kāmarāgānusayo appahīno tattha diṭṭhānusayo…pe… vicikicchānusayo appahīnoti? Āmantā.

Where the underlying tendency to sensual desire is unabandoned, are the underlying tendency to views... the underlying tendency to doubt unabandoned there? Yes.

Yattha vā pana vicikicchānusayo appahīno tattha kāmarāgānusayo appahīnoti?

Or where the underlying tendency to doubt is unabandoned, is the underlying tendency to sensual desire unabandoned there?

Dukkhāya vedanāya rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā ettha vicikicchānusayo appahīno; kāmarāgānusayo na vattabbo “pahīno”ti vā “appahīno”ti vā. Kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu ettha vicikicchānusayo ca appahīno kāmarāgānusayo ca appahīno.

In painful feeling, in the form realm, and in the formless realm, here the underlying tendency to doubt is unabandoned; the underlying tendency to sensual desire should not be said to be either 'abandoned' or 'unabandoned.' In the sense-sphere realm and in the two feelings, here both the underlying tendency to doubt is unabandoned and the underlying tendency to sensual desire is unabandoned.

(Ka) yattha kāmarāgānusayo appahīno tattha bhavarāgānusayo appahīnoti?

(Ka) Where the underlying tendency to sensual desire is unabandoned, is the underlying tendency to craving for existence unabandoned there?

Na vattabbo “pahīno”ti vā “appahīno”ti vā.

It should not be said to be either 'abandoned' or 'unabandoned'.

(Kha) yattha vā pana bhavarāgānusayo appahīno tattha kāmarāgānusayo appahīnoti?

(Kha) Or where the underlying tendency to craving for existence is unabandoned, is the underlying tendency to sensual desire unabandoned there?

Na vattabbo “pahīno”ti vā “appahīno”ti vā.

It should not be said to be either 'abandoned' or 'unabandoned'.

(Ka) yattha kāmarāgānusayo appahīno tattha avijjānusayo appahīnoti? Āmantā.

(Ka) Where the underlying tendency to sensual desire is unabandoned, is the underlying tendency to ignorance unabandoned there? Yes.

(Kha) yattha [V 2.0334] vā pana avijjānusayo appahīno tattha [M 2.0257] kāmarāgānusayo appahīnoti?

(Kha) Or where the underlying tendency to ignorance is unabandoned, is the underlying tendency to sensual desire unabandoned there?

Dukkhāya vedanāya rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā ettha avijjānusayo appahīno; kāmarāgānusayo na vattabbo “pahīno”ti vā [T 1.0711] “appahīno”ti vā. Kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu ettha avijjānusayo ca appahīno kāmarāgānusayo ca appahīno.

In the sense-sphere realm and in the two feelings, here both the underlying tendency to ignorance is unabandoned and the underlying tendency to sensual desire is unabandoned.
