312. (Ka) yattha vicikicchānusayo appahīno tattha bhavarāgānusayo appahīnoti?

312. (Ka) Where the underlying tendency to doubt is unabandoned, is the underlying tendency to craving for existence unabandoned there?

Kāmadhātuyā tīsu vedanāsu ettha vicikicchānusayo appahīno; bhavarāgānusayo na vattabbo “pahīno”ti vā “appahīno”ti vā. Rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā ettha vicikicchānusayo ca appahīno bhavarāgānusayo ca appahīno.

In the sense-sphere, in the three feelings, here the underlying tendency to doubt is unabandoned; the underlying tendency to lust for existence should not be said to be 'abandoned' or 'unabandoned'. In the fine-material sphere and the immaterial sphere, here both the underlying tendency to doubt and the underlying tendency to lust for existence are unabandoned.

(Kha) yattha vā pana bhavarāgānusayo appahīno tattha vicikicchānusayo appahīnoti? Āmantā.

But where the underlying tendency to lust for existence is unabandoned, is the underlying tendency to doubt unabandoned there? Yes.

(Ka) yattha vicikicchānusayo appahīno tattha avijjānusayo appahīnoti? Āmantā.

Where the underlying tendency to doubt is unabandoned, is the underlying tendency to ignorance unabandoned there? Yes.

(Kha) yattha vā pana avijjānusayo appahīno tattha vicikicchānusayo appahīnoti? Āmantā.

But where the underlying tendency to ignorance is unabandoned, is the underlying tendency to doubt unabandoned there? Yes.

313. (Ka) yattha [M 2.0259] bhavarāgānusayo appahīno tattha avijjānusayo appahīnoti? Āmantā.

313. Where the underlying tendency to lust for existence is unabandoned, is the underlying tendency to ignorance unabandoned there? Yes.

(Kha) yattha vā pana avijjānusayo appahīno tattha bhavarāgānusayo appahīnoti?

But where the underlying tendency to ignorance is unabandoned, is the underlying tendency to lust for existence unabandoned there?

Kāmadhātuyā tīsu vedanāsu ettha avijjānusayo appahīno; bhavarāgānusayo na vattabbo “pahīno”ti vā “appahīno”ti vā. Rūpadhātuyā [V 2.0337] arūpadhātuyā ettha avijjānusayo ca appahīno bhavarāgānusayo ca appahīno. (Ekamūlakaṃ)

In the sense-sphere, in the three feelings, here the underlying tendency to ignorance is unabandoned; the underlying tendency to lust for existence should not be said to be 'abandoned' or 'unabandoned'. In the fine-material sphere and the immaterial sphere, here both the underlying tendency to ignorance and the underlying tendency to lust for existence are unabandoned. (Single-rooted Section)

314. (Ka) yattha kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca appahīnā tattha mānānusayo appahīnoti? Natthi.

314. Where the underlying tendency to sensual lust and the underlying tendency to aversion are unabandoned, is the underlying tendency to conceit unabandoned there? No.

(Kha) yattha vā pana mānānusayo appahīno tattha kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca appahīnāti?

But where the underlying tendency to conceit is unabandoned, are the underlying tendency to sensual lust and the underlying tendency to aversion unabandoned there?

Rūpadhātuyā [T 1.0714] arūpadhātuyā ettha mānānusayo appahīno; kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca na vattabbā “pahīnā”ti vā “appahīnā”ti vā. Kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu ettha mānānusayo ca kāmarāgānusayo ca appahīnā; paṭighānusayo na vattabbo “pahīno”ti vā “appahīno”ti vā.

In the fine-material sphere and the immaterial sphere, here the underlying tendency to conceit is unabandoned; the underlying tendencies to sensual lust and aversion should not be said to be 'abandoned' or 'unabandoned'. In the sense-sphere, in the two feelings, here the underlying tendencies to conceit and sensual lust are unabandoned; the underlying tendency to aversion should not be said to be 'abandoned' or 'unabandoned'.

Yattha kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca appahīnā tattha diṭṭhānusayo…pe… vicikicchānusayo appahīnoti? Natthi.

Where the underlying tendency to sensual lust and the underlying tendency to aversion are unabandoned, is the underlying tendency to wrong views... the underlying tendency to doubt unabandoned there? No.

Yattha vā pana vicikicchānusayo appahīno tattha kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca appahīnāti?

But where the underlying tendency to doubt is unabandoned, are the underlying tendency to sensual lust and the underlying tendency to aversion unabandoned there?

Rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā ettha vicikicchānusayo appahīno; kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca na vattabbā “pahīnā”ti vā “appahīnā”ti vā. Kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu ettha vicikicchānusayo ca kāmarāgānusayo ca appahīnā; paṭighānusayo na vattabbo “pahīno”ti vā “appahīno”ti vā. Dukkhāya vedanāya ettha vicikicchānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca appahīnā; kāmarāgānusayo na vattabbo “pahīno”ti vā “appahīno”ti vā.

In the fine-material sphere and the immaterial sphere, here the underlying tendency to doubt is unabandoned; the underlying tendencies to sensual lust and aversion should not be said to be 'abandoned' or 'unabandoned'. In the sense-sphere, in the two feelings, here the underlying tendencies to doubt and sensual lust are unabandoned; the underlying tendency to aversion should not be said to be 'abandoned' or 'unabandoned'. In painful feeling, here the underlying tendencies to doubt and aversion are unabandoned; the underlying tendency to sensual lust should not be said to be 'abandoned' or 'unabandoned'.

Yattha kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca appahīnā tattha bhavarāgānusayo appahīnoti? Natthi.

Where the underlying tendency to sensual lust and the underlying tendency to aversion are unabandoned, is the underlying tendency to lust for existence unabandoned there? No.

Yattha vā pana bhavarāgānusayo appahīno tattha kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca appahīnāti? Na vattabbā “pahīnā”ti vā “appahīnā”ti vā.

But where the underlying tendency to lust for existence is unabandoned, are the underlying tendencies to sensual lust and aversion unabandoned there? They should not be said to be 'abandoned' or 'unabandoned'.

(Ka) yattha kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca appahīnā tattha avijjānusayo appahīnoti? Natthi.

Where the underlying tendency to sensual lust and the underlying tendency to aversion are unabandoned, is the underlying tendency to ignorance unabandoned there? No.

(Kha) yattha [V 2.0338] vā pana avijjānusayo appahīno [M 2.0260] tattha kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca appahīnāti?

But where the underlying tendency to ignorance is unabandoned, are the underlying tendency to sensual lust and the underlying tendency to aversion unabandoned there?

Rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā [T 1.0715] ettha avijjānusayo appahīno; kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca na vattabbā “pahīnā”ti vā “appahīnā”ti vā. Kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu ettha avijjānusayo ca kāmarāgānusayo ca appahīnā; paṭighānusayo na vattabbo “pahīno”ti vā “appahīno”ti vā. Dukkhāya vedanāya ettha avijjānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca appahīnā; kāmarāgānusayo na vattabbo “pahīno”ti vā “appahīno”ti vā. (Dukamūlakaṃ)

In the fine-material sphere and the immaterial sphere, here the underlying tendency to ignorance is unabandoned; the underlying tendencies to sensual lust and aversion should not be said to be 'abandoned' or 'unabandoned'. In the sense-sphere, in the two feelings, here the underlying tendency to ignorance and the underlying tendency to sensual lust are unabandoned; the underlying tendency to aversion should not be said to be 'abandoned' or 'unabandoned'. In painful feeling, here the underlying tendency to ignorance and the underlying tendency to aversion are unabandoned; the underlying tendency to sensual lust should not be said to be 'abandoned' or 'unabandoned'. (The Pair Section)

315. Yattha kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca mānānusayo ca appahīnā tattha diṭṭhānusayo…pe… vicikicchānusayo appahīnoti? Natthi.

315. Where the underlying tendency to sensual lust, the underlying tendency to aversion, and the underlying tendency to conceit are unabandoned, are the underlying tendency to wrong views and the underlying tendency to doubt unabandoned there? No.

Yattha vā pana vicikicchānusayo appahīno tattha kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca mānānusayo ca appahīnāti?

But where the underlying tendency to doubt is unabandoned, are the underlying tendency to sensual lust, the underlying tendency to aversion, and the underlying tendency to conceit unabandoned there?

Rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā ettha vicikicchānusayo ca mānānusayo ca appahīnā; kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca na vattabbā “pahīnā”ti vā “appahīnā”ti vā. Kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu ettha vicikicchānusayo ca kāmarāgānusayo ca mānānusayo ca appahīnā; paṭighānusayo na vattabbo “pahīno”ti vā “appahīno”ti vā. Dukkhāya vedanāya ettha vicikicchānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca appahīnā; kāmarāgānusayo ca mānānusayo ca na vattabbā “pahīnā”ti vā “appahīnā”ti vā.

In the fine-material sphere and the immaterial sphere, here the underlying tendency to doubt and the underlying tendency to conceit are unabandoned; the underlying tendencies to sensual lust and aversion should not be said to be 'abandoned' or 'unabandoned'. In the sense-sphere, in the two feelings, here the underlying tendency to doubt, the underlying tendency to sensual lust, and the underlying tendency to conceit are unabandoned; the underlying tendency to aversion should not be said to be 'abandoned' or 'unabandoned'. In painful feeling, here the underlying tendency to doubt and the underlying tendency to aversion are unabandoned; the underlying tendencies to sensual lust and conceit should not be said to be 'abandoned' or 'unabandoned'.

(Ka) yattha kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca mānānusayo ca appahīnā tattha bhavarāgānusayo appahīnoti? Natthi.

Where the underlying tendency to sensual lust, the underlying tendency to aversion, and the underlying tendency to conceit are unabandoned, is the underlying tendency to lust for existence unabandoned there? No.

(Kha) yattha vā pana bhavarāgānusayo appahīno tattha kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca mānānusayo ca appahīnāti[T 1.0716]?

But where the underlying tendency to lust for existence is unabandoned, are the underlying tendency to sensual lust, the underlying tendency to aversion, and the underlying tendency to conceit unabandoned there?

Rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā ettha bhavarāgānusayo ca mānānusayo ca appahīnā[V 2.0339]; kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca na vattabbā “pahīnā”ti vā “appahīnā”ti vā.

In the fine-material sphere and the immaterial sphere, here the underlying tendency to lust for existence and the underlying tendency to conceit are unabandoned; the underlying tendencies to sensual lust and aversion should not be said to be 'abandoned' or 'unabandoned'.

(Ka) yattha kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca mānānusayo ca appahīnā tattha avijjānusayo appahīnoti? Natthi.

Where the underlying tendency to sensual lust, the underlying tendency to aversion, and the underlying tendency to conceit are unabandoned, is the underlying tendency to ignorance unabandoned there? No.

(Kha) yattha vā pana avijjānusayo appahīno tattha kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca mānānusayo ca appahīnāti?

Or wherever the latent tendency to ignorance is not abandoned, are the latent tendency to sensual lust, the latent tendency to aversion, and the latent tendency to conceit not abandoned there?

Rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā ettha avijjānusayo [M 2.0261] ca mānānusayo ca appahīnā; kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca na vattabbā “pahīnā”ti vā “appahīnā”ti vā. Kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu ettha avijjānusayo ca kāmarāgānusayo ca mānānusayo ca appahīnā; paṭighānusayo na vattabbo “pahīno”ti vā “appahīno”ti vā. Dukkhāya vedanāya ettha avijjānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca appahīnā; kāmarāgānusayo ca mānānusayo ca na vattabbā “pahīnā”ti vā “appahīnā”ti vā. (Tikamūlakaṃ)

In the form realm and the formless realm, here the latent tendency to ignorance and the latent tendency to conceit are not abandoned; the latent tendency to sensual lust and the latent tendency to aversion cannot be said to be ‘abandoned’ or ‘not abandoned.’ In the sense-sphere realm, in the two feelings, here the latent tendency to ignorance, the latent tendency to sensual lust, and the latent tendency to conceit are not abandoned; the latent tendency to aversion cannot be said to be ‘abandoned’ or ‘not abandoned.’ In painful feeling, here the latent tendency to ignorance and the latent tendency to aversion are not abandoned; the latent tendency to sensual lust and the latent tendency to conceit cannot be said to be ‘abandoned’ or ‘not abandoned.’

316. (Ka) yattha kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca mānānusayo ca diṭṭhānusayo ca appahīnā tattha vicikicchānusayo appahīnoti? Natthi.

316. Where the latent tendency to sensual lust, the latent tendency to aversion, the latent tendency to conceit, and the latent tendency to views are not abandoned, is the latent tendency to doubt not abandoned there? There is no such case.

(Kha) yattha vā pana vicikicchānusayo appahīno tattha kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca mānānusayo ca diṭṭhānusayo ca appahīnāti?

Or wherever the latent tendency to doubt is not abandoned, are the latent tendency to sensual lust, the latent tendency to aversion, the latent tendency to conceit, and the latent tendency to views not abandoned there?

Rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā ettha vicikicchānusayo ca mānānusayo ca diṭṭhānusayo ca appahīnā; kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca na vattabbā “pahīnā”ti vā “appahīnā”ti vā. Kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu ettha vicikicchānusayo [T 1.0717] ca kāmarāgānusayo ca mānānusayo ca diṭṭhānusayo ca appahīnā; paṭighānusayo na vattabbo “pahīno”ti vā “appahīno”ti vā. Dukkhāya vedanāya ettha vicikicchānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca diṭṭhānusayo ca appahīnā; kāmarāgānusayo ca mānānusayo ca na vattabbā “pahīnā”ti vā “appahīnā”ti vā …pe…. (Catukkamūlakaṃ)

In the form realm and the formless realm, here the latent tendency to doubt, the latent tendency to conceit, and the latent tendency to views are not abandoned; the latent tendency to sensual lust and the latent tendency to aversion cannot be said to be ‘abandoned’ or ‘not abandoned.’ In the sense-sphere realm, in the two feelings, here the latent tendency to doubt, the latent tendency to sensual lust, the latent tendency to conceit, and the latent tendency to views are not abandoned; the latent tendency to aversion cannot be said to be ‘abandoned’ or ‘not abandoned.’ In painful feeling, here the latent tendency to doubt, the latent tendency to aversion, and the latent tendency to views are not abandoned; the latent tendency to sensual lust and the latent tendency to conceit cannot be said to be ‘abandoned’ or ‘not abandoned.’

317. (Ka) yattha [V 2.0340] kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca mānānusayo ca diṭṭhānusayo ca vicikicchānusayo ca appahīnā tattha bhavarāgānusayo appahīnoti? Natthi.

317. Where the latent tendency to sensual lust, the latent tendency to aversion, the latent tendency to conceit, the latent tendency to views, and the latent tendency to doubt are not abandoned, is the latent tendency to craving for existence not abandoned there? There is no such case.

(Kha) yattha vā pana bhavarāgānusayo appahīno tattha kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca mānānusayo ca diṭṭhānusayo ca vicikicchānusayo ca appahīnāti?

Or wherever the latent tendency to craving for existence is not abandoned, are the latent tendency to sensual lust, the latent tendency to aversion, the latent tendency to conceit, the latent tendency to views, and the latent tendency to doubt not abandoned there?

Mānānusayo ca diṭṭhānusayo ca vicikicchānusayo ca appahīnā; kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca na vattabbā “pahīnā”ti vā “appahīnā”ti vā.

The latent tendency to conceit, the latent tendency to views, and the latent tendency to doubt are not abandoned; the latent tendency to sensual lust and the latent tendency to aversion cannot be said to be ‘abandoned’ or ‘not abandoned.’

(Ka) yattha kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca mānānusayo ca diṭṭhānusayo ca vicikicchānusayo ca appahīnā tattha avijjānusayo appahīnoti? Natthi.

Where the latent tendency to sensual lust, the latent tendency to aversion, the latent tendency to conceit, the latent tendency to views, and the latent tendency to doubt are not abandoned, is the latent tendency to ignorance not abandoned there? There is no such case.

(Kha) yattha vā pana avijjānusayo appahīno tattha [M 2.0262] kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca mānānusayo ca diṭṭhānusayo ca vicikicchānusayo ca appahīnāti?

Or wherever the latent tendency to ignorance is not abandoned, are the latent tendency to sensual lust, the latent tendency to aversion, the latent tendency to conceit, the latent tendency to views, and the latent tendency to doubt not abandoned there?

Rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā ettha avijjānusayo ca mānānusayo ca diṭṭhānusayo ca vicikicchānusayo ca appahīnā; kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca na vattabbā “pahīnā”ti vā “appahīnā”ti vā. Kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu ettha avijjānusayo ca kāmarāgānusayo ca mānānusayo [T 1.0718] ca diṭṭhānusayo ca vicikicchānusayo ca appahīnā; paṭighānusayo na vattabbo “pahīno”ti vā “appahīno”ti vā. Dukkhāya vedanāya ettha avijjānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca diṭṭhānusayo ca vicikicchānusayo ca appahīnā; kāmarāgānusayo ca mānānusayo ca na vattabbā “pahīnā”ti vā “appahīnā”ti vā. (Pañcakamūlakaṃ)

In the form realm and the formless realm, here the latent tendency to ignorance, the latent tendency to conceit, the latent tendency to views, and the latent tendency to doubt are not abandoned; the latent tendency to sensual lust and the latent tendency to aversion cannot be said to be ‘abandoned’ or ‘not abandoned.’ In the sense-sphere realm, in the two feelings, here the latent tendency to ignorance, the latent tendency to sensual lust, the latent tendency to conceit, the latent tendency to views, and the latent tendency to doubt are not abandoned; the latent tendency to aversion cannot be said to be ‘abandoned’ or ‘not abandoned.’ In painful feeling, here the latent tendency to ignorance, the latent tendency to aversion, the latent tendency to views, and the latent tendency to doubt are not abandoned; the latent tendency to sensual lust and the latent tendency to conceit cannot be said to be ‘abandoned’ or ‘not abandoned.’

318. (Ka) yattha kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca mānānusayo ca diṭṭhānusayo ca vicikicchānusayo ca bhavarāgānusayo ca appahīnā tattha avijjānusayo appahīnoti? Natthi.

318. Where the latent tendency to sensual lust, the latent tendency to aversion, the latent tendency to conceit, the latent tendency to views, the latent tendency to doubt, and the latent tendency to craving for existence are not abandoned, is the latent tendency to ignorance not abandoned there? There is no such case.

(Kha) yattha [V 2.0341] vā pana avijjānusayo appahīno tattha kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca mānānusayo ca diṭṭhānusayo ca vicikicchānusayo ca bhavarāgānusayo ca appahīnāti?

Or wherever the latent tendency to ignorance is not abandoned, are the latent tendency to sensual lust, the latent tendency to aversion, the latent tendency to conceit, the latent tendency to views, the latent tendency to doubt, and the latent tendency to craving for existence not abandoned there?

Rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā ettha avijjānusayo ca mānānusayo ca diṭṭhānusayo ca vicikicchānusayo ca bhavarāgānusayo ca appahīnā; kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca na vattabbā “pahīnā”ti vā “appahīnā”ti vā. Kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu ettha avijjānusayo ca kāmarāgānusayo ca mānānusayo ca diṭṭhānusayo ca vicikicchānusayo ca appahīnā; paṭighānusayo ca bhavarāgānusayo ca na vattabbā “pahīnā”ti vā “appahīnā”ti vā. Dukkhāya vedanāya ettha avijjānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca diṭṭhānusayo ca vicikicchānusayo ca appahīnā; kāmarāgānusayo ca mānānusayo ca bhavarāgānusayo ca na vattabbā “pahīnā”ti vā “appahīnā”ti vā. (Chakkamūlakaṃ)

In the form realm and the formless realm, here the latent tendency to ignorance, the latent tendency to conceit, the latent tendency to views, the latent tendency to doubt, and the latent tendency to craving for existence are not abandoned; the latent tendency to sensual lust and the latent tendency to aversion cannot be said to be ‘abandoned’ or ‘not abandoned.’ In the sense-sphere realm, in the two feelings, here the latent tendency to ignorance, the latent tendency to sensual lust, the latent tendency to conceit, the latent tendency to views, and the latent tendency to doubt are not abandoned; the latent tendency to aversion and the latent tendency to craving for existence cannot be said to be ‘abandoned’ or ‘not abandoned.’ In painful feeling, here the latent tendency to ignorance, the latent tendency to aversion, the latent tendency to views, and the latent tendency to doubt are not abandoned; the latent tendency to sensual lust, the latent tendency to conceit, and the latent tendency to craving for existence cannot be said to be ‘abandoned’ or ‘not abandoned.’

(Ca) paṭilomapuggalokāsā

(Ca) The Reverse Person-Plane

319. (Ka) yassa [T 1.0719] yattha kāmarāgānusayo appahīno tassa tattha paṭighānusayo appahīnoti?

For whom, wherein the latent tendency to sensual lust is not abandoned, for him, therein is the latent tendency to aversion not abandoned?

Na vattabbo “pahīno”ti vā “appahīno”ti [M 2.0263] vā.

319. It cannot be said ‘abandoned’ or ‘not abandoned’.

(Kha) yassa vā pana yattha paṭighānusayo appahīno tassa tattha kāmarāgānusayo appahīnoti?

Or for whom, wherein the latent tendency to aversion is not abandoned, for him, therein is the latent tendency to sensual lust not abandoned?

Na vattabbo “pahīno”ti vā “appahīno”ti vā.

It cannot be said ‘abandoned’ or ‘not abandoned’.

(Ka) yassa yattha kāmarāgānusayo appahīno tassa tattha mānānusayo appahīnoti? Āmantā.

(Ka) For whom, wherein the underlying tendency to sensual desire is not abandoned, for him, therein is the underlying tendency to conceit also not abandoned? Yes.

(Kha) yassa vā pana yattha mānānusayo appahīno tassa tattha kāmarāgānusayo appahīnoti?

(Kha) Or, for whom, wherein the underlying tendency to conceit is not abandoned, for him, therein is the underlying tendency to sensual desire also not abandoned?

Anāgāmissa rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā tassa tattha mānānusayo appahīno; kāmarāgānusayo na vattabbo “pahīno”ti vā “appahīno”ti [V 2.0342] vā. Tasseva puggalassa kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu tassa tattha mānānusayo appahīno, no ca tassa tattha kāmarāgānusayo appahīno. Tiṇṇaṃ puggalānaṃ rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā tesaṃ tattha mānānusayo appahīno; kāmarāgānusayo na vattabbo “pahīno”ti vā “appahīno”ti vā. Tesaññeva puggalānaṃ kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu tesaṃ tattha mānānusayo ca appahīno kāmarāgānusayo ca appahīno.

For a Non-returner, in the form realm and the formless realm, for him, therein the underlying tendency to conceit is not abandoned; the underlying tendency to sensual desire should not be said to be 'abandoned' or 'not abandoned.' For that same individual, in the sense-sphere realm, in the two feelings, for him, therein the underlying tendency to conceit is not abandoned, but the underlying tendency to sensual desire is abandoned. For the three individuals, in the form realm and the formless realm, for them, therein the underlying tendency to conceit is not abandoned; the underlying tendency to sensual desire should not be said to be 'abandoned' or 'not abandoned.' For those same individuals, in the sense-sphere realm, in the two feelings, for them, therein both the underlying tendency to conceit and the underlying tendency to sensual desire are not abandoned.

Yassa yattha kāmarāgānusayo appahīno tassa tattha diṭṭhānusayo…pe… vicikicchānusayo appahīnoti?

For whom, wherein the underlying tendency to sensual desire is not abandoned, for him, therein is the underlying tendency to views... the underlying tendency to doubt also not abandoned?

Dvinnaṃ puggalānaṃ kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu tesaṃ tattha kāmarāgānusayo appahīno, no ca tesaṃ tattha vicikicchānusayo appahīno. Puthujjanassa kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu tassa tattha kāmarāgānusayo ca appahīno vicikicchānusayo ca appahīno.

For the two individuals, in the sense-sphere realm, in the two feelings, for them, therein the underlying tendency to sensual desire is not abandoned, but the underlying tendency to doubt is abandoned. For a worldling, in the sense-sphere realm, in the two feelings, for him, therein both the underlying tendency to sensual desire and the underlying tendency to doubt are not abandoned.

Yassa vā pana yattha vicikicchānusayo [T 1.0720] appahīno tassa tattha kāmarāgānusayo appahīnoti?

Or, for whom, wherein the underlying tendency to doubt is not abandoned, for him, therein is the underlying tendency to sensual desire also not abandoned?

Puthujjanassa dukkhāya vedanāya rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā tassa tattha vicikicchānusayo appahīno; kāmarāgānusayo na vattabbo “pahīno”ti vā “appahīno”ti vā. Tasseva puggalassa kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu tassa tattha vicikicchānusayo ca appahīno kāmarāgānusayo ca appahīno.

For a worldling, in painful feeling, in the form realm, and in the formless realm, for him, therein the underlying tendency to doubt is not abandoned; the underlying tendency to sensual desire should not be said to be 'abandoned' or 'not abandoned.' For that same individual, in the sense-sphere realm, in the two feelings, for him, therein both the underlying tendency to doubt and the underlying tendency to sensual desire are not abandoned.

(Ka) yassa yattha kāmarāgānusayo appahīno tassa tattha bhavarāgānusayo appahīnoti?

(Ka) For whom, wherein the underlying tendency to sensual desire is not abandoned, for him, therein is the underlying tendency to craving for existence also not abandoned?

Na vattabbo “pahīno”ti vā “appahīno”ti vā.

It should not be said 'abandoned' or 'not abandoned'.

(Kha) yassa vā pana yattha bhavarāgānusayo appahīno tassa tattha kāmarāgānusayo [M 2.0264] appahīnoti?

(Kha) Or, for whom, wherein the underlying tendency to craving for existence is not abandoned, for him, therein is the underlying tendency to sensual desire also not abandoned?

Na vattabbo “pahīno”ti vā “appahīno”ti vā.

It should not be said 'abandoned' or 'not abandoned'.

(Ka) yassa [V 2.0343] yattha kāmarāgānusayo appahīno tassa tattha avijjānusayo appahīnoti? Āmantā.

(Ka) For whom, wherein the underlying tendency to sensual desire is not abandoned, for him, therein is the underlying tendency to ignorance also not abandoned? Yes.

(Kha) yassa vā pana yattha avijjānusayo appahīno tassa tattha kāmarāgānusayo appahīnoti?

(Kha) Or, for whom, wherein the underlying tendency to ignorance is not abandoned, for him, therein is the underlying tendency to sensual desire also not abandoned?

Anāgāmissa dukkhāya vedanāya rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā tassa tattha avijjānusayo appahīno; kāmarāgānusayo na vattabbo “pahīno”ti vā “appahīno”ti vā. Tasseva puggalassa kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu tassa tattha avijjānusayo appahīno, no ca tassa tattha kāmarāgānusayo appahīno. Tiṇṇaṃ puggalānaṃ dukkhāya vedanāya rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā tesaṃ tattha avijjānusayo appahīno; kāmarāgānusayo na vattabbo “pahīno”ti vā “appahīno”ti vā. Tesaññeva puggalānaṃ kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu tesaṃ tattha avijjānusayo ca appahīno kāmarāgānusayo ca appahīno.

For a Non-returner, in painful feeling, in the form realm, and in the formless realm, for him, therein the underlying tendency to ignorance is not abandoned; the underlying tendency to sensual desire should not be said to be 'abandoned' or 'not abandoned.' For that same individual, in the sense-sphere realm, in the two feelings, for him, therein the underlying tendency to ignorance is not abandoned, but the underlying tendency to sensual desire is abandoned. For the three individuals, in painful feeling, in the form realm, and in the formless realm, for them, therein the underlying tendency to ignorance is not abandoned; the underlying tendency to sensual desire should not be said to be 'abandoned' or 'not abandoned.' For those same individuals, in the sense-sphere realm, in the two feelings, for them, therein both the underlying tendency to ignorance and the underlying tendency to sensual desire are not abandoned.

320. (Ka) yassa [T 1.0721] yattha paṭighānusayo appahīno tassa tattha mānānusayo appahīnoti?

320. (Ka) For whom, wherein the underlying tendency to aversion is not abandoned, for him, therein is the underlying tendency to conceit also not abandoned?

Na vattabbo “pahīno”ti vā “appahīno”ti vā.

It should not be said 'abandoned' or 'not abandoned'.

(Kha) Or, for whom, wherein the underlying tendency to conceit is not abandoned, for him, therein is the underlying tendency to aversion also not abandoned?

Na vattabbo “pahīno”ti vā “appahīno”ti vā.

It should not be said 'abandoned' or 'not abandoned'.

(Ka) yassa yattha paṭighānusayo appahīno tassa tattha diṭṭhānusayo…pe… vicikicchānusayo appahīnoti?

(Ka) For whom, wherein the underlying tendency to aversion is not abandoned, for him, therein is the underlying tendency to views... the underlying tendency to doubt also not abandoned?

Dvinnaṃ puggalānaṃ dukkhāya vedanāya tesaṃ tattha paṭighānusayo appahīno, no ca tesaṃ tattha vicikicchānusayo appahīno. Puthujjanassa dukkhāya vedanāya tassa tattha paṭighānusayo ca appahīno vicikicchānusayo ca appahīno.

For the two individuals, in painful feeling, for them, therein the underlying tendency to aversion is not abandoned, but the underlying tendency to doubt is abandoned. For a worldling, in painful feeling, for him, therein both the underlying tendency to aversion and the underlying tendency to doubt are not abandoned.

(Kha) yassa vā pana yattha vicikicchānusayo appahīno tassa tattha paṭighānusayo appahīnoti?

(Kha) Or, for whom, wherein the underlying tendency to doubt is not abandoned, for him, therein is the underlying tendency to aversion also not abandoned?

Puthujjanassa kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā tassa tattha vicikicchānusayo appahīno; paṭighānusayo na vattabbo “pahīno”ti vā “appahīno”ti vā. Tasseva puggalassa dukkhāya vedanāya [V 2.0344] tassa tattha vicikicchānusayo ca appahīno paṭighānusayo ca appahīno.

For a worldling, in the sense-sphere realm, in the two feelings, in the form realm, and in the formless realm, for him, therein the underlying tendency to doubt is not abandoned; the underlying tendency to aversion should not be said to be 'abandoned' or 'not abandoned.' For that same individual, in painful feeling, for him, therein both the underlying tendency to doubt and the underlying tendency to aversion are not abandoned.

(Ka) yassa [M 2.0265] yattha paṭighānusayo appahīno tassa tattha bhavarāgānusayo appahīnoti?

(Ka) For whom, wherein the underlying tendency to aversion is not abandoned, for him, therein is the underlying tendency to craving for existence also not abandoned?

Na vattabbo “pahīno”ti vā “appahīno”ti vā.

(Ka) yassa yattha paṭighānusayo appahīno tassa tattha avijjānusayo appahīnoti? Āmantā.

(Kha) yassa vā pana yattha avijjānusayo appahīno tassa tattha paṭighānusayo appahīnoti[T 1.0722]?

(Kha) Or, for whom, wherein the underlying tendency to ignorance is not abandoned, for him, therein is the underlying tendency to aversion also not abandoned?

Anāgāmissa kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā tassa tattha avijjānusayo appahīno; paṭighānusayo na vattabbo “pahīno”ti vā “appahīno”ti vā. Tasseva puggalassa dukkhāya vedanāya tassa tattha avijjānusayo appahīno, no ca tassa tattha paṭighānusayo appahīno. Tiṇṇaṃ puggalānaṃ kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā tesaṃ tattha avijjānusayo appahīno; paṭighānusayo na vattabbo “pahīno”ti vā “appahīno”ti vā. Tesaññeva puggalānaṃ dukkhāya vedanāya tesaṃ tattha avijjānusayo ca appahīno paṭighānusayo ca appahīno.

For a non-returner, in the sensual realm, in the two feelings, in the form realm, and in the formless realm, the underlying tendency to ignorance is unabandoned for him there; the underlying tendency to aversion should not be said to be ‘abandoned’ or ‘unabandoned’. For that same person, with painful feeling, the underlying tendency to ignorance is unabandoned for him there, but the underlying tendency to aversion is abandoned for him there. For three persons, in the sensual realm, in the two feelings, in the form realm, and in the formless realm, the underlying tendency to ignorance is unabandoned for them there; the underlying tendency to aversion should not be said to be ‘abandoned’ or ‘unabandoned’. For those same persons, with painful feeling, both the underlying tendency to ignorance and the underlying tendency to aversion are unabandoned for them there.

Tiṇṇaṃ puggalānaṃ kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā tesaṃ tattha mānānusayo appahīno, no ca tesaṃ tattha vicikicchānusayo appahīno. Puthujjanassa kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu rūpadhātuyā [V 2.0345] arūpadhātuyā tassa tattha mānānusayo ca appahīno vicikicchānusayo ca appahīno.

For a worldling, in the sensual realm, in the two feelings, in the form realm, and in the formless realm, both the underlying tendency to conceit and the underlying tendency to doubt are unabandoned for him there.

(Ka) yassa yattha mānānusayo appahīno tassa tattha avijjānusayo appahīnoti? Āmantā.

(Kha) yassa vā pana yattha avijjānusayo appahīno tassa tattha mānānusayo appahīnoti?

Or, for whomever, wherever the underlying tendency to ignorance is unabandoned, is the underlying tendency to conceit unabandoned for him there?

Catunnaṃ puggalānaṃ dukkhāya vedanāya tesaṃ tattha avijjānusayo appahīno; mānānusayo na vattabbo “pahīno”ti vā “appahīno”ti vā. Tesaññeva puggalānaṃ kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā tesaṃ tattha avijjānusayo ca appahīno mānānusayo ca appahīno.

325. For whomsoever, wherever both the underlying tendency to sensual desire and the underlying tendency to aversion are unabandoned, for them there, is the underlying tendency to conceit unabandoned? No.

Tasseva puggalassa dukkhāya vedanāya tassa tattha vicikicchānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca appahīnā; kāmarāgānusayo na vattabbo “pahīno”ti vā “appahīno”ti vā.

Tasseva puggalassa kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu tassa tattha avijjānusayo appahīno, no ca tassa tattha kāmarāgānusayo appahīno. Paṭighānusayo na vattabbo “pahīno”ti vā “appahīno”ti vā. Tasseva puggalassa dukkhāya vedanāya tassa tattha avijjānusayo appahīno, no ca tassa tattha [T 1.0727] paṭighānusayo appahīno; kāmarāgānusayo na vattabbo “pahīno”ti vā “appahīno”ti vā. Tiṇṇaṃ [V 2.0349] puggalānaṃ rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā tesaṃ tattha avijjānusayo appahīno; kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca na vattabbā “pahīnā”ti vā “appahīnā”ti vā. Tesaññeva puggalānaṃ kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu tesaṃ tattha avijjānusayo ca kāmarāgānusayo ca appahīnā; paṭighānusayo na vattabbo “pahīno”ti vā “appahīno”ti vā. Tesaññeva puggalānaṃ dukkhāya [M 2.0269] vedanāya tesaṃ tattha avijjānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca appahīnā; kāmarāgānusayo na vattabbo “pahīno”ti vā “appahīno”ti vā. (Dukamūlakaṃ)

For a non-returner, in the form realm and the formless realm, for them there the underlying tendency to ignorance is unabandoned; both the underlying tendency to sensual desire and the underlying tendency to aversion should not be said to be ‘abandoned’ or ‘unabandoned’. For that same individual, in the sense-sphere realm, with respect to two feelings, for them there the underlying tendency to ignorance is unabandoned, but the underlying tendency to sensual desire is not unabandoned. The underlying tendency to aversion should not be said to be ‘abandoned’ or ‘unabandoned’. For that same individual, with respect to painful feeling, for them there the underlying tendency to ignorance is unabandoned, but the underlying tendency to aversion is not unabandoned; the underlying tendency to sensual desire should not be said to be ‘abandoned’ or ‘unabandoned’. For three individuals, in the form realm and the formless realm, for them there the underlying tendency to ignorance is unabandoned; both the underlying tendency to sensual desire and the underlying tendency to aversion should not be said to be ‘abandoned’ or ‘unabandoned’. For those same individuals, in the sense-sphere realm, with respect to two feelings, for them there both the underlying tendency to ignorance and the underlying tendency to sensual desire are unabandoned; the underlying tendency to aversion should not be said to be ‘abandoned’ or ‘unabandoned’. For those same individuals, with respect to painful feeling, for them there both the underlying tendency to ignorance and the underlying tendency to aversion are unabandoned; the underlying tendency to sensual desire should not be said to be ‘abandoned’ or ‘unabandoned’. (The Dyad Root)

326. Yassa yattha kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca mānānusayo ca appahīnā tassa tattha diṭṭhānusayo…pe… vicikicchānusayo appahīnoti? Natthi.

326. For whomsoever, wherever the underlying tendencies to sensual desire, aversion, and conceit are unabandoned, for them there, is the underlying tendency to views… the underlying tendency to doubt unabandoned? No.

Yassa vā pana yattha vicikicchānusayo appahīno tassa tattha kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca mānānusayo ca appahīnāti?

Or alternatively, for whomsoever, wherever the underlying tendency to doubt is unabandoned, for them there, are the underlying tendencies to sensual desire, aversion, and conceit unabandoned?

Puthujjanassa rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā tassa tattha vicikicchānusayo ca mānānusayo ca appahīnā; kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca na vattabbā “pahīnā”ti vā “appahīnā”ti vā. Tasseva puggalassa kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu tassa tattha vicikicchānusayo ca kāmarāgānusayo ca mānānusayo ca appahīnā; paṭighānusayo na vattabbo “pahīno”ti vā “appahīno”ti vā. Tasseva puggalassa dukkhāya vedanāya tassa tattha vicikicchānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca appahīnā; kāmarāgānusayo [T 1.0728] ca mānānusayo ca na vattabbā “pahīnā”ti vā “appahīnā”ti vā.

For a worldling, in the form realm and the formless realm, for them there both the underlying tendency to doubt and the underlying tendency to conceit are unabandoned; both the underlying tendency to sensual desire and the underlying tendency to aversion should not be said to be ‘abandoned’ or ‘unabandoned’. For that same individual, in the sense-sphere realm, with respect to two feelings, for them there the underlying tendencies to doubt, sensual desire, and conceit are unabandoned; the underlying tendency to aversion should not be said to be ‘abandoned’ or ‘unabandoned’. For that same individual, with respect to painful feeling, for them there both the underlying tendency to doubt and the underlying tendency to aversion are unabandoned; both the underlying tendency to sensual desire and the underlying tendency to conceit should not be said to be ‘abandoned’ or ‘unabandoned’.

(Ka) yassa yattha kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca mānānusayo ca appahīnā tassa tattha bhavarāgānusayo appahīnoti? Natthi.

(Ka) For a person for whom, wherever the underlying tendencies to sensual lust, aversion, and conceit are unabandoned, for that person, is the underlying tendency to craving for existence also unabandoned there? No.

(Kha) yassa vā pana yattha bhavarāgānusayo appahīno tassa tattha kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca mānānusayo ca appahīnāti?

(Kha) Or again, for a person for whom, wherever the underlying tendency to craving for existence is unabandoned, for that person, are the underlying tendencies to sensual lust, aversion, and conceit also unabandoned there?

Mānānusayo [V 2.0350] appahīno; kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca na vattabbā “pahīnā”ti vā “appahīnā”ti vā.

The underlying tendency to conceit is unabandoned; the underlying tendencies to sensual lust and aversion cannot be said to be ‘abandoned’ or ‘unabandoned’.

(Ka) yassa yattha kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca mānānusayo ca appahīnā tassa tattha avijjānusayo appahīnoti? Natthi.

(Ka) For a person for whom, wherever the underlying tendencies to sensual lust, aversion, and conceit are unabandoned, for that person, is the underlying tendency to ignorance also unabandoned there? No.

(Kha) yassa vā pana yattha avijjānusayo appahīno tassa tattha kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca mānānusayo ca appahīnāti?

(Kha) Or again, for a person for whom, wherever the underlying tendency to ignorance is unabandoned, for that person, are the underlying tendencies to sensual lust, aversion, and conceit also unabandoned there?

Anāgāmissa rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā tassa tattha avijjānusayo ca mānānusayo ca appahīnā; kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca na vattabbā “pahīnā”ti vā “appahīnā”ti vā. Tasseva puggalassa kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu tassa tattha avijjānusayo ca mānānusayo [M 2.0270] ca appahīnā, no ca tassa tattha kāmarāgānusayo appahīno; paṭighānusayo na vattabbo “pahīno”ti vā “appahīno”ti vā. Tasseva puggalassa dukkhāya vedanāya tassa tattha avijjānusayo appahīno, no ca tassa tattha paṭighānusayo appahīno; kāmarāgānusayo ca mānānusayo ca na vattabbā “pahīnā”ti vā “appahīnā”ti vā. Tiṇṇaṃ puggalānaṃ rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā tesaṃ tattha avijjānusayo ca mānānusayo [T 1.0729] ca appahīnā; kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca na vattabbā “pahīnā”ti vā “appahīnā”ti vā. Tesaññeva puggalānaṃ kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu tesaṃ tattha avijjānusayo ca kāmarāgānusayo ca mānānusayo ca appahīnā; paṭighānusayo na vattabbo “pahīno”ti vā “appahīno”ti vā. Tesaññeva puggalānaṃ dukkhāya vedanāya tesaṃ tattha avijjānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca appahīnā; kāmarāgānusayo ca mānānusayo ca na vattabbā “pahīnā”ti vā “appahīnā”ti vā. (Tikamūlakaṃ)

For the non-returner, in the form element and the formless element, for that person the underlying tendencies to ignorance and conceit are unabandoned there; the underlying tendencies to sensual lust and aversion cannot be said to be ‘abandoned’ or ‘unabandoned’. For that same person, in the sense-sphere element, with respect to two feelings, for that person the underlying tendencies to ignorance and conceit are unabandoned there, but the underlying tendency to sensual lust is not unabandoned for that person there; the underlying tendency to aversion cannot be said to be ‘abandoned’ or ‘unabandoned’. For that same person, with respect to painful feeling, for that person the underlying tendency to ignorance is unabandoned there, but the underlying tendency to aversion is not unabandoned for that person there; the underlying tendencies to sensual lust and conceit cannot be said to be ‘abandoned’ or ‘unabandoned’. For the three individuals, in the form element and the formless element, for them the underlying tendencies to ignorance and conceit are unabandoned there; the underlying tendencies to sensual lust and aversion cannot be said to be ‘abandoned’ or ‘unabandoned’. For those same individuals, in the sense-sphere element, with respect to two feelings, for them the underlying tendencies to ignorance, sensual lust, and conceit are unabandoned there; the underlying tendency to aversion cannot be said to be ‘abandoned’ or ‘unabandoned’. For those same individuals, with respect to painful feeling, for them the underlying tendencies to ignorance and aversion are unabandoned there; the underlying tendencies to sensual lust and conceit cannot be said to be ‘abandoned’ or ‘unabandoned’.

327. (Ka) yassa yattha kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca mānānusayo ca diṭṭhānusayo ca appahīnā tassa tattha vicikicchānusayo appahīnoti? Natthi.

327. (Ka) For a person for whom, wherever the underlying tendencies to sensual lust, aversion, conceit, and views are unabandoned, for that person, is the underlying tendency to doubt also unabandoned there? No.

(Kha) yassa [V 2.0351] vā pana yattha vicikicchānusayo appahīno tassa tattha kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca mānānusayo ca diṭṭhānusayo ca appahīnāti?

(Kha) Or again, for a person for whom, wherever the underlying tendency to doubt is unabandoned, for that person, are the underlying tendencies to sensual lust, aversion, conceit, and views also unabandoned there?

Puthujjanassa rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā tassa tattha vicikicchānusayo ca mānānusayo ca diṭṭhānusayo ca appahīnā; kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca na vattabbā “pahīnā”ti vā “appahīnā”ti vā. Tasseva puggalassa kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu tassa tattha vicikicchānusayo ca kāmarāgānusayo ca mānānusayo ca diṭṭhānusayo ca appahīnā; paṭighānusayo na vattabbo “pahīno”ti vā “appahīno”ti vā. Tasseva puggalassa dukkhāya vedanāya tassa tattha vicikicchānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca diṭṭhānusayo ca appahīnā; kāmarāgānusayo ca mānānusayo ca na vattabbā “pahīnā”ti vā “appahīnā”ti [T 1.0730] vā …pe…. (Catukkamūlakaṃ)

For an ordinary person, in the form element and the formless element, for that person the underlying tendencies to doubt, conceit, and views are unabandoned there; the underlying tendencies to sensual lust and aversion cannot be said to be ‘abandoned’ or ‘unabandoned’. For that same person, in the sense-sphere element, with respect to two feelings, for that person the underlying tendencies to doubt, sensual lust, conceit, and views are unabandoned there; the underlying tendency to aversion cannot be said to be ‘abandoned’ or ‘unabandoned’. For that same person, with respect to painful feeling, for that person the underlying tendencies to doubt, aversion, and views are unabandoned there; the underlying tendencies to sensual lust and conceit cannot be said to be ‘abandoned’ or ‘unabandoned’.

328. (Ka) yassa yattha kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca mānānusayo ca diṭṭhānusayo ca vicikicchānusayo ca appahīnā tassa tattha [M 2.0271] bhavarāgānusayo appahīnoti? Natthi.

328. (Ka) For a person for whom, wherever the underlying tendencies to sensual lust, aversion, conceit, views, and doubt are unabandoned, for that person, is the underlying tendency to craving for existence also unabandoned there? No.

(Kha) yassa vā pana yattha bhavarāgānusayo appahīno tassa tattha kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca mānānusayo ca diṭṭhānusayo ca vicikicchānusayo ca appahīnāti?

(Kha) Or again, for a person for whom, wherever the underlying tendency to craving for existence is unabandoned, for that person, are the underlying tendencies to sensual lust, aversion, conceit, views, and doubt also unabandoned there?

Tiṇṇaṃ puggalānaṃ rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā tesaṃ tattha bhavarāgānusayo ca mānānusayo ca appahīnā, no ca tesaṃ tattha diṭṭhānusayo ca vicikicchānusayo ca appahīnā; kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca na vattabbā “pahīnā”ti vā “appahīnā”ti vā. Puthujjanassa rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā tassa tattha bhavarāgānusayo ca mānānusayo ca diṭṭhānusayo ca vicikicchānusayo ca appahīnā; kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca na vattabbā “pahīnā”ti vā “appahīnā”ti vā.

For the three individuals, in the form element and the formless element, for them the underlying tendencies to craving for existence and conceit are unabandoned there, but the underlying tendencies to views and doubt are not unabandoned for them there; the underlying tendencies to sensual lust and aversion cannot be said to be 'abandoned' or 'unabandoned'. For an ordinary person, in the form element and the formless element, for that person the underlying tendencies to craving for existence, conceit, views, and doubt are unabandoned there; the underlying tendencies to sensual lust and aversion cannot be said to be 'abandoned' or 'unabandoned'.

(Ka) yassa [V 2.0352] yattha kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca mānānusayo ca diṭṭhānusayo ca vicikicchānusayo ca appahīnā tassa tattha avijjānusayo appahīnoti? Natthi.

(Ka) For a person for whom, wherever the underlying tendencies to sensual lust, aversion, conceit, views, and doubt are unabandoned, for that person, is the underlying tendency to ignorance also unabandoned there? No.

(Kha) yassa vā pana yattha avijjānusayo appahīno tassa tattha kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca mānānusayo ca diṭṭhānusayo ca vicikicchānusayo ca appahīnāti?

(Kha) Or again, for a person for whom, wherever the underlying tendency to ignorance is unabandoned, for that person, are the underlying tendencies to sensual lust, aversion, conceit, views, and doubt also unabandoned there?

Anāgāmissa rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā tassa tattha avijjānusayo ca mānānusayo ca appahīnā, no ca tassa tattha diṭṭhānusayo ca vicikicchānusayo ca appahīnā[T 1.0731]; kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca na vattabbā “pahīnā”ti vā “appahīnā”ti vā. Tasseva puggalassa kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu tassa tattha avijjānusayo ca mānānusayo ca appahīnā, no ca tassa tattha kāmarāgānusayo ca diṭṭhānusayo ca vicikicchānusayo ca appahīnā; paṭighānusayo na vattabbo “pahīno”ti vā “appahīno”ti vā. Tasseva puggalassa dukkhāya vedanāya tassa tattha avijjānusayo appahīno, no ca tassa tattha paṭighānusayo ca diṭṭhānusayo ca vicikicchānusayo ca appahīnā; kāmarāgānusayo ca mānānusayo ca na vattabbā “pahīnā”ti vā “appahīnā”ti vā. Dvinnaṃ puggalānaṃ rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā [T 1.0732] tesaṃ tattha avijjānusayo ca mānānusayo ca appahīnā, no ca tesaṃ tattha diṭṭhānusayo ca vicikicchānusayo ca appahīnā; kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca na vattabbā “pahīnā”ti vā “appahīnā”ti vā. Tesaññeva [M 2.0272] puggalānaṃ kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu tesaṃ tattha avijjānusayo ca kāmarāgānusayo ca mānānusayo ca appahīnā, no ca tesaṃ tattha diṭṭhānusayo ca vicikicchānusayo ca appahīnā; paṭighānusayo na vattabbo “pahīno”ti vā “appahīno”ti vā. Tesaññeva puggalānaṃ dukkhāya vedanāya tesaṃ tattha avijjānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca appahīnā, no ca tesaṃ tattha diṭṭhānusayo ca vicikicchānusayo ca appahīnā; kāmarāgānusayo ca mānānusayo ca na vattabbā “pahīnā”ti vā “appahīnā”ti vā. Puthujjanassa [V 2.0353] rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā tassa tattha avijjānusayo ca mānānusayo ca diṭṭhānusayo ca vicikicchānusayo ca appahīnā; kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca na vattabbā “pahīnā”ti vā “appahīnā”ti vā. Tasseva puggalassa kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu tassa tattha avijjānusayo ca kāmarāgānusayo ca mānānusayo ca diṭṭhānusayo ca vicikicchānusayo ca appahīnā; paṭighānusayo na vattabbo “pahīno”ti vā “appahīno”ti vā. Tasseva puggalassa dukkhāya vedanāya tassa tattha avijjānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca diṭṭhānusayo ca vicikicchānusayo ca appahīnā; kāmarāgānusayo ca mānānusayo ca na vattabbā “pahīnā”ti vā “appahīnā”ti vā. (Pañcakamūlakaṃ)

For a non-returner, in the form realm and the formless realm, for that person, in those realms, the underlying tendencies to ignorance and conceit are not abandoned, but for that person, in those realms, the underlying tendencies to wrong view and doubt are abandoned; the underlying tendencies to sensual desire and aversion should not be said to be 'abandoned' or 'not abandoned'. For that same person, in the sensual realm regarding two feelings, for that person, in that context, the underlying tendencies to ignorance and conceit are not abandoned, but for that person, in that context, the underlying tendencies to sensual desire, wrong view, and doubt are abandoned; the underlying tendency to aversion should not be said to be 'abandoned' or 'not abandoned'. For that same person, regarding painful feeling, for that person, in that context, the underlying tendency to ignorance is not abandoned, but for that person, in that context, the underlying tendencies to aversion, wrong view, and doubt are abandoned; the underlying tendencies to sensual desire and conceit should not be said to be 'abandoned' or 'not abandoned'. For two persons, in the form realm and the formless realm, for them, in those realms, the underlying tendencies to ignorance and conceit are not abandoned, but for them, in those realms, the underlying tendencies to wrong view and doubt are abandoned; the underlying tendencies to sensual desire and aversion should not be said to be 'abandoned' or 'not abandoned'. For those same persons, in the sensual realm regarding two feelings, for them, in that context, the underlying tendencies to ignorance, sensual desire, and conceit are not abandoned, but for them, in that context, the underlying tendencies to wrong view and doubt are abandoned; the underlying tendency to aversion should not be said to be 'abandoned' or 'not abandoned'. For those same persons, regarding painful feeling, for them, in that context, the underlying tendencies to ignorance and aversion are not abandoned, but for them, in that context, the underlying tendencies to wrong view and doubt are abandoned; the underlying tendencies to sensual desire and conceit should not be said to be 'abandoned' or 'not abandoned'. For an ordinary person, in the form realm and the formless realm, for that person, in those realms, the underlying tendencies to ignorance, conceit, wrong view, and doubt are not abandoned; the underlying tendencies to sensual desire and aversion should not be said to be 'abandoned' or 'not abandoned'. For that same person, in the sensual realm regarding two feelings, for that person, in that context, the underlying tendencies to ignorance, sensual desire, conceit, wrong view, and doubt are not abandoned; the underlying tendency to aversion should not be said to be 'abandoned' or 'not abandoned'. For that same person, regarding painful feeling, for that person, in that context, the underlying tendencies to ignorance, aversion, wrong view, and doubt are not abandoned; the underlying tendencies to sensual desire and conceit should not be said to be 'abandoned' or 'not abandoned'. (Fivefold Root)

329. (Ka) yassa yattha kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca mānānusayo ca diṭṭhānusayo ca vicikicchānusayo ca bhavarāgānusayo ca appahīnā tassa tattha avijjānusayo appahīnoti? Natthi.

329. For a person for whom, in a certain sphere, the underlying tendency to sensual desire, the underlying tendency to aversion, the underlying tendency to conceit, the underlying tendency to wrong view, the underlying tendency to doubt, and the underlying tendency to craving for existence are not abandoned—for that person, in that sphere, is the underlying tendency to ignorance not abandoned? There is no such case.

(Kha) yassa vā pana yattha avijjānusayo appahīno tassa tattha kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca mānānusayo ca diṭṭhānusayo ca vicikicchānusayo ca bhavarāgānusayo ca appahīnāti?

Or again, for a person for whom, in a certain sphere, the underlying tendency to ignorance is not abandoned—for that person, in that sphere, are the underlying tendency to sensual desire, the underlying tendency to aversion, the underlying tendency to conceit, the underlying tendency to wrong view, the underlying tendency to doubt, and the underlying tendency to craving for existence not abandoned?

Anāgāmissa rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā tassa tattha avijjānusayo ca mānānusayo ca bhavarāgānusayo ca appahīnā, no ca tassa tattha diṭṭhānusayo ca vicikicchānusayo ca appahīnā; kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca na vattabbā “pahīnā”ti vā “appahīnā”ti vā. Tasseva puggalassa kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu tassa [T 1.0733] tattha avijjānusayo ca mānānusayo ca appahīnā, no ca tassa tattha kāmarāgānusayo ca diṭṭhānusayo ca vicikicchānusayo ca appahīnā; paṭighānusayo ca bhavarāgānusayo [M 2.0273] ca na vattabbā “pahīnā”ti vā “appahīnā”ti vā. Tasseva puggalassa dukkhāya vedanāya tassa tattha avijjānusayo appahīno, no ca tassa tattha paṭighānusayo ca diṭṭhānusayo ca vicikicchānusayo ca appahīnā; kāmarāgānusayo ca mānānusayo ca bhavarāgānusayo [V 2.0354] ca na vattabbā “pahīnā”ti vā “appahīnā”ti vā. Dvinnaṃ puggalānaṃ rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā tesaṃ tattha avijjānusayo ca mānānusayo ca bhavarāgānusayo ca appahīnā, no ca tesaṃ tattha diṭṭhānusayo ca vicikicchānusayo ca appahīnā; kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca na vattabbā “pahīnā”ti vā “appahīnā”ti vā. Tesaññeva puggalānaṃ kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu tesaṃ tattha avijjānusayo ca kāmarāgānusayo ca mānānusayo ca appahīnā, no ca tesaṃ tattha diṭṭhānusayo ca vicikicchānusayo ca appahīnā; paṭighānusayo ca bhavarāgānusayo ca na vattabbā “pahīnā”ti vā “appahīnā”ti vā. Tesaññeva puggalānaṃ dukkhāya vedanāya tesaṃ tattha avijjānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca appahīnā, no ca tesaṃ tattha diṭṭhānusayo ca vicikicchānusayo ca appahīnā; kāmarāgānusayo ca mānānusayo ca bhavarāgānusayo ca na vattabbā “pahīnā”ti vā “appahīnā”ti vā. Puthujjanassa rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā tassa tattha avijjānusayo ca mānānusayo ca diṭṭhānusayo [T 1.0734] ca vicikicchānusayo ca bhavarāgānusayo ca appahīnā; kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca na vattabbā “pahīnā”ti vā “appahīnā”ti vā. Tasseva puggalassa kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu tassa tattha avijjānusayo ca kāmarāgānusayo ca mānānusayo ca diṭṭhānusayo ca vicikicchānusayo ca appahīnā; paṭighānusayo ca bhavarāgānusayo ca na vattabbā “pahīnā”ti vā “appahīnā”ti vā. Tasseva puggalassa dukkhāya vedanāya tassa tattha avijjānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca diṭṭhānusayo ca vicikicchānusayo ca appahīnā; kāmarāgānusayo ca mānānusayo ca bhavarāgānusayo ca na vattabbā “pahīnā”ti vā “appahīnā”ti vā. (Chakkamūlakaṃ)

For a non-returner, in the form realm and the formless realm, for that person there the underlying tendencies of ignorance, conceit, and craving for existence are not abandoned, but for that person there the underlying tendency to wrong view and the underlying tendency to doubt are abandoned; the underlying tendency to sensual desire and the underlying tendency to aversion cannot be said to be 'abandoned' or 'not abandoned.' For that same individual, in the sensual realm regarding two kinds of feeling, for that person there the underlying tendencies of ignorance and conceit are not abandoned, but for that person there the underlying tendency to sensual desire, the underlying tendency to wrong view, and the underlying tendency to doubt are abandoned; the underlying tendency to aversion and the underlying tendency to craving for existence cannot be said to be 'abandoned' or 'not abandoned.' For that same individual, regarding painful feeling, for that person there the underlying tendency to ignorance is not abandoned, but for that person there the underlying tendency to aversion, the underlying tendency to wrong view, and the underlying tendency to doubt are abandoned; the underlying tendency to sensual desire, the underlying tendency to conceit, and the underlying tendency to craving for existence cannot be said to be 'abandoned' or 'not abandoned.' For two individuals, in the form realm and the formless realm, for those persons there the underlying tendencies of ignorance, conceit, and craving for existence are not abandoned, but for those persons there the underlying tendency to wrong view and the underlying tendency to doubt are abandoned; the underlying tendency to sensual desire and the underlying tendency to aversion cannot be said to be 'abandoned' or 'not abandoned.' For those same individuals, in the sensual realm regarding two kinds of feeling, for those persons there the underlying tendencies of ignorance, sensual desire, and conceit are not abandoned, but for those persons there the underlying tendency to wrong view and the underlying tendency to doubt are abandoned; the underlying tendency to aversion and the underlying tendency to craving for existence cannot be said to be 'abandoned' or 'not abandoned.' For those same individuals, regarding painful feeling, for those persons there the underlying tendencies of ignorance and aversion are not abandoned, but for those persons there the underlying tendency to wrong view and the underlying tendency to doubt are abandoned; the underlying tendency to sensual desire, the underlying tendency to conceit, and the underlying tendency to craving for existence cannot be said to be 'abandoned' or 'not abandoned.' For an ordinary person, in the form realm and the formless realm, for that person there the underlying tendencies of ignorance, conceit, wrong view, doubt, and craving for existence are not abandoned; the underlying tendency to sensual desire and the underlying tendency to aversion cannot be said to be 'abandoned' or 'not abandoned.' For that same individual, in the sensual realm regarding two kinds of feeling, for that person there the underlying tendencies of ignorance, sensual desire, conceit, wrong view, and doubt are not abandoned; the underlying tendency to aversion and the underlying tendency to craving for existence cannot be said to be 'abandoned' or 'not abandoned.' For that same individual, regarding painful feeling, for that person there the underlying tendencies of ignorance, aversion, wrong view, and doubt are not abandoned; the underlying tendency to sensual desire, the underlying tendency to conceit, and the underlying tendency to craving for existence cannot be said to be 'abandoned' or 'not abandoned.' (Sixfold Root)

Pahīnavāre paṭilomaṃ.

The reverse order in the section on abandonment.

Pahīnavāro.

The Section on Abandonment.

6. Uppajjanavāro

6. The Section on Origination

330. (Ka) yassa [M 2.0274][V 2.0355] kāmarāgānusayo uppajjati tassa paṭighānusayo uppajjatīti? Āmantā.

330. (Ka) For one in whom the underlying tendency to sensual desire arises, does the underlying tendency to aversion arise? Yes.

(Kha) yassa vā pana paṭighānusayo uppajjati tassa kāmarāgānusayo uppajjatīti? Āmantā.

(Kha) Or for one in whom the underlying tendency to aversion arises, does the underlying tendency to sensual desire arise? Yes.

(Ka) yassa kāmarāgānusayo uppajjati tassa mānānusayo uppajjatīti? Āmantā.

(Ka) For one in whom the underlying tendency to sensual desire arises, does the underlying tendency to conceit arise? Yes.

(Kha) yassa vā pana mānānusayo uppajjati tassa kāmarāgānusayo uppajjatīti?

(Kha) Or for one in whom the underlying tendency to conceit arises, does the underlying tendency to sensual desire arise?

Anāgāmissa mānānusayo uppajjati, no ca tassa kāmarāgānusayo uppajjati. Tiṇṇaṃ puggalānaṃ mānānusayo ca uppajjati kāmarāgānusayo [T 1.0735] ca uppajjati (vitthāretabbaṃ).

For a non-returner, the underlying tendency to conceit arises, but for that person the underlying tendency to sensual desire does not arise. For three individuals, both the underlying tendency to conceit and the underlying tendency to sensual desire arise (to be elaborated).

331. (Ka) yassa kāmarāgānusayo nuppajjati tassa paṭighānusayo nuppajjatīti? Āmantā.

331. (Ka) For one in whom the underlying tendency to sensual desire does not arise, does the underlying tendency to aversion not arise? Yes.

(Kha) yassa vā pana paṭighānusayo nuppajjati tassa kāmarāgānusayo nuppajjatīti? Āmantā.

(Kha) Or for one in whom the underlying tendency to aversion does not arise, does the underlying tendency to sensual desire not arise? Yes.

(Ka) yassa kāmarāgānusayo nuppajjati tassa mānānusayo nuppajjatīti?

(Ka) For one in whom the underlying tendency to sensual desire does not arise, does the underlying tendency to conceit not arise?

Anāgāmissa kāmarāgānusayo nuppajjati, no ca tassa mānānusayo nuppajjati. Arahato kāmarāgānusayo ca nuppajjati mānānusayo ca nuppajjati.

For the non-returner, the underlying tendency to sensual desire does not arise, but for that person the underlying tendency to conceit does arise. For the Arahant, both the underlying tendency to sensual desire and the underlying tendency to conceit do not arise.

(Kha) yassa vā pana mānānusayo nuppajjati tassa kāmarāgānusayo nuppajjatīti? Āmantā. (Vitthāretabbaṃ).

(Kha) Or for one in whom the underlying tendency to conceit does not arise, does the underlying tendency to sensual desire not arise? Yes. (To be elaborated).

Uppajjanavāro.

The Section on Origination.

341. Kāmadhātuyā [M 2.0281][V 2.0362] cutassa kāmadhātuṃ upapajjantassa kassaci satta anusayā anusenti, kassaci pañca anusayā anusenti; anusayā bhaṅgā natthi. 349. Na kāmadhātuyā na rūpadhātuyā cutassa kāmadhātuṃ upapajjantassa satteva anusayā anusenti; anusayā bhaṅgā natthi. Na kāmadhātuyā na rūpadhātuyā cutassa arūpadhātuṃ upapajjantassa kassaci satta anusayā anusenti, kassaci pañca anusayā anusenti, kassaci tayo anusayā anusenti; anusayā bhaṅgā natthi.

349. For one who has passed away from neither the sense-sphere realm nor the form-sphere realm and is being reborn in the sense-sphere realm, only seven latent tendencies lie latent; there is no classification of latent tendencies. For one who has passed away from neither the sense-sphere realm nor the form-sphere realm, there is no such thing as rebirth in the form-sphere realm; if being reborn in a lower realm, one is reborn only in the sense-sphere realm, and only seven latent tendencies lie latent; there is no classification of latent tendencies. For one who has passed away from neither the sense-sphere realm nor the form-sphere realm and is being reborn in the formless-sphere realm, for some, seven latent tendencies lie latent; for some, five latent tendencies lie latent; for some, three latent tendencies lie latent; there is no classification of latent tendencies.

Na kāmadhātuyā na rūpadhātuyā cutassa na kāmadhātuṃ upapajjantassa [T 1.0753] kassaci satta anusayā anusenti, kassaci pañca anusayā anusenti, kassaci tayo anusayā anusenti; anusayā bhaṅgā natthi. Na kāmadhātuyā na rūpadhātuyā cutassa na rūpadhātuṃ upapajjantassa kassaci satta anusayā anusenti, kassaci pañca anusayā anusenti, kassaci [V 2.0369] tayo anusayā anusenti; anusayā bhaṅgā natthi. Na kāmadhātuyā na rūpadhātuyā cutassa na arūpadhātuṃ upapajjantassa satteva anusayā anusenti; anusayā bhaṅgā natthi.

For one who has deceased from the formless realm and is being reborn not in the sense-sphere realm: for some, seven latent tendencies lie dormant; for some, five; for some, three. There is no distribution of latent tendencies. For one who has deceased from the formless realm and is being reborn not in the form realm: for some, seven latent tendencies lie dormant; for some, five; for some, three. There is no distribution of latent tendencies. For one who has deceased from the formless realm and is being reborn not in the formless realm: only seven latent tendencies lie dormant. There is no distribution of latent tendencies.

Na [M 2.0288] kāmadhātuyā na rūpadhātuyā cutassa na kāmadhātuyā na arūpadhātuyā upapatti nāma natthi, heṭṭhā upapajjamāno kāmadhātuṃyeva upapajjati, satteva anusayā anusenti; anusayā bhaṅgā natthi. Na kāmadhātuyā na rūpadhātuyā cutassa na rūpadhātuṃ na arūpadhātuṃ upapajjantassa satteva anusayā anusenti; anusayā bhaṅgā natthi. Na kāmadhātuyā na rūpadhātuyā cutassa na kāmadhātuṃ na rūpadhātuṃ upapajjantassa kassaci satta anusayā anusenti, kassaci pañca anusayā anusenti, kassaci tayo anusayā anusenti; anusayā bhaṅgā natthi. (Nakāmanarūpadhātumūlakaṃ)

For one who has deceased from the formless realm, there is no such thing as rebirth in the form realm. If one is being reborn below, one is reborn only in the sense-sphere realm, and only seven latent tendencies lie dormant; there is no distribution of latent tendencies. For one who has deceased from the formless realm and is being reborn in the sense-sphere realm: only seven latent tendencies lie dormant. There is no distribution of latent tendencies. For one who has deceased from the formless realm and is being reborn in the formless realm: for some, seven latent tendencies lie dormant; for some, five; for some, three. There is no distribution of latent tendencies. (The section rooted in 'not in the sense-sphere realm, not in the form realm'.)

Dhātuvisajjavāro.

The Chapter of Exposition on the Realms.

Anusayayamakaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Yamaka on Latent Tendencies is concluded.

Namo tassa bhagavato arahato sammāsambuddhassa

Homage to the Blessed One, the Arahant, the Perfectly Self-Enlightened One.

1. (B) Or again, to whomsoever consciousness will not cease but will arise, for them is consciousness not arising but ceasing?

8. (Ka) For whom consciousness is ceasing, for them will consciousness cease?

20. (Ka) yassa [T 2.0005] cittaṃ uppajjamānaṃ khaṇaṃ khaṇaṃ vītikkantaṃ atikkantakālaṃ, nirujjhamānaṃ khaṇaṃ khaṇaṃ vītikkantaṃ atikkantakālaṃ tassa cittaṃ?

20. (Ka) For whom the arising moment of consciousness has passed and is of past time, for them, is the ceasing moment of that consciousness also passed and of past time?

(Kha) yassa vā pana cittaṃ nirujjhamānaṃ khaṇaṃ khaṇaṃ vītikkantaṃ atikkantakālaṃ, uppajjamānaṃ khaṇaṃ khaṇaṃ vītikkantaṃ atikkantakālaṃ tassa cittaṃ?

(Ka) yassa cittaṃ na uppajjamānaṃ khaṇaṃ khaṇaṃ vītikkantaṃ atikkantakālaṃ, na nirujjhamānaṃ khaṇaṃ khaṇaṃ vītikkantaṃ atikkantakālaṃ tassa cittaṃ?

(Ka) For whom the arising moment of consciousness has not passed and is not of past time, for them, is the ceasing moment of that consciousness also not passed and not of past time?

(Kha) yassa vā pana cittaṃ na nirujjhamānaṃ khaṇaṃ khaṇaṃ vītikkantaṃ atikkantakālaṃ, na uppajjamānaṃ khaṇaṃ khaṇaṃ vītikkantaṃ atikkantakālaṃ tassa cittaṃ?

(Kha) Or else, for whom the ceasing moment of consciousness has not passed and is not of past time, for them, is the arising moment of that consciousness also not passed and not of past time?

(Kha) yaṃ vā pana cittaṃ na uppajjissati taṃ cittaṃ na uppajjittha?

Is the consciousness that is not arising, one that will not cease?

(Kha) yaṃ vā pana cittaṃ na nirujjhissati taṃ cittaṃ na uppajjittha?

Or again, is the mind that will not cease also one that did not arise?

40. (Ka) yaṃ [T 2.0009][M 2.0296] cittaṃ uppajjamānaṃ khaṇaṃ khaṇaṃ vītikkantaṃ atikkantakālaṃ, nirujjhamānaṃ khaṇaṃ khaṇaṃ vītikkantaṃ atikkantakālaṃ taṃ cittaṃ?

40. (Ka) The mind that, while arising, has passed its moment of arising and is past time—is that mind, while ceasing, also one that has passed its moment of dissolution and is past time?

(Kha) yaṃ [V 2.0381] vā pana cittaṃ nirujjhamānaṃ khaṇaṃ khaṇaṃ vītikkantaṃ atikkantakālaṃ, uppajjamānaṃ khaṇaṃ khaṇaṃ vītikkantaṃ atikkantakālaṃ taṃ cittaṃ?

(Ka) yaṃ cittaṃ na uppajjamānaṃ khaṇaṃ khaṇaṃ vītikkantaṃ atikkantakālaṃ, na nirujjhamānaṃ khaṇaṃ khaṇaṃ vītikkantaṃ atikkantakālaṃ taṃ cittaṃ?

(Ka) The mind that, while arising, has not passed its moment of arising and is not past time—is that mind, while ceasing, also one that has not passed its moment of dissolution and is not past time?

(Kha) yaṃ vā pana cittaṃ na nirujjhamānaṃ khaṇaṃ khaṇaṃ vītikkantaṃ atikkantakālaṃ, na uppajjamānaṃ khaṇaṃ khaṇaṃ vītikkantaṃ atikkantakālaṃ taṃ cittaṃ?

(Kha) Or again, the mind that, while ceasing, has not passed its moment of dissolution and is not past time—is that mind, while arising, also one that has not passed its moment of arising and is not past time?
